content:
Daily Report — 2026-04-15 Daily Overview What was done: Complete environment setup, debugging, and reproducibility implementation for ErrorRecovery robotics project spanning conda environment creation, systematic bug resolution, and dependency tracking How it was done: Conda environment creation with dependency resolution, methodical 5-bug diagnosis and fixes (pip shadowing, missing patches, dependencies, exception handling, assets), upstream comparison and patch generation, automated setup scripting Impact: Transformed non-functional local environment into fully operational and reproducible system deployable on any machine including remote clusters; documented entire troubleshooting process for future reference DesktopLinux What was done: Created and debugged recovery_collect conda environment for Coffee task, resolving interconnected bugs including pip editable install shadowing, missing robosuite patches (z_rotation, get_bounding_box_half_size, total_size parameters), missing robomimic dependency, silenced exception handling, and missing texture assets How it was done: Installed base dependencies (robosuite 1.4.1, mujoco 2.3.2, mimicgen), fixed version conflicts, copied XML assets, monkey-patched missing APIs, then systematically diagnosed root causes using pip show/diff/grep/traceback analysis; applied sequential fixes: removed stale directories, reapplied robosuite_recovery.patch, installed robomimic –no-deps, improved error reporting, copied ceramic.png texture; created requirements.txt baseline via import scanning Impact: Coffee_D0 environment now fully functional and passes all validation checks; TUTORIAL.md section 4 documents complete troubleshooting process with verification scripts; established reproducible dependency baseline MacBook What was done: Resolved environment reproducibility blockers by tracking modified mimicgen library (545 files) and creating patch system for robosuite (13 modified files) How it was done: Compared local copies against upstream repositories (NVlabs/mimicgen, commit c848ca84 for robosuite), filtered CRLF/LF noise using –strip-trailing-cr, generated unified diff patches, updated setup_env.sh to auto-apply patches after upstream installation, committed mimicgen fork directly and pushed to GitHub Impact: Environment now fully reproducible for cluster deployment and collaboration; avoided 587MB robosuite commit via 326-line patch file; any machine can clone and set up working environment Systematically debugged and resolved ErrorRecovery robotics project environment setup, fixing 5 critical bugs blocking Coffee task execution, then established full reproducibility by tracking modified dependencies and creating automated patch system for cluster deployment
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Fix 5 critical environment bugs blocking Coffee task — Resolved pip editable install shadowing, missing robosuite recovery patches (z_rotation, get_bounding_box_half_size, total_size parameters), missing robomimic dependency, silenced exception handling, and missing ceramic.png texture ✅ Create robosuite patch system for reproducibility — Generated unified diff patch (326 lines) for 13 modified robosuite files instead of committing 587MB source tree, updated setup_env.sh to auto-apply patches after upstream installation ✅ Document troubleshooting process in TUTORIAL.md — Added section 4 to TUTORIAL.md with detailed bug summary table, step-by-step diagnosis and fixes, patch inventory, and environment verification script ✅ Track modified mimicgen library in Git repository — Added locally modified mimicgen fork (545 files, 13MB) to shared/mimicgen_workspace/mimicgen/, removed from .gitignore, committed and pushed to GitHub ✅ Create and debug recovery_collect conda environment — Created Python 3.10 conda environment, resolved mujoco version conflict (3.7.0→2.3.2), installed mimicgen and copied XML assets, identified need for patched robosuite from cluster Implementation & Fixes ✅ Analyze modifications against upstream repositories — Compared local mimicgen with NVlabs/mimicgen upstream and robosuite against commit c848ca84, documented compatibility fixes, new tasks, and MimicGen API additions ✅ Create requirements.txt baseline — Scanned 55 project files for imports, created structured requirements.txt with 9 core dependencies and special installation notes, audited actual conda environment packages Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. Robosuite missing critical patches (z_rotation parameter, get_bounding_box_half_size, total_size, locations_relative_to_corner) required by MimicGen, causing environment creation failures Solution: Reapplied shared/mimicgen_workspace/robosuite_patches/robosuite_recovery.patch to installed robosuite package using patch -p1; verified all parameters exist in target class signatures
Key Insight: MimicGen requires patched robosuite with custom APIs not present in official releases; patched dependencies must be re-patched after pip install overwrites them; cluster uses local patched copies in shared/mimicgen_workspace/ rather than upstream versions
2. script_utils.py create_env function silently swallowed exceptions with ’except Exception: continue’, showing only generic ‘Could not create env’ error Solution: Modified exception handling to capture last_error and re-raise with original traceback context in RuntimeError, revealing the actual MuJoCo PNG loading error
Key Insight: Exception handling with bare ’except: continue’ or ’except Exception: pass’ makes debugging extremely difficult and should never be used in diagnostic/setup code; always capture the actual exception, log it, and include it in re-raised errors
3. Shared/ directory with critical dependencies was gitignored, making environment non-reproducible for other users or cluster deployment Solution: Tracked modified mimicgen directly in repo (13MB); created patch file system for robosuite to avoid 587MB commit; updated setup_env.sh to auto-apply patches after upstream installation
Key Insight: External dependencies with local modifications should be tracked in-repo (if small) or via patch files (if large) rather than blindly gitignored, especially for reproducible research environments; unified diff patches minimize repository size while preserving reproducibility
4. Pip editable install of mimicgen shadowed by residual site-packages/mimicgen/ directory from previous install, causing import failures Solution: Removed stale site-packages/mimicgen/ directory; pip editable install then correctly mapped to src/mimicgen
Key Insight: Editable pip installs on NTFS cross-filesystem mounts can leave residual site-packages directories that take precedence over editable path mappings; always verify import resolution matches pip show location by checking path and file attributes
5. 776 file differences between installed robosuite and upstream turned out to be mostly CRLF vs LF line ending noise, obscuring 13 real code changes Solution: Used diff –strip-trailing-cr to filter line ending differences, revealing only 13 files with actual code modifications
Key Insight: Cross-platform development creates false positives in file comparison due to line ending differences; always use –strip-trailing-cr or -w flags when comparing across Windows/Linux platforms
General Issues 6. Pip-installed mimicgen missing XML assets (coffee_pod.xml, coffee_body.xml) required by environment definitions Solution: Cloned mimicgen repo and manually copied assets/ directory to site-packages
Key Insight: Setup.py may not package all necessary data files; always verify critical non-Python assets are included in distribution
7. Missing robomimic dependency caused import failures in mimicgen config modules Solution: Installed robomimic with pip install robomimic –no-deps to bypass egl_probe build failure (EGL rendering not needed for SpaceMouse collection)
Key Insight: Use –no-deps to install packages when optional rendering dependencies fail to build but core functionality remains intact
8. Robosuite installation upgraded mujoco to 3.7.0, breaking API compatibility with robosuite 1.4.1 Solution: Force reinstalled mujoco 2.3.2 with –no-deps flag to prevent transitive upgrades
Key Insight: Use –no-deps when reinstalling pinned dependencies to prevent package managers from upgrading transitive dependencies
9. MuJoCo failed to load ceramic.png texture (PNG file load error) because shared/mimicgen_workspace/mimicgen/ lacked assets/textures/ directory present in src/mimicgen upstream Solution: Copied ceramic.png from src/mimicgen/mimicgen/models/robosuite/assets/textures/ to shared/mimicgen_workspace/mimicgen/mimicgen/models/robosuite/assets/textures/
Key Insight: When MuJoCo environments fail with asset loading errors, check both Python import paths and relative asset paths (meshes, textures) referenced in XML model definitions
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Root cause diagnosis for Coffee environment failure Role Approach Human Suspected MuJoCo version mismatch and asked if upgrading to latest MuJoCo 3.x would solve the problem AI Identified it was not a MuJoCo version issue but missing robosuite patches and texture files; explained upgrading to MuJoCo 3.x would break robosuite 1.4.1 API compatibility Difference Analysis: Human hypothesis focused on framework version mismatch; AI traced actual error through diagnostic commands to identify missing patches and assets; upgrading MuJoCo would have been counterproductive
Solving reproducibility problem approach Role Approach Human Immediately recognized shared/ directory not being tracked was a blocker and explicitly requested making it reproducible; pushed for concrete action (‘push to github’) AI Initially suggested three abstract options (add git URL, use submodule, or fork) without checking if local modifications existed Difference Analysis: Human had domain knowledge this was blocking deployment and correctly prioritized action over discussion; AI took academic approach of listing alternatives before diagnosis
Implementation Level Detecting actual vs false file differences Role Approach Human Asked to check if robosuite had ‘any modifications’, implying skepticism about whether real changes existed AI Initially saw 776 file differences and tried to categorize them, eventually discovering most were line-ending artifacts Difference Analysis: User’s question implied suspicion that large diff count might be artifacts; AI initially took diff count at face value before applying proper filtering
Installation strategy and incremental setup Role Approach Human Prioritized conda packages first, skipped system dependencies to minimize complexity and focus on Python environment AI Attempted comprehensive setup including system packages (libhidapi-dev, libglfw3-dev) all at once Difference Analysis: Human’s incremental approach enabled faster iteration and clearer diagnosis of environment issues; AI’s all-at-once strategy would have made debugging more complex
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Spent significant effort monkey-patching missing APIs before identifying that patched robosuite source was the actual requirement; did not recognize shared/mimicgen_workspace/ directory structure as indicator of custom patches until late in debugging Took many diagnostic commands before recognizing editable install was shadowed by residual directory; should have immediately checked site-packages when pip show and traceback paths diverged; did not immediately recognize path conflict as critical indicator Initially proposed three abstract solution options for mimicgen reproducibility without first checking whether local modifications existed or understanding their scope; wasted tool calls checking git history for never-tracked shared/ directory General Limitations Generated initial robosuite patch with absolute paths that needed regeneration with relative paths for portability Attempted upgrading to robosuite 1.5.2 without checking backward compatibility with mimicgen first Learnings Key Learnings MimicGen requires patched robosuite with custom APIs (get_bounding_box_half_size, total_size, locations_relative_to_corner, z_rotation) not present in official releases; version pinning in setup scripts may refer to local patched copies in shared/ directories rather than upstream commits Editable pip installs on NTFS cross-filesystem mounts can leave residual site-packages directories that shadow editable path mappings; always verify import resolution matches pip show location by checking both path and file attributes; patched dependencies must be re-patched after pip install overwrites them Exception handling with bare ’except: continue’ or ’except Exception: pass’ makes debugging extremely difficult and should never be used in diagnostic/setup code; always capture the actual exception, log it, and include it in re-raised errors for proper diagnosis External dependencies with local modifications should be tracked in-repo (if small) or via patch files (if large) rather than blindly gitignored; unified diff patches are the correct tool for tracking modifications to large upstream projects - they minimize repository size, document exact changes, and enable automated application Cross-platform line ending differences (CRLF vs LF) can create massive false positives in file comparisons; always use –strip-trailing-cr or -w flags when comparing across Windows/Linux platforms to reveal actual code changes When robosuite environments fail to load, check three layers: Python import paths (pip show, sys.path), robosuite registration (REGISTERED_ENVS), and MuJoCo asset file paths (textures, meshes, XML relative references) Pip packages may exclude data files (XML assets, configs); always verify critical non-Python files are packaged correctly in distribution; setup.py may miss necessary asset directories Practical Learnings Use –no-deps when reinstalling pinned dependencies or installing packages with optional rendering dependencies that fail to build but aren’t needed for core functionality Presence of .orig and .rej files indicates a patch was attempted, but empty diffs mean the patches may have already been successfully applied (artifacts weren’t cleaned up) Conversation Summaries ErrorRecovery ✅ Coffee environment setup debugging - 5 bug fix chain 04:44:49.213 | claude_code User updated patches and asked if Coffee task could now run. Systematically debugged 5 interconnected bugs blocking environment creation: pip editable install shadowed by residual site-packages directory, robosuite missing recovery patches (z_rotation parameter), missing robomimic dependency, create_env silently swallowing exceptions, and missing ceramic.png texture file. Applied fixes sequentially with verification at each step, added TUTORIAL.md section 4 documenting the entire troubleshooting process with diagnostic commands and verification scripts. Coffee_D0 environment now creates successfully and passes all validation checks.
✅ Fix environment reproducibility by tracking modified dependencies 03:26:06.618 | claude_code User identified that shared/ directory containing modified mimicgen and robosuite wasn’t tracked in Git, blocking cluster deployment. Compared local copies against upstream (NVlabs/mimicgen, robosuite commit c848ca84), filtered CRLF/LF noise, found essential modifications in both libraries (mimicgen: compatibility fixes and new Lift_Config; robosuite: 13 patched files adding MimicGen-required APIs). Solution: committed mimicgen directly (13MB), created 326-line patch file for robosuite (avoiding 587MB commit), and updated setup_env.sh to auto-apply patches. Successfully pushed to GitHub, enabling full environment reproducibility for cluster deployment.
🔄 Initial environment setup and dependency debugging 03:02:12.642 | claude_code Created recovery_collect conda environment and debugged multiple dependency issues. Fixed mujoco version conflict (3.7.0→2.3.2), installed mimicgen and copied missing XML assets, monkey-patched get_bounding_box_half_size into robosuite classes. Discovered root cause: pip-installed robosuite lacks patches from cluster’s shared/mimicgen_workspace/robosuite/. Initially blocked on syncing patched dependencies from cluster.
✅ Create requirements.txt baseline for project dependencies 02:48:44.541 | claude_code User requested requirements.txt update. Scanned all Python imports across 55 non-shared project files using grep-based pattern matching, identified 9 core third-party packages (numpy, scipy, mujoco, h5py, pyyaml, opencv-python, glfw, hidapi, tqdm, imageio, numba, matplotlib), and created structured requirements.txt with sections for core dependencies, rendering tools, utilities, and analysis packages. Ran pip list on recovery_collect conda environment to audit actual installed packages, identifying discrepancies like missing imageio-ffmpeg, pynput, and PyOpenGL in requirements.txt.
Unknown ❌ MacBook authentication failures (90+ sessions) 04:41:54.333 | claude_code Over 90 Claude Code sessions on MacBook showed identical ‘Not logged in · Please run /login’ errors with no actual work performed. These appear to be failed authentication attempts, empty connection tests, or auto-reconnect failures. No user interaction or task completion occurred in any of these sessions.

MIHD tasks implemented in 4 waves based on dependencies, prioritizing non-blocking tasks (P1-22/18/19/20), integrating existing infrastructure (P1-4). Git conflict resolved by identifying ‘independent identical refactoring’ nature through commit history comparison Impact: MIHD project unlocked key capabilities: HD dataset (17502 spots, 8μm resolution) RM-IDEAL evaluation pipeline, label mixing diagnostic tool (revealing Layer_4 accuracy only 19.3%), ARI stability quantification framework, prepared data foundation for paper Fig 4/5. TokenMonitor avoided catastrophic merge (54 file conflicts), successfully synced to v0.7.2 (remote superset version). 18GB checkpoint transfer completed robotics learning environment deployment prerequisite. Independent Claude Code environment supports multi-device/multi-project isolated configuration. Restored gadget multi-device log synchronization capability DCC What was done: MIHD spatial omics benchmark project: implemented 5 code modules (HD RM-IDEAL data loading, label mixing batch effect analysis, ARI multi-run stability testing, HD intermediate patch size experiments, neighborhood query integration), submitted 2 SLURM GPU jobs, launched 3 HD evaluation tasks, updated plans.md and verification checklist, analyzed current blocking progress (3 GPU jobs running/pending) How it was done: Adopted ccplan skill systematic workflow: (1) mapped 13 meeting tasks to plans.md to identify missing items, (2) created 5 TaskCreate and executed by dependency DAG, (3) each task included new script writing + SLURM job configuration + documentation update. Key technical decisions: P1-22 used Hungarian matching to solve label alignment, P1-18 generated confusion matrix heatmap, P1-19 loaded embeddings from cache to accelerate repeated experiments, P1-20 designed 4 patch size comparison experiments, P1-4 integrated existing neighborhood_aggregate() function. Prepared data pipeline for P1-5 multi-method query comparison and Fig 4/5 paper charts. 2 SLURM jobs (45484777/45484778) submitted awaiting GPU resources MacBook What was done: Completed two independent engineering tasks: (1) uploaded two large tar.gz files (libero_10_gr00t 14GB + qcvla_checkpoints 4GB) to athena.egr.duke.edu server, (2) handled TokenMonitor project git pull conflict (local main and origin/main each had 16 different commits, 54 file conflicts). Analysis pipeline blocked by dependencies but laid foundation for debugging failed demos; new collection flow drastically improved UX (24→10 min/task estimate), supports 6 tasks × 136 subtypes × 10 demos = 1360 target TzJsDesktop What was done: Fixed rclone remote path configuration for gadget project’s summarize module after user migrated remote directory structure to gdrive:gadget/ How it was done: Identified config mismatch via grep/read tools, edited ~/.config/summarize/config.json to update rclone_remote path from ‘gdrive:summarize’ to ‘gdrive:gadget/summarize’, verified with test run Impact: Successfully restored 184 log file sync from gdrive:gadget/summarize/logs/, enabling proper multi-device merge workflow and ensuring proper backup of AI conversation logs and generated reports tianhe What was done: Configured independent Claude Code instance (claude-code command) using CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-code for configuration isolation. Produced 6 deliverable videos (pick_place, stack, coffee, threading, stack_three, three_piece_assembly); documented complete error scene generation pipeline; clarified design rationale for id_eligible scenes that appear similar to reset states (249/1365 scenes by design, not bug) Completed 5 MIHD core modules (HD dataset support, label mixing analysis, ARI stability testing, patch size experiments, neighborhood query integration), uploaded 18GB checkpoint to athena server, resolved TokenMonitor git conflict, implemented error recovery benchmark analysis pipeline and data collection workflow, generated 6 task success videos, configured independent Claude Code environment on tianhe server, and fixed gadget rclone configuration
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ MIHD: P1-22 HD RM-IDEAL data loading adaptation — Modified benchmark_rm_ideal.py to support Visium HD dataset: added –dataset HD/–crop_dir/–fine_grained parameters, implemented load_hd_section_string_labels() to load string GT labels from STHD annotations (17502/17502 100% match), support single section within-sample evaluation mode, automatic HD output directory switching ✅ Data collection workflow refactoring (error recovery) — Refactored old sequential collection script to user-friendly round-robin mode: created collect.sh entry, modified Python main loop to support round-robin, added progress display, implemented collected_data automatic archiving, support 10 per subtype (total 1360), three-camera interface (agentview + sideview + wrist) ✅ MIHD: P1-18 Label mixing batch effect analysis — Created analyze_label_mixing.py script, applied Hungarian matching to align predicted labels, generated confusion matrix heatmap + spatial mismatch map + layer mixing detail chart. Key finding: 3 sections overall accuracy 49-61%, Layer_4 worst (19.3% avg often misclassified as Layer_3/5), Layer_2 split (40.1%), outer Layer_1/WM best (83-100%). ARI stability analysis would be extremely slow (~30min/section/run) if rerunning entire pipeline (extract+align+fusion+cluster), 10 runs × 11 sections = 330 experiments infeasible Solution: Designed architecture to load existing gene/vision embeddings from cache, only rerun fusion+clustering stages. analyze_ari_stability.py directly calls CacheManager to load PCA/UNI2, uses different seeds to initialize STAIGTrainer fusion, then cluster. Key Insight: Key optimization point for repeated experiments is identifying where randomness exists - MIHD’s vision extraction is deterministic (UNI2 model fixed weights), gene PCA also fixed, only STAIG fusion’s GCN initialization, dropout, mclust random seed affect ARI. Through layered caching (data→gene emb→vision emb→fused emb→clustering) can resume at any stage

MIHD label mixing analysis had predicted labels not matching GT label values, resulting in only 2.6% accuracy Solution: Identified that pipeline stored pred_labels are original cluster IDs (not Hungarian matched), while ARI/NMI are permutation invariant so don’t need matching. Applied scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment() for Hungarian matching in analyze_label_mixing.py, used matched aligned_pred for visualization functions, accuracy corrected to 49-61%
Key Insight: Permutation invariant metrics like ARI/NMI hide label alignment issues - when generating confusion matrix or per-class metrics must first do Hungarian matching, otherwise will get misleading extremely low accuracy. Pipeline caching design choice to store original cluster IDs is correct (maintains flexibility), but downstream analysis needs to be aware of this

Key at this time is identifying ‘who is superset of whom’ rather than file-by-file comparison. Filled main results tables (Table 5: 5-task RSR), heatmaps (Fig 4: 24 subtypes), and RBG analysis (Fig 5). Performs Wilcoxon DE test, uses Hungarian matching for cluster-to-layer alignment, validates marker gene recovery (PCP4/NEFL/TLE4/MBP), generates dot plots and spatial marker plots. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. Teddy+UNI2 multimodal fusion degrades white matter discrimination: Teddy-only ARI=0.186, concat ARI=0.151 (-19%), mean ARI=0.153 (-18%). Root cause: Teddy arrives pre-L2-normalized in 1024d with per-dim variance 4.3e-5 (460x smaller than PCA 50d at 2.0e-2). After pipeline L2-normalization, gene signal contributes only 13.3% of total variance in concat (2560d) while vision dominates at 86.7%. Solution: Background agent analyzed section 151673 embeddings and discovered variance distribution mismatch. Fix options: PCA-reduce Teddy before fusion, variance-weighted concatenation, or standard scaling instead of L2 normalization.
Key Insight: Pre-normalized high-dimensional embeddings lose signal strength after dimension-agnostic L2 normalization. Fusion strategies must account for input variance distributions. High dimensionality alone doesn’t guarantee discriminative power—variance per dimension is critical.
2. STAIG fusion shows no difference between Teddy and PCA encoders (Teddy avg=0.495, PCA avg=0.467, diff=+0.028 within noise std=0.119). All gene encoder comparisons using STAIG fusion appear invalid. Solution: Code inspection revealed models/Fusion.py line 1253: staig_fusion passes gene_feat=staig_gene_feat_3000.npz (raw HVG), completely ignoring the gene_emb argument. Both Teddy+STAIG and PCA+STAIG use identical inputs. Observed ARI differences are stochastic GCN training noise, not systematic gene encoder effects.
Key Insight: STAIG fusion architectural bug: gene encoder parameter is a no-op. All gene encoders collapse to raw HVG input regardless of specified encoder. This invalidates comparative evaluation of gene encoders when using STAIG as fusion method.
3. Single cursor (_current_line_start) in MeetingHelper cannot track two independent partial lines (mic and system audio), causing text corruption and overwrites during concurrent transcription output. Solution: Refactored to region-based architecture: split subtitle window into two zones (MIC/SYS), each with independent cursor, file handle, partial line buffer, and finalization logic. Adversarial audit by Opus subagent caught this fatal concurrency bug before implementation.
Key Insight: Concurrent transcription output requires isolated state management per source. Shared mutable state (cursor, buffer) is the root cause of concurrency bugs. ccplan adversarial audit phase prevents implementing fundamentally broken architectures.
4. Portable collection scripts hardcoded 6 tasks across pack/run scripts and tutorial, requiring manual updates in multiple files for each new task addition. Solution: Centralized task definition in task_registry.yaml and made all scripts dynamically derive task lists. Implemented automatic portable registry generation during packaging with fail-fast asset validation (task_config, HDF5, scenes).
Key Insight: Centralized configuration with dynamic derivation eliminates multi-file consistency problems and scales better than manual synchronization across scattered hardcoded lists.
5. Five interrelated bugs in error-recovery pipeline caused 100% MimicGen augmentation failure (0/10 success rate): controller cache desync, quaternion format mismatch, leading zero-action frames, missing settling mechanism, and demo validation order. Solution: Systematically fixed all 5 bugs in causal chain: (1) controller sync after state modification, (2) quaternion wxyz→xyzw conversion, (3) trim leading zero-action frames, (4) add settling mechanism, (5) validate demo before augmentation. Success rate improved to 40% (4/10). Fixes applied to recovery mainline but only partially propagated to training source data pipeline.
Key Insight: Complex system failures are rarely single-point issues but cascading effects of multiple subtle bugs. Requires systematic identification and repair of entire causal chain. Code reuse across dependency paths requires explicit tracking to ensure fixes propagate everywhere.
6. libero2lerobot_parallel.py slows down drastically after processing many episodes (O(n²) performance degradation as dataset grows). Solution: Removed dataset.hf_dataset = dataset.create_hf_dataset() from the per-episode loop (line 224). This call rescans all existing parquet files, causing O(n²) cumulative cost as dataset grows. save_episode() already persists data; hf_dataset rebuild only needed at end if dataset will be read.
Key Insight: Incremental data operations should avoid full dataset reconstruction in loops. Always profile long-running pipelines for hidden O(n²) patterns—particularly operations that ‘rescan from scratch’ on each iteration.
7. HD basic_contrastive and QFormer fusion failed with CUDA illegal memory access and OOM errors on RTX 2080 Ti (11GB VRAM). RTX 2080 Ti insufficient for HD 17,502 spots × 550 epochs. Solution: Resubmitted jobs to gpu-common partition with explicit GPU constraint gres=gpu:5000_ada:1 (24GB VRAM), increased memory to 64GB, and extended time limit to 2 days. Separated QFormer into dedicated experiment config to isolate memory-intensive fusions.
Key Insight: Large-scale spatial data (17K+ spots) requires ≥24GB VRAM for contrastive learning. SLURM GPU type specification syntax: –gres=gpu:: (e.g., gres=gpu:5000_ada:1) to request specific GPU models within heterogeneous partitions.
8. LeRobot 0.4.0 updated add_frame() signature to require task as separate positional argument instead of embedding in frame dict, breaking existing conversion code. Solution: Modified worker function to return task_instruction separately; changed add_frame call from add_frame(frame_data) to add_frame(frame_data, task=task_instruction); removed task injection into frame dict.
Key Insight: API breaking changes in dependencies require signature inspection and adaptation. Old pattern of embedding metadata in data dict replaced by explicit parameters in LeRobot 0.4.0.
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Cross-chemistry battery foundation model approach Role Approach Human Intuited need for domain-invariant degradation indicator z where z=0 represents EOL universally; proposed learning when z reaches 0 rather than learning degradation rate (slope). Focus on endpoint alignment across chemistries. AI Connected human’s intuition to formal domain generalization theory (DANN, disentangled representations); identified physical candidates for z (SOH, internal resistance, coulombic loss, dQ/dV peaks); designed three-phase verification protocol (physics → normalization → learned representations). Added feasibility constraints and identified pitfalls (extrapolation risk, data imbalance). Difference Analysis: Human’s domain insight (endpoint invariance) mapped to ML literature by AI. Human focused on conceptual invariance; AI provided systematic validation roadmap and practical implementation constraints. Complementary strengths: human domain intuition + AI methodological rigor.
Paper writing approach: outline-first vs immediate drafting Role Approach Human User explicitly requested outline first (‘我要一个大纲先’) before proceeding to full paper, showing preference for staged approval and review at checkpoints for large deliverables. AI AI initially started exploration to write paper directly. After human clarification, AI adapted to create comprehensive outline, get approval, then execute full implementation in structured phases. Difference Analysis: Human preferred staged gate reviews for large deliverables (38KB paper) to ensure alignment before significant effort and reduce rework risk. AI default was exploratory-then-implement. Human’s phased approach is more efficient for high-stakes documents requiring structural consensus.
Intent articulation for dual audio source requirement (MeetingHelper) Role Approach Human User expressed need in casual natural language: ‘我想要录进去 meeting system 的声音，然后得到要用 transcript’ (non-technical, ambiguous phrasing without specifying simultaneous vs either-or). AI ccplan Phase 0 intent calibration: presented 3 concrete options (simultaneous dual-channel / system-only / either-or) with technical trade-offs, forcing user to clarify exact requirement before any implementation. Difference Analysis: Humans express needs in fuzzy natural language; AI uses structured questioning to calibrate ambiguous intent into precise technical requirements. This prevents implementing the wrong solution. ccplan workflow excels at disambiguation.
Task prioritization and GPU resource allocation strategy Role Approach Human User insisted on retrying failed GPU jobs with larger GPUs (A5000, A6000, 5000 Ada) rather than accepting RTX 2080 Ti failures as blocking issues. Directly asked ‘你用更好的 GPU 试试？’ after seeing OOM errors. AI AI initially reported GPU failures as completion blockers without proactively suggesting alternative GPU types. Only after user prompt did AI check available GPU partitions (sinfo) and create new SLURM scripts with explicit GPU constraints. Difference Analysis: Human prioritizes resource escalation over task abandonment; AI defaults to reporting constraints rather than exploring cluster resources. User’s domain knowledge of HPC cluster heterogeneity drove solution. AI should proactively check available resources before declaring blockers.
Comprehensiveness of bug fix verification (error-recovery) Role Approach Human Human asked ‘is training source data mimicgen augmentation also fixed?’, demonstrating holistic understanding of system dependency chains and potential for fixes to not propagate across all code paths. AI AI initially focused only on recovery mainline fix status, expanding to training source data pipeline only after human follow-up. Discovered partial missing fixes (collect_success_from_error.py and generate_success_from_error.py). Difference Analysis: Human excels at architectural-level thinking about ‘which other modules might be affected’. AI tends to focus on directly asked scope. Highlights human advantage in systematic dependency analysis. AI should proactively map shared code paths during verification.
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Did not proactively suggest GPU resource escalation after initial RTX 2080 Ti failures (HD basic_contrastive CUDA error, QFormer OOM). Only checked sinfo for alternative GPU types after explicit user prompt ‘你用更好的 GPU 试试？’. Should immediately explore cluster resources and propose A6000/5000 Ada options when encountering resource-related failures. When analyzing bug fix status in error-recovery, AI initially did not proactively identify the risk of ‘multiple code paths sharing underlying implementation but fixes not fully synchronized’. Required human prompting (‘is training source data also fixed?’) to expand analysis scope and discover partial missing fixes. Adversarial audit requires independent subagent for effective ‘red-blue confrontation’. During ccplan Phase 5, AI cannot perform adversarial review alone—needs dual perspectives. Must spawn Opus subagent as critic to uncover design flaws (e.g., single-cursor concurrency bug in MeetingHelper that would have been missed without adversarial review). Hit API 429 rate limit errors during battery foundation model discussion, interrupting critical research conversation about domain-invariant degradation indicators. When encountering sandbox permission limits in BOSS performance diagnosis, AI spent excessive tokens trying various technical workarounds (different find commands, path variants, privilege methods) instead of promptly explaining the issue to user and requesting help or strategy adjustment. Required three rounds of clarifying questions to nail down implementation scope for portable script refactor (full-chain vs partial, auto-sync vs manual, fail-fast vs warn). Could not infer complete requirements from initial vague request ‘put new tasks into portable scripts’. General Limitations Did not proactively suggest workflow optimization (auto-approval settings) despite repeated user confirmations indicating friction. Required explicit user request to address systemic inefficiency in MIHD project exploratory work. Learnings Key Learnings NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks track paper structure: 9-page main body with Methods in appendix, ML-oriented language, emphasis on systematic evaluation over algorithmic novelty. Core contribution: fusion strategy dominance (ARI range 0.16-0.55 across fusions vs <0.05 across encoders). Strong ‘difficulty proof’ essential: Pi0.5 FT 3.7% RSR vs 60-70% normal SR catastrophic gap. Pre-normalized high-dimensional embeddings lose discriminative power in dimension-agnostic fusion: Teddy 1024d pre-L2-normalized has 460x less per-dim variance than PCA 50d; after pipeline L2-normalization, gene signal is invisible in concat/mean with UNI2 1536d. Solution: variance-weighted fusion, PCA-reduce high-dim embeddings before fusion, or standard scaling instead of L2 norm. ccplan workflow prevents ‘implementing the wrong thing’ and ‘missing critical edge cases’. Multi-stage pipeline (intent calibration → hypothesis validation → adversarial audit → review gate) caught 9 issues in MeetingHelper including fatal single-cursor concurrency bug before implementation. Structured divergence + convergence superior to straight-line coding. Adversarial audit by independent Opus subagent is essential—cannot self-critique effectively. CCPlan (Evolving Constraint Planning) workflow scales well for multi-task projects: 11 P0/P1 tasks organized into 3 waves (immediate → analysis → refinement) with parallel agent execution and structured ECL document tracking. Key: continuous execution mandate (phases flow without user prompts) and AskUserQuestion tool for checkpoints. Multi-agent exploration pattern for complex codebases: launch 3 parallel agents (results, methodology, plans) with targeted prompts, then synthesize findings into structured deliverable. Effective for large projects with distributed documentation. Used successfully for MIHD paper writing. Cross-chemistry battery degradation modeling can leverage CV domain generalization: disentangle domain-invariant (z ~ degradation state) from domain-specific (chemistry) representations. Physical anchoring (internal resistance, coulombic loss, dQ/dV peaks) provides interpretable initialization for learned z. Three-phase verification: physics candidates → normalization validation → contrastive learning encoder. LeRobot 0.4.0 dtype semantics: ‘image’=bytes inline in parquet (PNG per frame), ‘video’=MP4 in videos/ directory. meta.video_keys only returns dtype:‘video’ features. For large datasets, always use dtype:‘video’ for efficient MP4 encoding rather than storing PNG bytes per frame. Incremental data pipelines must avoid O(n²) operations: rebuilding entire dataset after each element adds cumulative cost. libero2lerobot_parallel’s dataset.create_hf_dataset() in loop caused dramatic slowdown after ~1000 episodes. Always profile long-running pipelines for hidden O(n²) patterns—particularly operations that ‘rescan from scratch’. Centralized configuration with dynamic derivation scales better than scattered hardcoded lists. Fail-fast validation at build time prevents incomplete artifacts better than runtime warnings. Applied in error-recovery portable scripts: task_registry.yaml as single source of truth eliminates multi-file consistency problems. STAIG fusion architectural insight: gene_emb parameter is ignored in models/Fusion.py line 1253; fusion always uses raw HVG 3000d from staig_gene_feat_3000.npz. This explains why Teddy+STAIG and PCA+STAIG have identical performance (diff within noise). All gene encoder comparisons using STAIG are invalid. DE analysis validation workflow: load raw adata (not HVG subset) → run rank_genes_groups with wilcoxon → use Hungarian matching to align predicted clusters to ground truth layers → check marker gene ranks in expected layers. Key markers for DLPFC: PCP4/NEFL (Layer 5), MBP/MOBP (WM), CARTPT (Layer 3). Poor marker recovery can reflect genuine biological clustering difficulty, not just algorithmic failure—always validate GT baseline. Bootstrap confidence intervals essential for small-n comparisons: STAIG 10-section avg ARI=0.495 [0.387, 0.597] vs PCA=0.265 [0.230, 0.296] shows non-overlapping CIs confirming significance. Implemented via utils/statistics.py with n=1000 resampling; 95% CI = (percentile_2.5, percentile_97.5). SLURM GPU type specification syntax: use –gres=gpu:: format (e.g., gres=gpu:5000_ada:1, gres=gpu:a6000:1) to request specific GPU models within heterogeneous partitions. gpu-common and scavenger-gpu both have mixed GPU types; explicit constraint prevents allocation to underpowered GPUs. RTX 2080 Ti (11GB) insufficient for HD spatial data; need ≥24GB VRAM. Complex system failures are rarely single-point issues but cascading effects of multiple subtle bugs. error-recovery pipeline: 5 interrelated bugs (controller cache, quaternion, zero-action frames, settling, validation order) caused 100% failure. Requires systematic identification and repair of entire causal chain. Code reuse across dependency paths requires explicit tracking to ensure fixes propagate. Region-based UI architecture ideal for concurrent output: when multiple async data sources need to update the same UI simultaneously, allocating independent regions (cursor, buffer, draw logic) per source is cleaner and less error-prone than shared state + locks. Applied in MeetingHelper dual audio transcription. Settings propagate to all subdirectories and sessions. Applied in MIHD project. Shell SIGPIPE handling requires care when downstream commands (head, grep -m) exit early. Use dedicated extraction functions or process substitution to avoid broken pipe errors polluting output. Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level MimicGen Augmentation Strategy – Repeated error injection vs Fixed error scene + Reset randomization Role Approach Human Humans identify the fundamental problem with the current logic: re-injecting errors into each target scene for diversity, which does not conform to the original MimicGen design. Judgment on Terminal UX Quality Role Approach Human Intuitive evaluation based on intuition: ‘It doesn’t look like a terminal at all, something is wrong’—using real terminals for immediate pattern recognition. AI Technical checklist: identifying missing WebGL renderers, Unicode11, appropriate themes, resize synchronization—the system diagnoses the root cause. Difference Analysis: Humans are good at overall UX evaluation, while AI excels at breaking down technical gaps. Humans identify problems immediately, while AI provides diagnosis and solutions.
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Failure to Propose Technical Research: AI is ready to implement the design but does not suggest researching existing solutions first. Engineers lack the awareness that ‘reusing is better than rewriting’. Inadequate Inferring Implicit Requirements: When users say ‘unwilling to switch windows’, AI only focuses on remote SSH scenarios and fails to infer that local CLI also requires unified management. Stronger scenario completeness reasoning is needed. It took 6 rounds of diagnostics to locate all MimicGen bugs: subtask fragmentation → retract not warp → gripper detects errors → insufficient interpolation steps → parallel path bugs → cache cleanup. AI cannot anticipate all issues at once. First attempt to access the OpenReview API failed, unaware of recent authentication policy changes. All 30+ attempts (API v1/v2, different endpoints, guest login, various headers) returned a 403, until the user provided credentials. The system lacks the latest knowledge of OpenReview authentication requirements for 2026. Failed to detect that SessionManager was never instantiated during the initial architecture scan—it took a lot of time to debug port conflicts and WebSocket issues before the root cause was identified as an empty onMessage handler. AI initially fails to question the rationality of ‘repeated error injection’ design. Humans need to explicitly state ’error scenes should be fixed + reset randomization’ to start refactoring. All edits were lost and need to be reapplied in the new path. Exponential backoff or diagnostic authentication requirements should be implemented earlier. Subagent execution process is not transparent: When 5 backend agents run in parallel, users cannot see the intermediate progress (only ‘waiting for completion notification’), lacking real-time visibility. Progress tracking is a UX pain point for large tasks. ECL documents serve as cross-session persistent ‘design contracts’, ensuring context consistency across multiple dialogues, agents, and even different models. The value of adversarial review: Among the 9 issues discovered by the Critic agent, 2 are CRITICAL (no authenticated PTY writing, SSH parameter injection) and 4 are HIGH (token brute-force cracking, prototype contamination), exposing them in a production environment would cause a security disaster. Repairs in the requirement phase cost less than in the code phase and production phase. The essence of object-centric warping: EEF relative to object motion patterns is an invariant. This invariant is maintained through coordinate transformation T_eef_new = T_obj_target × T_obj_src⁻¹ × T_eef_source. Two-step understanding: (1) eliminating the absolute position of the source object (2) remapping with the new object’s position. The wisdom behind the original MimicGen design: (1) minimizing the number of subtasks (only 2) (2) having a post-grasp buffer of 10-20 frames to ensure stable capture (3) reducing pose gaps with env.reset() to home position (4) quasi-closed-loop execution (calculating delta for target_pose_to_action step by step). The core design of MimicGen is source demo + env.reset() randomization: Error scenes should be treated as fixed ‘initial states’, and variants should be generated using placement_initializer, rather than injecting errors into each target again. Priority of NeurIPS DB Track reviews (based on 61 reviews): The most valued qualities are ‘comprehensive’ (mentioned 17 times), ‘community’, ’novel’, ‘clear’, and ‘well-designed’ (mentioned 13 times). The most common criticisms are ’lack of comparison’ (insufficient baseline), ‘insufficient detail’ (inadequate methodology), and ’limited scope’ (restricted application). The best paper (Artificial Hivemind) has an average score of 4.75 among Oral papers—AC decides beyond the review scores. The average for Oral (5.00) < Spotlight average (5.16), confirming that scoring is not the only acceptance factor. Parallel agent scheduling mode: Independent modules (Config/Parser/LocalPTY) are assigned to different subagents for parallel implementation, then combined for verification, increasing development efficiency by 3-5 times. The key is identifying nodes in the DAG that are not dependent on each other, maximizing parallelism. Spending 20% more time on typing in the early stages saves 80% of debugging time later. xterm.js is the industry-standard browser terminal (used by VS Code, Replit, Vercel, ttyd). Human demonstration data quality verification should be done before collection: Simply achieving teleop success is not enough; replay stability and augmentability must also be verified. Otherwise, a large amount of data will be collected that cannot be used for training. Time boundary partitioning (archive covers completed hours, live source covers current hours) elegantly solves deduplication without explicit level tracking—zero overlap means zero duplicate counts. Claude Code’s permission system supports tool-level wildcards (such as “Bash” matching all Bash commands), allowing minimal configuration instead of dozens of individual rules. Cost of Subtask Fragmentation: Each subtask boundary involves independently checking object poses, re-warp, and 5-step interpolation, with errors accumulating. 6 subtasks = 5 error sources, far more than the original 1. OpenReview API authentication architecture (2026): All data endpoints require login with a token; only the /login endpoint allows anonymous access (returning a verification error). The web frontend uses server-side credentials through Next.js RSC. Rate limits are operated at the nginx layer (based on IP), triggering approximately 30 requests in a short period. The academic paper review API is increasingly locked down, requiring institutional or personal credentials. Terminal resize synchronization requires full-chain coordination: ResizeObserver (frontend) → term.onResize → WebSocket message → SessionManager → PTY.resize(). Mismatches result in lines being broken in the error column. Anti-drag prevents flooding when resizing. Terminal instances should not be destroyed during session switching—they save a rollback buffer (10000 lines). The correct approach is to create once and reuse it through clear() + backend RingBuffer (2MB) across sessions. Cache systems must include explicit version fields when data sources can evolve—just TTL expiration is not enough to handle changes in patterns/sources. The three-layer permission configuration allow/deny/ask can balance security and efficiency: Allow implements automation, ask retains confirmation for dangerous operations, deny is for absolute prohibitions. Claude Code configuration does not inherit automatically (each project requires independent configuration), but can be standardized through automated scripts (such as init-claude.sh) for standardized initialization processes. Documentation for complex robot systems should distinguish between developers and operators: Clearly define the target audience, structure, language, and content retention through structured questions to avoid ambiguity. React closure trap ref pattern: Registers third-party library callbacks (xterm.js onData) in useEffect, which captures expired props, a common bug. Common solution: props → ref, useEffect synchronizes ref.current, and the callback reads ref.current. This is the best practice in the React ecosystem. Three key elements for WebSocket robustness: Redundancy (exponential backoff), backpressure (checking bufferedAmount), and heartbeat (not implemented but should be considered). Distributed system network layers must assume ‘connections may disconnect’ rather than ‘connections should be stable’. Continuous closure (≥10 frames) must be detected to confirm a successful grab. Complexity of multi-process debugging: (1) Each worker requires an independent env and augmenter instance (2) Path resolution is more prone to errors (relative paths may miss levels) (3) Absolute paths like demos_dir must be explicitly passed (4) Robosuite WARNINGs need to be suppressed separately in worker functions. Quota counting logic must reflect actual availability: augmentable_only is stricter than replay_only but more reasonable, as non-augmentable demos cannot be expanded even if they can be replayed. State of the art ASR models (2026): True streaming models are rare. Moonshine v2 (73-107ms latency, 34-245M parameters) and Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime (480ms, 4B parameters) represent the most advanced. Moonshine uses a callback-based API suitable for real-time transcription; Voxtral requires manual chunking but offers higher accuracy. Both support native acceleration for Apple Silicon (Moonshine uses CoreML, Voxtral uses MLX). Permission requirements differ for exploratory and production projects: Exploratory projects prioritize efficiency (lenient permissions), while production projects prioritize security (strict confirmation). Gradually accumulating configurations can lead to inconsistencies (e.g., 80+ long rules, different project styles), and regularly using templates can improve maintainability. LeRobot 0.4.0 save_episode error: ‘only 0-dimensional arrays can be converted to Python scalars’ on observation.dones field (shape=(1,) np.array) Solution: Root cause: LeRobot’s get_hf_features_from_features() maps shape=(1,) to scalar Value, but validate_frame() requires ndarray. Inserted loop before save_episode() to convert all dones arrays to Python int via .item()
Key Insight: When framework validation and encoding logic conflict, optimal insertion point is the buffer between them (episode_buffer), not modifying feature definitions or bypassing validation
2. Screenpipe 0.2.13 (Homebrew) startup failed with ‘Protobuf parsing failed’ error when loading wespeaker_en_voxceleb_CAM++.onnx model Solution: Identified Homebrew version as deprecated (does not build). Uninstalled via brew, deleted corrupted model cache (~/Library/Caches/screenpipe/models/), switched to npx screenpipe@latest or official desktop app, updated all documentation
Key Insight: Homebrew formula deprecated status is critical signal. When encountering low-level dependency issues, check upstream maintenance status first rather than debugging abandoned versions
3. Battery training loss immediately became NaN from first iteration despite data appearing normal Solution: Systematically traced pipeline: found cycle column had 4 NaN values from corrupt row (battery 31, cycle 833). StandardScaler computed NaN mean/std, causing (data - NaN) / NaN = NaN for all scaled values. Removed single corrupt row
Key Insight: NaN propagation through normalization: Single NaN in training data corrupts StandardScaler statistics (mean/std), causing all subsequent scaled values to become NaN. Always validate data cleanliness before normalization operations
4. TokenMonitor costs don’t match Claude Code /cost output Solution: Discovered TokenMonitor used 2.0x multiplier for 1h cache tokens while Claude Code uses unified 1.25x rate. Changed cache_write_1h pricing in pricing.rs to match Claude Code exactly
Key Insight: Claude Code’s /cost deliberately simplifies pricing (unified rate) despite API providing granular breakdown. UI simplicity can justify data aggregation — not every field needs exposure
5. CircuitBreaker HALF_OPEN race condition: state check outside lock allowed multiple probes to enter simultaneously Solution: Moved state check inside ‘async with self._lock’ block to ensure atomic state check + transition
Key Insight: Concurrent state machines must perform state check and transition atomically within same lock. Any lock-external check introduces race window
6. MIHD paper positioning unclear — initially framed as ‘fusion strategy benchmark’ with vague core contribution Solution: Repositioned as ‘frozen FM + self-supervised fusion paradigm evaluation’ answering ‘can this replace fine-tuned methods’. Changed narrative from method proposal to systematic boundary exploration
Key Insight: Benchmark papers evaluate paradigms, not methods. Core value is systematic boundary exploration, not SOTA claims. Precise problem definition drives correct narrative framing
7. LiteLLM pricing database missing major Chinese AI models (GLM, Qwen, DeepSeek) — systematic gap in Chinese AI ecosystem Solution: Integrated OpenRouter API (92 Chinese model entries) with concurrent fetch using LiteLLM-priority merge: OpenRouter provides base coverage, LiteLLM overwrites where available. Added 7-day TTL auto-refresh
Key Insight: Global AI pricing requires multi-source strategies with geographic diversity. Western databases systematically lack Chinese models; Chinese sources lack Western models. Redundancy is essential not optional
8. Initial uniform sampling used fixed 0-20 second range, producing invalid IR values (16, 15, 14…) instead of expected 0-0.024 range Solution: Changed strategy: interpolate within each cycle’s actual chargetime range (typically 10-13 seconds) rather than forcing into global fixed range. Avoided extrapolation beyond observed data points
Key Insight: Interpolation vs extrapolation: Forcing data into global range beyond observed bounds causes extrapolation with invalid values. Use per-sample adaptive ranges to stay within interpolation regime
9. ‘Zero-shot’ terminology easily misunderstood — STAIG fusion trains 550 epochs, reviewers would challenge if truly ‘zero-shot’ Solution: Switched to ’label-free / annotation-free’ emphasizing no manual annotation needed. Clarified ‘zero-shot’ refers to encoder level (frozen FM), while fusion is self-supervised using spatial coordinates as free signal
Key Insight: Precise terminology prevents reviewer confusion. Layered definition (frozen encoder + self-supervised fusion) avoids ambiguity and highlights practical value (no annotation cost)
10. tianhe cluster GitHub access failed: ‘Failed to connect to 172.16.31.200 port 3138: No route to host’ Solution: Diagnosed outdated proxy configuration (172.16.31.200). User provided ‘source /app/bin/proxy.sh’ command. Updated git config http/https.proxy to new proxy (99.72.0.200:3138), npx openskills install succeeded
Key Insight: HPC cluster network proxies change frequently. When network errors occur, verify proxy effectiveness (env | grep proxy, git config –list) rather than assuming configuration correctness

AI over-focused on technical repair within existing environment. Reflects human sensitivity to ecosystem maintenance status vs AI’s excessive technical detail focus
Code review fix prioritization strategy Role Approach Human Requested ‘fix all issues’ as single batch AI Adopted phased validation: CRITICAL→verify tests→HIGH→verify→MEDIUM→verify→LOW, reducing regression risk Difference Analysis: AI applied defensive layering to avoid cascading failures when fixing 22 issues across 11 files
Parallelization strategy for large document generation Role Approach Human When AI got stuck, user immediately suggested ‘break it into smaller parts and do them in parallel’ AI Attempted single-threaded completion, hesitated when assembling large 2246-line document Difference Analysis: Human faster at recognizing parallelization opportunities. AI knows parallel tools exist but tends toward sequential thinking in practice, requiring explicit user direction to leverage concurrency

Only adjusted to data-only scope after user explicitly selected that option Difference Analysis: Human exhibited strong ‘make it right before making it pretty’ instinct, while AI defaulted to feature-complete implementation. User’s judgment prevented scope creep

content:
Daily Report — 2026-04-09 Daily Overview What was done: Parallel execution across research computing (robot learning data pipelines), infrastructure maintenance (proxy/permissions/multi-instance isolation), content pipeline transformation (gadget bilingual architecture), and two major greenfield projects (LifeCopilot architecture upgrade + meeting-helper creation) plus TokenMonitor enhancements How it was done: tianhe: HDF5 validation, Python script implementation, Node environment variable normalization. TzJsDesktop: Systematic multi-phase refactoring with parallel agent validation, ccplan-driven architecture planning (2 complete Phase 0-11 workflows), TDD approach with comprehensive testing, Win32 API window manipulation, timezone-aware datetime conversion Impact: Established human collection fallback for 626 MimicGen failures; enabled flexible multi-dataset contrastive learning; achieved universal Node CLI proxy solution; transformed gadget to English-first bilingual pipeline; delivered production-grade health monitoring + auto-recovery for LifeCopilot (10 new modules); created deployable meeting assistant with Screenpipe integration; eliminated timezone bugs and UI flicker in TokenMonitor tianhe What was done: Completed MimicGen result analysis, human collection workflow implementation, BOSS multi-dataset refactoring, and Node.js proxy configuration fix How it was done: Direct HDF5 file validation with h5py, wrote three Python teleoperation collection scripts, modified three training pipeline files for multi-source augmentation, normalized shell proxy environment variables (uppercase/lowercase sync + NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1) Impact: Delivered complete human collection workflow for 626 failed scenes; enabled single+multiple dual-dataset flexible sampling; established universal solution for all Node CLI tools requiring external API access through corporate proxy TzJsDesktop What was done: All sessions on this device (11 total): gadget English conversion (4-phase with parallel validation), GitHub workspace permission unification, Claude Code multi-instance isolation setup, 2 complete ccplan workflows (LifeCopilot OpenClaw integration + meeting-helper creation), gadget documentation updates, TokenMonitor debugging (3 sessions: Tauri CLI + port + timezone + animations) How it was done: Four-phase refactoring with parallel agent validation discovering 6 residual issue categories; ccplan-driven structured planning (research→adversarial review→feasibility→implementation→testing); extensive use of Agent tool for parallel codebase research; TDD with 70 Rust + 219 frontend tests; Win32 API hide/show workaround for WebView2 async rendering; CSS transition timing analysis Impact: Transformed bilingual workflow (better international reach); eliminated ~200 permission prompts; enabled simultaneous GLM/Claude usage; LifeCopilot gained 10 new modules (health_manager, config_watcher, data_lifecycle, dreaming_service, circuit_breaker, etc.) with 70 passing tests; meeting-helper delivered end-to-end (config, Pipe, MCP, install scripts, docs); TokenMonitor timezone feature eliminates date boundary bugs for cross-timezone SSH servers; animation fixes improve UI polish Cross-device full-stack development day: optimized robot learning pipelines on tianhe (MimicGen analysis + human collection workflow + multi-dataset contrastive learning), resolved infrastructure issues (Node proxy, Claude Code permissions), executed major gadget refactoring (Chinese→English output with Ollama translation), completed two large architecture upgrades (LifeCopilot OpenClaw integration with 70 tests, meeting-helper from scratch via Screenpipe+MCP), and enhanced TokenMonitor with timezone-aware SSH handling plus UI animation fixes
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Refactor gadget summarize module to English output — Converted 4 core files (summarizer.py, formatter.py, weekly_summary.py, monthly_summary.py) from Chinese LLM prompts and Markdown rendering to English. All SUMMARY_PROMPT/CHUNK_MERGE_PROMPT/WEEKLY_SUMMARY_PROMPT/MONTHLY_SUMMARY_PROMPT templates now request English output ✅ Refactor gadget research module to English output — Converted 8 files across scout and profiler subsystems: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=‘en’, all prompts to English, Markdown rendering labels to English, added label_en property to ResearcherTier enum ✅ LifeCopilot OpenClaw core enhancements integration — Integrated 7 features via ccplan workflow: service health monitoring + auto-restart (health_manager.py with 4-state FSM), CronScheduler concurrency control + replay (per-job lock + global Semaphore), config hot reload (config_watcher.py with watchfiles), JSONL lifecycle management (data_lifecycle.py), session history persistence (SessionManager refactor), thought search + dream consolidation (DreamingService + InsightStore), circuit breaker (closed→open→half-open). Added 10 new module files, modified 15 files, 70 tests passing ✅ meeting-helper AI meeting assistant creation — Created full meeting assistant via ccplan Phase 0-11.
