Implemented 5 features: Screenpipe config (Whisper large-v3-turbo + bilingual + custom vocabulary), custom meeting summary Pipe, MCP setup script, CLAUDE.md Q&A system prompt (27 MCP tools guide), cross-platform install scripts (macOS/Windows). Includes complete ECL planning documentation ✅ Implement human collection workflow scripts — Created three scripts for manual success demo collection: identify_failed_scenes.py (parse logs, output 626 scene IDs), collect_success_from_error.py (SpaceMouse teleoperation with progress tracking), convert_teleop_to_hdf5.py (NPZ→HDF5 conversion and merging) ✅ Refactor PairedDataset for multi-aug-dataset support — Modified build_paired_mapping.py (multi-source input with source tags), paired_dataset.py (aug_datasets list, source-based selection), config.py (aug_repo_ids/aug_sources lists) to support simultaneous sampling from single and multiple OSS augmentation datasets ✅ Fix Node.js proxy for CLI tools — Fixed npx ccusage and all Node CLI tools failing to fetch through corporate proxy. Root cause: Node 24’s –use-env-proxy only reads uppercase HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY. Modified .bashrc and .bashrcy proxy helper functions to synchronize uppercase/lowercase variables and export NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 ✅ Fix residual Chinese in LLM prompts and outputs — Used 3 parallel validation agents to discover 6 issue categories: merge prompt context strings, matplotlib chart labels, DEEP_EVAL comments, overview.md template, JSON repair prompt, config init prompt. Fixed all 6 categories ✅ SSH remote timezone handling — Implemented timezone-aware date filtering for SSH remote servers. Added TZ_OFFSET detection, local timezone conversion for all date operations, timezone persistence and UI display. Fixed 4 instances of incorrect date extraction plus Codex since filter. Added 8 new unit tests. All 307 Rust + 219 frontend tests pass ✅ MimicGen result analysis and verification — Analyzed MimicGen success demo generation results (1282 success / 953 failed), identified 626 failed scenes needing human collection; corrected reporting script bug that misreported pick_place/coffee numbers via direct HDF5 inspection ✅ Float ball collapse flicker fix — Fixed visual flicker when float ball collapses on Windows (direction=‘left’ only). Root cause: WebView2 async rendering during SetWindowPos. Solution: Hide window before resize, show after completion ✅ Float ball collapse movement bug — Fixed ball moving left-then-right during collapse animation. Root cause: CSS .expanded class removal caused justify-content jump during 250ms transition. Solution: Remove .expanded condition from direction-based justify-content rules Implementation & Fixes ✅ Code optimization for gadget summarize/research modules — Implemented 7 optimizations: extracted _render_content_list(), removed unnecessary OrderedDict import, replaced loop+break with next(), extracted _truncate() and _field() helpers, added _load_profile() with error handling, added None guards. Eliminated ~50 lines of duplication ✅ Configure unified Claude Code permissions for GitHub workspace — Created/updated settings.local.json for 6 subdirectories with consistent permissions: auto-allow all built-in tools + common commands, require confirmation only for destructive operations (rm/rmdir/del/rd) ✅ Claude Code multi-instance isolation strategy — Provided 3 solutions for running GLM 5.1 and official Claude Code simultaneously: (1) CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR environment variable (recommended), (2) wrapper script with hardcoded env var, (3) symlink switching. Enables isolated ~/.claude-glm/ and ~/.claude/ directories ✅ Update gadget CLAUDE.md documentation — Updated 5 key sections to reflect Ollama translation architecture migration: Environment Setup (added Ollama installation), Architecture (added common/ollama.py, translation.py, bilingual.py), Cross-Module Dependencies (updated dependency graph), Translation Architecture (new section), Tests (added pytest commands) ✅ meeting-helper project permission configuration — Modified .claude/settings.local.json with three-tier permission strategy: auto-allow 60+ common commands, ask for rm/git push, deny rm -rf/git push –force/git reset –hard/git clean -f ✅ Fix TokenMonitor Tauri CLI failure — Resolved ’tauri’ is not recognized error caused by missing Windows native binding (@tauri-apps/cli-win32-x64-msvc). Deleted node_modules and package-lock.json, reinstalled to trigger correct platform dependency resolution Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. npx ccusage and all Node.js CLI tools couldn’t fetch external data despite working http_proxy/https_proxy environment variables and local proxy running on 127.0.0.1:10087 Solution: Discovered Node 24’s –use-env-proxy feature only reads uppercase HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY, not lowercase variants. Modified .bashrc and .bashrcy to export both uppercase and lowercase variables in proxy_on/net_on functions, and set NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 to enable Node’s native fetch() proxy support
Key Insight: Node.js 24+ has built-in environment variable proxy support via –use-env-proxy flag/NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY env var, but it strictly requires uppercase variable names. This is a cleaner solution than injecting undici ProxyAgent or wrapping individual CLI tools. Universal fix for all Node CLI tools, not tool-specific workarounds
2. After converting LLM prompts and Markdown rendering to English, validation revealed 6 categories of residual Chinese text that would break the English-first pipeline: LLM context strings, matplotlib chart labels, DEEP_EVAL annotations, project templates, JSON repair instructions, config defaults Solution: Used 3 parallel validation agents (one per module) to systematically grep for Chinese patterns and verify full pipeline consistency. Fixed all 6 issue types across summarize, research, and website modules
Key Insight: LLM prompt translation requires checking not just main PROMPT constants but also: (1) context strings injected during execution, (2) non-text output (charts), (3) code comments appearing in prompts, (4) generated templates, (5) error recovery prompts. Parallel agent validation (split by subsystem) is more thorough than single-pass grep for discovering runtime-injected strings
3. Remote SSH servers in different timezones caused incorrect date filtering - a record timestamped 2024-01-01T23:00:00+00:00 (UTC) was treated as Jan 1 instead of Jan 2 when local timezone is UTC+8 Solution: Added parse_remote_ts_to_local_date() helper that converts FixedOffset timestamps to Local timezone before extracting date. Modified 4 call sites to use local-timezone-aware conversion. Fixed Codex since_iso_filter to include UTC offset for correct cross-timezone string comparison
Key Insight: DateTime::date_naive() extracts the date in the server’s timezone, not local. Must convert to Local timezone first with .with_timezone(&chrono::Local) before calling date_naive(). Critical for any distributed system with cross-timezone data
4. meeting-helper needs Chinese-English mixed language transcription, but Whisper’s language detection is per-chunk (~30s) not per-sentence, causing poor quality for intra-sentence code-switching like “我们需要implement这个feature” Solution: Multi-layer mitigation: (1) added custom vocabulary in screenpipe-settings.json for common bilingual terms, (2) added retranscription workflow in CLAUDE.md guiding users to POST /audio/retranscribe API with bilingual prompt when quality is poor, (3) added Step 4 in pipe to check transcription quality and trigger retranscription for mixed segments, (4) documented limitation explicitly to manage user expectations
Key Insight: Whisper’s architectural limitation (per-chunk language detection) cannot be fully solved by model parameters. More effective strategy: custom vocabulary + secondary transcription + user feedback loop for incremental quality improvement, while honestly disclosing limitations in documentation rather than over-promising
5. LifeCopilot’s BackgroundCoordinator manages 18+ background services but has no health check mechanism. Service crashes only log errors without auto-restart, causing partial system failure without user awareness Solution: Ported health monitoring pattern from OpenClaw: created health_manager.py implementing ServiceHealthManager (4-state FSM: HEALTHY→DEGRADED→FAILED→STOPPED, restart budget 10/hour, exponential backoff 1→2→4→8→60s). Modified BackgroundCoordinator to integrate health management: 5min health checks, auto-restart on failure, mark as degraded when budget exhausted, EventBus notifications. Added GET /api/health endpoint exposing all service status
Key Insight: Porting mature patterns from production-validated open source projects (like OpenClaw’s health monitoring) is more reliable than designing from scratch. Key is understanding original design rationale (why 4-state FSM? why limit restart count? why exponential backoff?) and adapting to target project context
6. Float ball collapse animation on Windows showed visual flicker, but only when direction=‘left’ (ball on right side). Direction=‘right’ (ball on left) did not flicker Solution: Root cause: SetWindowPos simultaneously moves and resizes the window, but WebView2 rendering is async. When ball position jumps (x=96→x=0) during resize, the 1-2 frame gap shows old content clipped incorrectly. Fix: Wrap SetWindowPos with ShowWindow(SW_HIDE) before and ShowWindow(SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE) after, so WebView2 doesn’t render intermediate frames. Applied only to collapse (!expanded) to minimize side effects
Key Insight: Native window geometry changes (SetWindowPos) are synchronous, but WebView2 content rendering is asynchronous. When the window’s left edge moves (direction=‘left’ collapse), the WebView content coordinate system shifts, causing visible flicker during the 1-2 frame rendering lag. Direction=‘right’ doesn’t flicker because the left edge stays at x=0 - only the right edge shrinks
7. Reporting script bug caused pick_place and coffee to read stale full_run_200attempts.log, both showing incorrect 398/260 numbers instead of actual 168/85 Solution: Bypassed log parsing and directly inspected HDF5 files with h5py to get ground truth demo counts
Key Insight: Log-based reporting can drift from actual data artifacts; HDF5 files are the authoritative source for data validation
8. Float ball collapse animation caused ball to move left then right instead of staying in place Solution: Root cause: Setting expanded=false immediately removes .shell.expanded class, causing CSS justify-content to jump from flex-end/flex-start to center. During the 250ms capsule width transition, the ball drifts toward center. Fix: Remove .expanded condition from direction-based justify-content rules so they apply throughout the transition
Key Insight: CSS transitions interact with native window resize timing. Frontend CSS transition (250ms) completes before backend window resize (t=260ms). If CSS rules change immediately based on expanded state, the ball floats during transition. Direction-based positioning must persist throughout transition to anchor the ball
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Search-First strategy (research before implementation) Role Approach Human User emphasized “先搜索现有开源方案再实现” for meeting-helper and interrupted AI when it started requirements analysis: “你能用websearch先研究现有方案吗” AI AI initially wanted to proceed directly to ccplan Phase 0 requirements analysis, preparing to design architecture from scratch. After interruption, AI executed deep research (Screenpipe, Meetily, Natively) and adjusted entire architecture direction (from custom audio capture to Screenpipe+MCP) Difference Analysis: Human knows from experience that “don’t reinvent the wheel” is a golden rule in software engineering, prefers search→evaluate→reuse. AI knows this principle (mentioned in ccplan skill) but in execution tends toward “I can solve this” mindset and skips research phase. Human’s interruption corrected this tendency, teaching AI that mandatory research phase must precede ccplan Phase 0
Node.js CLI proxy fix strategy Role Approach Human User framed problem as ’npx ccusage@latest doesn’t go through proxy’ and asked for ‘one-time-fix solution’, likely thinking about wrapping npx command, modifying ccusage source, or creating custom launch script AI AI investigated full dependency chain: checked ccusage source → confirmed it uses native fetch() without custom dispatcher → checked Node version (24.12.0) → found –use-env-proxy support → discovered uppercase-only variable requirement → verified user only had lowercase variables → proposed shell-level solution by unifying variable case in proxy helper functions Difference Analysis: Human focused on tool-specific workaround; AI found root cause at Node runtime level, enabling universal fix for all Node CLI tools. AI’s solution was simpler (3-line shell function change) vs wrapping/patching individual tools. Key: checking tool dependencies first before proposing solutions
Scope of English conversion for content generation pipeline Role Approach Human User initially requested: ‘modify JSON report → generate_markdown() to only output English version, then translate to Chinese at website level’. This suggested modifying only Markdown rendering layer AI AI recognized this required changing entire LLM prompt chain (not just rendering), proactively checked research module for similar patterns. During validation phase, AI used 3 parallel agents to discover residual Chinese in 6 additional categories (context strings, chart labels, templates, etc.) not obvious from initial requirement Difference Analysis: Human specified desired behavior but didn’t articulate all necessary changes; AI inferred full technical scope (prompts → rendering → charts → templates → error messages). AI’s multi-phase approach (convert → validate → fix residuals → optimize) was more thorough than user’s initial single-step request. Demonstrates AI’s strength in dependency analysis and completeness checking
Realistic limitations of Chinese-English mixed transcription Role Approach Human User asked “你能解决一下关键风险吗?” after meeting-helper v1 completion - explicitly pointing to ECL-documented CRITICAL risk (poor quality for intra-sentence code-switching) AI AI was overly optimistic in Phase 0-9 about Whisper large-v3-turbo’s multilingual capability (DEC-003 confidence=0.75), suggesting it could be “solved”. Only after user explicitly demanded “solve critical risk” did AI adopt more pragmatic mitigation strategy (retranscription API + custom vocabulary + documentation) Difference Analysis: AI tends toward technical optimism (“better model will solve it”), while human knows from practice that some technical limits are architectural (Whisper’s per-chunk language detection can’t be changed by tuning). Human intervention forced AI from “solve problem” mindset to “mitigate risk + manage expectations” mindset, which is more mature for handling inherent technical constraints
Testing hide/show workaround necessity Role Approach Human User asked to test direct SetWindowPos first before adding hide/show complexity, saying ‘ok，可以试试’ - pragmatic approach of validating whether workaround is actually needed AI AI initially proposed hide/show as definitive solution based on theoretical WebView2 async rendering behavior without testing if flicker actually occurs with direct resize Difference Analysis: Human favored empirical testing (’try it first’) over theoretical analysis. This revealed that direction matters - only left direction flickers, making the solution more targeted. AI jumped to fix without establishing baseline. Empirical testing beats theoretical analysis for edge cases
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Initial English conversion (Phase 1-2) missed 6 categories of residual Chinese text: LLM context strings in merge prompts, matplotlib chart labels, prompt annotations, templates, error recovery prompts, and config defaults. Only discovered after user asked ‘check the complete pipeline’. AI’s first-pass conversion focused on obvious locations (PROMPT constants, Markdown labels) but missed execution-time injected strings and non-text outputs AI didn’t anticipate Phase 11 user requests in meeting-helper (retranscription workflow, Q&A logging, speaker management). Though Phase 5 adversarial review found Chinese-English mixed transcription limitation, didn’t propose retranscription as mitigation; though researched Screenpipe’s speaker system, didn’t proactively include in Feature list; designed Q&A interaction but didn’t consider logging requirement. AI’s forward planning still has blind spots - can identify problems but may not propose best solutions, can research features but may not proactively recommend AI understanding of Whisper language detection mechanism was insufficient. Actually Whisper’s detection is per-chunk (~30s) not per-sentence, poor for intra-sentence code-switching. AI tends to rely on “model is powerful” intuition when assessing technical feasibility, overlooking architectural-level inherent constraints Misread stale log file (full_run_200attempts.log) when pick_place and coffee lacked run_200att_*.log files, causing incorrect 398/260 reporting; failed to verify against actual HDF5 output artifacts before summarizing. For data validation tasks, AI should always verify against authoritative source (HDF5 files) rather than relying on potentially stale intermediate logs AI proposed CSS pre-positioning workaround (moving ball left then resizing window) for float ball flicker without fully analyzing IPC timing constraints. Only after user questioned it did AI realize CSS changes and Win32 SetWindowPos cannot synchronize across Tauri IPC boundary - they will always be 1+ frames apart, making approach fundamentally unworkable AI didn’t anticipate second animation bug (left-then-right movement during collapse) that emerged from first fix. Only user testing revealed CSS justify-content issue caused by immediate .expanded class removal during transition General Limitations AI couldn’t complete interactive shell verification on tianhe server: when testing Node fetch() through proxy, got ‘TypeError: fetch failed’ with EPERM. AI correctly identified this as sandbox proxy connection issue rather than code problem, but couldn’t complete real-world validation. Had to rely on theoretical correctness (bash -n syntax check + environment variable verification) instead of end-to-end test Over-reliance on file content caching led to multiple ‘File has been modified since read’ errors. AI should adopt paranoid strategy: always re-read immediately before Edit even if file was just accessed, especially in workflows with linters/formatters or multi-agent concurrency Learnings Key Learnings ccplan’s adversarial review (Phase 5 Adversarial Filtering) is extremely valuable. In meeting-helper, code-reviewer subagent as adversarial critic found 6 critical problems main planner missed, including CRITICAL-level Chinese-English mixed transcription limit (Whisper per-chunk detection causes poor intra-sentence code-switching quality), long meeting context overflow, speaker identification limits, installation complexity, privacy compliance. These weren’t sufficiently identified in Phase 0-4 single-perspective planning. Key insight: complex project planning must introduce independent critical perspective (adversarial review) focusing on “what planner would miss” not “whether plan is correct” MimicGen success rates from error scenes are low (57.4% overall for success demos, 9.57% for stack human demo augmentation); human teleoperation fallback is necessary for comprehensive coverage when automated generation hits success rate plateau Node.js 24+ has built-in environment variable proxy support (–use-env-proxy flag / NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1), but it ONLY reads uppercase HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY, not lowercase variants. Common pitfall when shell proxy setup scripts only export lowercase. Solution: always sync both cases in proxy helper functions. Universal fix for all Node CLI tools When refactoring LLM-driven pipelines from one language to another, validation must cover: (1) static prompt templates, (2) runtime context injection, (3) non-text outputs (charts/images), (4) code comments appearing in prompts, (5) generated templates/scaffolds, (6) error recovery logic. Parallel agent validation pattern (one per subsystem) is more thorough than single-pass grep Porting validated architecture patterns from mature open source projects is more efficient and reliable than designing from scratch. LifeCopilot’s OpenClaw integration demonstrated: health monitoring (4-state FSM + restart budget + exponential backoff), circuit breaker (closed→open→half-open), config hot reload (watchfiles + EventBus), speaker diarization (voice embeddings + calendar assist) all from production-grade implementations. Key: understand original design rationale (why 4 states not 3? why limit restart count? why exponential backoff?) then adapt to target context. “Understand → port → adapt” workflow significantly reduces design risk since source project already discovered pitfalls MCP (Model Context Protocol) as standard interface between AI assistants and external tools greatly simplifies integration complexity. meeting-helper demonstrated MCP’s power: Screenpipe exposes all capabilities through 27 MCP tools (list-meetings, get-meeting, search-content, list-speakers, update-speaker, etc.), Claude Code CLI achieves complete meeting Q&A functionality (real-time query, history search, speaker management) without any custom code. Proves value of standard protocols in AI tool ecosystem - tool providers implement MCP server once, all MCP-supporting AI assistants (Claude, Codex, etc.) can use directly. Compared to REST API or custom integration, each AI assistant would need separate adaptation DateTime timezone handling nuance: date_naive() on DateTime extracts date in source timezone, not local. For remote timestamp filtering, must explicitly convert to Local timezone first with with_timezone(&chrono::Local) before extracting date. Critical for any distributed system with cross-timezone data Multi-dataset contrastive learning requires mapping-level source tagging and Dataset-level list-based architecture; enables flexible sampling from heterogeneous augmentation sources (single vs multiple OSS perturbations) JSONL (append-only log) + in-memory cache hybrid architecture is highly effective for scenarios requiring both persistence and performance. LifeCopilot’s multiple subsystems use this pattern: session history (deque(maxlen=100) + data/sessions/{user_id}.jsonl), audit log, thoughts, mismatches. Key design points: (1) write with atomic operation (write tmp → os.replace) to prevent corruption on crash, (2) lazy load on read (first access reads recent N records) to avoid slow startup, (3) use bounded buffer in memory (like deque(maxlen)) to prevent memory leak, (4) unified timestamp with ISO 8601 UTC for timezone safety, (5) periodic archival (data_lifecycle.py cleans by retention_days) to prevent infinite growth. This architecture is best practice validated at scale in logging systems, event sourcing, audit trails WebView2 rendering is asynchronous relative to native window geometry changes. SetWindowPos modifies window size/position synchronously, but Chromium needs 1-2 frames to render new content. For transparent windows with complex layouts, this async gap causes visible flicker. ShowWindow(SW_HIDE) before geometry change and SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE after prevents intermediate frames from being composited by DWM SetWindowPos anchor point behavior: top-left corner is fixed, so resizing smaller means right/bottom edges move inward. When content needs visual anchor to right (like direction=‘left’ float ball), must simultaneously adjust x position by width delta. Fundamental Win32 API constraint affecting all window resize logic CSS transitions interact with React/Svelte state changes non-obviously. Removing class (like .expanded) immediately changes computed styles, but transitions may still be in progress. For multi-step animations involving both CSS and native operations, CSS rules must persist throughout transition period regardless of logical state, or use separate ’transitioning’ state Practical Learnings Character-ratio language detection (5% CJK threshold) is sufficient for technical content classification. English technical docs with occasional Chinese terms typically have <1% CJK ratio, providing wide margin. No need for complex NLP-based language detection for content pipeline classification tasks Code optimization pattern: extract reusable helper for complex parsing, then compose higher-level functions from it. parse_remote_ts → parse_remote_ts_to_local_date pattern eliminates duplication and is easier to maintain than copy-pasting RFC3339 format strings. Performance optimization should reduce redundant work without sacrificing clarity Configuring lenient permissions (auto-allow most operations) for exploratory projects significantly improves development experience while balancing security and efficiency. meeting-helper’s .claude/settings.local.json demonstrated this strategy: add 60+ common commands (Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep/WebFetch/git status/npm/python, etc.) to allow list for auto-pass; keep ask confirmation only for destructive operations (rm delete files, git push, git reset –hard); directly deny extremely dangerous operations (rm -rf recursive force delete, git push –force, git clean -f). This three-tier permission strategy (allow/ask/deny) avoids frequent interruptions (exploratory work needs lots of file reads/writes, command runs) while preventing irreversible errors (deletion, remote push need manual confirmation) - best config for exploratory dev environments Conversation Summaries error-recovery-benchmark ✅ MimicGen result analysis and human collection workflow 05:38:51.216 | claude_code Analyzed MimicGen success demo generation (739/1365 scenes succeeded, 626 failed). Crossformer LIPM version (MSE=9, MAE=1.3) performs 18x worse than master version (MSE≈0.5) despite patch mechanism designed for irregular battery data Solution: Diagnosed fundamental architecture mismatch: Crossformer’s DSW_embedding assumes continuous seg_len time steps with positional encoding, but LIPM patch method creates irregular gaps filled with zeros that break temporal continuity, waste model capacity, and lose time interval information. Recommended: interpolation to uniform grid, time window aggregation, or irregular time-series models (GRU-D, BRITS, NAOMI)
Key Insight: Zero-padding is NOT neutral for sequence models with positional encodings - it actively misleads model to learn ‘zero patterns’ instead of temporal dependencies. Architecture assumptions must match data preprocessing; forcing irregular data into patch+zero format breaks semantic meaning

Daily Report — 2026-04-07 Today’s Overview What was done: Conducted a comprehensive review of website/update.sh, fixed 4 script bugs, and assisted in setting up a complete Hugo site deployment environment, recovering the website update pipeline from repeated failures (exit codes 1/127/128) to all 7 steps passing How it was done: Layered validation strategy — read code first, then check dependencies, then run the script; incrementally identified missing environment components (Hugo, theme, deployment repo) and logic bugs (duplicate PID, file not replaced, missing directory guard); multiple validation rounds after user manually installed missing components Why it matters: The website CI pipeline is restored, Hugo build and GitHub Pages deployment paths are both working, and future content publishing requires no manual intervention; also discovered and fixed a silent error in the video compression fallback branch, preventing future content loss Fixed 4 script bugs in website/update.sh and set up a complete Hugo deployment environment, recovering the website update pipeline from total failure to all 7 steps passing; also initiated a full daily/weekly report MCP sync workflow
Today’s Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Validate website/update.sh script usability — Systematically checked all dependencies and directory structure for update.sh; found fatal and minor issues including Hugo not installed, themes/PaperMod/ missing, public/ deployment repo missing, and pngquant/HandBrakeCLI not installed ✅ Fix bugs in update.sh — Fixed 4 bugs: inconsistent step numbering (1/6→1/7), duplicate PID entries for video compression into the pids array, HandBrakeCLI fallback branch not replacing the original file after compression, and find triggering set -e termination when static/images or static/videos directories don’t exist Implementation & Fixes ✅ Set up complete Hugo deployment environment — Completed by the user: installed Hugo extended v0.154.5, cloned PaperMod theme into themes/PaperMod, cloned tzj2006.github.io into public/, and configured GitHub authentication 🔄 Initiated full daily/weekly/monthly MCP sync and merge — Checked status via MCP gadget tools: found 6 dates (Apr 1–5, Apr 7) with session data but no reports, and no weekly reports. Initiated data export for Apr 7; subsequent batch merge of all dates and weekly report generation still pending Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. Hugo not installed — script terminated at Step 5 with ‘hugo: command not found’ (exit 127) Solution: User installed Hugo extended v0.154.5 via the system package manager
Key insight: set -e converts any command failure directly into script termination; a missing Hugo binary prevents the entire 7-step pipeline from ever reaching the critical build stage
2. themes/PaperMod/ and public/ directories both absent — Hugo build and deployment cannot run Solution: User cloned the PaperMod theme and the tzj2006.github.io deployment repo
Key insight: Hugo site deployment depends on three independent components (hugo binary, theme repo, deployment git repo); any one missing causes either a silent or a hard failure — prerequisites should be explicitly documented
General Issues 3. static/videos directory does not exist — find returns an error, set -e causes Step 4 to terminate unexpectedly Solution: Added a directory existence check before find ([ -d “$DIR” ]); skip the step if the directory does not exist
Key insight: find operations on optional/empty directories in set -e scripts must be guarded; an ordinary “directory not yet created” scenario will otherwise trigger unexpected script termination
4. HandBrakeCLI inline fallback branch PID added to pids array twice, and compressed file not used to replace original (output is .hb.mp4) Solution: Moved pids+=($!) and echo statements into their respective if/else branches; added && mv after the HandBrakeCLI command to replace the original file
Key insight: PID tracking logic for parallel background tasks must align precisely with if/else control flow boundaries; placing shared code outside branches easily introduces duplicate execution and silent data-loss bugs
5. git push failed due to unconfigured GitHub authentication (‘could not read Username for https://github.com’) Solution: User configured an SSH key or gh auth, then re-ran the script successfully end-to-end
Key insight: HTTPS remotes require pre-configured credentials in non-interactive shells; the deployment repo should use an SSH remote to avoid environment-specific failures
Human Thinking vs. AI Thinking Strategic Level Script Validation Strategy Role Approach Human User raised the validation task without specifying a method; expected to know whether the script would work AI AI prioritized static analysis: read the script and CLAUDE.md to understand the architecture, then verified external dependencies, directory structure, and logic correctness one by one before actually running the script Analysis: AI’s layered validation caught all fatal issues before any run, avoiding multiple blind attempts; however, AI cannot independently resolve sudo-level environment problems and ultimately relied on the user to act manually
Implementation Level Hugo Installation Method Role Approach Human User chose the system package manager (Ubuntu apt), obtaining v0.154.5 AI AI suggested snap or downloading a precompiled binary from GitHub releases (v0.147.4), but could not execute due to missing sudo access Analysis: The user’s system-package approach was simpler and yielded a newer version than AI suggested; AI’s recommendation leaned toward version control and cross-distro compatibility, which was slightly over-engineered for a local development environment
AI Limitations General Limitations Cannot execute commands requiring sudo (installing Hugo, pngquant, etc.); can only generate scripts for the user to run manually — cannot complete environment setup end-to-end Cannot configure GitHub authentication (SSH key or gh auth), which blocked the first complete deployment run and required manual user intervention Parallel tool calls failed multiple times during this session due to race-condition cancellations, forcing a switch to sequential calls and significantly reducing inspection efficiency Today’s Takeaways Core Takeaways Hugo site deployment has three independent prerequisites that must all be in place simultaneously (hugo binary, theme repo, deployment git repo); any one missing causes failures at different stages — these prerequisites should be explicitly listed in project documentation Practical Takeaways find operations on optional directories in bash set -e scripts must include a directory existence check; otherwise an ordinary “directory not yet created” scenario triggers unexpected script termination Code for parallel background tasks (& + pids tracking) must align precisely with if/else control flow boundaries; placing shared code outside branches easily introduces duplicate PID tracking and silent file-replacement omission bugs Session Summaries Gadget Website ✅ Validated and fixed fatal environment issues and logic bugs in website/update.sh, fully establishing the Hugo deployment pipeline 04:12:15.435 | claude_code User requested validation of whether the website update script could run correctly. AI used a layered inspection approach to identify 3 fatal environment issues — Hugo not installed, PaperMod theme missing, public deployment repo missing — as well as 4 script logic bugs: inconsistent step numbering, duplicate video PID tracking, HandBrakeCLI fallback not replacing the file, and set -e termination triggered by missing optional directories. After the user progressively installed environment dependencies and configured GitHub authentication, all 7 steps passed and both Hugo build and GitHub Pages deployment were verified successfully.
Gadget Summarize 🔄 Initiated full daily/weekly/monthly sync and merge workflow via MCP gadget tools 04:25:03.485 | claude_code User requested parallel execution of daily/weekly/monthly sync and merge. AI first checked status via MCP and found that Apr 1–5 and Apr 7 — 6 dates in total — had session data but no reports, and no weekly reports existed. Given the day→week→month dependency order, AI decided to export Apr 7 data first, then perform a batch merge; the session ended while the export was in progress and the subsequent steps were not completed.

Daily Log — 2026-04-06 Today’s Overview What was done: Systematically planned and executed three editorial annotation tasks for the MIHD paper draft: Abstract query motivation supplement, Introduction P1 structural rewrite, R5 cross-section analysis expansion (from 4 to 6 paragraphs), and R6 P3 immune microenvironment case writing How it was done: First used multiple sub-agents to deeply explore the codebase and existing experimental results, designed a detailed execution plan, then ran three new RM-IDEAL cross-section benchmark experiments in parallel (CPU background) while performing text edits, correcting original expected narratives with actual data results Why it matters: The paper draft transitioned from placeholder text to data-driven narrative; notably discovered a new core argument around the clustering-retrieval tradeoff (STAIG excels at clustering but over-homogenizes boundaries, while Attention fusion is better suited for immune microenvironment retrieval), and fixed the invisible query point issue in HD Niche Query visualization Completed planning and execution of three editorial annotation tasks for the MIHD paper draft, including rewriting Intro P1, expanding Abstract and R5/R6, while running three new cross-section query experiments and fixing HD Niche Query visualization
Today’s Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Three new cross-section RM-IDEAL experiments — Ran benchmarks for 151673↔151674 (same donor D3), 151508↔151509 (same donor D1), and 151673↔151669 (cross-donor D3↔D2); each took ~40 minutes of CPU computation, with complete results backed up ✅ Planning for three paper editorial annotations — Analyzed three handwritten annotations in draft_en.md (Abstract missing query motivation, Intro P1 needs to open from main figure, R5 needs expansion to 6 paragraphs citing QueST+TLS), explored codebase and experimental results, generated a detailed step-by-step execution plan that was approved ✅ R5 expanded to 6 paragraphs + QueST citation — R5 P1 added QueST citation and explanation of cross-section retrieval’s unique value; P2 updated method description; R6 P3 changed from placeholder to clustering-retrieval tradeoff argument based on actual HD immune analysis data; synced in both Chinese and English ✅ Introduction P1 rewrite — Rewrote the original general background paragraph into a 6-sentence roadmap structure directly corresponding to R1–R6 Results headings; opening sentence provides the key figure of ARI 0.26→0.55; synced in both Chinese and English ✅ Abstract patch-level query motivation supplement — Added to the Abstract an explanation of how frozen FM embeddings naturally support cross-section retrieval, and the clustering-retrieval tradeoff finding (later updated from ‘immune boundary discovery’ to the more accurate ’tradeoff’ framing based on experimental results); synced in both Chinese and English ✅ HD immune microenvironment Niche Query analysis — Created analyze_hd_immune_niche.py, computed T cell/B cell marker scores, identified 23 epithelial-connective tissue boundary T cell-enriched spots, and compared retrieval results across PCA/Attention/STAIG methods Implementation & Fixes ✅ HD Niche Query visualization fix — Fixed invisible query point issue in visualize_hd_niche_query.py: star marker enlarged from 20 to 26 with white outer ring at 32; annotations added to all 4 panels; H&E panel received arrow label; regenerated 3 figures ✅ W14 weekly report — Generated WEEKLY_REPORT_2026_W14.md with 8 sections covering Leiden experiments, HD experiments, paper writing, code updates, and more, with complete numerical data tables Problems & Solutions Key Issues 1. HD immune analysis revealed extremely sparse T cell marker expression (1278/17502 spots, mean 0.014); TLS markers even sparser (242 spots); the expected argument of ‘multimodal outperforming unimodal for capturing immune infiltration’ was not supported Solution: Changed the R6 P3 narrative from ‘multimodal identification of immune infiltration boundaries’ to ‘clustering-retrieval tradeoff’: STAIG retrieval results were 96% concentrated in the epithelial domain (over-homogenized); PCA gene expression showed 3.8x T cell enrichment vs. STAIG’s 2.2x; Attention fusion was most balanced at the boundary (60/40 Epi/CT)
Key insight: The optimal strategy for clustering (spatial graph contrastive learning) and retrieval (attention fusion) with frozen FM embeddings differs — this is a more meaningful finding than originally anticipated
General Issues 2. benchmark_rm_ideal.py defaults to writing results into the same summary.csv, so each new pair’s results overwrite the previous pair’s Solution: Backed up results immediately after each pair’s experiment completed (summary_151673_151674.csv, etc.); 151673↔151669 results were manually reconstructed via heredoc (had been overwritten by 151674’s results)
Key insight: Long-running batched experiments need per-pair output directories designed at the script level, or unified aggregation after the pipeline completes
3. conda activate produces no output in background commands; output files for all three experiment processes (bgqoqyepm, etc.) remained at 0 bytes Solution: Replaced conda activate General && python ... with conda run -n General python ... to ensure background output was written correctly
Key insight: Claude Code’s background bash command environment does not inherit the shell’s activate state; conda run must be used to guarantee environment isolation
4. The same experiments were launched twice (conda activate version + conda run version), with 6 benchmark processes running simultaneously and wasting resources Solution: Used ps aux to find the conda run process PIDs, then killed the 3 duplicate processes, keeping the original conda activate versions
Key insight: When background process output is empty, first confirm whether the process is actually running (ps aux) before resubmitting
5. HD Niche Query visualization query points (red stars) were not visually discernible, making them unsuitable for paper presentation Solution: Fixed the script: star marker size increased from 20 to 26, added white background marker (size=32), drew markers on all 4 panels, added arrow + text label to the first panel
Key insight: Query spots in paper figures require multiple visual cues (color + size + outer ring + label); a single red star is completely lost against a heatmap background
Human Thinking vs. AI Thinking Strategic Level Correction of the TLS/T cell Argument Role Thinking Human Human annotation said ‘TLS T cell’, expecting to find TLS/T cell-enriched regions in the HD colorectal cancer data as a case study for multimodal advantage AI AI ran the actual analysis, found T cell markers extremely sparse (7.3% of spots), and that PCA gene expression outperformed STAIG multimodal in detecting T cell enrichment — so proposed the more accurate ‘clustering-retrieval tradeoff’ argument Difference analysis: Human intuition was based on prior knowledge that TLS is a common immune structure in colorectal cancer, but AI found through actual data that immune infiltration in this crop region was insufficient to support the original argument; AI discovered a theoretically more valuable tradeoff finding
Paper Annotation Content Identification and Prioritization Role Thinking Human Human already clearly knew what the three annotations were (query motivation, Intro structure, R5 expansion), and knew to cite QueST and add TLS/T cell biological cases AI AI needed to first read files and compare differences, then explain each annotation’s meaning, and finally explore the codebase via multiple sub-agents to understand experimental results and feasibility Difference analysis: Human provided direction and scientific requirements; AI handled feasibility verification and execution details; AI was more thorough than humans in codebase exploration, but relied on code exploration to judge which experiments had existing results vs. which needed to be newly created
Implementation Level Visualization Quality Judgment Role Thinking Human Human directly looked at the figure and noticed ‘can’t tell where the query point is’, providing clear UX feedback AI AI also confirmed the issue after reading the image file, but only noticed it after the human pointed it out; AI located and fixed the specific cause at the code level (markersize too small, insufficient contrast) Difference analysis: Human visual perception and paper usability judgment outperform AI’s code review; AI is more efficient at implementing fixes
AI Limitations General Limitations After generating visualization figures, did not proactively read images to verify quality (e.g., query point visibility); required user feedback to discover the problem; lacks proactive QA for image usability Did not detect in advance that benchmark_rm_ideal.py would overwrite summary.csv, causing 151673↔151669 results to be overwritten and requiring manual reconstruction from memory via heredoc Initially misused conda activate as a background command prefix, causing all three experiment process outputs to be empty and wasting time on debugging; should prioritize using conda run Due to uncertainty about the first batch of process status, resubmitted the same three experiments, causing 6 processes to run in parallel and requiring manual killing of duplicate processes Today’s Takeaways Core Takeaways Discovered that the optimal fusion strategy for clustering and retrieval diverges: STAIG spatial graph contrastive learning is best for global domain clustering (Avg ARI 0.546), but its strong spatial homogenization property causes boundary retrieval to over-focus on the same domain (96% Epithelium); Attention fusion (60/40 distribution) is more balanced for boundary microenvironment retrieval — this is the core new argument for paper R6 Three new RM-IDEAL experiment results: same-donor cross-section (151673↔151674) Layer 3 Spearman ρ reached 0.86; same-donor (151508↔151509) Layer 3 same_label@50 reached 100%; cross-donor (151673↔151669) Layer 3 showed negative correlation (ρ=-0.73), suggesting systematic differences in Layer 3 morphological structure between donors T cell markers (CD3D/CD3E, etc.) are extremely sparse in HD colorectal cancer data at 8μm spots (7.3% with expression); gene expression (PCA) detects T cell enrichment (3.8x) more effectively than visual+gene fusion (STAIG 2.2x), indicating T cell signal is primarily driven by gene expression rather than tissue morphology Introduction opening strategy: directly presenting the most critical numerical finding (ARI from 0.26 to 0.55) is more persuasive than general background setup; having each paragraph correspond to a Results section heading strengthens paper structural consistency Session Summaries ✅ Paper editing execution: Intro P1 rewrite, Abstract update, R5/R6 expansion (bilingual sync) 21:30:00.000 | claude_code AI simultaneously executed the Introduction P1 6-sentence roadmap structure rewrite (bilingual), Abstract query motivation supplement at the end, R5 P1/P2 QueST citation additions, and R6 P3 update from placeholder to substantive content. Three new cross-section RM-IDEAL experiments and HD immune niche analysis ran in the background. HD analysis found T cell markers extremely sparse, and the unexpected result of STAIG over-homogenizing boundaries prompted AI to revise R6 P3 and Abstract arguments from ‘immune infiltration identification’ to ‘clustering-retrieval tradeoff’ — the most important narrative adjustment in this round of editing.
✅ Three cross-section RM-IDEAL experiments completed: same-donor vs. cross-donor conservation comparison 22:00:00.000 | claude_code All three experiments completed in approximately 2 hours (CPU computation). Same-donor groups (151673↔151674, 151508↔151509) showed high Spearman ρ in Layers 3–5 (up to 0.86) and high same_label@50 (up to 100%), while the cross-donor group (151673↔151669) showed strong negative correlation in Layer 3 (ρ=-0.73). Results revealed high conservation of tissue microarchitecture between same-donor sections and systematic differences across donors, providing key quantitative evidence for paper R5.
✅ Paper draft annotation analysis: content identification and execution plan for three editorial comments 21:02:12.402 | claude_code User provided two versions of the paper draft; AI identified three handwritten annotations through file comparison. AI used multiple sub-agents to deeply explore the codebase, existing experimental results, and the RM-IDEAL implementation, completing a comprehensive feasibility assessment of the annotations and generating a detailed execution plan combining computational experiments and text edits, which was approved by the user. The plan’s core strategy was to run new experiments in the background while performing text edits that didn’t depend on results, improving parallel efficiency.

Total size: 185MB. Simultaneously extracted UNI2 staig_strict visual features (256×256 patch, no ImageNet normalization, frequency domain filtering) 🔄 HD learning-based fusion GPU experiment (2026-04-01) — staig(ARI=0.258)/llava(ARI=0.201)/adaln(ARI=0.003) completed. basic_contrastive is still running (48h limit). Key negative finding: adaln completely crashes on large HD data (17502 spots), revealing data scale as a key variable in fusion method selection ✅ docs/ folder reorganization and code gap analysis (2026-04-03) — Archived 5 expired documents. Created a three-level directory structure of docs/paper/figures. Systematically analyzed the capabilities required by draft_en.md vs existing code. Archived 12 expired scripts. Planned scripts for Leiden result restoration, figure generation, spatial continuity metrics, and four code tasks supporting multi-seeds Problems and Solutions 1. GTK bottom-up size negotiation causes FloatBall window to always be 400x400, Tauri set_size() is completely ineffective [TokenMonitor] (2026-04-04) Solution: Use the with_webview() callback to call widget.set_size_request() in the GTK main thread, breaking theWebKitGTK natural size constraint. Remove the set_resizable switch (with_webview is asynchronous, subsequent API calls will be queued before the callback execution, locking the old size). Keep resizable enabled permanently on Linux
2. Dynamic resize of Linux transparent borderless window causes systematic WM +305px/+113px position offset, probe/corrective mechanisms cause visible flickering, size inconsistency between WebView and native window [TokenMonitor] (2026-04-05) Solution: Architectural refactoring to a fixed expanded size window + GDK input_shape_combine_region: Only the ball area (56×56) accepts events when collapsed; the whole window accepts events during expansion and dragging. Completely eliminates resize operations. Remove 150 lines of patch code
3. On Linux/Wayland, Tauri main window set_position() is completely ignored by the compositor, causing the window to appear in the center of the screen [TokenMonitor] (2026-04-02) Solution: Detect WAYLAND_DISPLAY at the run() entry point and force GDK_BACKEND=x11, enabling the application to run via XWayland, bypassing the fundamental limitation of the Wayland protocol prohibiting client absolute position settings
4. In ssh_remote.rs, assert!() panics the entire program when path validation fails, provider parameters not validated allow path traversal attacks [TokenMonitor] (2026-04-02) Solution: Change the function signature to Result<PathBuf, String>, using? for error propagation;Add a whitelist function validate_provider() (only allowing ‘claude’ and ‘codex’).
5. sync_ssh_host blocks all readers when holding a RwLock read lock during an SSH I/O await point that lasts several seconds [TokenMonitor] (2026-04-02) Solution: Add #[derive(Clone)] to SshCacheManager to clone the manager before await and release the lock in advance.
6. The three-layer architecture of Life-Copilot MCP services is broken simultaneously: FastMCP does not call run(), mcp_servers.json is missing, and Butler commands are never passed to the Claude CLI child process [Life-Copilot] (2026-04-04)Solutions: Create main.py to start the stdio transport; create.claude/mcp_servers.json; ClaudeAdapter adds –append-system-prompt parameter; simultaneously create convention files (AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md) for Codex/Gemini, and all 19 MCP tools are restored. 7. Discord Bot continues to reply with ‘OAuth authentication required’ when querying schedules, due to two overlapping issues: Claude -p does not load project-level MCP configurations + non-interactive mode permissions are silently denied [Life-Copilot] (2026-04-05) Solutions: Add –mcp-config .claude/mcp_servers.json and –permission-mode bypassPermissions in the command sequentially; the wildcard in –allowedTools is unreliable due to contention with MCP server initialization, and bypassPermissions is the correct pattern for backend service calls.
8. ClaudeCLIAdapter.is_available() lacks async and await synchronous methods cause TypeError, which is silently ignored by except Exception, resulting in Claude being silently downgraded to Codex and timeout [Life-Copilot] (2026-04-04) Solution: Add the async keyword, and Claude available: True returns to normal. Synchronous fix for context loss during multiple rounds of dialogue (_process_input never passes last_assistant_message and last_intent parameters).
9. The initial solution for Linux Screen Time Tracker uses xdotool, but the user’s Wayland environment (GNOME) is completely unavailable [Life-Copilot] (2026-04-04) Solution: Switch to GNOME Introspect D-Bus (org.gnome.Shell.Introspect.GetWindows()) as the main path, use xprop as a XWayland fallback, and use PID→cmdline as the final fallback. All subprocess calls add a 5-second timeout + proc.kill(). This issue was actively discovered by Critic subagent adversarial review.
10. evaluation_planner.py makes a false positive in the check of staig_gene_feat cache for slice 151676 (hardcoded check for 3000 genes, but the actual file has 5000), leading to Phase 2 sys.exit(1) termination [MIHD] (2026-03-30) Solution: Modify the check logic for has_staig_gene_feat to dynamically parse the actual top_genes count from the slice configuration (from num_gene field in staig_utils.py).
11. STAIG HD experiment result ARI=1.0 anomaly, due to old cache file (missing staig_gene_feat cache causes silent failure of experiment but retains old npz file on Feb 28) [MIHD] (2026-04-01) Solution: Investigate the timestamp of the npz file to confirm the source of the old cache, manually prepare the HD STAIG gene feature cache, then delete the old npz and run again. Also identify that the skip_completed mechanism in the pipeline cannot detect structural defects in invalid content.
12. Leiden clustering cannot accurately match n_clusters, limited by fair comparison with KMeans [MIHD] (2026-03-31) Solution: Implement a binary search in cluster_with_leiden(): perform up to 20 iterations of adjustment on resolution within [0.01, 10] range until the number of clusters matches, using the monotonic relationship between resolution and number of clusters for efficient convergence.
13. lark-oapi WebSocket client runs blockingly, Client.start() conflicts with FastAPI asyncio main loop [Life-Copilot] (2026-04-04) Solution: Start the Feishu bot in a separate daemon thread, and use asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe() to bridge message callbacks to the main event loop. This issue was pre-discovered by Critic subagent adversarial review.
Learning Insights Architecture The correct architecture for Linux transparent borderless Tauri/WebKitGTK floating windows is a fixed large-native window + internal pure CSS expansion/collapse, without relying on frequent resize of the outer window. GTK bottom-up negotiation takes max(window_requested, widget_natural_size); the with_webview() callback must call widget.set_size_request() to break theWebKitGTK natural size constraint; dimensions and positions of content areas in WM, GTK, and WebView do not sync automatically—this is platform constraint, not a bug. The Wayland protocol prohibits client-controlled absolute window position at the design level; any set_position() retry strategy is ineffective. The correct solution is to detect WAYLAND_DISPLAY and force GDK_BACKEND=x11 to fallback to XWayland. X11 WM will force the undecorated window into the visible area, and the edge offset varies by platform (Linux edge_offset=0, macOS/Windows can be half-screen). Aggressive simplification is often more effective than incremental fixes: the Thin Adapter+MCP Server+Skills three-layer model replaces the 3170-line proprietary routing logic, removing 2823 lines and achieving cross-CLI generality. Multi-CLI systems should use convention files (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md) rather than runtime injection; unifying the history ring buffer is more reliable than adapting to each CLI session mechanism. The complete MCP configuration for Claude CLI -p non-interactive mode requires two steps: (1) explicitly pass –mcp-config to load project-level tools; (2) add –permission-mode bypassPermissions to bypass permission confirmation. The wildcard in –allowedTools is unreliable in this mode due to contention with MCP server initialization, and bypassPermissions is the correct pattern for backend service calls. Debugging Runtime logs are the fundamental means of underlying system debugging: when underlying system behaviors such as GTK, WM, or OS occur, priority should be given to verification through logs/monitors (e.g., backend.log shows +305px systematic offset) rather than inference from code. After multiple failed fixes, identify the boundary where “continuing fixes cannot solve architectural issues” and stop local fixes to focus on root cause analysis. “Parameters are implemented in code” does not mean “parameters are passed”: the integration layer is the most common connection break point; verify by checking the calling side rather than just the implementation side. In Python, synchronous await methods cause TypeError; if silently caught by except Exception, it leads to silent functionality downgrade instead of an error, making troubleshooting difficult. When debugging nested process CLI tools (main process→Claude CLI→MCP server), record actual command-line parameters first and then isolate each parameter to verify its effect, which is more efficient than guessing parameter behavior directly. The skip_completed mechanism in the pipeline cannot detect files with invalid content (all gt_labels are -1); active verification of content validity is required. Tools The divergent exploration of ccplan skills (multiple solutions) + Critic adversarial review + feasibility probing process can effectively transform complex platform architecture issues into executable plans. During this week’s Critic phase, high-value issues such as Wayland compatibility, lark-oapi thread blocking, ThoughtStore not being a singleton, and 4 hidden code dependencies were pre-discovered, offering high ROI and serving as key engineering practices for handling high uncertainty tasks. GDK input_shape_combine_region intercepts events at the X11 layer; setPointerCapture cannot bypass it. In drag scenarios, input shape should be temporarily extended to the full window on the Rust side. GTK’s resizable(false) WM hint prevents both user dragging and programmatic set_size(), and dynamic size adjustment requires temporary unlocking. assert!() and unwrap() in Rust production code are potential crash points when accepting external inputs; uniformly change to Result and use? for propagation. Lock cross-await points are common risks in asynchronous programming; the solution is to Clone the required data before await to release the lock in advance. Any user input concatenated into a file path must be validated via a whitelist (more reliable than a blacklist). When wrapping stdlib logging with structlog, explicitly add ExtraAdder() processor; otherwise, the extra={} field silently disappears without error. git reset –soft is an efficient way to organize commit history, allowing any number of commits to be compressed into semantically clear commits, suitable for CI environments and automation tools. Domain Knowledge Core MIHD experiment conclusion: High-quality embeddings are more important than clustering method selection (STAIG+mclust ARI=0.546 vs STAIG+Leiden=0.513); the STAIG fusion framework is highly robust to gene encoders (Teddy ARI=0.495 vs PCA ARI=0.497); the space graph contrast learning mechanism dominates clustering performance, and the impact of gene embedding quality is greatly diluted. Foundation Models suffer from systematic transfer loss in cross-domain downstream tasks (Teddy gene-only ARI=0.186 is inferior to PCA=0.255; optimization goals do not match); HD dimension imbalance issues (concatenation of 1586d=50d PCA+1536d UNI2 is worse than single modality); data scale is a key variable (adaln is effective in DLPFC but completely fails in HD 17502 spots). The narrative of multimodal fusion papers should equally emphasize negative and positive results. The paper setting should define research gaps (“no system study on zero-shot FM fusion currently exists”) rather than method performance; claiming single modality can also perform retrieval adds stronger argumentation by including this rebuttal (simple fusion is a trap→space graph learning is the bridge→correct fusion can surpass single modality). NeurIPS D&B Track submission strategy: “domain correctors” (quantifying specific benchmark defects) are more accepted than “new method proposers”; reviewers value multi-dimensional evaluation, fair baseline comparisons, manual verification mechanisms (κ≥0.68), and counterintuitive negative findings. Nature Methods Analysis level requires each method to run 10 times with mean±std and 4-dimensional evaluation. Modern Linux desktops (Ubuntu 22.04+) default to Wayland; cross-platform window tracking should use GNOME Introspect D-Bus as the main path, with xdotool/xprop only as XWayland fallback. Background sampling tasks should not rely on CronScheduler with a minimum tick of 60s; non-minute interval tasks require independent asyncio.Task loop. AI Usage Notes Effective Modes:
✓ Critic subagent adversarial review: actively discovers high-value architectural risks such as Wayland compatibility, lark-oapi thread blocking, ThoughtStore not being a singleton, and 4 hidden code dependencies during planning, avoiding large-scale rework later and being key to successful delivery of multiple projects this week. ✓ Parallel subagents generate code in batches: create multiple analysis scripts (cross-slice Query aggregation, Fig visualization, HD Marker Gene visualization) simultaneously, significantly reducing serial processing time for multiple tasks. ✓ Systematic multi-layer troubleshooting: start from log evidence (+305px offset in backend.log, permission_denials field) and confirm assumptions layer by layer to locate the root cause, showing strength in complex issues such as MCP three-layer breakage and GTK size negotiation. ✓ ccplan structured planning breaks complex platform issues like FloatBall Linux fixes into 6 alternatives, and converges on the optimal solution after feasibility probing. ✓ ECL documentation persistence across sessions: during multiple days of continuous FloatBall fixes, use /compact to restore context, reducing repeated analysis costs.Limitations: ✗ When no running environment is available, incorrect assumptions were made that the underlying APIs (Tauri set_size, GTK gravity, Google Calendar calendarList scope) work as expected. Multiple iterations of fixes were carried out at the wrong level, and direction needs to be corrected through user testing feedback or log evidence. ✗ After multiple rounds of fixing attempts, the system failed to actively identify the boundary that “continuing patching cannot resolve architectural issues”. Every time new logs appeared, another solution was tried. Root cause analysis only occurs upon explicit user request. ✗ Outdated or fabricated information was provided in the fast-iteration product area (AionUI slash commands, Claude context window specifications). Technical parameters updated rapidly should not be stated in a definitive tone. ✗ Lack of local environment awareness: It defaults to cloning repositories already present locally from GitHub instead of prioritizing search in the local file system. ✗ Mistake in judgment of git operation scope: When users requested “rolling back changes in this session”, git stash was used incorrectly, affecting all uncommitted changes and nearly causing loss of historical work. ✗ Incomplete awareness of global dependencies in large code repositories. Issues such as broken connections in the integration layer (parameters not passed) require multiple rounds of investigation to be identified. Next Week’s Plan Four key areas for next week: (1) MIHD paper — collect the complete HD evaluation table for basic_contrastive HD experiments, advance the code gap tasks (Leiden result restoration script, figure generation script, spatial continuity metrics, multi-seed support), start paper figure generation and draft writing, with the goal of reaching a submitable draft level; (2) TokenMonitor — finally verify the fixed window + GDK Input Shape solution on real Linux devices, confirm that the WM clamp issue is resolved. If verified, a PR will be merged, and the Linux FloatBall fix will be completed, ending this long-running task that has lasted nearly two weeks; (3) Life-Copilot — obtain OpenReview account credentials to unlock the NeurIPS review feedback function, verify the stability of Screen Time Tracker in production environments, and continuously observe the performance of the 11-level fallback chain in real use; (4) Research exploration — convert the conclusions of the NeurIPS D&B Track survey into specific experimental designs, evaluate the feasibility of a multi-dimensional evaluation benchmark for VLM credibility, and follow up on the AionUI remote SSH access feature request.

title: Weekly Summary 2026-W14

content:
Daily Log — 2026-04-05 Today’s Overview What was done: Refactored Linux FloatBall from a dynamic-resize architecture to a fixed-size window + GDK Input Shape approach; added a structlog structured logging/operation audit system to the Life-Copilot Discord Bot; fully fixed two compounding issues in Claude CLI -p mode: missing MCP tool configuration and permission denial How it was done: FloatBall used ccplan to evaluate six approaches before implementing the cairo::Region + GTK geometry_hints fixed-window solution, temporarily expanding the input shape to the full window during dragging; Life-Copilot issues were resolved by tracing the nested process call chain layer by layer, sequentially adding the –mcp-config parameter and –permission-mode bypassPermissions to fix non-interactive mode permission denial Why it matters: Eliminated the Linux WM +305px/+113px systematic position offset and removed ~150 lines of probe/corrective patch code; Discord Bot now persists complete conversation records to disk, and Google Calendar MCP tools are fully operational in production Completed architectural refactor of Linux FloatBall to fixed-window + GDK Input Shape to eliminate platform-level geometry offsets, and systematically resolved two root-cause issues in Life-Copilot Discord Bot: missing structured logging and MCP tool permission denial
Today’s Tasks Architecture & Strategy 🔄 TokenMonitor FloatBall Linux Architectural Refactor (Fixed Window + GDK Input Shape) — After evaluating 6 candidate approaches via ccplan, implemented the fixed-window solution: window permanently uses expanded dimensions (152×56) without resizing, using GDK input_shape_combine_region to control click-through regions (collapsed: ball area only; expanded: full window; dragging: temporarily full window). Added cairo-rs dependency, removed ~150 lines of probe/corrective reapply mechanism, and additionally fixed three issues: ball appearing squashed (GTK geometry_hints), unable to expand (CSS direction positioning), unable to drag (set_float_ball_dragging command), and removed snap functionality to prioritize movement stability. 284 Rust + 205 frontend tests passing, awaiting final runtime validation. ✅ Life-Copilot Discord Bot MCP Tool Call Complete Fix — Two-phase fix: Phase 1 discovered that claude -p does not automatically load project-level .claude/mcp_servers.json, added –mcp-config parameter to the command in claude_adapter.py (loading 19 MCP tools); Phase 2 reproduced permission_denials root cause by running claude -p directly (non-interactive mode cannot complete permission confirmations), –allowedTools wildcards proved unreliable due to timing issues, ultimately resolved with –permission-mode bypassPermissions, verified that calendar queries return results correctly. ✅ Life-Copilot Structured Logging System (structlog + file rotation + operation audit) — Replaced stdlib logging with structlog, implementing dev colored output + prod JSON format + 10MB rotation; created audit_log.py to write JSONL audit records at three points: Discord on_message, FastAPI middleware, and CLISelector.send, covering complete conversations (user input + bot replies); fixed a bug where missing ExtraAdder processor caused extra fields to be silently dropped; cleaned up 4 print() statements. 420 tests passing. Implementation & Fixes ✅ FloatBall Session Changes Rollback — A CSS min() modification and collapse flow refactor from an AI session caused additional issues; user requested rollback. The AI incorrectly used git stash, rolling back all uncommitted changes; after git stash pop restored changes, the three specific modifications from that session were manually and precisely reverted. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. Linux WM cannot atomically handle dynamic resize of transparent borderless windows, causing systematic +305px/+113px position offset, probe/corrective mechanism flickering, and size mismatch clipping between WebView and native window Solution: Fixed window size to expanded (152×56) permanently with no resizing; used GDK input_shape_combine_region to control click-through: collapsed shows only ball area (56×56), expanded and dragging accept events across the full window
Key Insight: This is a platform architecture problem, not a calculation bug: Linux WM interprets the same rect request with different semantics; eliminating resize is the cure, not local patches that merely shift symptoms around
2. Life-Copilot Discord Bot continuously replied “OAuth authentication required” to calendar queries, root cause being two compounding issues: (1) claude -p does not load project-level MCP config; (2) MCP tool call permissions are silently denied in non-interactive mode Solution: Sequentially added –mcp-config .claude/mcp_servers.json and –permission-mode bypassPermissions to the command in claude_adapter.py; reproduced permission_denials field by running claude -p directly to locate root cause
Key Insight: Claude CLI session-less mode and interactive mode have different MCP loading behavior; –allowedTools wildcards are unreliable in non-interactive mode due to a race condition with MCP server initialization; bypassPermissions is the correct mode for backend service calls
3. Three platform-specific issues appeared after the first fixed-window implementation: ball displayed squashed (window builder still using 56×56), unable to expand (CSS not applying per data-direction), drag broken (input shape blocking X11 events after mouse leaves ball area) Solution: (1) Changed window builder to use expanded dimensions and locked min=max with GTK geometry_hints; (2) CSS justify-content always applied based on data-direction; (3) Added set_float_ball_dragging command to expand input shape to full window during dragging and restore afterward
Key Insight: WebKitGTK has default minimum natural size constraints; X11-layer input shape event interception occurs before setPointerCapture, requiring synchronous region expansion on the Rust side
General Issues 4. structlog wrapping stdlib logging causes extra={} fields to silently disappear from JSON output Solution: Added structlog.stdlib.ExtraAdder() to shared_processors to merge extra fields into structured output
Key Insight: When structlog wraps stdlib, extra parameters are not automatically passed through — ExtraAdder must be explicitly added, as fields are silently dropped without any error
5. When the user requested rollback of “current session changes,” the AI incorrectly used git stash, nearly causing loss of historical work Solution: After git stash pop restored changes, manually identified the three specific modifications from that session and precisely reverted them
Key Insight: git stash affects all uncommitted changes and is not appropriate for “only revert current session changes”; git diff should be used first to understand the scope of changes before reverting them individually
Human Thinking vs. AI Thinking Strategic Level Linux FloatBall Root Cause Diagnosis and Solution Selection Role Approach Human Completed full diagnosis before the session began: 4-layer geometry system mismatch, 11 previous attempts and their failure reasons, log evidence (+305px = expanded width, +113px = collapsed width as systematic patterns) AI After confirming the diagnosis via Explore agent, structured it into 6 candidate solutions and drove adversarial review and feasibility validation, then fully implemented the recommended fixed-window solution Analysis: Human’s diagnostic depth and evidence quality far exceeded AI’s; AI’s value was in structured solution design and execution, not problem discovery
MCP Issue Investigation Strategy Role Approach Human Continuously pushed the AI to investigate deeply rather than accepting surface-level explanations AI Systematically traced layer by layer from token → MCP server startup → CLI call chain, ultimately reproducing permission_denials by directly testing the claude -p command to locate the root cause Analysis: Human ensured the problem was thoroughly resolved rather than superficially patched through continuous pressure; AI provided a systematic multi-layer investigation methodology
Discovering Bot Replies Were Not Being Logged Role Approach Human Intuitively asked “how did the discord bot reply to me?”, discovering that logs only recorded user input and omitted AI replies AI During implementation, only focused on the user-input-side audit entry point without proactively considering conversation completeness Analysis: Human identified a critical omission (conversation completeness) from a user perspective; AI only considered audit entry points from a system architecture standpoint
Defining the Scope of the Logging System Requirements Role Approach Human Simply said “write some code to record logs,” then after being prompted, explicitly chose file persistence + structured logging + full operation audit AI Scanned existing code and found 73/114 files already had logging, proactively identified requirement ambiguity, and presented three directional options for the user to choose from Analysis: Human provided a vague requirement; AI made it concrete through code exploration into selectable options; final direction was chosen by human, executed by AI
Implementation Level git Rollback Scope Judgment Role Approach Human Intended to only revert the current AI session’s changes while preserving previous historical work AI Used git stash, affecting a scope far beyond the user’s intent (rolling back all uncommitted changes) Analysis: AI failed to accurately understand the boundary between “current session changes” and “all uncommitted changes,” choosing an operation with too broad an impact
