content:
Daily Report — 2026-03-24 Daily Overview Completed work: Large-scale refactoring and skill design of the Gadget toolkit, as well as architectural planning and basic implementation for TokenMonitor cross-platform migration. Implementation methods: Using ccplan skills for systematic ECL method planning, parallel agents for module extraction and adversarial review, Smoke tests for migration to ensure backward compatibility, and atomic modifications to cross-platform base code. Impact: Achieved Gadget modularization (from 2930-line monolithic code to 8 modules, each with 72 tests), established paper-style code documentation capabilities, removed limitations of TokenMonitor on macOS (more than 350 lines of code were deleted), and developed an executable cross-platform implementation roadmap. The refactored Gadget summary module consists of 8 components, each with 72 tests. Three Claude Code skills based on paper-style documentation methods were designed, and a comprehensive cross-platform migration plan for TokenMonitor was completed. In the initial implementation, more than 350 lines of code specific to macOS were removed.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ TokenMonitor cross-platform ECL planning (Phase 0–8) — Completed the full ccplan skill workflow: assumption verification → divergent exploration → adversarial filtering → feasibility probing → review approval. The doc/ecl/cross-platform-ccusage-ssh.yaml file was created, recording 8 validated requirements, architectural decisions, and 11 task implementation roadmaps. ✅ Refactored summary module: splitting files, packaging, and adding tests — Split daily_summary.py (2930 lines) into 8 modules (configuration, remote, parser, usage, summarizer, formatter, daily, CLI), eliminated sys.path hack, and added 72 tests. ✅ Redesigned summary skill with a six-part structure — Shifted from a four-dimensional plane structure to a six-part narrative structure (highlights → introduction → architecture → implementation → results → conclusion and future work). ✅ Implementation of TokenMonitor Phase E (E-1 to E-6) — Removed objc2 dependencies, deleted glass/transparent window code, cleaned up macOS-specific import statements in lib.rs, implemented cross-platform tray display (set_title + tooltip), and replaced NSApplication theme detection with a default dark fallback. ✅ Renaming cchelper to ccplan and fixing workflow interruption issues — Renamed the skill, added CONTINUOUS EXECUTION MANDATE, inserted ‘→ NEXT:’ phase transition, and completed multi-round protocols for all phases. 🔄 Remaining tasks for TokenMonitor Phase E (E-7 to E-11) — To-do items: remove front-end glass code, set up CI/CD matrix, create platform-aware setup UI, perform end-to-end validation on Windows. ✅ Create code summary and code optimization skills — Extracted and adapted SKILL.md from Claude.ai .skill ZIP package, creating two new skills for code summary and optimization. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Creation of TokenMonitor tutorial documentation — Created comprehensive documentation/tutorial.md covering installation, UI navigation, setup, and troubleshooting. ✅ Improvement of TokenMonitor CLAUDE.md — Enhanced CLAUDE.md by adding platform limitations specific to macOS, pre-submission hooks, release sections, rate limiting/pricing/ tray rendering explanations, and ccusage directory comments. ✅ Configuring rclone for private file synchronization — Used sync.py to push research data (cache, project, report) and configuration files to Google Drive. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. daily_summary.py is 2930 lines long with mixed responsibilities, exceeding maintainability thresholds Solution: Split it into 8 modules based on functional boundaries: configuration (75 lines), remote (100 lines), parser (460 lines), usage (460 lines), summarizer (340 lines), formatter (440 lines), daily (750 lines), CLI (130 lines). Keep daily_summary.py as a fallback to maintain backward compatibility.
Key insight: Large-scale refactoring requires Smoke tests (47 import contract tests) for migration to ensure zero disruption. Parallel agent execution can accelerate module extraction.
2. In LLM pipeline code exceeding 2930 lines, 5 dialogue parser and hierarchical merging logic have no test coverage Solution: Create 72 tests in 5 test files: test_imports.py (47 Smoke tests), test_config.py (7 tests), test_parsers.py (6 tests), test_formatter.py (6 tests), test_summarizer.py (6 tests).
Key insight: Write import contract tests before refactoring (run twice: before and after transformation). This provides a safety net, making large-scale changes more reliable.
3. Technical documentation generated by code summary skills is too flat, lacks narrative and context, and is not suitable for different readers Solution: Re-design as a six-part structure similar to a paper (highlights → introduction → architecture → implementation → results → conclusion and future work). Add scale-adaptive adjustments (≤3 files: simplified version, 4–10: standard version, 11–50: full version, >50: focus on architecture). Implement a three-level fallback mechanism for results (read output → read documentation example → infer from code).
Key insight: Documentation needs to match scale and audience. Critic Agent review identified a contradiction between “all readers” and “fixed structure”; this was resolved by layering within each part.
4. TokenMonitor users initially wanted direct rendering of cost text onto tray icon pixels for unified cross-platform display, but Windows/Linux trays are fixed-size squares (16–32px), making ‘$12.45’ unclear to display Solution: Switch to a hybrid approach after feasibility probing: macOS continues using native set_title() for the icon next to the text; Windows/Linux use set_tooltip() for hover-based cost display (simplified rendering like ‘$12’ may be provided in the future).
Key insight: Research via parallel agents revealed that platform constraints (tray icon size) hindered architecture progress before implementation; feasibility probing identified this issue, avoiding unnecessary effort.
5. Initially planned integration of ccusage backend called direct CLI subprocess invocation, but supporting multiple providers (Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Amp) required managing 5 npm packages with different binary names Solution: Found that ccusage provides @ccusage/mcp (model context protocol server), which already aggregates CLI from all providers via stdio JSON-RPC. Changed architecture to a single long-lived MCP process instead of generating subprocesses repeatedly.
Key insight: Phase 1 assumption verification revealed ‘ccusage’ was actually 5 independent packages; deeper research showed MCP server is a better integration point, solving performance and multi-CLI coordination issues.
6. Using sys.path.insert() techniques in 3 places (mcp_server.py, monthly_summary.py, weekly_summary.py) causes fragile module identity issues Solution: Packaged summarize/ via init.py, updated pyproject.toml package list, and changed all imports to ‘from summarize.xxx import …’. Remove all sys.path operations. Key insight: Workarounds for sys.path cause module identity issues (_cached_config loaded twice). Correct packaging can completely avoid such errors.
7. ccplan skill workflow terminates early at phase boundaries, failing to complete the full cycle Solution: Add “continue execution instruction” at the skill header and insert “→ Next: immediately enter Phase X” prompts at each phase boundary (10 phases total), completing multi-round protocol parts for all 9 phases, with phase transition marked as mandatory.
Key insight: For multi-phase workflows, prompt engineering needs to explicitly indicate continuation at each boundary. Implicit expectations (“just continue”) cannot be reliably enforced.
8. Original TokenMonitor plan included retaining change_stats and subagent_stats functions after migration to ccusage (currently marked as #[allow(dead_code) dead code), but ccusage lacks corresponding features Solution: After user confirmation, decided to retain a simple JSONL reader for these two functions during migration of token/cost/pricing logic to the ccusage MCP server.
Key insight: Adversarial review (FIND-001 CRITICAL) forced us to clarify feature scope before migration; recording the retention plan avoids implicit loss of features.
Human and AI Methodology Strategic Level Discovery of ccusage CLI and MCP Server Role Method Human User initially described ccusage as “npm install -g ccusage” (single tool), then corrected to “npx install” after AI clarified the structure of 5 packages. AI AI actively explored ccusage/ subdirectory, identified the monolithic repository architecture, studied the MCP server, and provided a comprehensive survey before proposing integration suggestions. Analysis: Human understanding of ccusage was limited to treating it as a black-box tool; AI’s deep exploration of code revealed internal architecture, fundamentally changing integration strategy. This is where parallel agent research is more advantageous than human memory.
Simplification of TokenMonitor window appearance for decision-making Role Method Human User chose to remove all glass/fog/transparent effects (“transparent background across platforms”), instead of searching for cross-platform alternatives (Windows Mica/Acrylic, Linux compositor). AI AI suggested exploring platform-specific alternatives (implementing Windows Mica via windows-rs crate, using GNOME/KDE compositor detection for Linux versions) to maintain visual consistency. Analysis: Human prioritized simplicity and reduced maintenance burden over visual consistency; AI tends to retain features. User decision was pragmatic—removing 350 lines of platform-specific code was more important than aesthetic benefits.
Decision on refactoring scope: Atomic or incremental? Role Method Human User chose to solve three issues simultaneously in a single PR (splitting files + packaging + testing) to speed up completion, despite higher risk. AI AI initially proposed incremental approach (Option D: two-phase refactoring) as a safer alternative. Analysis: Human values completion speed and comprehensive testing as risk mitigation. AI prefers risk-avoiding incremental methods. User’s trust in smoke tests made atomic method reasonable.
Acceptance of Critic Agent’s architectural feedback Role Method Human User accepted Critic’s suggestion, reducing chapter count from 7 to 6 (merging introduction and motivation sections, splitting methodology sections), and adjusted initial idea based on technical analysis. AI Critic Agent identified the contradiction between “all readers” and fixed chapter structure, proposing a 6-chapter compromise. Analysis: When faced with valid criticism, user was willing to modify the idea rather than stick to the original concept. This collaborative approach led to better design (motivation naturally fits in the introduction section of code projects).
Design philosophy for skill: Monolithic or modular? Role Method Human User immediately decided to separate “code summary” and “code optimization” instead of merging them into one tool. AI AI initially considered both parts as a single unit, without suggesting separation. Analysis: Human prioritized completion speed and reduced maintenance; AI tends to retain features. User’s decision was practical—removing 350 lines of platform-specific code was more important than aesthetic benefits.Difference Analysis: Humans apply Unix philosophy to skill design. This reflects design intuition: separating different concerns clarifies trigger conditions, thereby improving user experience.
Limitations of Artificial Intelligence Key Limitations The original ccplan skill design lacks clear instructions for continuing operations between stages, leading to premature termination of the workflow. Prompts for “continue execution instruction” and “→ next step” are needed at each boundary. AI initiated 4 background agents for adversarial review and research, but 3 agents never completed or returned empty output files—yet AI continued stage 8 review without waiting for their results, making architectural decisions under incomplete analysis. AI cannot execute Rust cargo commands on users’ Windows systems (cargo is not in the Git Bash PATH), so it relies on type-checking logic instead of compilation verification—this caused runtime errors (E-1 to E-6) in 6 completed code changes. The initial summary skill design did not address the conflict between “all reader levels” and “fixed chapter structure” requirements until the Critic Agent conducted review. General Limitations The.skill file being a ZIP archive was not automatically detected, requiring manual extraction using the Python zipfile module to read its content. When users ask “What about Windows and Linux systems now?” after tutorial creation, AI offers 3 options but does not consider this as implicit approval for cross-platform work—/ccplan must be explicitly called instead of treating it as a signal to continue operations. Lessons Learned Key Experience – ECL method successfully identified key issues before implementation through hypothesis verification, adversarial filtering, and feasibility probing. Examples include: tray icon size limitation, lack of ccusage function, and performance impact of child process startup. This verifies the premise that “needs are assumptions”—every proposed need should be questioned. ECL documentation enables persistent and traceable design decisions across sessions. State fields track workflow stages, and the pending_input field maintains continuity during context compression. Migration smoke tests are crucial for large-scale refactoring: write import contract tests covering all external consumers and test them before and after migration. This ensures reliable changes (47 tests × 2 runs = 94 verifications). Tauri v2’s tray.set_title() is only applicable on macOS (not explicitly stated in TokenMonitor code); set_tooltip() is the alternative for Windows/Linux. This is an important cross-platform consideration for Tauri menu bar applications. Adversarial review (Critic Agent) identified blind spots in design: more than 12 issues were found, including serious contradictions between two projects. Red-blue adversarials during the requirement phase can prevent rework later. Multi-stage prompt workflows require clear continue instructions at each boundary: continuous execution instruction (global), “→ NEXT:” transformation (per stage), multi-round protocol (per stage). Implied expectations do not apply. When migrating from platform-specific code to a cross-platform architecture, removing all platform-specific features (such as glass blur, Dock icon visibility) is easier to maintain than finding minimal common standards alternatives—in infrastructure code, simplicity outweighs functional equivalence. Parallel agent execution can accelerate independent tasks: 5 module extraction agents run simultaneously, reducing sequential bottlenecks. Clear task boundaries are needed, and shared state is not allowed. Adaptive scale design can improve user experience across different project sizes: fewer than 3 files yield simplified output (avoiding over-documentation), 11–50 files receive full processing, and more than 50 files are grouped to focus on architecture (avoiding context overflow). Critic Agent identified 12 issues (2 of which are critical), all of which have been resolved. 72 tests were created, including 47 import contract smoke tests. All sys.path tricks were eliminated through proper packaging. content:
Daily Report — 2026-03-23 Today’s Overview What was done: Completed gadget project data sync, cchelper skill installation, and GPU resource survey on the DCC HPC cluster, while systematically documenting the core challenges of the MIHD spatial transcriptomics multimodal clustering project into a persistent problem summary document. How it was done: Used rclone + sync.py to pull data from Google Drive, queried cluster resources with SLURM commands (sinfo/sacctmgr), manually installed the cchelper skill directory to ~/.claude/skills/, and integrated the full picture of issues by reading plans.md/RESULTS.md/diagnostic reports. Why it matters: The new DCC machine went from zero to a fully operational environment, and the MIHD project’s historical issues were consolidated into PROBLEM_SUMMARY.md for the first time, providing a structured entry point for future ablation experiments and debugging. Completed environment initialization on the DCC HPC cluster (rclone sync, GPU node survey, skill installation), and documented current issues for the MIHD research project.
Today’s Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ MIHD project progress and issue review — Reviewed the current state of the MIHD project (best ARI 0.546, root cause of cross-slice retrieval failure, list of fixed bugs) and generated a structured problem summary document at docs/PROBLEM_SUMMARY.md. Implementation & Fixes ✅ DCC environment initialization: rclone sync of Google Drive data — Created ~/.config/gadget/sync.json on the DCC cluster and used sync.py pull to sync the four data categories (summarize/research/test/website) from gdrive:gadget to local storage. Successfully synced 11 directories and 3 file groups. ✅ DCC GPU node survey — Used sinfo/sacctmgr to identify GPU partitions available to user account (yizhanglab): common (RTX 2080), gpu-common, scavenger-gpu (A6000/RTX 5000-6000 Ada), scavenger-h200 (H200×8). Account TRES limits are cpu=100, mem=500G. ✅ Install cchelper skill on DCC — Installed the project’s skills/cchelper directory to ~/.claude/skills/cchelper/, containing 4 files: SKILL.md, helper.md, ecl-schema.md, methods-catalog.md. Issues & Solutions Critical Issues 1. MIHD cross-slice retrieval almost completely failed (10 out of 14 query directions had SL@50=0) Solution: Diagnosis confirmed the root cause is that PCA/STAIG processes each slice independently, producing incomparable embedding spaces. The fix is to use scGPT embeddings directly (shared space, average SL@50=0.416, 100% hit rate).
Key insight: Embedding space comparability (whether a shared coordinate system exists) is more fundamental than embedding quality. Cross-slice tasks and single-slice clustering should use different encoders.
2. MIHD single-slice ARI gap vs. SOTA (current 0.546 vs. target 0.60+) Solution: A 4-phase ablation experiment plan was drafted (clustering ablation → batch effect analysis → retrieval probing → 151676 targeted diagnosis), but not yet fully executed.
Key insight: Zero-variance embeddings on slice 151676 cause mclust to fail and fall back to KMeans, which is the key factor dragging down the average. Root cause still unknown.
General Issues 3. Missing ~/.config/gadget/sync.json on DCC, preventing sync.py from running Solution: AI read the existing summarize config to obtain the rclone_remote setting, manually created sync.json, verified the remote directory structure, then executed the pull.
Key insight: Config files are not automatically migrated to new machines and must be inferred from existing configs and rebuilt.
4. cp -r flattened the cchelper directory into ~/.claude/skills/ instead of preserving the subdirectory structure Solution: After discovering the issue, used mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/cchelper to create the subdirectory, then moved the scattered files into it.
Key insight: When the target directory already exists, cp -r expands the source directory’s contents directly into it. The target path must be confirmed beforehand.
Human Thinking vs. AI Thinking Strategic Level Persisting problem summaries as documentation Role Approach Human After the AI verbally summarized the issues, the user proactively requested to “write the problems in detail to a .md file,” driving the externalization of knowledge. AI The AI defaulted to answering in conversational form and did not proactively suggest writing the analysis to a file. Analysis: Humans have an instinct to externalize session content into documents; AI tends to deliver answers within the conversation without proactively persisting them.
Implementation Level Clarifying an ambiguous personal file sync request Role Approach Human The user requested to “sync personal files on gdrive,” which was vague — no target directory or specific folders were specified. AI The AI listed the directory structure on Google Drive, then asked the user to clarify their specific needs, making no assumptions before executing. Analysis: When requirements are unclear, the AI chose to confirm rather than guess — the correct approach — but the session ended without completing the actual sync as a result.
AI Limitations Significant Limitations When reviewing the MIHD project issues, the AI’s summary relied entirely on existing documentation (plans.md/RESULTS.md/diagnostic reports) and could not independently infer undocumented implicit progress or judge the priority of ablation experiments. General Limitations Overlooked the behavior difference of cp -r when the target already exists, causing files to be flattened rather than keeping the subdirectory structure. The user needed to notice this before it was corrected (in practice the AI itself discovered and corrected it). Glob search for rclone config files timed out (20 seconds) on the large HPC filesystem, requiring a fallback to a more targeted path search strategy. Today’s Takeaways Core Insights In cross-slice spatial transcriptomics tasks, the comparability of the embedding space (shared coordinate system) is more critical than local embedding quality. Foundation Models (e.g., scGPT) are naturally suited for cross-slice retrieval because they output a fixed representation space, whereas PCA/STAIG processes each slice independently, making coordinate systems incomparable. The optimal method for single-slice clustering (STAIG) and the optimal method for cross-slice retrieval (scGPT) are different. Different encoders must be chosen for different task objectives rather than seeking a single unified optimal solution. Practical Insights The DCC cluster’s scavenger-h200 partition provides H200×8 nodes (preemptive), which is an important resource for training tasks requiring large GPU memory. The account TRES limits of cpu=100/mem=500G are hard constraints when submitting large jobs. AI found the skills/cchelper directory (Evolving Constraint Planning skill) and installed it to ~/.claude/skills/. After reading plans.md/RESULTS.md and two diagnostic reports, AI compiled: the completed framework and evaluation of 10 fusion strategies; four unresolved issues (ARI gap / cross-slice retrieval failure / 151676 crash / scGPT paradox); and 5 previously fixed historical bugs. 5. π₀.₅ Pi0WithCompletionHead uses a combination approach that adds pi0/ prefix to all parent module parameter paths, causing pytree merge to throw ‘2 children vs 1 child’ ValueError, and checkpoints cannot be loaded at all [π₀.₅] (2026-03-18) Solution: Change to inheritance (class Pi0WithCompletionHead(Pi0)), and align Pi0 parameters directly with the checkpoint path at the top level; inheritance in Flax NNX is the only way to keep checkpoint path compatibility
6. RobotwinOutputs.call only returns the {actions} field, silently discarding manip_progress; even if the model correctly predicts the progress field, external parties can never obtain it, and the eval txt file remains empty always [π₀.₅] (2026-03-18) Solution: Modify the return dict of the output transform to include the manip_progress field, and re-establish the data flow; to troubleshoot such bugs, track upward from the end of the data flow
7. When CalendarPro batch reports task status, the system returns ‘I’m not sure’ instead of processing the request [CalendarPro] (2026-03-18) Solution: Analyze the complete root cause chain: low embedding similarity → LLM classifier lacks this intent → GENERAL handler discards the AI response; add BATCH_UPDATE support across the routing/classification/processing three layers, and keyword counting rules can compensate for embedding blind spots
8. In MIHD all_aligned mode, the –alignment parameter is not injected during the evaluate phase, so EvaluationJob.alignment remains None, Harmony alignment results are completely ignored, and the alignment function actually fails [MIHD spatial transcriptomics] (2026-03-18) Solution: Add 3 lines of code before the run_pipeline.py evaluate phase: when phase==‘all_aligned’ and args.alignment has a value, inject alignment into extra_config for each experiment
9. drop_in_transit_D0 generates very few valid scenarios, with min_hold_height=0.85 being too low; objects on the desktop (z≈0.88) are misclassified as in the air, resulting in 80% false positives [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-20) Solution: Raise the threshold to 0.93 (desktop height 0.80 + Milk object height 0.08 + margin 0.05), eliminating false positives, and increasing D0 success rate from 10% to 50%
10. python summarize/daily_summary.py gets stuck permanently at @ccusage/codex step, with no output or error [gadget] (2026-03-21) Solution: Use subprocess.run(capture_output=True) to redirect stdin to DEVNULL, and the npx installation prompt for the first time forces infinite waiting; add –yes parameter to skip interactive confirmation in all 3 npx calls
11. In multi-object tasks like threading/pick_place, phase detection fails systematically, and all frames in threading are marked as pre_reach, causing 12/13 skills to fail to find an opportunity [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-21) Solution: Add InteractionSegmenter to segment trajectories by object interactions (EEF proximity + gripper state + co-motion detection), clearly define target_object and phase for each segment; completely bypass single-object phase detection instead of fixing the defect—increase threading subtypes from 3 to 25
12. The Panda robotic arm gripper action polarity is opposite to the code assumption: Panda requires action=+1 to close, but hardcoding -1 actually opens the gripper, leading to all injections for coffee/stack failing [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-22) Solution: Detect polarity via robot arm type in EnvWrapper.init, set PandaGripper to close_action=+1.0, and RethinkGripper to -1.0; add a helper and replace all hardcoded actions [-1]
13. drop_with_interaction generates 0 scenes for all tasks: the original implementation only applies a 1–3 cm offset before releasing, and objects spaced 10–20 cm never touch neighbors [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-22) Solution: Rewrite the inject logic: actively move the object directly above the non-target (+0.15m), then release the gripper to allow free fall, and track object-object contact throughout the settle process
Learning Insights Architecture Pipeline contract alignment must track the complete data flow: not only modify processing logic but also ensure data is persisted at the storage layer (e.g., segment_interactions() results written to NPZ); output transform is an implicit filter in the inference chain, and any field not in the return dict is silently discarded; CLI parameters in multi-stage pipelines must be explicitly passed to each downstream stage, not relying on implicit sharing. “Passing unit tests ≠ E2E correctness” In multi-object robot manipulation tasks, target_object must pass through all three stages (detector/injector/validator) as a primary citizen; objects[0] is the first object in dictionary insertion order, and using it in multi-object scenarios causes complete semantic errors without errors, leading to systematic misjudgments based on object state. graspable objects and fixtures must be distinguished by the grasp_geoms field, and target selection cannot rely solely on distance/position Independent processing per section (PCA/training) produces non-comparable embedding spaces, which is a fundamental architectural limitation and cannot be fixed through normalization or post-processing. The only correct zero-shot solution is pre-trained Foundation Model (shared weights). Gene FM (scGPT 100%) outperforms Vision FM (UNI2 71%) because gene expression has stronger cross-sample consistency due to the batch effect in H&E images Flax NNX extended models: inheritance (class Child(Parent)) is the only way to keep checkpoint path compatibility; combination (self.pi0 = Pi0(…)) adds a prefix before all parent module parameter paths, causing pytree merge to fail completely. The freezing mechanism (freeze_filter+nnx.DiffState) in existing frameworks usually considers scalability—prioritize reuse over creation Facing architectural design flaws, “bypassing” is more fundamental than “fixing”: the single-object phase detection assumption cannot be fixed through parameter tuning; directly bypassing it with InteractionSegmenter is a more elegant solution. Do not fix but bypass the flawed abstraction level Debugging State machine design principle: completing an event must do two things simultaneously—reset trigger conditions (clear current_prompt) and broadcast state change (_publish_state(‘idle’)). Doing only one of them leaves hidden bugs like infinite loops or upstream perception failure. None checks must precede any property access (defensive programming) When diagnosing behavior of unknown third-party libraries, writing a minimal test script is more reliable and efficient than static code analysis (robosuite gripper polarity case); log counter statistics are more effective for locating systematic bugs than reading each entry (1698 occurrences of ‘gripper not closed’ directly point to target_object ambiguity); troubleshoot implicit filtering bugs by tracking upward from the data flow Experiment naming conventions must strictly match actual implementation; inconsistent naming like “pca_uni2_staig_fusion” leads to long-term misunderstandings, and actual configuration must be confirmed by reading logs rather than just experiment names. Benchmark data quality issues (uneven distribution, all phase annotations as pre_reach) should include monitoring mechanisms during pipeline design Tools subprocess.run(capture_output=True) redirects stdin to DEVNULL, and CLI tools with interactive prompts (npx, etc.) must use –yes/-y, otherwise they hang indefinitely instead of timing out. capture_output=True is the high-level cause of hanging Slurm HPC cluster’s pam_slurm_adopt policy kills all related processes at job end, and SSH nohup cannot bypass this; long training tasks must submit formal jobs with sbatch. MuJoCo physics simulation (enable_camera=False) is a pure CPU task, and MUJOCO_GL=disabled can completely bypass OpenGL, with worker count exactly matching –cpus-per-task JAX has_aux mechanism: nnx.value_and_grad supports has_aux=True, compute_loss returns (loss_array, aux_dict) after which gradients are calculated only for loss_array, and aux_dict transparently carries monitoring metrics; stop_gradient strictly limits aux loss to MLP parameters, and the numerical ratio of action/aux loss does not indicate training imbalance Hugo best practices: .Title is the most stable field for identifying specific sections (.Section and.RelPermalink case sensitivity varies across platforms); static directory names matching content page base names cause path conflicts; auto-generated frontmatter should not use current system time as date; project-level layouts/partials can cover themes partially without forking the theme Spatial data nearest-neighbor query: Large point clouds (>10K points) should prioritize KD tree (O(N log N) preprocessing) instead of cdist (O(N²) memory); in HD spatial transcriptomics (17K+ cells), differences can reach OOM vs normal operation. Single truth source principle: constants referenced across multiple files must be imported from the only defined place Domain Knowledge- Recovery Behavior Group (RBG) grouping strategy: 29 error subtypes are clustered into 5 groups based on motor primitives, and demos within the same group can be cross‑augmented. MimicGen generates over 1,000 demos from 10 source demos; 1,740 simple requirements are compressed to 329 (saving 81%). This is a paradigm applicable widely to robot recovery data engineering. π₀.₅ computational graph characteristics: Reasoning follows a natural two‑step process (VLM prefix forward → action expert denoising). During training, Exp1–4 can be combined into one joint forward using teacher forcing. The from_hidden mode introduces circular dependencies due to the dependence on model output for conditioning, requiring an additional prefix‑only forward. Mean pooling of prefix_output is more suitable for classification tasks than suffix_output of action expert (for encoding global state understanding). The depth of LLM understanding in academic trajectory analysis exceeds expectations: It can automatically identify advanced features such as ‘infrastructure‑thinking researchers’ and ‘technical prerequisites for paradigm shifts’. The why_not_before field (attributing each breakthrough to data, compute, and insight across three dimensions) is the most valuable feature in researcher profiling. The recognition of conference awards has very low ROI with current LLM capabilities; it should be replaced by an external data source solution (exact title matching JSON library). AI Usage Notes Effective Patterns:
✓ Parallel multi‑agent code review (independent analysis of reuse, quality, and efficiency across three dimensions for the same diff): Issues that do not overlap are found in all three dimensions, and parallel execution saves time. ✓ Systematic code tracking to locate root causes: Tracing upward from the data flow end point reveals silent bug elimination in output transform and S2 speed limit recursive loops. ✓ Proactive quality checks beyond task boundaries: Automatically identifying混淆 with the same name (abnormal ratio of h‑index to paper count, impossible domain span, etc.) during researcher profiling, without explicit requirement in the prompt. ✓ Academic trajectory analysis reaches the level of academic review: Automatically identifying advanced features such as ‘infrastructure‑thinking researchers’, and the why_not_before field exceeds expected value. ✓ Log aggregation and statistics to locate systematic bugs: Counter statistics of 1,698 “gripper not closed” events directly point to the ambiguity root cause of target_object, which is more efficient than individual analysis. Limitations:
✗ Tendency to locate isolated bugs when dealing with complex system problems; lacks the ability to analyze contract inconsistencies from the full data flow perspective, requiring human guidance at the architecture level. ✗ Lack of proactive global data flow verification after local fixes are implemented; passing unit tests gives a false sense of completion, and multiple omissions (e05/e06/e09, target_pos transmission, collect script not integrated) require systematic human review. ✗ Environment configuration not pre‑verified leads to full batch failure over multiple rounds (Agent sub‑agent lacks Bash permissions, conda activation fails, PYTHONPATH missing, API key type issues); individual tasks should be validated before batch expansion. ✗ Failure to actively identify efficiency bottlenecks: Only setting waiting periods when generating in serial mode, without proposing parallelization; no consideration of resource isolation due to Slurm job expiration when starting SSH with nohup. ✗ Insufficient anticipation of framework‑specific behaviors: No prediction of the impact of Flax NNX inheritance vs. combination on checkpoint paths; no realization that JAX/NNX TrainConfig mechanisms can be directly reused. ✗ Lack of knowledge about latest tool features (effortLevel: max only known after discovery), resulting in knowledge lag compared to rapidly evolving AI tool ecosystems. Next Week’s Priorities Core priorities next week:
(1) Complete Error Recovery Benchmark — fix three_piece_assembly (change get_target_object and InteractionSegmenter to _get_graspable_objects() with fallback to all objects), aiming to increase the number of subtypes from 4 to over 20; complete the collect script call to segment_interactions() to persist segmented data in NPZ.
(2) Restart π₀.₅ training — submit six sbatch tasks for Pi0.5‑base LoRA combined fine‑tuning, and generate 2,000 D0 data points; monitor the comparison of action_loss/task_loss curves for Exp1–4 and Exp5–9.
(3) Advance MIHD research — start writing a paper on cross‑slice analysis based on the zero‑sample advantage established this week with scGPT, integrating Harmony alignment results (batch_entropy 0.52) as a baseline.
(4) Release Research Profiler version 3 — implement support for paper title search (planned but not implemented this week), replace conference award recognition with an external Best Paper JSON database.
(5) Stabilize infrastructure — promote the completed unified staging architecture to all tools in research, summarize, and benchmark, and verify that sync.py synchronization works uniformly across all categories.

summary: This week, efforts were made across three devices—DCC, tianhe, and TzJsDesktop—to comprehensively advance two major research directions: robot operation and spatial transcriptomics. The Error Recovery Benchmark achieved progress from design of collection schemes (RBG group with 329 demo budgets) to architectural-level trajectory segmentation reconstruction (InteractionSegmenter), with a total of 1627 training scenes (covering 148 subtypes, +35%); MIHD spatial transcriptomics completed the full pipeline for cross-slide Embedding and established the zero-sample advantage of scGPT (100% accuracy vs UNI2’s 71%); π₀.₅ completed the full training process with loss ≈0.253, and five conditioning strategies (Exp5-9) were designed; the gadget toolchain completed the architectural reconstruction of Research Profiler disambiguation, the construction of a unified deploy staging architecture for the website, and the full upgrade of ECC to opus+max thinking. The key breakthroughs this week focused on “identifying and resolving architectural root causes”: the non-comparable per-section PCA coordinate system, ambiguity in multi-object target_object, and Flax NNX inheritance vs combination—these three systematic issues were fundamentally resolved this week.
title: Weekly Summary 2026-W12

content:
Daily Report — 2026-03-22 Daily Overview Completed work: Established a complete weekly report archive (W05-W12), resolved blocking issues in website deployment, and reorganized the entire Hugo deployment process by centralizing all automatically generated content (summaries, research, benchmarks) into a hierarchical navigation test directory. Implementation methods: Batch-generated 8-week structured reports using an LLM; updated the PaperMod theme, and enhanced the update.sh script to handle exceptions (no change submissions, detection of race conditions); built the common.site_staging infrastructure with link or copy synchronization functionality, migrated all tool deployment logic to the test environment, created website/sync_staging.py for guided migration, and implemented a custom Hugo header section with hover drop-down CSS. Impact: Created comprehensive project history documentation; eliminated three deployment blocking issues, making the system production-ready; established a single source for automatically generated content, avoiding dual-write inconsistency issues, achieved atomic updates, and automatically implemented cross-platform fallback, while providing a clearer content organization structure with multi-level navigation. Completed batch generation of W05-W12 historical weekly reports, fixed critical website deployment errors (update of PaperMod theme, robustness improvement of update.sh script), and refactored the gadget’s Hugo deployment architecture to implement unified output/test environment, bugJournal drop-down navigation, and integrated benchmark report publishing functionality.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Designed and implemented a unified test environment architecture — Created common/site_staging.py with helper functions such as resolve_site_staging_root, write_site_content, copy_site_static; defined outputs/site/{content,static} as standardized test root directories; added paths.SITE_OUTPUTS_DIR to common/paths.py. ✅ Built website/sync_staging.py synchronization script — Created a Python script that implements link or copy functionality and uses os.link as a fallback to shutil.copytree; included bootstrap_source to move existing content from the website/migration to outputs/site on first use; manages bugJournal/{daily,weekly,monthly}, research, benchmark.md, and static/{images,benchmark-report}. ✅ Resolved blocking issues in website deployment and deployed the website to GitHub Pages — Updated the PaperMod theme to the latest version, fixed missing issues, resolved merge conflicts, retained custom settings for MathJax and checkboxes, enhanced the update.sh script to handle no-change cases and detect race conditions, and successfully completed full deployment. ✅ Moved summary deployment migration to the test environment — Refactored daily_summary.py, weekly_summary.py, and monthly_summary.py so their output goes to outputs/site instead of website/content; updated deployment detection logic to check test environment paths; retained the existing CLI interface. ✅ Moved research deployment migration to the test environment — Updated deploy_to_hugo in research/output.py and generate_hugo_post in research_scout.py to use common.site_staging helper functions; integrated researcher profiles and daily reports into a single research section. ✅ Added a benchmark Hugo publishing layer — Created test/benchmark/publish.py with the stage_benchmark_report function; added –deploy flag to the benchmark CLI; generated /benchmark/ wrapper pages and embedded /benchmark-report/report.html using an iframe; used a fixed past date to prevent Hugo from skipping future content; added benchmark menu item. ✅ Added bugJournal hierarchical drop-down navigation — Implemented parent-child menu structure in Hugo config.yml, created custom layout/section/header.html with submenu rendering and hover drop-down CSS, updated section _index.md file with descriptive text, lowercased all URLs to avoid case issues on host recognition. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Updated website build scripts (update.sh and update.ps1) — Modified both scripts to run python sync_staging.py before the Hugo build steps; retained the existing incremental image/video compression and git push workflow; updated the rclone configuration in sync.py to synchronize outputs/site/* instead of website/content*. ✅ Batch-generated historical weekly reports (W05-W12) — Generated structured weekly reports for weeks 5–12 of 2026, covering MIHD, error recovery benchmarks, CalendarPro, RoboBrain, Life Copilot, and multiple other devices projects. ✅ Verified end-to-end test environment synchronization and Hugo build — Verified py_compile on all modified files, executed sync_staging.py to confirm the bootstrap program and link/copy logic, ran hugo –destination .verify-public3 to confirm /benchmark/index.html, /benchmark-report/report.html, and all bugjournal sections were rendered correctly; no final push to GitHub Pages was performed. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. The first test environment synchronization overwrites months of accumulated website/content history Solution: Implemented bootstrap_source in sync_staging.py: if the test environment path does not exist but the website path exists, move the website content to the test environment first, then perform normal synchronization; a single migration preserves all historical records.
Key insight: Switching truth sources requires migration paths to retain existing data; the initial run mode makes safe switching possible without manual migration or risk of data loss.
2. Outdated PaperMod theme caused Hugo v0.157.0 build failure due to missing get-page-images section Solution: Cleaned up macOS resource folder files (._pack-*) that cause Git corruption, stored local changes, and pulled the latest theme; manually resolved merge conflicts in head.html, retained upstream theme switching, and kept local MathJax and checkboxes scripts.
Key insight: macOS resource folder files (._ prefix) corrupt the Git repository of cross-platform projects; theme updates require careful retention of local custom settings through manual conflict resolution.
3. update.sh script aborts when git commit returns a non-zero exit code Solution: Added a git diff –cached –quiet check before committing; when no changes are detected, skip commit and send a friendly message.
Key insight: Shell scripts using set -e must explicitly handle all normal failure cases; relying on command exit codes without status checks makes the automation process vulnerable.
4. /benchmark/ wrapper page cannot be rendered: Hugo identifies content/benchmark.md but does not generate /benchmark/index.html Solution: Changed the date of the wrapper page from datetime.now() to a fixed past date of 2025-01-01; moved /content/benchmark/_index.md section to /content/benchmark.md to avoid conflict with the static/benchmark directory.
Key insight: Hugo defaults to ignoring future content; sections with the same name as the static directory produce ambiguous output paths—a single page is more suitable as the wrapper content path.
General Issues 5. The find command in update.sh fails when accessing subfolders after deleting parent directories during recursive cleanup Solution: Added 2>/dev/null || true after find … -exec rm -rf {} + to gracefully ignore expected race condition errors. Key insight: Recursive deletion causes race conditions because find traverses the deleted paths; explicit error suppression is required to achieve this behavior.
6. Hugo URL case normalization: /bugJournal/ is used in config.yml but the generated path is /bugjournal/, which may cause 404 errors on GitHub Pages. Solution: Normalized all bugJournal references in config.yml and content preamble to lowercase/bugjournal/ to align with Hugo’s normalization behavior.
Key insight: Hugo’s canonifyURLs and slug generation automatically convert some names to lowercase; mixed-case URLs in config may cause inconsistency on static hosts with case sensitivity issues.
7. Windows PowerShell execution policy blocks the running of py_compile and verification scripts Solution: Use python -m py_compile directly, or embed Python code into PowerShell strings to bypass script file execution restrictions.
Key insight: Environment execution policies may block even non-destructive verification commands; Python code passed via stdin can bypass file-based restrictions without elevation.
Human and Artificial Intelligence Methodology Strategic Level Deployment Architecture: Unified Test Directory as the Single Data Source Role Method Human Users identified dual-write issues (tools writing to both output and website) and proposed a clean architectural solution: centralize all tool outputs in outputs/site, then automatically link or copy them to the final location, followed by Hugo build. Artificial Intelligence AI first checked the deployment paths of each tool scattered on the website to find opportunities for gradual refactoring within the existing structure without questioning the basic architecture. Difference analysis: Humans can detect system design flaws early and propose architectural solutions; AI relies on existing code patterns and may continue refactoring step by step without clear architectural guidance.
Iterative Repair Process of Website Deployment System Role Method Human Users executed scripts after AI repairs to verify results, discovered new issues through actual testing, and maintained system integrity throughout multi-phase repairs. Artificial Intelligence AI adopts a gradual repair strategy, solving only currently visible issues; multiple user feedbacks are needed for full stability across all edge cases. Difference analysis: User empirical testing ensures the completeness of repairs; AI’s initial solution addresses surface issues but deeper edge cases are discovered during actual execution.
Implementation Level Benchmark Publishing Strategy: Wrapper Page with Embedded iframe Role Method Human Users did not specify detailed implementation details; accepted the AI’s proposal using an iframe when Hugo path conflicts occurred. Artificial Intelligence Initially tried chapter-based publishing (content/benchmark/_index.md and static/benchmark/report.html), encountered Hugo rendering conflicts, then changed to a page+independent static directory model with an iframe. Difference analysis: AI explored multiple Hugo content model options (chapters, pages, static files) through trial and error; users trusted AI to find the correct Hugo model without proposing technical solutions in advance.
Limitations of Artificial Intelligence Key Limitations 1. Overwriting months of accumulated website/content history during first test environment synchronization- When fixing update.sh, all edge cases of the shell script were not anticipated, and multiple user testing feedback was required to resolve issues with no-change submission processing and sequential processing race conditions General limitations Three iterations were needed to diagnose Hugo/benchmark/render failures: initially thought to be a test path issue, then confusion between chapters and pages, and finally determined to be content issues caused by date:datetime.now() There was no active verification of Hugo’s URL case-insensitivity behavior, nor warnings about the impact of case sensitivity hosting; users had to discover the inconsistency between /bugJournal/ and /bugjournal/ on their own When resolving git merge conflicts, key code (theme-toggle and local custom settings) was correctly preserved, but this judgment depends on understanding the code functionality—complex scenarios may require manual review Lessons learned Key lessons learned For migrating from decentralized deployment targets to a centralized test directory, a guided migration strategy can be used: first run detection during migration from decentralized targets to the centralized test directory, and automatically reposition content (move existing websites to outputs/site), which avoids data loss and eliminates the manual effort before migration A three-layer approach is required when updating Hugo themes: ① integrity of the git repository (cleaning up damaged resource folder files), ② alignment of dependencies (compatibility between theme versions and Hugo versions), ③ saving local custom settings (manually resolving head.html and configuration overriding issues) Edge cases of Hugo content model: chapters with the same name (_index.md) conflict with static directories, leading to unclear paths; a single page(foo.md) is more suitable as wrapper content; future content will be automatically skipped if the –buildFuture flag is not used Principles of robustness for shell scripts: ① check git status before operations instead of relying on exit codes, ② add error handling for file system operations (use 2>/dev/null || true for expected failures), ③ explicitly exclude normal failures when using set -e Link or copy sync mode: when the file system supports hard links, os.link provides zero-copy atomic updates; automatic fallback to shirley.copytree ensures cross-platform compatibility (Windows FAT32, network drives) without manual intervention or user configuration Dialogue summary gadget/summarize ✅ Batch-generated historical weekly reports for W05-W12 19:30:00.000 | claude_code The dailySummary.py tool generated structured weekly reports for weeks 5 to 12 of 2026. The report covers MIHD spatial transcriptomics (STAIG alignment fix, scGPT fusion, Harmony experiments), error recovery benchmark tests (error injection framework, Mitai architecture), CalendarPro (intent classification upgrade), RoboBrain (task completion detection), Life Copilot (multi-intent restructuring), and the performance of Pi0.5 LoRA training on DCC, tianhe, MacBook, and TzJsDesktop devices. Progress of multiple high-density parallel projects is emphasized. ✅ Deployment blocking issues were resolved, and it was successfully deployed to GitHub Pages 20:55:34.064 | claude_code A build failure caused by an outdated PaperMod theme lacking the get-page-images section was diagnosed. The theme was updated to the latest version, the merge conflict in head.html was resolved, and local MathJax and checkboxes custom settings were preserved. Two stability issues in update.sh were fixed: the way no-change submissions are processed (added git diff –cached –quiet check) and the race condition in the find function (added 2>/dev/null || true statement). The entire deployment process was completed successfully, and it was deployed to GitHub Pages.
Small tool ✅ Reconstructed Hugo navigation structure and unified deployment architecture 01:21:42.819 | codex A layered bugJournal drop-down navigation based on a custom header section was implemented, along with daily/weekly/monthly submenus. Users suggested centralizing all tool outputs in the outputs/site staging directory to avoid inconsistency due to duplicate writing. The deployment logic for summarize, research, and test tools was refactored using the common.site_staging helper function; the website/sync_staging.py file was created, supporting link copying and Bootstrap migration features; a benchmark Hugo publishing layer wrapped with iframe was added; the build script was updated to ensure the staging directory is synchronized before Hugo build. Verification through Hugo build shows /benchmark/, /bugjournal/{daily,weekly,monthly/}, and /research/ are all displayed correctly. Issues such as Hugo URL case normalization, future content dates, and chapter/static path conflicts were resolved.
Token usage Total usage: $8.07 — 17 million tokens
summary: The batch generation of the W05-W12 historical weekly reports has been completed, and serious issues encountered during website deployment have been resolved (such as PaperMod theme updates and improvements to the reliability of the update.sh script). Meanwhile, the Hugo deployment architecture for Gadget has been refactored, with a unified output/site testing area, a drop-down navigation function for bugJournal, and a integrated benchmark report publishing mechanism.
title: Bug Journal 2026-03-22

content:
Daily Report — 2026-03-21 Daily Overview Completed work: Synchronized repository status via git and rclone, fixed a subprocess vulnerability in the summary tool, integrated the Codex usage tracking feature into the monthly report, upgraded the ECC plugin to use Opus 4.6 on all agents, and created detailed documentation. Execution methods: Used git conflict resolution with remote priority, fixed Windows paths via Path.as_posix(), added the –yes flag in npx subprocess calls, modified monthly_summary.py to summarize codex_token_usage separately, batch edited YAML files for 28 agents using sed, and created tutorials and contributor documents. Impact: Established a reliable data synchronization workflow between devices and cloud storage, eliminated suspended subprocess calls that hindered daily summary operations, enabling the monthly report to fully track Codex usage, improved AI inference quality through Opus 4.6 and effortLevel maximum values, and provided clear introductory materials for the ECC plugin system. Configured the development environment, fixed critical vulnerabilities in the summary process, integrated Codex support, and upgraded all AI agents to Opus 4.6.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ ECC Plugin Exploration and Configuration — Explored the Everything Claude Code plugin (28 agents, over 47 skills), upgraded all agents from sonnet/haiku to opus, changed effortLevel from “high” to “maximum”, and created detailed ECC_TUTORIAL.md. ✅ Fixed npx subprocess suspension issue — Found that npx without the –yes flag would cause the interactive prompt during subprocess execution to freeze, preventing the collection of token usage. The –yes flag was added to all three npx calls in daily_summary.py. ✅ Integrated Codex into the monthly summary process — Modified monthly_summary.py to separate codex_token_usage from token_usage, added combined_token_usage_summary for charts, updated format_monthly_markdown to display the Codex section, and updated all documents (README.md, summarize/README.md, AGENTS.md) to mention Codex support. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Rclone data synchronization setup — Created ~/.config/gadget/sync.json configuration file, extracted personal data from gdrive:gadget/ (12 directories), and used Path.as_posix() to fix Windows path errors in sync.py. ✅ Git repository synchronization and merge conflict resolution — Pulled the latest changes from origin/main, resolved 13 merge conflicts by accepting the remote version, and discarded local changes based on user preferences. ✅ Document updates (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md) — Added missing CLI parameters (–paper, –author-id, –homepage, –deploy) to research/CLAUDE.md; created AGENTS.md (395 words) containing project structure, commands, and conventions. ✅ PowerShell execution policy diagnosis — Found that the PowerShell execution policy blocked the npx/codex.ps1 wrapper program, providing a workaround using .cmd wrapper programs and Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. When calling npx @ccusage/codex@latest from a Python subprocess, it gets suspended indefinitely. Solution: Added the –yes flag to the npx call to skip the interactive “Are you sure? (y)” prompt, as capture_output=True in the subprocess execution cannot receive standard input.
Key insight: Subprocess executions with captureOutput=True have no standard input, so any interactive prompt will freeze permanently; always use –yes or -y flags for package managers in automated scripts.
2. Although Codex token usage is collected daily, the monthly summary does not summarize or display it. Solution: Added a separate summary path for codex_token_usage in aggregate_token_usage(), created combine_usage_summaries() for merging, and updated format_monthly_markdown() to display the Codex section.
Key insight: When adding a new data source to the summary process, not only must the input parsing be updated, but the summarization logic, LLM input cleaning (removing mechanical fields), and output format also need to be updated.
General Issues 3. Windows Path().parent produces backslashes, causing problems with rclone remote paths (e.g., ‘gdrive:gadget/website\personal’). Solution: Used Path.as_posix() to convert Windows paths to forward slashes for building rclone remote paths.
Key insight: Even on Windows, rclone remote paths must use forward slashes; when constructing remote URI, the Path operation requires explicit.as_posix() conversion.
4. The PowerShell execution policy blocks the npx and codex.ps1 wrapper programs. Solution: It is recommended to use .cmd wrapper programs (npx.cmd, codex.cmd) as a temporary solution, and use Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned for a permanent fix.
Key insight: On Windows, npm installations create both .cmd and .ps1 wrapper programs; when the PowerShell execution policy is restricted, .cmd wrappers can be used universally, while .ps1 wrappers require policy changes.
5. Git merge conflicts occur after pulling changes from remote. Solution: Use git stash, then git pull, and finally resolve the remaining conflicts by accepting the upstream version and discarding the stash.
Key insight: When syncing to remote after local cleanup, accepting the remote version with –theirs is simpler than manually resolving conflicts, especially if local changes are intended to be discarded.

Post-fusion Harmony alignment improved batch mixing metrics but reduced the quality of cross-sample expertise retrieval Solution: After analysis, it was concluded that Harmony’s linear correction cannot handle non-linear dimensional meanings, leading to inconsistency in independent training of each part. It is recommended to use Joint STAIG multi-part training in the next iteration.Key Insight: Batch correction methods like Harmony assume a linear offset, but this correction fails when embeddings trained independently have inaccurate dimension semantics—batch mixing and semantic alignment are distinct properties. Linear correction on individually trained embeddings cannot maintain semantic consistency across samples.
2. CalendarPro can only handle a single intent per message, thus losing subsequent operations, such as “scheduling a meeting at 3 PM and changing dinner time to 7 PM” Solution: The dual validation process for a single intent was replaced by the Claude CLI MultiIntentAnalyzer, which returns a list of intents. The _process_message_queue function was updated to loop through intents and combine responses. The 7-layer keyword coverage system was removed.
Key Insight: Single-intent classification is a fundamental architectural limitation, not a parsing issue. Keyword techniques (always generic, dependent on context, 7-layer coverage) are symptoms of chaotic abstraction levels. Switching to native multi-intent processing in LLMs can eliminate all heuristic methods.
3. MimicGen enhancement failed: pos_delta was calculated but never applied to action deformation, resulting in a success rate below 5% Solution: replay_with_warping was fixed—pos_delta was applied to warped_actions[:, :3] before adding noise, achieving correct object-centered trajectory transformation. The expected success rate is above 50% when there are D0 translation errors.
Key Insight: MimicGen enhancement requires actual coordinate transformation, not just noise injection. The path from 10 to 1000 depends on: 10 seeds × 200 targets × 50% success rate = 1000 demonstrations. Without pos_delta correction, the success rate drops sharply.
4. Yuke Zhu’s initial deep-width analysis using a single 5MB prompt (100 full papers) far exceeds the processing capacity of LLMs, leading to failure Solution: A three-layer solution was implemented: (1) a threshold of _MAX_PROMPT_CHARS=150K was added to automatically trigger segmentation; (2) a greedy algorithm grouped by year and segmented per paper was used to process papers within a year; (3) an LLM was used to combine 47 analyses into a complete report.
Key Insight: The key to ultra-large text analysis is “segmentation + semantic merging”: technically, dynamic segmentation can control the burden on a single LLM, while cognitively, it guides the LLM to extract consistency across paragraphs rather than simply connecting via merged prompts. 150K characters correspond to about 15–20 medium-length papers—this is the empirically optimal point.
5. The task completion model training stagnated with a loss of approximately 0.035, despite grad_norm=0.7–1.0 and a positive sample ratio of 4% and a negative sample ratio of 96% Solution: Positive sample weighting (pos_weight=10) was applied to the BCE loss to balance gradient contributions, effectively increasing the positive sample ratio from 4% to about 30%.
Key Insight: Under low loss conditions, a good positive sample recall rate in an imbalanced dataset does not guarantee success. Focusing only on gradient magnitude is misleading because negative samples dominate. Class imbalance requires explicit gradient balance.
6. CalendarPro returns a “no events today” query result immediately after creating an event, applicable for queries “this week” and “tomorrow” Solution: A three-layer solution was adopted: (1) query intent classification was added to BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT (not just INTENT_PROMPT_FRAGMENTS for multi_intent.py); (2)_handle_query() added keyword fallback detection to handle LLM failures; (3) get_today_events() was fixed to display already started events in get_today_events(); (4)_DPending_warnings was added for Discord error feedback.
Key Insight: INTENT_PROMPT_FRAGMENTS and BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT serve different code paths—main LLM classification uses BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT. Keyword fallback is a reliable LLM safety net. Past events must remain visible to prevent re-creation.
7. The code repository contains 8 fully implemented modules (about 2400 lines of code), all of which have comprehensive tests, but they are not imported at runtime, creating maintenance burden Solution: A systematic four-stage refactoring was adopted: (1) all import statements were mapped and isolated modules identified; (2) unused modules were archived with a README; (3) duplicate modules were merged into the specification location; (4) truly useless code was removed. All passed 373 tests.
Key Insight: For full implementations, archiving and removal should be used. Isolated but still usable code is saved in archive/ with relevant context for future integration. Audits found misconfigurations and import errors.

Due to always failing checks, duplicate dining events were repeatedly created (19 breakfast, 19 lunch, 18 dinner) Solution: The priority in _check_meal_exists was changed from start_time (displaying “08:00”) to start_iso field (ISO date and time). schedule_essentials function was changed to get_today_events(include_past=True) so already started dining events remain visible.
Key Insight: Field parsing order is crucial—ISO-form fields should always be processed first to avoid silent parsing failures. Past events must remain visible to prevent re-creation.
9. The finalization mechanism of the toolset caused a deadlock: historical log files with _finalized=False persisted permanently, making report._finalized never true, leading to sync-all continuously calling the LLM merge and wasting API costs Solution: The root cause was identified: a two-stage finalization mechanism (log + report) requires marking the report complete only after all source logs are finalized. Only when target_date != today() AND conversation_count unchanged does the export setting _finalized=True occur. The reason historical logs remain False is: (a) exported once only at target_date == today(), thus False; (b) after the first export, the number of conversations changes, resulting in False. _finalized flag is embedded in JSON content and synchronized via rclone. Solution: re-export on affected devices—since the date has passed and the number of conversations is stable, it will automatically be marked True. Another method is manually editing _finalized in JSON to True and uploading via rclone.
Key Insight: The two-stage finalization mechanism requires all source data to be finalized before the report is marked; _finalized flag in JSON content is synchronized via rclone to ensure cross-device consistency; however, historical False entries cause permanent deadlock. The core value is saving LLM API costs (merge stage), not rclone download time. Re-exporting via “data repair” respects the existing architecture better than “logical change,” which would disrupt consistency.
10. When using a block size of 60K for the first time, 100 papers were divided into 102 blocks (almost one paper per block), leading to excessive LLM calls and lack of context per paper Solution: The block size was increased from 60K to 150K, and the segmentation logic was adjusted to prioritize year integrity. The number of blocks was reduced from 102 to 47, significantly reducing LLM calls while preserving temporal context.
Key Insight: Segmentation granularity needs balance between “LLM processing capacity limits” and “semantic coherence”: too fine segmentation loses temporal relationships, while too coarse segmentation causes timeouts. 150K roughly corresponds to 15–20 medium-length papers—this is the empirically optimal point.
11. Confusion of researchers with the same name in academic databases: Semantic Scholar merged multiple researchers with the same name into a single entry, leading to misleading trajectory analysis (e.g., Yuke Zhu involves medical imaging, computer vision, and astrophysics—clearly different individuals) Solution: AI actively identifies confusion signals in analysis: large domain span, fragmented co-author networks, mismatch between citation counts and paper numbers. A warning is added at the beginning of the trajectory summary, suggesting manual splitting or paper-level analysis. For Yuke Zhu, based on institutional affiliation and research area consistency, it is distinguished from robot researchers at UT Austin/NVIDIA, researchers at Mybank Technology, mathematicians at Zhejiang University, and researchers at Ant Group.
Key Insight: The automated researcher profiling system must include multi-dimensional signal detection modules for the same name: co-author clustering, theme clustering, temporal continuity, and consistency in institutional affiliation. It cannot rely on the identity recognition features provided by the database.
12. Since _finalized defaults to True, old conversation logs were incorrectly skipped during export Solution: Line 1726 in daily_summary.py was changed from data.get('_finalized', True) to data.get('_finalized', False), and –force flag was added to explicitly control re-export.
Key Insight: Default values in data pipeline logic must be consistent with semantics: during export, missing _finalized should be treated as incomplete (False), while during merge, it can be treated as stable (True).
13. Multiple analysis failures due to LLM timeout (the initial 300 seconds is insufficient for 187K merged prompts, and 420 seconds is still insufficient) Solution: A dynamic timeout formula was designed: 300 + max(0, (len-50000) // 50000) * 120, i.e., 300 seconds as the base timeout, plus 120 seconds for each additional 50K characters. The final merge step was successfully completed within about 660 seconds of timeout.
Key Insight: Timeout design should be linearly related to data scale, not a fixed value: large models have relatively stable processing speed (about 200–300 characters per second). Estimating time based on prompt length plus 50% buffer is a reliable strategy.
14. Systematic unescaped quotes in the JSON fields of LLM-generated researcher profiles cause JSON parsing failure (over 12 errors) Solution: Special characters were identified in fields like trajectory_summary and breakthrough[].description, and manually escaped (e.g., “let the robot…” → “let the robot…”, single quotes in technical terms); for truncated JSON objects, missing right parentheses and array end symbols were added based on context.
Key Insight: LLM handling of embedded quotes is unstable when generating long JSON fields, especially in academic texts where terms are frequently referenced (e.g., “viewing while moving” becomes “viewing while moving”). Solutions include: (1) explicitly requiring escaping special characters in prompts; (2) setting a length limit for ultra-long text fields or using multi-round segmentation; (3) adding JSON pattern validation after generation to automatically fix common format errors.
15. Systematic format errors in LLM-generated long JSON outputs: truncation (especially in final fields), unescaped Chinese quotes (“”), missing closing brackets in nested structures, especially when including technical descriptions, Chinese text, and deep nesting (>3 levels) Solution: A four-stage repair process was implemented: (1) directly attempt json.loads; (2) extract ```json code blocks; (3) close unclosed structures based on depth matching; (4) use model upgrade (haiku → 14-line poem → long poem) to fix complex errors. A dedicated JSON repair prompt instructs AI to extract and fix JSON, returning only pure JSON without explanations. All failed cases are recorded in outputs/logs/json_repair_failed/ for pattern analysis and future optimization.
Key Insight: Long JSON generation in LLMs exhibits systematic failure patterns; even with the same prompt, differences exist between sessions (e.g., string escaping issues, truncation errors, nesting errors). A single repair strategy is insufficient; a layered fault tolerance mechanism is needed. Chinese quotes (“”) are semantically valid but must be converted to ASCII double quotes in JSON string values. Production systems should validate generated JSON and support automatic repair retries.
For high-volume researchers (over 130 papers), analyzing the entire corpus at once causes prompt length errors or insufficient depth. For the analysis of Yuke Zhu’s 206 papers, the error “too long prompt” occurred.Solution: Adopt an iterative analysis strategy segmented by year: Group papers by publication year, and analyze 1–3 representative papers per round to deeply explore their breakthroughs (description, why other methods were not used, impact, technical insights). While controlling the complexity of a single call, maintain the depth of analysis. Paper selection: based on year grouping + citation count ranking + identification of conference awards (best paper/highlight/focus/oral report identified by LLM), up to 10 papers per year can be analyzed. Key Insight: The analytical strategy segmented by year is superior to a one-time full corpus analysis (due to long prompts/insufficient analysis) or random sampling (which cannot capture temporal evolution). This strategy ensures both temporal integrity and paper quality. The “small but deep” iterative pattern is more suitable for academic analysis than the “large but superficial” one-time approach.
Repeating forward VLM prefix processing is required to complete the head reasoning (once in sample_actions, once in predict_task_completion) Solution: A sample_actions_with_completion() function was created, which captures the forward output of the first VLM and reuses it for completing the head, returning a tuple of (actions, completion_prob).
Key Insight: Process matching denoising consumes many resources, but unnecessary VLM forward processing increases measurable overhead. The unified method eliminates redundancy through minimal reconstruction.
Despite normal physical connection, the SpaceMouse device cannot be activated due to an exclusive driver lock Solution: The 3Dconnexion driver process was terminated, and the robosuite macros_private.py file was modified by setting SPACEMOUSE_PRODUCT_ID to 0xc63a to allow access to the physical device.
Key Insight: macOS system drivers can exclusively lock HID devices. Use the macros_private.py file override instead of modifying the main configuration file.
Daily report merging task: How to avoid copying all task items individually and instead create a comprehensive view Solution: Specific actions include: (1) merging similar tasks into one entry while retaining the latest status; (2) integrating human and AI analyses on the same theme; (3) merging multiple sessions within the same project into a single dialogue summary; (4) preserving high-impact content during deduplication. This requires the LLM to understand the causal relationships between tasks (e.g., “implementation of functionality” → “error correction” → “verification of fix” are considered different stages of the same work thread) as well as theme similarity.
Key Insight: Direct concatenation leads to information redundancy. Synthesis requires identifying causal relationships between tasks (sequential stages or true parallelism) and theme similarity (repeated debugging of the same module should be treated as a single task), rather than just string matching.
