The AI defaults to a technical overview, lacking historical insights, and requires structured prompts for guidance.
Determining error correction strategies: data repair or logic change Role Method Human The user identified the problem as a permanent historical error and advocated solving it by re-running the export on the affected device, rather than modifying the final logic of merge. This prevented the AI from trying to change the logic AI The AI initially proposed modifying the final logic of the merge stage (removing all_sources_finalized check) to solve the fundamental problem Difference Analysis: User method: “repair data” (re-exporting to automatically mark the correct flag while respecting the existing architecture). AI method: “change logic” (modifying code so merge no longer depends on the final state of source logs). The user prevented the AI from modifying and explicitly stated that just one export operation is sufficient to solve the problem.
Researchers’ analysis iterative strategy: multi-angle sampling to verify robustness Role Method Human The user selected to analyze the same researcher (Yuke Zhu) multiple times using subsets of papers from different years (2022/2023/2025/2026), implicitly testing whether the tool can infer global research directions from partial information AI The AI independently generated trajectory summaries and breakthroughs for each analysis, lacking consistency checks across analyses. It failed to explicitly express the inheritance relationship between papers from different periods Difference Analysis: The human implicitly tests the tool’s robustness through multiple sampling; the AI treats each analysis as an independent task without actively establishing a causal chain over time.
Reconstruction scope: cleaning of keyword logic Role Method Human When asked whether to clean up keywords hack now or later, the user chose “clean up together” and expanded the cleaning scope to handle cumulative technical debt AI The AI provided two options: minimal scope cleaning (only adding multi-intent) or expanded scope cleaning (including keyword hack) and offered trade-offs Difference Analysis: The human prioritizes thorough cleaning over incremental improvement. The user believes keyword hack is a code异味 that deserves fixing within the same time period.
Limitations of AI Key Limitation – Systematic format instability in generating long JSON: Even with the same prompt, different sessions produce different failure patterns (Chinese quotation marks mixed, truncation, nesting errors). Over 12 repair cycles are required in daily reports and research analyses, especially when containing a large amount of Chinese text, technical terms, and nested structures (>3 layers depth). No self-verification of JSON integrity is provided before output.- Without checking whether exploration is necessary, the resource-intensive Explore agent was deployed in an empty directory, wasting time until the user interrupted it. When the --force flag was added, the_finalization_default logic during export and merge stages was not reviewed; users had to discover semantic inconsistencies. The code library audit task was overly delegated to 3 parallel agents, although it requires overall architecture judgment. Users correctly recognized that this would分散 understanding, so they stopped delegating it. The risk of data pollution was not identified: initially, it was suggested to generate scenarios without training/test splits until the user explicitly requested separate directories. During the YuZhuYue analysis, the AI attempted 5 retries, adjusting parameters (block size, timeout formula) each time, but no optimal parameters could be predicted through a single analysis or reasoning, significantly prolonging the total time (about 2–3 hours). Due to prompt length limits, researcher data with a complete publication history (more than 200 papers) could not be processed. The YuZhuYue analysis failed because the “prompt was too long.” There is no built-in sampling or hierarchical analysis strategy for large corpora. Initially, researchers with the same name could not be detected autonomously through paper metadata alone. Users needed explicit labeling to distinguish different researchers with the same name. After the first correction, it was improved to actively flag cases of institution/field mismatch. In the daily report merging task, initially, listing all details was preferred instead of active synthesis. Users had to repeatedly emphasize “focus on synthesis and refinement, rather than verbatim copying” to trigger the integration logic, indicating a lack of awareness about the balance between readability and information density. When analyzing multiple papers by the same researcher, the temporal evolution between papers from different years was not identified. Each analysis was conducted independently, without a time-causal inference dimension. When analyzing academic papers, the focus was on describing “what was done” and “impact,” but to explore the historical dimension of “why it was previously impossible,” users needed explicit hints to deepen the analysis. By default, only technical summaries were provided, without historical insights. Initially, name conflicts among researchers could not be detected without clear hints, and a unified trajectory was generated for papers by different researchers until the user flagged field inconsistencies. The initial renaming plan only covered display names/code references, lacking the infrastructure layer (such as conda environments, folders, repositories, systemd). Manual correction was needed to expand the scope. The problem of poor performance efficiency was optimized: duplicate VLM forward passes were accepted as “acceptable overhead” without optimization until the user questioned the redundancy issue. Query intent classification was added to INTENT_PROMPT_FRAGMENTS (used only by multi_intent.py), instead of BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT (used by the main classification process), and the code path differences were not understood. When handling ultra-long text fields (e.g., the full trajectory summaries of 86 papers), truncation risks occurred, resulting in incomplete JSON objects (field_impact and other fields were truncated mid-way). There is no active output length monitoring or warning mechanism. The AI initially chose a block size of 60K (too conservative, leading to 102 blocks), and it failed to identify the implicit constraint of “a reasonable number of blocks” during attempts, requiring timeout failure feedback before adjusting to 150K. There is no prior reasoning about “the user expects a reasonable number of blocks (10–50).” When using the ‘from src.browser’ mode to search for modules, relative imports were not identified, and browser/ was mistakenly treated as dead code. The error was only discovered by directly checking executor.py. The implicit intent of the user could not be captured autonomously. Multiple rounds of analysis of the same researcher across different year subsets actually tested the tool’s paper selection ability, but the AI did not realize this validation purpose. The AI processed the gadget/summarize tools in batches, resulting in 4–5 failures due to API 32000 token output limits, but it did not actively detect output length restrictions or propose batch processing solutions, passively accepting the failure results. Self-generated JSON format errors could not be actively identified; human external verification (e.g., JSON parser) was needed to detect issues and provide feedback. There is no global progress tracking for batch tasks—it is impossible to actively tell users “N days of historical data remain to be processed” or the current completion percentage. Users must manually track task progress. The initially designed daily report tool was a single-layer end-to-end generation, lacking hierarchical aggregation (dialogue → device summary → daily report), until the user modified it with a recursive architecture. Batch correction methods such as Harmony can achieve global distribution mixing, but when embeddings generated independently have misaligned dimension meanings, semantic consistency cannot be maintained. Shared training or a base model is required. Batch mixing and semantic consistency are independent properties. MimicGen-style enhancement is essentially about coordinate transformation, not noise injection. pos_delta must be applied to the action trajectory (offset from source object to target object). Without this, the 10→1000 enhancement effect will fail due to a success rate below 5%. Ultra-large text analysis engineering paradigm: ① Automatic segmentation (150,000 characters, approximately the optimal granularity for 15–20 papers); ② Semantic merging (driven by LLM, not concatenation); ③ Dynamic timeout mechanism (linear adjustment based on prompt length, baseline of 300 seconds, +120 seconds per 50,000 characters); ④ Caching mechanism (to avoid retry costs). These four are key elements for deep wide mode availability. Multi-angle verification methods for academic trajectory analysis: Iterative analysis of subsets of papers by the same researcher over time (from 1 paper to 100 papers) allows constructing a holistic cognition from micro-level (in-depth analysis of individual representative works) to macro-level (description of complete publication list trajectories). Zhu YuZhe’s case shows: Visual Genome → Embodied AI (AI2-THOR) → RoboSuite/RoboTurk → Embodied AI driven by LLM (MineDojo/Voyager) → Clear evolutionary trajectory of geometric intermediate representations aligned with VLM. Only when a complete paper list is available can this entire trajectory be fully presented. Zhu YuZhe’s research trajectory shows an obvious evolution from “perception→control→infrastructure→open world”: from visual reinforcement learning in early 2012 to DreamDojo world model in 2026, the core proposition remains “enabling robots to efficiently learn from data and generalize to the real world.” This represents a development process from “data infrastructure builder” to “base model pioneer” and then to “world model architect.” A single intent classification is an architectural constraint that cannot be solved through keyword tricks. CalendarPro’s 7-layer keyword coverage system only addresses the symptom of lack of abstraction. Multi-intent LLM analysis eliminates the need for all heuristics. In binary classification, class imbalance requires explicit gradient balance. When 96% of samples belong to the same class, low overall loss may hide learning issues in minority classes. pos_weight can effectively rebalance gradient contributions. Key dimensions in analysis mode design: ① Data scale (papers/year); ② Analysis depth (summary vs. full text); ③ Computing cost (number of LLM calls). The five-mode system combines two boolean dimensions with a numerical dimension, covering the full range from “quick overview” to “in-depth exploration.” Basic elements of structured data generation prompt engineering: For fixed-mode JSON output, all required fields, their types (string/array/object), length limits, default values (placeholder text when no data), and special character escaping rules must be explicitly stated in the prompt. The evolution of the daily overview hierarchical format for the gadget summarize tool proves that relying solely on example reasoning cannot ensure consistent output; enumeration specifications must be used to clarify the generation logic for each field. The path toward building research infrastructure in the robotics learning field: Zhu YuZhe’s academic trajectory reveals an important pattern—field breakthroughs often accompany infrastructure work (e.g., AI2-THOR simulation environment, robosuite standard benchmarks, RoboTurk crowdsourcing platform, MineDojo internet-scale dataset). Although the citation counts of these works do not exceed those of algorithm innovation papers, their actual impact on field development may be greater. For any emerging research direction, establishing reproducible evaluation benchmarks and data collection tools is more strategic than publishing a single algorithm paper. The two-level finalization mechanism (log + report) requires all source logs to be finalized before marking the report; the _finalized flag in JSON content is synchronized via rclone to ensure consistency across devices; however, historical error entries cause permanent deadlocks. The real value lies in saving LLM API costs (merge stage), not rclone download time. The fix is to re-execute power-of-one operations (export) to automatically correct historical metadata while respecting the architectural design. Batch iterative workflows (processing daily reports day by day, analyzing academic data year by year) are more reliable than single batch processing, effectively avoiding JSON truncation and insufficient analysis depth issues. For the gadget tool, adding an automatic retry mechanism and JSON validation is very important. The ambiguity of same-name researchers in academic databases is a frequent and high-impact data quality problem in automated researcher profiling. Multi-dimensional signal-based name detection modules are necessary: co-author clustering, theme clustering, temporal continuity, and consistency in institutional affiliations. In machine learning workflows, the separation of training/validation data is non-negotiable. The validation set must not leak into the training set. Different data uses require different generation quotas and strategies. Even if a complete and tested implementation is achieved, archiving > deletion should be performed. The archive/ mode with a README retains options (for future re-integration), while cleaning up the active tree structure. Default values in data processing workflows must match the semantics of each stage: export (missing = incomplete → False) vs. merge (missing = stable → True). Subtle inconsistencies may lead to silent failures. The parsing order of date/time fields is crucial—ISO format fields (start_iso) should always be prioritized over display format strings (start_time ‘08:00), to avoid silent parsing failures due to broken existence checks. The daily report generation tool for gadget projects demonstrates strong information extraction and structuring capabilities in complex multi-device, multi-project, cross-time scenarios. It can accurately distinguish parallel work across devices, identify task causality, synthesize dialogue summaries, and verify production readiness. The research analyzer always recognizes Zhu YuZhe’s core research direction and methodological evolution in papers from different years, proving the tool’s academic trajectory extraction ability. Voyager (2023) demonstrated the paradigm of LLM as an autonomous agent: In Minecraft, the number of unique items increased 3.3 times, and the unlocking speed of the technical tree increased 15.3 times. Skills are stored in executable JS code instead of neural weights, avoiding catastrophic forgetting. Open X-Embodiment (2023): 22 robots, 21 institutions, 160,000 tasks demonstrated positive transfer between different embodiment styles, establishing an ImageNet-moment for robot data integration. The information density hierarchy of researcher profiles: First layer = h-index/citation count (quantitative metrics); second layer = list of representative works (enumerable facts); third layer = research trajectory narrative (requires LLM to extract implicit evolution logic). These three layers correspond to rapid/normal/deep output complexity. The fault tolerance mechanism for LLM-generated long-text JSON outputs requires multi-layer processing: direct parsing → code block extraction → bracket matching → LLM repair (model upgrade). A single strategy cannot cover all failure modes. All failures should be recorded for human review and further optimization. The breakthrough paper feature analysis framework (why → impact → technical insight) can effectively reveal the historical inevitability of technological innovation, field impact, and core insights, being more valuable than simple abstract summaries. Researchers’ analysis of papers should balance time completeness and quality. A three-tier mechanism combining year grouping, citation count ranking, and conference award recognition via LLM can balance foundational early work and recent前沿 breakthroughs within controllable computing costs. JSON system error patterns generated by LLM: Through more than 12 JSON repair tasks, unescaped citation errors mainly focus on: (1) academic term references (e.g., “visual understanding”); (2) mixed use of quotation marks in Chinese and Western contexts; (3) special symbols in technical terms (e.g., + in C++, σ_w² in mathematics). Solutions require multi-level protection: explicit requirement to follow escaping rules in the prompt, output format validation, and regular expression-based automatic pattern correction. Hierarchical analysis by year is better than processing the full text at once (too long/insufficient depth) or random sampling (missing time evolution). While maintaining temporal completeness, it ensures paper quality. For academic analysis, “small but deep” iterative patterns are more effective than “large but superficial” single-pass approaches. When implementing a repeated event scheduler, already-started events must be included in existence checks (include_past=True); otherwise, past events become invisible, and each cycle recreates them. In multi-component systems, it is necessary to understand where the prompt is actually used. INTENT_PROMPT_FRAGMENTS and BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT serve different code paths—main LLM classification uses BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, while multi_intent.py uses INTENT_PROMPT_FRAGMENTS. The workload of filling historical daily reports is high but valuable: Historical records over 30 days cover multiple projects on 4 devices, involving dozens of technical decisions and hundreds of task entries.Establishing a complete work record system is crucial for the subsequent monthly report generation and project review.- Code refactoring backward compatibility strategy: The default value is changed from fast to normal, but still falls back to fast from _dict (to protect old configuration file data); list expansion does not damage old configuration files; re-exporting the shim allows relevant parties to migrate without being aware. This “gradual evolution” approach is superior to “destructive rewrite”. Optimization of long-running task development experience: ① Caching mechanism makes retry costs controllable (47 chunks are fully cached, only the merge operation needs to be run again) ② Progress visibility (using tqdm+PYTHONUNBUFFERED) ③ Adaptive timeout formula (avoid manual parameter adjustment) ④ Parallel Agent handles independent sub-tasks (updates documents) The research toolkit consists of three independent tools (paper discovery, researcher analysis, citation graph analysis), all managed under the research_scout.py CLI. Researcher analysis uses citation counts and awards weights to select papers, instead of LLM scores. When refactoring the mode system, the existing sorting logic is preserved, and new dimensions (quantity, processing depth) are added as independent parameters. This minimizes risk and maintains predictable behavior. System import analysis (using grep to find patterns + verifying whether init.py exports) is crucial before declaring a module “dead”. Relative imports (..module) require a separate search pattern, while absolute imports (src.module) need a different search method. The keyword fallback mechanism is a reliable LLM safety net—even if the LLM cannot return structured data, routing can be done correctly by detecting keywords in the raw input. Project renaming requires a dual-layer approach: (1) Code/document (automated via search replacement), (2) Infrastructure (manual: conda, git, hosting, services). Checking both layers in advance avoids partial migration. Daily report synthesis “distillation” requires the LLM to understand causal relationships and inclusion relations of tasks. Treating “implementing features” → “fixing errors” → “verifying fixes” as different stages of the same work thread, rather than three independent tasks. This semantic relationship understanding ability is key to report readability. pip install -e . (editable mode) is the correct way to import shared toolkits into multi-tool projects, rather than using PYTHONPATH operations. For Python with a state system, hot reload is almost impossible (e.g., Discord bots with event loops, singleton caches, background schedulers). Process-level restart via watchfile is the viable solution. Practical Learning Robosuite provides official tools (input2action, inputUtils) that can correctly handle device→action conversion. Manual parsing of action_dict loses coordinate transformation and controller scaling information. Strengthening test infrastructure (pytest-timeout, @pytest.mark.external, skip logic) can prevent trivial tests from causing the entire suite to crash. This approach can be reused across different projects. Using max_per_year=0 as a sentinel value for “infinite papers” is clearer than a boolean flag or None, because zero is never an effective use case for paper limits. The Git rebase workflow (repository → pull –rebase → repository pop) can cleanly integrate divergent branches and independent changes, avoiding merge commit chaos. Dialogue Summary MIHD Spatial Transcriptomics ✅ Post-fusion harmony alignment experiments, strategic planning for ARI improvement and batch effect reduction, Claude code demo preparation 02:04:13.480 | claude_code The benchmark_rm_ideal.py file was modified, adding the –harmony flag for batch correction during post-fusion, processed between embedding loading and cross-sample evaluation. Experiments were conducted, comparing section 151508–151673 with and without Harmony. Main findings: Harmony improved the batch mixing metric by 36% (ASW_batch) and 32% (graph_connectivity), but reduced semantic alignment accuracy (Spearman r 0.189→0.023). The conclusion is that Harmony’s linear correction cannot handle the non-linear dimension misalignment caused by independent training per section. The next step suggests Joint STAIG multi-section training. Multi-agent exploration was initiated to diagnose the cluster ARI gap (0.475 vs SOTA 0.66+) and cross-sample batch effects, and a dual-track approach was decided. A comprehensive 30-minute Claude code demo for the Friday lab meeting was prepared, covering planning mode, permissions, CLAUDE.md rules, examples of AI overconfidence using DLPFC spatial data, and the complete demo materials and presentation script.
Error Recovery (Algorithms and Benchmarks) ✅ Environment setup, optimization of task completion model training, comprehensive recovery collection refactoring, training scenario generation, MimicGen deformation error fixing 04:16:46.552 | claude_code Using the mujoco/robosuite stack in a conda environment, recovery_collect was set up. The error in EnvWrapper.env was fixed. The locking issue of the SpaceMouse device was resolved by terminating the 3Dconnexion driver and configuring product_id=0xc63a. Device connection was successful, but only 11/29 error types could generate scenarios. Training stagnation was diagnosed (loss ≈ 0.035, positive samples 4%), and a weighted BCE loss with pos_weight=10 was implemented to balance gradients. The predict_task_completion inference method was added, optimized by creating sample_actions_with_completion to reuse VLM prefix features and avoid redundant forward propagation. Major refactoring included: fixing SpaceMouse initialization issues (removing environment parameters, using input2action), adding rendering support, and implementing dynamic PROJECT_ROOT resolution. A portable deployment package was created (from 171MB to 252MB after compression), including setup/run scripts and tutorials, and all 139 unit tests passed. generate_training_scenes.py was implemented to generate exactly 10 scenarios per task×sub-type, with amplitudes evenly distributed between 0.0 and 1.0. The ControlledRng class was created to make the uniform() function deterministic (based on fractional interpolation) while keeping the randn() function random, to increase directional diversity. In-depth technical discussion clarified the data collection architecture: collect 5–10 examples/sub-types, no failed examples, start with 1–2 tasks. It was found that RecoverySegmenter is suitable for Phoenix MCM/MPM (not MimicGen). Key errors were identified: pos_delta was calculated in _replay_with_warping but never applied. Deformation issues were fixed, resulting in 1000 enhanced examples with 10 seeds×200 targets×50% success rate. Three data pools were defined: training set (10), enhancement set (200), evaluation set (over 100).
CalendarPro/Life Copilot ✅ Complete system refactoring: multi-intent classifier, calendar query fix, code library audit and second-stage cleanup, duplicate meal issue fix, project renaming, development mode implementation, test suite optimization 00:53:36.473 | claude_code The complete refactoring of the intent classification system was completed. The Claude CLI MultiIntentAnalyzer replaced double verification and 7-layer keyword techniques, supporting multi-intent decomposition. The MultiIntentAnalyzer class was created with a 4-stage JSON parsing function, the MultiIntentResult/AnalysisContext model was added, the always_general_keywords and context_dependent_keywords collections were removed, and process_input was simplified from 7 steps to 4. Errors in the CLI were fixed. Weekly query support was added. 30 new tests were written, and all 424 tests passed. Users identified fundamental limitations (double verification returns only one intent, complex messages lose subsequent actions). The existing architecture was studied, the 7-layer keyword technique was identified, and a dual-layer solution was designed. A comprehensive implementation plan was formulated. dev.py was implemented, using watchfiles to monitor src/*.py files and multiprocessing.spawn for clean process isolation. The --dev flag was added. debounce, grace period, and ignore filters were configured. pytest tests/hung indefinitely. pytest-timeout dependencies were added, with a global timeout of 30 seconds, external service tests marked with @pytest.mark.external, and skipif was used for automatic detection. Typer CLI functions were renamed to avoid collection. Now all 399 tests pass in 40 seconds. The 29K-line code was systematically mapped using grep/glob/read tools, distributed across over 90 files (executed directly after the user rejects proxy delegation). 8 isolated modules (≈2400 lines of code), a duplicate parse_datetime_with_timezone function, broken broker_models.py, 3 isolated configuration settings, and a damaged browser_service import were identified. A detailed phased refactoring plan was generated. All 4 phases were implemented: 8 source modules + 9 test files + check_skills_status.py were archived, and related content was explained in the README; the duplicate parse_datetime_with_timezone was merged; broker_models.py and 3 isolated configuration settings were removed; the damaged browser import was fixed. Verified through 373 tests. CLAUDE.md was updated. Users reported 19 duplicate Breakfast events, 19 Lunch events, 18 Dinner events. The root cause was diagnosed: _check_meal_exists uses a display-format time string but fails with fromisoformat(), while schedule_essentials excludes past events. Both errors were fixed, a cleanup script was created, 53 duplicates were removed, and tests passed. Users requested a renaming plan, then interrupted work to expand the scope, including conda environment, folder, repository, and Discord application. The code library was re-studied, approximately 62 lines of modifications were made in 15 files (code, documentation, scripts, configuration), and a 6-item manual checklist was provided. Users executed init to trigger CLAUDE.md improvements. 4 new architecture modules were added, and multiple details were corrected. Then users reported calendar query errors (queries for this week/next day always return “no events today”). A three-layer solution was used for repair: guidance on Query Classification was added to BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, keyword fallback was added to handle_query(), inclusion of past parameters was added to get_today_events(), and a Discord error feedback mechanism was added. All tests passed, and documentation and functionality were improved.
gadget (Summary + Research Tools) ✅ Comprehensive knowledge management infrastructure expansion: Upgrade of the 5-mode research tool system, including chunked long-text analysis function, full academic trajectory analysis by Yuke Zhu (over 10 iterations, 100 papers), batch historical daily report integration (over 30 dates), finalization of mechanism failure diagnosis scheme, JSON repair process _04:10:40.556 | claude_code_When running the daily_summary.py export file, users encountered the 'ModuleNotFoundError: common' error. Upon diagnosis, the relevant package was missing, so the packages were installed in editable mode using 'pip install -e .'. The date information of 23 conversation logs was successfully exported. It was found that the 'finalized default=True' option was used during the export phase (line 1726), causing old logs to be incorrectly skipped. The default setting for export was changed to False, and the --force flag was added to provide clearer control. A forced export operation was performed for 17 dates, and all data were successfully uploaded to rclone. The local and remote gadget repositories were synchronized using git stash, rebase, and push workflows. Using the gadget/summarize tool in daily_summary.py, approximately 30 historical conversation logs from February to mid-March 2026 were processed in large batches. These include work records for multiple devices (DCC/MacBook/TzJsDesktop/tianhe) and multiple projects (MIHD, error-recovery-benchmark, CalendarPro, Desktop Video, gadget). Each generated report includes structured daily_overview (global and device-level information), tasks, issues and solutions, comparisons between humans and AI, limitations of AI, lessons learned, and conversation summaries. Twelve JSON format errors were identified, requiring specialized repair work. A deadlock issue was detected in the finalization mechanism: three device-date combinations had permanently 'finalized=False', preventing report completion and causing an infinite loop-like LLM API cost problem. The solution is to re-run the export operation or manually edit the JSON file. A (finalized) suffix was added to the export output to make diagnosing issues clearer. The user provided a detailed implementation plan, aiming to expand the mode from 2 to 5 (fast/regular/in-depth/wide/wide-in-depth), and added automatic splitting and merging functions for the wide and wide-in-depth modes. AI modified 7 source files (adding MODE_CONFIG and chunking logic to analysis.py, adding TRAJECTORY_MERGE_PROMPT to prompts.py, and updating options in cli.py/research_scout.py/config.py/models.py), and modified 3 documentation files. A dynamic timeout formula (300 seconds + 120 seconds/50K characters) and a 150K characters/block splitting algorithm were implemented. The Yuke Zhu deep-wide analysis was successfully completed: 100 full-text papers were retrieved from ArXiv, automatically split into 47 time blocks, analyzed via LLM for each block, and finally merged into a complete trajectory report (including 7 breakthroughs, evolution of research themes, mentor relationships, etc.). After 5 iterations of optimization, a complete academic figure report was generated. A comprehensive academic analysis of Yuke Zhu was conducted, involving over 10 iterations, analyzing 18 to 100 representative papers, covering Visual Genome (2016), robomimic/MAPLE (2021), CDL/MineDojo/VIMA (2022), Voyager/S3O/LIBERO (2023), DexMimicGen/Sirius-Fleet/PRESTO/LongVILA (2024), and DEAS/Cosmos-Predict2.5/QLIP/ASAP/GraspMolmo/DreamDojo (2025-2026). Each analysis generated a detailed trajectory summary, including dimensions such as why, impact, and technical insights, research themes, methodological evolution, and domain impact. It was found that Yuke Zhu’s research evolved from “data infrastructure builder” (robosuite/ROBOMIMIC) to “basic model pioneer” (MineDojo/VIMA/Voyager), and then to “world model architect” (Cosmos/DreamDojo). Researchers with the same name were actively detected and marked. There were 9 JSON repair cycles due to truncated or malformed output. An attempt was made to perform a full analysis on all 206 papers, but it failed due to the error “prompt too long”, confirming the necessity of an annual stratified sampling strategy. The user ran the run/init commands to verify the accuracy of research/CLAUDE.md. The assistant identified two minor errors and fixed them. Subsequently, the user proposed expanding the researcher analysis mode from 2 to 5 and adjusting the limits and processing depth for each paper. After clarifying that paper selection should be based on citation counts and awards, the assistant developed an implementation plan, including modifications to analysis.py, cli.py, and prompts.py. Approximately 16 historical dates were processed in batches, generating structured daily reports from 2026-02-08 to 2026-03-17. Malformed JSON files generated by LLM, including truncated content, unclosed quotes, unescaped Chinese quotes, and missing closing parentheses, were fixed. A four-stage repair process was applied. research/CLAUDE.md (6 modifications), research/TUTORIAL.md (4 modifications), and parent CLAUDE.md (1 modification) were updated, while all mode descriptions, example commands, and parameter tables were kept consistent with the code via parallel proxies.

content:
Daily Report — 2026-03-18 Daily Overview Completed work: Expanded the intent classification system in CalendarPro by adding a new BATCH_UPDATE intent to handle users’ multi-task status reports. Implementation: Semantic routing was implemented in 8 files, keyword scoring used 21 expressions, LLM prompt snippets with completion verb detection and calendar integration handlers were included. Impact: Resolved a severe user experience issue where users couldn’t efficiently report multiple task statuses simultaneously, eliminating the “I don’t understand” fallback response during batch updates. The BATCH_UPDATE intent was added to CalendarPro to handle multi-task status reports, and comprehensive test coverage and documentation updates were performed.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Implement BATCH_UPDATE intent functionality — New intent types were added in 8 files: enumeration definitions, semantic routing (21 expressions), keyword scorer enhanced with 2+ completion verbs, LLM prompt snippets containing update array patterns, context assembly mapping, double verification default responses, discord_bot handler with task-level calendar operations, and improved GENERAL fallback mechanism. ✅ Diagnose failure in batch update classification — 3 parallel exploration agents were launched to understand the intent routing system (24 types), task completion processing, and general intent protection mechanisms. The root cause was found to be the absence of BATCH_UPDATE intent; semantic router score was approximately 0.20 while the threshold should be 0.50. The LLM classifier defaults to GENERAL, and clarifying the type triggers a fixed “I don’t understand” template. ✅ Develop implementation plan for batch update functionality — A comprehensive 8-step implementation plan covering intent type enumeration, semantic routing, keyword patterns, LLM prompts, context assembly, double verification default values, discord_bot handler with calendar integration, improved GENERAL fallback mechanism, routing JSON generation, and test suite was designed. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Create comprehensive test suite for BATCH_UPDATE — 21 tests were created covering keyword scoring, enumeration, handlers (completion/cancel/rearrange/notes/multi-task/null/permissions), routing registration, context mapping, prompt snippets, and double verification default responses. All tests passed, with no regressions in the 72 test suites. ✅ Update CLAUDE.md documentation — CLAUDE.md was rewritten to highlight unclear architectural details: redundant file list was removed, “Common multi-file changes” section was added, step-by-step guide for adding AI provider/intent/service/event was provided, isolation of singleton tests was recorded, and architectural patterns were integrated. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. Robots cannot classify multi-task status updates (e.g., “A is completed, B is also solved, C needs time adjustment”), and even with substantial user input, they fallback to “I don’t understand”. Solution: BATCHUPDATE intent was added, including semantic routing (21 expressions), enhanced keyword scorer for 2+ completion verbs, LLM prompt snippets for learning update array patterns, and handlers for searching calendar, deleting completed tasks, rearranging/receiving notes for other tasks, recording completion status, and sending EventBus events. Additionally, the GENERAL fallback mechanism was improved, using substantive LLM responses instead of discarding them.
Key Insight: Intent classification failures usually stem from three issues: (1) absence of enumeration members, (2) lack of semantic routing examples, and (3) absence of LLM prompt snippets. Solving these three issues plus keyword scoring can create strong classification capability. The GENERAL fallback mechanism should retain useful LLM responses rather than blindly using templates.
2. Semantic router scores for batch updates are approximately 0.20, below the 0.50 threshold, resulting in LOW_CONFIDENCE classification. Solution: BATCHUPDATE_ROUTE entries with multiple Chinese/English expressions (“A is completed, B is also done”, “Tasks A and B are completed, C needs rearrangement”) were created, and a keyword scoring rule was added: 2+ different completion keywords → increased score by 0.30 to capture batch update features.
Key Insight: Embedding-based semantic routing cannot recognize multi-entity status patterns. Explicit keyword counting (2+ completion verbs) is a simple but effective batch detection heuristic that can complement embedding similarity.
3. The LLM classifier does not allow use of batch_update intent; it defaults to GENERAL with type clarification, triggering a fixed “I don’t understand” template and discarding useful AI-generated responses. Solution: BATCHUPDATE intent was added to INTENT_PROMPT_FRAGMENTS, including update array patterns (task name, operation, note, new time), and added to the allowed intent list in build_prompt(). The GENERAL handler was improved to check whether replies with type clarification contain substantive LLM content (>20 characters, not template phrases), and it is used instead of the fixed template.
Key Insight: Fallback templates should be a last resort rather than a default option. When the LLM generates substantive responses, even if the confidence is low, they should be retained. Template overriding wastes the LLM’s reasoning ability and leads to worse user experience.
Human and AI Approaches Strategic Level Diagnosis Strategy for Batch Update Failures Role Method Human The user provided a real Discord conversation failure case (“Hello → robot replies with task summary → user provides batch status info → robot says I don’t understand”), and asked “How should we solve this problem?”. Specific symptoms were given, but no diagnostic method was specified. AI Claude launched 3 parallel exploration agents to systematically understand: 1) all 24 intent types and routes, 2) task completion processing, 3) general intent protection mechanisms. Then key files were read to verify details, and the Plan agent transformed findings into an implementation plan. Analysis of Differences: Humans provided “what” (symptoms) and “why we care” (user experience issues), but did not provide “how to investigate”. AI adopted a parallel exploration approach based on agents rather than sequential file reading, showing strategic use of sub-agents for extensive discovery. Humans might adopt a more linear “read this file, then that file” method.
Implementation Method for BATCHUPDATE Functionality Role Method Human Before requesting Claude to execute, the user provided a fully structured 8-step implementation plan, including exact file paths, line numbers, code snippets, data patterns, and test requirements. AI Claude strictly followed the plan, read files in parallel, edited sequentially where dependencies existed, re-generated derived data (route JSON), and wrote comprehensive tests. Analysis of Differences: Humans designed the architecture upfront and specified specific changes; AI executed the plan as a reliable executor. This indicates that humans act as “architects” while AI acts as “builders”, which is highly efficient for complex multi-file changes since humans have already thought through the system.
Limitations of AI General Limitation — In test_batch_update.py, Claude initially tried to import the DiscordBot class, causing an import error, and then switched to testing the handler separately. The import structure should be checked first or a better simulation mode should be used. During the first attempt to run all test suites, Claude used pytest tests/ -v --timeout=30 -x, but failed due to the lack of pytest-timeout plugin. Therefore, only some tests were run instead of installing the plugin or removing the initial flag setting. Learning Outcomes Key Learnings Multi-layer intent classification requires collaborative updates across 8+ files: enumeration file (models.py), semantic routing file (intent_routes.py), keyword scorer (keyword_scorer.py), LLM prompt file (prompts.py), context assembly file (context_assembler.py), double verification default (dual_verify.py), handler and route files (discord_bot.py), and derived data (route JSON). Missing any layer leads to classification failure. Parallel agent exploration (3 agents for intent routing, task processing, and overall protection) is more efficient than sequential file reading, suitable for complex diagnostic tasks. Each agent provides a focused perspective, ultimately leading to a complete understanding. Fallback templates in AI systems should retain useful LLM-generated content rather than blindly replacing them. Before replacing hardcoded fallback content, check whether the LLM response contains substantive content (>20 characters, not template phrases). Keyword scoring can capture patterns that embedding similarity cannot detect: 2+ different completion verbs is a simple batch update heuristic that can complement semantic routing. In neural systems, explicit pattern detection remains valuable. Practical Learnings When implementing the user-provided plan, parallel reading all affected files first instead of one by one helps understand dependencies and enables Claude to edit files more efficiently in batches. Conversation Summary ✅ Implement BATCHUPDATE intent to handle multi-task status reports 23:05:55.704 | claude_code The user provided an 8-step implementation plan requesting the addition of BATCHUPDATE intent in the CalendarPro classification system. Claude executed the plan: enumeration members were added, semantic routing with 21 statements, keyword scorer enhanced with 2+ completion verbs, LLM prompt snippets, context assembly mapping, double verification default values, discord_bot handler with calendar operations, and improved GENERAL fallback content to retain useful LLM responses. 21 test cases were written to cover all components; all tests passed, with no regressions. The route JSON containing 25 routes was regenerated.
✅ Diagnose why robots fail in batch status updates 22:35:46.066 | claude_code The user demonstrated a real Discord failure case: the robot cannot understand multi-task status updates (“A is viewed, B and C are solved”), and the robot responds with “I don’t understand”. Claude invested maximum effort by launching 3 parallel exploration agents to handle the intent system (24 types), task processing, and overall protection. Key files were read to verify details. The Plan agent integrated findings into a root cause: absence of BATCHUPDATE intent, low semantic router score (approximately 0.20), default use of GENERAL for clarification by the LLM, triggering a hardcoded template. An 8-step implementation plan was created and saved in the .claude/plans/ directory. This plan was executed in the first session.
