Daily Report — 2026-03-13 Daily Overview Completed work: Two independent systems were developed: (1) An analysis toolkit for academic researchers in robotics/VLA, including ArXiv/Semantic Scholar integration, LLM trajectory analysis, and student discovery features; (2) A frame-by-frame variable collection system to track progress of RoboTwin control tasks and target poses. Implementation method: The research tool is implemented via modular Python packages, including multi-stage JSON parsing, SHA-256 disk caching, and a year-based paper selection function; RoboTwin replaces pickle files after trajectory completion through post-processing procedures, adding new variables. Impact: The research tool enables researchers to understand how pioneers in robotics can make breakthroughs through recursive student discovery; the RoboTwin system provides richer training signals for VLA models, allowing them to learn control progress and predict end-effector poses. MacBook Completed work: A complete Gadget research tool was implemented (15 modules, over 2000 lines of code), critical errors in JSON parsing and paper selection logic were fixed, and detailed analysis was performed on Levine/Abbeel trajectories. Implementation method: An API layer (ArXiv HTML/PDF extraction, Semantic Scholar metrics), a prompt layer (Chinese output templates), a BFS-recursive analysis scheduler, a scoring algorithm, and a CLI supporting sub-commands for analysis/display/listing/configuration were created. Impact: The tool now supports quick mode (only summary) and detailed mode (full text download), year-level paper selection (≤10 papers per year), LLM award recognition, and generation of JSON and Markdown reports with bilingual support. tianhe Completed work: A new variable collection system for RoboTwin Place Dual Shoes task was designed and implemented: the critical_region variable was removed, and 5 new frame-by-frame variables were added (manip_progress_time, manip_progress_distance_left/right, target_endpose, target_joint). Implementation method: Code library analysis was performed using Explore and Plan agents; the post-processing procedure was implemented by overriding the move() method to track EE positions and modify pkl files; behavior of the base class was debugged, and a progress value clipping function was added. Impact: The data collection functionality was successfully extended without modifying the base task architecture or disrupting the existing pkl to hdf5 conversion process, enabling VLA models to learn richer control signals. An analysis toolkit for academic researchers driven by LLM was built, along with a frame-by-frame control progress tracking system for RoboTwin Place Dual Shoes task.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Build an academic researcher analysis tool — A complete Python package was created, including ArXiv/Semantic Scholar integration, LLM trajectory analysis, award recognition, student discovery, and a CLI interface. ✅ Add target_endpose and target_joint prediction variables — The final 7D end pose (xyz + quat) and joint angles are recorded when move() is completed, serving as frame-by-frame labels for VLA target prediction. ✅ Fix JSON parsing cascading errors — The parse_json_response was refactored using a cascade chain from Haiku→Sonnet→Opus; failed responses were saved to disk to prevent infinite recursion via the _try_parse_json helper function. ✅ Implement year-based paper selection and award priority ranking — Year-level grouping replaced the single-reference ranking (≤10 papers per year); rankings were based on award weights (best_paper=4, highlight=3, spotlight=2, oral=1), ordered chronologically. ✅ Analyze Sergey Levine and Pieter Abbeel’s trajectories — Detailed academic trajectory analysis was generated for the two robotics pioneers; breakthrough achievements (TRPO, MAML, SAC, DDPM, Decision Transformer) were identified, along with explanations of why they succeeded while others failed. ✅ Add manip_progress_distance_left/right tracking — The value 1 - |current_pos - final_pos| / |start_pos - final_pos| for both arms was calculated; np.clip was used to limit the result to [0,1] to handle curved trajectories. ✅ Add LLM-based award recognition — A new analysis stage was implemented to identify best papers/highlights/spotlight/oral awards using LLM from paper titles, journals, and years. ✅ Add manip_progress_time tracking — Linear interpolation from 0 to 1 was implemented in the move() call. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Create documentation (tutorial.md, CLAUDE.md) — Comprehensive Chinese tutorials covering installation, usage, analysis modes, student discovery, scoring system, etc. were written, preparing for future AI applications. ✅ Fix paper download scope issues in detailed mode — The download scope was changed from only 10 most cited papers to full texts of all filtered papers (limited to ≤10 per year by the selection logic). ✅ Fix issue where critical_region still appears in HDF5 output — pkl_data.pop(‘critical_region’, None) was added in the post-processing stage, after unconditional writing of this key by the base class get_obs(). ✅ Fix uncertainty in Semantic Scholar log messages — The log message ‘[S2] 获取论文: 1736651’ was changed to ‘[S2] 获取作者1736651的论文…’ to avoid misinterpreting author ID as the number of papers. ✅ Fix negative progress_distance values issue — After users reported negative values during actual data execution, np.clip(progress_dist, 0.0, 1.0) was applied. ✅ Remove critical_region variable from Place Dual Shoes task — The override of get_critical_region_label() was deleted, and the key was removed from the base class get_obs() after pkl post-processing. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. When Haiku repair fails, JSON parsing crashes, causing loss of original LLM response and inability to debug. Solution: A cascading repair chain (Haiku→Sonnet→Opus) was implemented; _try_parse_json helper function was used to avoid recursion, and failed responses were saved to output/logs/json_repair_failed/.txt for debugging.
Key insight: When using LLM-based repairs, pure parsing logic (_try_parse_json) and repair logic (parse_json_response) must be separated so the original output can be retained in case of total failure.
2. ArXiv only returns the last 100 papers, while Semantic Scholar has 500 papers with citation data, but the merging logic discards S2 papers without ArXiv matches, causing most historically high-impact works to be lost. Solution: The priority of data sources was reversed: S2 became the primary source (with year/citation/journal/abstract), ArXiv was supplemented via arxiv_id/pdf_url/categories, and then the lone ArXiv paper was added. As a result, a comprehensive Timeline coverage was achieved.
Key insight: When merging datasets with different biases (ArXiv = latest, S2 = comprehensive), the more complete data source should be used as the basis, and information should be supplemented from professional sources, not the other way around.
3. Papers sorted only by citation count lose time research trajectories, making it impossible to understand changes in researchers’ research focus at different career stages. Solution: Year-level grouping was implemented: papers were grouped by year and ranked by award weight and citation count within the year; ≤10 works per year were selected, and they were presented chronologically. While preserving the narrative of works, the best works from each period were highlighted.
Key insight: For longitudinal analysis, the time structure is often more valuable than global rankings; stratifying by year allows both dimensions to be considered simultaneously.
4. Collected data contain negative manip_progress_distance_left/right values and values greater than 1. Solution: np.clip(progress_dist, 0.0, 1.0) was applied to limit left/right progress distances within the valid [0,1] range.
Key insight: Curved robot trajectories may cause the current EE position to temporarily exceed the distance from start to target during interpolation, breaking the assumption of 1 - |current-final|/|start-final|. For progress metrics, setting clear boundaries is necessary.
5. ArXiv and Semantic Scholar APIs cannot provide award data (best paper, highlight, etc.), but this is crucial for identifying breakthrough works. Solution: Users suggested using LLM training data: paper titles and conference locations were sent to the LLM to recall known awards. This approach was implemented as a new analysis stage with a separate caching mechanism.
Key insight: LLMs can serve as auxiliary knowledge bases to obtain data that APIs cannot provide, especially well-known but unstructured metadata such as conference awards.
6. Even after removing the override method, critical_region still appears in HDF5 files. Solution: Analysis of base class base_task.py:510 revealed that get_obs() unconditionally writes pkl_dic[‘critical_region’]. A post-processing step was added to remove this key from the repaired pickle file.
Key insight: Removing the override only changes the return value; the path of the base class code must be tracked to ensure the key is truly removed from the output. Post-processing the pickle file before conversion to HDF5 can effectively remove unnecessary keys.
Common Issues 7. Log message ‘[S2] 获取论文: 1736651’ is ambiguous — it seems that 173,300 papers were obtained, but actually it is the author ID. Users immediately identified this issue. Solution: It was changed to ‘[S2] 获取作者1736651的论文…’ and ‘[S2] 作者1736651: 获取到500篇论文’. A clear subject-verb-object structure eliminated ambiguity.
Key insight: Log messages must be clear even when read in irrelevant contexts. Numbers should always have a clear label to indicate their semantic type.
8. Detailed mode only downloads the top 10 most cited papers, but after year-level grouping, there are already ≤10 papers per year — all papers should be analyzed in detailed mode. Solution: The ‘sorted(…, reverse=True)[:10]’ filter was removed, and ‘papers_for_download = [p for p in papers if p.arxiv_id]’ was used. Now all filtered papers’ full texts are downloaded.
Key insight: When quality thresholds are enforced upstream by selection logic, downstream should not use different standards for re-filtering — this leads to inconsistency between modes.
Human and Artificial Intelligence Approaches Strategic Level Award Data Source Strategy Role Method Human Users suggested “first download paper titles, then let Claude search whether it is a highlight” — directly using LLM as a knowledge base. AI AI initially focused on API-based solutions, seeking structured award datasets or information from conference websites. Artificial Intelligence Claude removed the coverage method and assumed that the default behavior of the base class (returning 0) is sufficient; the execution path of get_obs() in the base class was not tracked during the initial implementation. Difference Analysis: The human verifies the effectiveness of the removal operation through empirical testing; artificial intelligence relies on static code analysis and misses the unconditional writing operations in the base class. The user’s black-box testing method discovers issues ignored by the artificial intelligence white-box analysis.
Upgrade and fallback in error handling Role Method Human The user specified “if haiku cannot be fixed, use sonnet; if still failed, use opus; if still failed, write logs to file” — with a clear upgrade chain and terminal failure handling mechanism. Artificial Intelligence Artificial intelligence initially implemented a single-stage fix (using only haiku) and returns when it fails early, treating the fix as a binary operation. Difference Analysis: The human adopts a cost-increasing retry strategy (from cheap to expensive, then abandonment), which is common in production systems but not evident in prototype code. This indicates that failure modes are considered at the operational level.
Handling edge cases of progress_distance Role Method Human The user noticed negative values in the actual data and requested clear limits to the [0,1] range based on the semantic meaning of “progress”. Artificial Intelligence Claude initially implemented the mathematical formula 1 - Difference Analysis: The human reasons from the semantic perspective of data (progress must be limited) and observes failure cases; artificial intelligence focuses on the correctness of the formula and does not consider physical edge cases such as non-linear trajectories. The user’s domain knowledge about operational progress drives the solution proposal.
Implementation Level Recognizing ambiguity in log messages Role Method Human The user immediately realized that “get paper: 1736651” might be misunderstood as the number of papers rather than the author ID, and discovered an UX issue without testing. Artificial Intelligence Artificial intelligence writes log messages that focus on technical accuracy (recordings of author IDs), but does not consider potential ambiguity in isolated numeric IDs. Difference Analysis: The human instinctively reads logs from the reader’s perspective (what does this mean?), while artificial intelligence focuses on the completeness of information from the author’s perspective (does it contain the required data?). UX requires reader-centered design.
Limitations of Artificial Intelligence Key Limitation – Using a smaller dataset (ArXiv 100 latest) as the base for merging, rather than a comprehensive dataset (S2 500 historical data), emphasizes algorithm simplicity over semantic completeness in trajectory analysis Static code analysis is insufficient to track data flow: Claude removed the coverage method for get_critical_region_label(), but cannot track the unconditional writing of pkl_dic[‘critical_region’] by the base class get_obs(), requiring user testing at runtime to detect this issue. The traditional data pipeline approach (API extraction, structured datasets) was initially used to obtain award information, ignoring the fact that LLMs already “know” the awards of famous conferences from training data. A single-stage LLM fix mechanism was implemented (only for haiku), rather than a multi-stage upgrade mechanism, treating error recovery as a binary issue rather than a progressive cost-benefit issue. Lack of physical reasoning about edge cases: no expectation was made that curved robot trajectories may cause progress_distance to exceed [0,1], so geometric constraints of the trajectory were not considered in the formula implementation. Over-reliance on method inheritance logic: it was assumed that removing the coverage method would remove variables from the output, but all code paths that write data structures were not verified. Experience testing is needed to discover the unconditional writing behavior of the base class. General Limitations Failure to anticipate ambiguity in log messages: the string ‘[S2] Get paper: 1736651’ was written, but the ambiguity of naked numbers for readers was not considered. Users need to correct it to make the subject-verb-object structure clearer. No active verification that the paper selection logic in the detailed mode matches the annual stratification selection — allowing a upper limit of ≤10 years, but downloading summaries of the top ten globally is inconsistent. Learning Outcomes Key Learning Points For researcher trajectory analysis, maintaining the time structure (annual stratification sampling) is more valuable than global citation rankings. This indicates that sampling strategies specific to a particular field are more important than the general “sort by metric” approach. For the post-processing method of “future dependency” variables: when each frame variable needs to understand the state of move(), it is usually recorded that the frame number was taken, and then the pickle file is repaired after move() is completed. This is simpler than using a complex state machine during frame capture. LLMs can serve as a knowledge base for unstructured metadata (conference awards, paper reputations) when APIs cannot provide this information. This “LLM as auxiliary database” pattern has not been fully utilized yet — prompt design skills are needed, but no additional infrastructure is required. When implementing LLM-based fixes in recursive parsing logic, the non-LLM stage must be extracted to avoid infinite loops. The pattern is: _try_parse (pure) and parse_response (with fix). Merging multi-source data: when sources have different biases (latestness and comprehensiveness), the most complete data should be used as the base, and supplemented from professional fields. ArXiv = latest, S2 = historical → S2 as base, ArXiv for supplementation. Error recovery should implement a cost-increasing upgrade mechanism (cheap model → expensive model → manual intervention via logs), rather than binary failure/success. This maximizes automatic recovery efficiency while retaining debugging information. Base class data flow requires deep tracking: in a complex object-oriented hierarchy with data collection per frame, removing the coverage method may not remove variables from the output. The execution path of the base class (e.g., get_obs() → _take_picture() → pkl file) must be tracked to ensure variables are truly excluded. Physical quantities require mandatory semantic ranges: progress indicators derived from geometric formulas should be clearly limited within their semantic range [0,1], even if the formula theoretically produces valid values, because real-world trajectories introduce edge cases. Practical Learning Outcomes ArXiv’s HTML rendering is now more suitable than PDF for full-text extraction: faster, without OCR errors, and preserves structure. For pre-Html papers, PDF is a alternative option. This indicates that infrastructure evolution requires regular re-examination of “best practices”. Numerical logs without semantic tags produce ambiguity: ‘1736651’ may be a count/ID/size. Always use clear labels: ‘Author 1736651’ or ‘1,736,651 papers’. The extra two words cost little, but can avoid entire category interpretation errors. For academic analysis tools, the narrative part prefers Chinese output, while technical terms prefer English output. Dual-language method: write structure in English (breakthroughs, why not before, impact), and explain in Chinese. When there is upstream selection logic (annual stratification → ≤10 years), downstream stages should not use different standards for re-filtering. This leads to inconsistent patterns (fast mode sees papers different from detailed mode). Multi-agent exploration pattern: use Explore agent to understand the code library → use Plan agent for design → implement sequentially through user verification. This clearly separates concerns and allows review of the plan before execution. Daily Report — 2026-03-12 Daily Overview What was done: Cross-platformly resolved technical issues for 3 independent projects: upgrade of the sandbox permission architecture for macOS wallpaper apps, optimization of the GPU monitoring tool output, and repair of the dependency chain in the deep learning evaluation environment. How it was done: Identified macOS TCC permission mechanism issues through system-level log analysis, tracked ABI compatibility in the PyTorch ecosystem via dependency version matrix, and resolved the C++ extension local compilation environment using CUDA toolchain configuration. Impact: macOS applications now have production-level file access persistence capability; two research projects on the tianhe server have returned to operational status (although the checkpoint path issue has not been fully resolved). MacBook What was done: Completed sandbox migration and permission system refactoring for desktop-video applications, and fixed a critical bug where historical records cannot open old files. How it was done: Enabled App Sandbox to make security-scoped bookmarks effective, repaired the bookmark parsing fallback logic, and added an NSOpenPanel reauthorization mechanism. Impact: The user history feature is now fully restored; the app adheres to macOS best practices, paving the way for App Store submission. tianhe What was done: Resolved PyTorch environment dependency conflicts in the RoboTwin project, fixed the curobo compilation issue, and improved the readability of the GPU monitoring tool. How it was done: Matched torch/torchvision via pip version matrix, configured the CUDA toolchain path (CUDA_HOME and CPATH) in the conda environment, and rewritten the process aggregation logic to limit output width. Impact: The robot policy evaluation environment has mostly returned to normal operation; GPU resource monitoring is more efficient, but the checkpoint path mapping issue remains unresolved. Fixed the sandbox permission architecture of the macOS wallpaper app and resolved PyTorch dependency chain and CUDA compilation issues in the deep learning evaluation environment
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Fixed the inability to open old videos in historical records of the macOS wallpaper app — enabled App Sandbox, repaired bookmark parsing logic (added non-scoped fallback), added a permission error retry mechanism (NSOpenPanel reauthorization), and updated localization and ChangeLog. ✅ Resolved the torch/torchvision version conflict in the RoboTwin evaluation environment — upgraded torchvision from 0.21.0 to 0.22.1+cu126 to match torch 2.7.1, and fixed the failure to register torchvision::nms operators. ✅ Recompiled curobo to match the current PyTorch ABI — removed old.so files, installed ninja, set CUDA_HOME and CPATH, and recompiled from source using pip install -e . ❌ Resolved the checkpoint path missing issue in RoboTwin — the eval.sh parameter specifies checkpoint_id=5000, but only 15000/25000/29999 entries exist in the directory. Analyzing the parameter mapping logic interrupted sessions. Implementation & Fixes 🔄 Optimized the output format of the GPU monitoring tool — limited width to 80 columns, removed duplicate processes, and filtered noise sub-processes. The user pointed out that understanding errors would interrupt sessions. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. macOS non-sandbox applications cannot persist file access permissions; old videos in historical records report Operation not permitted error Solution: Enable App Sandbox permissions (com.apple.security.app-sandbox and files.user-selected.read-write), fix ensureFileAccess to add non-scoped bookmark fallback parsing, and add NSOpenPanel reauthorization mechanism to showVideo/showImage.
Key Insight: The macOS TCC mechanism requires App Sandbox to create security-scoped bookmarks. Non-scoped bookmarks can only parse URLs but do not grant access permissions, resulting in inability to open old files. A combination of sandbox + downgrade path is required.
2. Incompatibility between torch 2.7.1 and torchvision 0.21.0 ABI causes failure to register torchvision::nms operators Solution: Upgrade torchvision to 0.22.1+cu126 to match torch 2.7.1.
Key Insight: Custom operators in torchvision are linked to the C++ API of torch during compilation; version mismatch leads to invalid operator registration interface. torchvision 0.21.0 corresponds to torch 2.6.x and cannot be used with torch 2.7.x.
3. Pre-compiled .so files of curobo are incompatible with the current PyTorch ABI; JIT compilation fails to find cuda_runtime.h Solution: Remove old.so files, install ninja compiler tools, set CUDA_HOME=/path/to/conda/env and CPATH=/path/to/targets/x86_64-linux/include, and recompile using pip install -e .
Key Insight: C++ extensions require recompilation after PyTorch version upgrade. The nvidia package installed via conda in the environment places CUDA headers in non-standard paths (targets/x86_64-linux/include/), and environment variables need to be correctly configured for JIT compilation to find them.
General Issues 4. The GPU monitoring tool output has excessive width and duplicate process displays, making it difficult to read Solution: Limit output to 80 columns, aggregate GPUs per process, and filter noise sub-processes such as multiprocessing workers.
Key Insight: The original implementation grouped by GPU caused a multi-card process to appear repeatedly across multiple GPUs. Aggregation per process and display of all used card numbers in the GPU column are needed.
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Deep explanation of macOS file permission issues Role Approach Human Directly asks ‘Why is there insufficient permission?’ and requests AI to explain the underlying principles of TCC and sandbox mechanisms AI Provides technical solutions but does not actively explain background principles; human follow-up is required for a complete context Difference Analysis: Human problem-oriented thinking guides AI to give a more complete background explanation rather than directly jumping to solutions. Humans focus on ‘why’, while AI focuses on ‘how’.
Selection strategy for repair solutions Role Approach Human Explicitly chooses a defensive approach (sandbox + NSOpenPanel reauthorization) AI Provides two independent options (sandbox or reauthorization) but does not suggest a combination. Difference Analysis: Humans prefer defensive programming (multiple layers of protection), while AI tends to favor a single optimal solution. Human combined strategies address both root causes and provide a downgrade path, making them more robust.
Implementation Level Understanding of the GPU monitoring tool requirement Role Approach Human Corrects ’each process appears once per GPU’ instead of ’each process appears once’ and emphasizes the many-to-many relationship AI Misunderstands the requirement, aggregates multi-GPU processes into a single line, and displays card numbers separated by commas in the GPU column. Difference Analysis: Humans accurately understand the multi-to-many relationship display requirement; AI’s over-optimization causes information loss (resource usage of a process on GPU0 and GPU1 should be displayed in two lines).
AI Limitations General Limitations Failed to actively explain technical background (macOS TCC/sandbox mechanisms); human follow-up is required for a complete context. AI should explain ‘why’ when proposing solutions. Misunderstood the GPU monitoring requirement, simplifying the multi-to-many relationship into a one-to-many aggregation, leading to information loss. Inaccurate understanding of visualization needs for complex data relationships. When analyzing checkpoint path issues, started overly detailed code analysis (continuous Read operations) without first confirming the problem scope with the user. High-level parameter mapping logic should be understood first. Learnings Key Learnings macOS TCC permission mechanism: Non-sandbox applications cannot create security-scoped bookmarks; only non-scoped bookmarks (only parsing URLs without access permissions) can be created, causing historical file access to fail after app restart. App Sandbox must be enabled to persist file access permissions. PyTorch C++ extension ABI compatibility: Custom operators in torchvision (e.g., torchvision::nms) are linked to the C++ API of torch during compilation; versions must match exactly (torchvision 0.21→torch 2.6, torchvision 0.22→torch 2.7). Version mismatch leads to operator registration failure. Conda environment CUDA toolchain configuration: The nvidia package installed via pip places CUDA headers in targets/x86_64-linux/include/ instead of standard include/ paths. JIT compilation of C++ extensions requires setting CUDA_HOME to point to the conda env and CPATH to include the targets path. Defensive programming principle: A combination of sandbox + reauthorization is more robust than a single solution. Sandbox addresses the root cause (persistent permissions), NSOpenPanel provides a downgrade path (temporary authorization), and their combination ensures users can always access files. Conversation Summaries Desktop Video ✅ Fixed the permission issue preventing opening old videos in historical records 07:52:05.359 | claude_code The user reported that old videos cannot be opened in historical records (Operation not permitted Code=257). Log analysis revealed that the app did not enable sandbox, causing failure to create security-scoped bookmark; ensureFileAccess only tried with .withSecurityScope parsing, resulting in permanent non-scoped bookmark failure, and finally macOS TCC denied access. Three-layer fixes were implemented: enable App Sandbox permissions, fix bookmark parsing by adding non-scoped fallback, and add NSOpenPanel reauthorization mechanism to showVideo/showImage. Code modifications, localization updates, and ChangeLog were completed; build verification passed.
robobrain GPU monitor 🔄 Optimized the output format of the GPU monitoring tool 15:48:28.705 | claude_code The user requested limiting the output width of gpumon.py to 80 columns and removing duplicate processes. AI rewrote the process table logic, aggregating each process into a single line, displaying card numbers separated by commas in the GPU column, and filtering out noise sub-processes such as multiprocessing workers. The user corrected their understanding: it should be ’each process appears once per GPU’ rather than aggregated display, causing session interruption.
RoboTwin Policy Evaluation**🔄 Dependency conflicts causing the failed execution of eval.sh diagnosis** 02:23:18.758 | claude_code The user encountered an error when running bash eval.sh; the AI identified three types of dependency issues: 1) torch 2.7.1 does not match torchvision 0.21.0, resulting in failure to register the torchvision::nms operator; 2) curobo pre-compiled.so is incompatible with torch ABI, and JIT compilation lacks ninja; 3) the checkpoint path does not exist (the parameter specifies 5000, but only 15000/25000/29999 exists). The AI provided a version upgrade solution, and the user chose to upgrade torchvision.
🔄 Fixed dependencies and resolved subsequent compilation issues 02:34:02.614 | claude_code Implementation of fix plan: successfully upgraded torchvision to 0.22.1+cu126 and verified compatibility with torch 2.7.1; installed ninja compilation tool; after removing the old.so file, recompiled curobo by configuring CUDA_HOME and CPATH (pointing to conda env’s targets/x86_64-linux/include/); verified that curobo is properly imported. After re-running eval.sh, the issue of missing checkpoint path occurred again, and the AI started analyzing the parameter mapping logic in deploy_policy.yml and eval_policy.py, causing the session to be interrupted.
