Daily Report — 2026-03-09 Daily Overview Completed Work: Parallel progress on five major directions across three devices: (1) Development of core algorithms for MIHD spatial transcriptomics project (cross-sample structure evaluation + cross-modal enhancement architecture), (2) Development of VLA/robotics learning system (documentation, data pipeline, theoretical analysis), (3) Transformation of gadget tool architecture (CLI → MCP server), (4) Cross-project integration (CalendarPro automated workflow), (5) Enhancement of research tools (multi-data source + production-level logs) Implementation Methods: Establishment of spatial structure evaluation benchmarks using WWL graph kernel, design of cross-attention mechanism based on spatial neighborhoods (and resolution of CUDA hardware compatibility issues), systematic literature review for foundation model performance, creation of MCP protocol wrapper layer and tool exposure, cross-environment invocation via conda subprocess, expansion of research_scout to three academic data sources (arXiv/bioRxiv/PubMed), establishment of production-level log system Impact: Establishment of reusable cross-sample spatial evaluation toolchain and cross-modal enhancement methods, key discovery that scGPT foundation model is inferior to traditional methods, enabling gadget tools to be discovered and used by all AI agents, implementation of CalendarPro automated daily research and summarization workflow, expansion of research coverage from a single arXiv source to three academic sources and establishment of a complete error tracking mechanism DCC Completed Work: Full process work for MIHD spatial transcriptomics project: cross-sample RM-IDEAL experiments and visualization (151673-151508/151676), design and implementation of CrossModalEnhancer (including multiple rounds of CUDA debugging), maintenance of CLAUDE.md, literature review on scGPT Implementation Methods: Running large-scale experiments in HPC environment (3639 spots), use of conda environment management + multiple rounds of CUDA error debugging (final solution: mini-batch workaround and CPU training fallback), parallel web search and WebFetch to obtain benchmark data, generation of spatial heatmap visualizations Impact: Production of complete cross-sample evaluation report (7 spatial heatmaps + Chinese technical documentation), delivery of functional CrossModalEnhancer module (integrated into Fusion.py), key insights on scGPT performance (zero-shot inferior to traditional methods), identification of PyTorch CUDA version compatibility issues and establishment of CPU training fallback process TzJsDesktop Completed Work: Full-stack integration and tool enhancement work: creation of workspace documentation (5 projects), implementation of gadget MCP server (9 tools), CalendarPro-gadget integration bridge (13 tests), enhancement of research_scout (log system + multi-data sources, 500+ lines of new code), documentation maintenance updates Implementation Methods: Use of parallel agent orchestration for code library exploration, systematic file-by-file implementation and validation at each stage, integration across repos via subprocess isolation, comprehensive testing (import checks, CLI verification, log file verification), implementation of zero-dependency API client using urllib.request Impact: Establishment of a unified development environment and clear documentation, enabling gadget tools to be accessed by all AI agents in the workspace, implementation of CalendarPro automated daily research workflow, transformation of research_scout from a single arXiv source to a three-source system with production-level observability, maintenance of synchronization between all tool documentation and code tianhe Completed Work: Promotion of multiple VLA/robotics projects: creation of UniVLA documentation, troubleshooting of CALVIN environment, data conversion from RoboTwin → LeRobot, theoretical analysis of Pi0 flow matching Implementation Methods: Creation of comprehensive CLAUDE.md (build/test commands, architecture overview), diagnosis of DNS parsing failures (Kubernetes environment), implementation of convert_robotwin_democlean_to_lerobot.py (14-DOF, 50 episodes, 11,459 frames), detailed explanation of conditional flow matching (Beta(1.5,1) time sampling + Euler integration) Impact: Establishment of documentation standards for complex VLA code libraries, support for re-use of demo_clean data in pi0.5 training, clarification of flow matching implementation details for robot action generation Completion of core MIHD spatial transcriptomics functions (cross-sample RM-IDEAL evaluation, CrossModalEnhancer cross-modal enhancement, scGPT literature review), advancement of multiple VLA/robotics projects (UniVLA documentation, RoboTwin data conversion, flow matching analysis), MCP serverization of gadget tools and integration with CalendarPro, enhancement of research_scout multi-data source support
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Run 151673-151508 cross-sample RM-IDEAL benchmark — Execute the benchmark to compare the similarity of spatial niche structures between two DLPFC parts, using PCA+UNI2+STAIG_fusion to embed vectors. Generate detailed correlation metrics (Spearman ρ) for all 7 organizational levels. ✅ Implement CrossModalEnhancer module — Creation of a model containing CrossModalAttentionBlock and CrossModalEnhancer classes/CrossModalEnhancer.py (≈350 lines), supporting 3 modes (gene→image, image→gene, bidirectional). Integrated into the Fusion.py scheduler. ✅ Debug CUDA/cuBLAS compatibility issues — Resolution of the vulnerability in PyTorch 2.9/CUDA 12.9 cuBLAS on RTX 2080 Ti, which causes crashes during large matrix operations. Final solution: use mini-batch (512 samples) InfoNCE loss to avoid N×N full matrix backpropagation. ✅ Study scGPT clustering benchmark literature — Systematic web search and literature extraction to evaluate scGPT and scGPT-space clustering performance. Found that zero-shot scGPT performance is lower than traditional methods (PCA, scVI), while scGPT-space clustering lacks independent SOTA comparisons. ✅ Create CLAUDE.md documentation for UniVLA repository — Provide detailed documentation covering build commands (torchrun, accelerate), linting (black/ruff), training phases (LAM, VLA pre-training, fine-tuning), evaluation (LIBERO, CALVIN, R2R, SimplerEnv) and architecture overview (VLM→PrismaticVLM→OpenVLA, visual/LLM backbone, action segmentation, draccus configuration, RLDS process). ✅ Refactor MCP tools to return content — Modified 5 MCP tools (summarize_export/merge, research_report, benchmark_run/report) to return complete content (markdown/JSON) and allow parameter selection for saving, bypassing cmd_* wrappers to control file I/O. ✅ Convert gadget tools to MCP server — Created mcp_server.py, exposing 9 tools (summarize_export/merge/list_dates, research_search/report/list_projects, benchmark_run/report/system_info), and implementing stdout capture and SystemExit handling. ✅ Integrate gadget tools into CalendarPro — Built an external tool integration layer (src/tools/), implemented asynchronous subprocess execution via conda run, implemented ResearchScoutTool and DailySummaryTool, created a background service with cron scheduling functionality, and wrote 13 unit tests. ✅ Add bioRxiv and PubMed support to research_scout — Implemented search_biorxiv() and search_pubmed(), using urllib.request (no additional dependencies), added multi-source coordination, expanded CLI features, added –source flag, and retained paper_id/arxiv_id handling, ensuring backward compatibility. ✅ Generate RM-IDEAL spatial heatmap visualization — Modified _viz_rm_ideal.py script to generate 7 PNG files (one for each niche label), showing true values, RM-IDEAL scores, and similarity of embedded vectors, applicable to 151673↔151508 data. ✅ Write comprehensive cross-sample patch query documentation (Chinese) — Created docs/CROSS_SAMPLE_PATCH_QUERY_REPORT.md, including complete methodology (WWL graph kernel, Wasserstein distance, dual-path evaluation), code paths, data flow, result analysis, and reproducibility guidelines. ❌ Use STAIG fusion for MIHD cross-sample patch visualization — Implemented patch query visualization using UNI2+PCA+STAIG_fusion to embed vectors for 151673→151676. However, due to GPU CUDA compatibility issues (PyTorch 2.9.0+cu129 and CUDA 13.1 driver incompatibility), the visualization function was interrupted. CPU training was used as a temporary solution. ✅ Convert RoboTwin demo_clean to LeRobot format — Created convert_robotwin_democlean_to_lerobot.py script, converting 50 episodes (11,459 frames) from demo_clean (14-DOF HDF5 format) into LeRobot dataset structure, saved in RoboTwin/data/place_dual_shoes_lerobot. ✅ Add logging system to research_scout — Implemented RotatingFileHandler (5MB, 3 backups), migrating approximately 77 print statements to logger, adding empty field and zero-score warnings, enhancing error handling for API calls and cache operations. ✅ Design CrossModalEnhancer architecture — Designed the cross-modal enhancement module using spatial k-NN neighbors as K/V sequences to avoid degradation of single-mark attention mechanism. Designed symmetric InfoNCE loss and residual connection. ✅ Analyze Pi0 flow matching implementation — Explained conditional flow matching in pi0.py: linear interpolation path x_t = t·noise + (1-t)·actions, Beta(1.5,1) time sampling, MSE loss ‖v_t - u_t‖², using Euler method to sample 10 steps from t=1→0. ✅ Analyze CALVIN training data flow — Detailed explanation of how finetune_calvin.py loads auto_lang_ann.npy and episode_*.npz files via DiskCalvinDataset, extracts rgb_static/rel_actions/robot_obs, and processes through LAM encoder and ActionDecoder. Implementation and Fixes - ✅ Create CALVIN dataset extraction script — Created extract_eval_files.py to extract only necessary evaluation files from the complete dataset (validation/.hydra/merged_config.yaml, metadata), reducing dataset size from 1.3GB to 600KB.- ✅ Created a CLAUDE.md document at the workspace level — Analyzed 5 independent projects (CalendarPro, OCR, gadget, get-shit-done, openclaw), and created a unified CLAUDE.md document containing quick-reference commands and architectural highlights. ✅ Updated the CLAUDE.md document for research_scout.py — Identified and recorded functions that were previously unrecorded: author search (–author flag, search_arxiv_author), init –from-overview (project creation based on LLM), and increased the line count from approximately 2500 lines to about 2650 lines, adding a caching mode for author search. ✅ Updated the CLAUDE.md document containing cross-modal and RM-IDEAL content — Added CrossModalEnhancer to the core module, added the RM-IDEAL benchmark command to common commands, added references to cross-sample documents, and enriched the description of utils (rm_ideal.py, niche_utils.py). ✅ Simplified the CLAUDE.md module list — Compressed the architecture section of each module from about 30 lines to about 10 lines, focusing on unobvious module relationships. All key architectural patterns were retained. ❌ Resolved the CALVIN environment installation issue — Diagnosed DNS resolution failure (Errno -3), causing pip to cannot access pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn or pypi.org. A proxy configuration (http_proxy=localhost:9997) was found, but the problem was not solved. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. A vulnerability in PyTorch 2.9/CUDA 12.9 cuBLAS on RTX 2080 Ti causes crashes during the backpropagation of large matrix operations (the comparison loss requires 3639×3639 logical labels). Multiple architectural rewrites were attempted before finding the root cause. Solution: Redesigned the comparison loss function, using small batch sampling (512 samples per batch) to avoid full N×N matrix calculations. Added gradient clipping and LayerNorm to improve stability. For cross-sample visualization tasks, when GPU compatibility is confirmed, switching to CPU training as a fallback (PyTorch 2.9.0+cu129 with CUDA 13.1 driver).
Key Insight: Model architecture alone cannot resolve GPU hardware/driver compatibility issues—algorithmic workaround measures at the loss function level are required. Mismatches between PyTorch CUDA versions and driver versions occasionally cause “illegal memory access” errors, which can be detected by basic tests but fail in complex training loops. For medium-scale training (3460 positions), using CPU as a fallback is an effective strategy.
2. Corrupted MCP server stdout: The gadget tool uses too much print(), but MCP uses stdout as a JSON-RPC transmission method. Solution: Created a capture_stdout() context manager to redirect print() output, wrapping all tool calls in _safe_call(), capturing stdout/stderr and converting SystemExit to RuntimeError, returning the captured logs to the _logs field of the JSON response.
Key Insight: Isolating stdout is important when integrating existing CLI tools into protocol-based systems. The context manager provides a clean, recoverable redirect method without modifying the original code.
3. research_scout hardcodes arxiv_id throughout the code repository, hindering multi-source data expansion. Solution: Introduced paper_id as a canonical ID with a source field, keeping arxiv_id as a backward-compatible alias, created _paper_id()/_paper_url() helper functions, updated prompts to use paper_id, and checking both fields when matching LLM responses.
Key Insight: When expanding from single-source data to multi-source data, introducing a new abstraction level while keeping old fields as aliases. The helper functions centralize the logic for IDs/URLs, making future data source addition simple.
4. In the 151673-151508 cross-sample query, Layer_3 has low relevance (ρ=-0.21/-0.36), while Layer_1/4/5 show high positive relevance (ρ>0.4). Solution: Analysis shows that Layer_3 is the largest DLPFC layer with high internal heterogeneity, preventing embeddings from capturing a unified spatial structure. Smaller and well-defined layers (Layer_1: ρ=0.62, Layer_4: ρ=0.66) perform best.
Key Insight: The size and internal heterogeneity of organizational layers significantly affect the quality of spatial structure embeddings. Different layers with clear boundaries achieve better cross-sample matching than large heterogeneous regions.
5. When each point has only one gene vector and one image vector, single-label cross-attention degrades to a linear projection. Solution: Used spatial k-NN neighbors to build K/V sequences, allowing cross-attention to operate in a neighborhood context. Reused the batch-neighbor construction infrastructure of QFormerFusion.
Key Insight: Spatial transcriptomics data provide natural sequence context through neighborhood structures. Utilizing spatial adjacency allows meaningful attention mechanisms to be implemented even without time or batch dimensions.
6. RoboTwin demo_clean data (14-DOF, based on directory) is incompatible with the existing LeRobot conversion script (16-DOF, based on zip). Solution: Created a new script convert_robotwin_democlean_to_lerobot.py: directly reads data from the data/instruction directory, changes ACTION_DIM/STATE_DIM to 14, uses LeRobotDataset.create() and passes the root parameter, instead of using the HF_LEROBOT_HOME environment variable for modification.
Key Insight: Changes in robot data format (number of DOF, storage format) require specialized conversion scripts. Directory structure and HDF5 key names are project-specific.
7. Due to JSON parsing failures in LLMs, the motivation/innovation fields in research_scout’s filtering stage are empty. Solution: Added a empty field detection function after _screen_papers() and _screen_papers_chunked(), recorded warning messages including the number and detailed information for each paper at DEBUG level, improved _try_repair_result() function, and recorded a preview of the original response when fixing fails.
Key Insight: The silent.get() fallback mechanism hides data quality issues. Clear validation and logging at the aggregation point (after batch processing) can provide useful debugging information without complicating the logic of each project.
8. The original CrossModalEnhancer design triggers cuBLAS GEMM failures during the projection from 128→1536 when outputting the original modality dimension (image is 1536d). Solution: Redesigned the architecture to output in the hidden dimension space (128d), avoiding the problem of large matrix projections. Used a projection head in the comparison loss while maintaining the compactness of the core output.
Key Insight: Engineering constraints (GPU errors) may force architectural decisions different from ideal semantic designs. Real systems must balance theoretical elegance and implementation robustness.
General Issues 9. The FastMCP constructor rejects the ‘version’ parameter in the user conda environment. Solution: Used inspect.signature() to check the actual constructor, removed the version parameter, and passed only ’name’ and ‘instructions’, letting the mcp library handle version management internally. Key Insight: SDK API evolves continuously. When integration issues occur, check the actual signature rather than relying on documentation or assumptions. The FastMCP API in the mcp library changes between different versions.
10. The CLAUDE.md document is outdated—lacks author search functionality, init –from-overview, and incorrect line count statistics. Solution: Systematically searched the code repository using Grep to find unrecorded functions (such as search_arxiv_author, create_project_from_overview), verified line counts with wc -l, and made 6 targeted modifications to the document sections to update the content (instructions, code organization, key implementation details, file layout).
Key Insight: In actively developed tools, document evolution is inevitable; systematic code searching (using grep for patterns like –author, –from-overview) is more reliable than manual review.
11. DNS resolution failure in Kubernetes Pod causes pip to cannot access PyPI images. Solution: Diagnosed that the issue lies with domain server 10.96.0.10 and proxy localhost:9997, but the problem remains—possibly a cluster-level network configuration issue.
Key Insight: Kubernetes cluster DNS and出口 proxy configurations may disrupt standard pip workflows. Cluster administrators may need to intervene or use cached wheel packages.
12. An “unrecognized parameter” error occurs when using –no-banner with conda run on user conda versions. Solution: Completely removed the –no-banner flag. conda run works without this flag, and the banner output is sent to stderr (does not damage stdout). Testing confirmed that conda run -n calendarpro python -c ‘print(test)’ can run normally.
Key Insight: If certain optional flags introduce compatibility issues, they should be omitted because they do not have functional requirements. Banners in stderr do not affect the stdout-based protocol.
Human and Artificial Intelligence Approaches Strategic Level MCP Tool Design Philosophy Role Method Human Summarization/research is considered “Claude code enhancement skills”—it should return content, not just write files. Explicitly reflect it as an architectural principle. Artificial Intelligence Initially implemented tools as file writes with metadata returns, without considering usage patterns in context. Analysis of Differences: Human users understand tool-assisted interaction models and expect specific workflow patterns. AI initially implemented tools as scripts with metadata returns, without considering integration context.
CalendarPro Tool Integration Methods: MCP vs. Subprocess vs. Shared Code Role Method Human Although AI recommended the MCP server as the main method, users chose subprocess and conda run. Users understand that small tools are large CLI scripts (2800+ lines), and prefer zero-code modifications through subprocess boundaries, maintaining clear responsibility division. Artificial Intelligence AI initially recommended the MCP server as the main method, considering it the “cleanest” approach because tools can be discovered directly. Only after explicit user instruction did AI fully adopt the subprocess method and design a detailed ToolRunner. Analysis of Differences: Humans prioritize maintainability and responsibility division (zero cross-repo dependencies) over protocol “simplicity”. AI initially favored protocol elegance. Human choices reflect pragmatic system thinking regarding long-term development of independent code repositories.
Decision on Using GPU or CPU for Training after CUDA Errors Role Method Human Immediately questioned “Why use CPU training? It can run on GPU!”—prioritize faster hardware and debug GPU issues. Artificial Intelligence After encountering CUDA errors, conservatively switch to CPU training to avoid failure, without deeply investigating the root cause of GPU issues. Analysis of Differences: Humans strongly prefer optimal performance (GPU) and tend to debug problems; AI avoids errors and chooses safer alternatives (CPU). Human intuition assumes GPUs “should” work, exceeding the initial sign of failure.
CrossModalEnhancer Output Dimension Design Role Method Human Originally intended to match the output dimension with the original modality (image is 1536 dimensions) to maintain semantic space, prioritizing theoretical rationality. Artificial Intelligence After encountering cuBLAS errors in large matrix projections, actually adjusted to output in the hidden dimension space (128 dimensions) to avoid hardware limitations. Key Insight: Engineering constraints (GPU errors) may force architectural decisions different from ideal semantic designs. Real systems must balance theoretical elegance and implementation robustness.Difference Analysis: Humans theoretically maintain ideal architectural designs. Artificial intelligence adjusts the architecture based on identified implementation constraints, prioritizing “working code” when there is a conflict between “working code” and “elegant design”.
Repositioning Strategy for Data Files Role Method Human Directly suggests “just cut it out directly”—realizing that the correct data already exists, and uses file system move operations. Artificial Intelligence Plans to delete old data and regenerate it from scratch—while somewhat conservative, this approach wastes resources when the correct data is already available. Difference Analysis: Humans quickly identify the validity of existing data and choose direct file system operations; artificial intelligence defaults to regenerating data to ensure correctness. The trade-off between human efficiency and artificial intelligence’s caution.
Implementation Level scGPT Benchmark Research Method Role Method Human Raises a broad question: “What are the views on scGPT and clustering benchmark tests via searching existing papers?” in hopes of a comprehensive analysis. Artificial Intelligence Breaks down into multiple target keyword searches (zero-shot, ARI/NMI metrics, specific comparisons), runs WebSearch and WebFetch in parallel, and then synthesizes findings in a structured summary format. Difference Analysis: Humans pose questions at the conceptual level (“What do people think?”). Artificial intelligence converts questions into specific search strategies, including specific metrics, datasets, and comparison baselines, and then reconstructs conceptual answers.
RM-IDEAL Visualization Requirements Role Method Human Immediately asks “Where is your visualization output?” when noticing that the benchmark script only produces numerical CSV output—expecting visualization output as a standard deliverable. Artificial Intelligence Initially runs the benchmark and reports numerical results (Spearman ρ, Precision@K), but does not generate visualization output, prioritizing quantitative metrics over visual outputs. Difference Analysis: Humans emphasize visual verification and easy-to-present results, considering them important parts of the analysis completion. Artificial intelligence defaults to the correctness of numerical values and views visualization as an optional extra step.
Limitations of Artificial Intelligence Key Limitation – Due to insufficient CUDA debugging experience, 4 architectural rewrites were performed before identifying cuBLAS large matrix errors as the root cause (from collecting neighbor data to projectization, from projectization to collecting neighbor data, outputting results in hidden dimensions, using small batch loss). Known GPU driver compatibility issues were not identified early. The initially designed MCP tool was a file writing script that returns metadata, without realizing the tool should directly return content for use by Claude code. When CUDA errors occurred, a too-conservative CPU training method was chosen without thoroughly investigating GPU compatibility issues. Multiple solutions were tried before recognizing that the PyTorch CUDA build version did not match the driver version. Initially, no awareness existed that torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) conflicted with PyG’s scattering operations on CUDA, and multiple solutions were tried before identifying the core issue. The issue was not anticipated before understanding the stdout/stderr isolation requirements of the MCP server. It was only realized during the design of the wrapping layer, and the gadget CLI tool was explored initially without noticing this issue. Overall Limitations When a user proposes a large-scale refactoring task (“organize all documents, merge duplicate functions, archive unused code”), 3 parallel Explore agents are launched, but the session is interrupted before the agent returns, indicating poor performance in handling long-running multi-agent workflows across sessions. WebFetch encountered 403 errors on several important papers (bioRxiv scGPT-spatial preprint, ResearchGate link), and no alternative strategies such as archive.org snapshots or manual PDF downloads were attempted, limiting the depth of literature analysis. When running RM-IDEAL benchmarks, no visual results are actively generated, requiring the user to explicitly ask “Where are the visualization results?” No expectation was placed on the need for visual verification in spatial analysis. When supporting bioRxiv/PubMed, no question is asked whether the user wants to modify a single 2600-line file or refactor it into modular packages. Implementation follows the user’s request directly, without providing other architectural options. The DNS troubleshooting session failed to resolve the issue—no sufficient exploration of cluster network configuration was done, and no alternative software distribution methods are suggested. Lessons Learned Key Lesson – RM-IDEAL uses the WWL (Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman) graph kernel to compute spatial niche matching: through iterative neighbor tag hashing → node feature distribution → optimal transfer between subgraphs (Wasserstein distance). This provides a topological-based benchmark for evaluating embedding quality. Cross-attention processing on a single token degrades to linear projection. Spatial transcriptomics offers a natural solution: k-NN neighbors form a K/V sequence, encoding neighborhood context. This pattern (using spatial neighbors as attention context) applies to various spatial omics architectures. PyTorch 2.9 + CUDA 12.9 has errors in cuBLAS on RTX 2080 Ti, leading to illegal memory access issues during large-scale matrix operations (e.g., gemm failures occur when the shape is 128→1536, and problems also occur in N×N operations when N>3500). Solution: use small batch processing to keep the matrix size small. The PyTorch CUDA build version (e.g., cu129) must match the GPU driver’s CUDA version. The scGPT base model performs worse than traditional methods (PCA, scVI, Harmony) in zero-shot clustering benchmarks (Genome Biology 2025). The AvgBIO score on the Pancreas/PBMC dataset shows that scGPT scores are between 0.52–0.60, while HVG baseline scores are between 0.60–0.77. scGPT-spatial requires fine-tuning and is only compared with weaker baselines (SpaGCN, stLearn), not with state-of-the-art models. Independent benchmark results are more reliable than those described in the original paper. Conditional flow matching for robot action generation: learning vector fields u_t via linear interpolation path x_t = t·noise + (1-t)·actions, using Beta(1.5,1) time sampling to maintain stability near noise endpoints, and using Euler integration for reasoning. The key idea is: time conditioning via sine embedding and MLP (or adaRMS for Pi0.5). Design principles of the MCP tool: tools in Claude Code should default to returning content (Markdown reports, JSON data) and allow optional file persistence. This allows direct use of these tools without passing through the file system. Summary/research is “skill enhancement”, not just file generation tools. When wrapping existing CLI tools for protocol-based systems (MCP, JSON-RPC), isolating stdout/stderr is a top priority architectural consideration, not a later issue. Using a context manager enables clean, reversible redirection without modifying the original code. When expanding a single-source system to multiple sources, introduce a new abstraction level (paper_id) while retaining the old field (arxiv_id) as an alias. Helper functions (_paper_id, _paper_url) can handle cross-source logic centrally, making future expansion simple. The characteristics of the DLPFC organizational layer directly affect cross-sample matching of embedded data: Layer_1 (surface, thin layer) and Layer_4 (granular, cell-dense) show Spearman ρ>0.6; Layer_3 (maximal, highly heterogeneous) shows ρ<-0.2. The quality of embedded data is related to structural uniqueness and boundary clarity, not the size of the layers. RoboTwin data format: 14-degree-of-freedom action space (6 degrees of freedom for left arm + 1 degree of freedom for gripper + 6 degrees of freedom for right arm + 1 degree of freedom for gripper), stored in HDF5 format, containing joint_action/vector information; observation data is stored in compressed image format. Demo_clean directory structure: data/episodeX.hdf5, instructions/episodeX.json, including language variants seen/unseen. STAIG fusion training for spatial omics: UNI2 (1536-dimensional visual data) + PCA (50-dimensional gene data) → STAIG fusion encoder (64 dimensions). Key findings: alignment mode uses tau=26, softmax_log edge weights, 300 pseudo-clusters, 550 training cycles. If training fails, the model may collapse (all embeddings are zero). UniVLA training process: divided into three stages (LAM stage 1/2, VLA pre-training, fine-tuning for each benchmark). CALVIN training: DiskCalvinDataset loads auto_lang_ann.npy to get episode language mapping, reads episode_*.npz window data (12–13 frames), extracts rgb_static → LAM → latent_action_idx → VLA input → ActionDecoder → relactions. Cross-environment tool invocation (conda run -n ) provides a clean isolated environment for sibling projects with conflicting dependencies. Setting cwd as the root of the tool repository is very important because many Python scripts use relative imports and sys.path operations. Production-level logging requires two processors: StreamHandler (INFO level) for user-visible progress information, RotatingFileHandler (DEBUG level) for diagnostic details. The print() function is retained in interactive UI commands, but all operations/diagnostic messages are migrated to logger. Structure of the CALVIN evaluation dataset: only validation/.hydra/merged_config.yaml files are needed for environment initialization. During evaluation, the episode_.npz file is not read (online simulation generates observation data). Data extraction can reduce dataset size from 1.3GB to 600KB. A zero-dependency API client (urllib.request + xml.etree) is suitable for production tools when avoiding new dependencies is crucial. bioRxiv and PubMed use only the standard library to implement these clients, maintaining the minimal dependency principle. Python package distribution for MCP servers: for stateless tools, the standard mode uses PyPI + uvx; when the server depends on the repository’s data directory, pip install -e . is required (editable installation). The entry point [project.scripts] in pyproject.toml is used, followed by Claude mcp add gadget –gadget-mcp. Practical Experience When integrating a new fusion strategy into the existing process: (1) register in apply_fusion() scheduler, (2) add needs_coords tuple in runner.py and evaluation_planner.py, (3) add configuration dictionary entry in runner.py, (4) define the experiment in pipeline_config.yaml. This four-step integration pattern applies to all trainable fusion methods. When updating documentation, use grep to find CLI flags and function names so that missing items can be systematically identified, rather than relying on manual code review. Dialogue Summary MIHD Spatial Transcriptomics**✅ Full-day work covering cross-sample analysis, cross-modal enhancement, and literature review** 23:31:05.195 | claude_code Comprehensive development was carried out in 6 sessions: (1) Using PCA+UNI2+STAIG_fusion to perform cross-sample RM-IDEAL benchmark tests on 151673–151508/151676, revealing high correlation between different layers (Layer_1/4 ρ>0.6), while heterogeneous Layer_3 shows negative correlation; 7 spatial heatmaps were generated and a detailed Chinese documentation was written. (2) The CrossModalEnhancer was designed, using spatial k-NN neighbors as attention context to avoid performance degradation due to single tokens. (3) The CrossModalEnhancer (approximately 350 lines of code) was implemented and 3 modes were added, integrated into 5 workflow files; after 4 architecture iterations, the PyTorch 2.9/CUDA 12.9 cuBLAS error was resolved using small batch losses. (4) The CLAUDE.md file was updated, adding the CrossModalEnhancer, RM-IDEAL commands, and detailed tool descriptions. (5) The architecture section of CLAUDE.md was streamlined from approximately 30 lines to about 10 lines. (6) A systematic scGPT literature review was conducted, revealing that its performance in zero-sample clustering is inferior to traditional methods (PCA, scVI). GPU compatibility issues were encountered, requiring fallback to CPU for cross-sample visualization tasks.
UniVLA**✅ Created comprehensive CLAUDE.md documentation and analyzed the training workflow** 03:35:00.014 | claude_code Used/init skills to explore the UniVLA code repository and create the CLAUDE.md document. Recorded build, lint, and test commands (torchrun, accelerate, black/ruff), training phases (LAM, VLA pre-training, fine-tuning), evaluation methods (LIBERO/CALVIN/R2R/SimplerEnv), and architecture design (VLM→PrismaticVLM→OpenVLA, visual/language model architecture, action tokenization path, draccus configuration, RLDS workflow). Subsequently discussed the requirements of the CALVIN dataset and analysis of the training data workflow (using DiskCalvinDataset to load auto_lang_ann.npy and episode_*.npz files).
OpenPI (Pi0) ✅ Explained the flow matching implementation in pi0.py 11:37:19.597 | claude_code The user requested an explanation of the flow matching implementation in policy/pi05/src/openpi/models/pi0.py. Analyzed the implementation of conditional flow matching: linear interpolation path x_t = t·noise + (1-t)·actions, Beta(1.5,1) time sampling [0.001,1], target vector field u_t = noise - actions, MSE loss training, and sampling from t=1 to 0 using the Euler integration method. Explained the time control method implemented via sine embedding + MLP or adaRMS.
VLA (RoboTwin) ✅ Converted RoboTwin demo_clean to LeRobot format 16:18:03.707 | claude_code The user collected 50 datasets of place_dual_shoes data under the demo_clean/ directory via RoboTwin/collect_data.sh. A plan was developed to convert the data to LeRobot format (different from the existing zip-based script: 14-DOF instead of 16, extracting directories instead of compressed packages). The convert_robotwin_democlean_to_lerobot.py script was implemented, successfully converting 11,459 frames of data. The output directory issue was resolved using the LeRobotDataset.create(root=…) parameter, and the dataset was moved from cache to RoboTwin/data/place_dual_shoes_lerobot/.
CALVIN Environment 🔄 Resolved pip installation failure and created a dataset extraction script 10:24:15.816 | claude_code When running calvin/install.sh in a Kubernetes pod, users encountered DNS resolution failure (Errno -3: temporary name resolution failure). Diagnosis revealed: name server is 10.96.0.10 (cluster DNS), proxy is localhost:9997, unable to resolve pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn or pypi.org. Cluster network issues were identified but not resolved. The extract_eval_files.py script was also created, extracting only validation/.hydra/merged_config.yaml and metadata from the CALVIN dataset, reducing file size from 1.3GB to 600KB.
Gadget MCP Server ✅ Converted gadget tool to MCP server for AI agent discovery 19:34:52.537 | claude_code The MCP server was designed and implemented, providing 9 gadget tools (summarize, research, benchmark). Files pyproject.toml, .mcp.json, and mcp_server.py were created, along with stdout capture and SystemExit handling. The FastMCP version parameter issue was fixed, the mcp package was installed, and all tool functions were verified. Distribution options (PyPI, Smithery) were discussed. Ultimately, default return content instead of writing files was chosen; thus, 5 tools were refactored to return full markdown/JSON content, with optional save parameters.
Workstation Documentation ✅ Created CLAUDE.md documentation for multi-project workstations 18:36:35.440 | claude_code The user triggered the -init command. The AI started 5 parallel Explore agents to analyze all projects (CalendarPro, OCR, gadget, get-shit-done, openclaw). CalendarPro ✅ Integrated gadget research/summary tools into CalendarPro 18:59:53.249 | claude_code The user wanted CalendarPro to automatically run the research_scout and daily_summary functions of gadgets according to schedules. After exploration and user feedback, a sub-process + conda run method was chosen instead of MCP. Modifications were made to 6 new files (protocol, runner, gadgetTools, two services) and adjustments were made to 2 files (configuration, coordinator). 13 unit tests were created, all passing. The –no-banner conda flag issue was fixed. CLAUDE.md documentation was updated, adding new subsystems.

(2) A 5-phase plan was implemented: adding RotatingFileHandler logging (approximately 77 print statements migrated), warning for empty fields/zero scores,泛izing arxiv_id to paper_id, maintaining backward compatibility, adding bioRxiv and PubMed search functions (using urllib.request, no new dependencies), and multi-source coordination with –source CLI flag. Weekly Report — 2026-W10 (2026-03-02 ~ 2026-03-08) This week, four main initiatives were advanced concurrently across three devices: DCC, Tianhe Supercomputing, and TzJsDesktop, including space transcriptome research, robot operation training/ evaluation, AI personal assistant, and paper management tools. The MIHD project completed the full set of integrated experiments for scGPT+UNI2 (QFormer avg ARI=0.370, +117% vs scGPT-only) and established a zero-shot cross-sample evaluation framework; Pi0.5 LoRA fine-tuning achieved a total success rate of 58.9% and fully surpassed BC-RNN (0%), quantitatively validating the advantages of the VLA model; CalendarPro achieved a structural leap from passive response to active decision-making (321 tests all passed), while exposing and fixing critical integration defects such as BackgroundCoordinator never starting; gadget Research Scout was built from scratch to production-ready, completing a two-stage LLM paper evaluation pipeline in one day and producing three research direction suggestions for the first time; error_recovery_benchmark completed the full cleanup of 65 symlinks and the infrastructure for visualizing error scenarios in MP4 format. The most important engineering experience this week is: test pass ≠ system availability (the integration layer must be verified separately), and before designing an agentic system, actively study the architecture patterns of mature similar projects.

found threshold τ=0.10m was underestimated, changed to record original ee_target_distances for data-driven calibration 🔄 Design of GPU utilization optimization scheme for VLA eval pipeline (2026-03-02) — Confirmed action chunking as the root cause of only 10% GPU utilization, designed BatchedVLAServer batch inference scheme, but not finalized 🔄 Root cause analysis and fix specifications for CalendarPro Discord bot context-aware bug (2026-03-06) — Identified three causes: pre-check truncation of general_keywords in follow-up messages, _llm_classify not passing conversation history, GENERAL routing containing confirmation words. Fix specifications designed for implementation 🔄 zhaoganlong: Pipeline for data preparation and dual-path training start for 9 tasks (2026-03-05) — 4-step pipeline executed completely, Diffusion Policy and Pi0.5 FSDP successfully started; LLaVA MPM blocked due to lack of base model 🔄 Development of storage layer for pre-error trajectory replay (2026-03-08) — rollout_generator added action_history collection and initial_state saving, NPZ extended storage, visualization script replay logic incomplete due to context exhaustion Issues and Solutions 1. STAIG two-stage completely ignores gene encoder output, uses raw HVG as GCN input, resulting in scGPT+UNI2+STAIG ≡ PCA+UNI2+STAIG [MIHD] (2026-03-02) Solution: Three-layer code tracking (Fusion.py → runner.py → STAIGTrainer.py) confirmed the architecture: gene encoder is decoupled from GNN training, improvement should start with the GNN structure rather than replacing the gene encoder
2. Pi0.5 eval client reports keepalive ping timeout, SR is 0% for all; multi-client concurrency is 24% slower in reverse serial order [Pi0.5/VLA evaluation] (2026-03-02) Solution: Add ping_timeout=None to connect() to disable the 20s timeout (JAX JIT compilation takes 30–60s, exceeding the default); confirmed that VLA inference is strictly serial, multi-clients are ineffective, the correct solution is BatchedVLAServer batch inference
3. STAIG fusion embedding training collapses on some sections (all zero), leading to NaN Spearman r in cross-sample evaluation [MIHD] (2026-03-03) Solution: Add zero-embedding detection (norm<1e-6) to load_fused_embeddings(), automatically trigger –recompute_fusion to re-train STAIG (about 50 seconds)
4. Pi0.5 LoRA training configuration name contains ‘pi05_libero’, users suspect initialization weights come from libero rather than pi05_base [Pi0.5/VLA training] (2026-03-03) Solution: Three-layer evidence (config.py weight_loader field + training log Restoring checkpoint path + comparison group configuration) confirmed both sides use pi05_base correctly; the configuration name describes data loading, weight_loader is the only basis
5. BC-RNN has SR=0% on all normal tasks, completely inconsistent with training rollout [error_recovery_benchmark] (2026-03-04) Solution: Code exploration identified a bug in baseline_accuracy evaluation regarding object observation keys, strategy receives empty observations; M14 with nearly 0% Error SR is the core argument of the benchmark (existing strategies lack error recovery capability), comparison with Normal SR clarifies the issue
6. Openpi-moe training feature norm_stats.json lacks prev_actions key but no error; hist_actions (unnormalized) directly concatenated with actions (normalized) causes scale mismatch in VAE [zhaoganlong/openpi] (2026-03-05) Solution: Modify compute_norm_stats.py to dynamically detect prev_actions and write statistics; the root mechanism is apply_tree(strict=False) silently skipping missing keys, new training features must force synchronized normalization scripts
7. All background services in CalendarPro never run in production environment, 321 tests all passed but no integration defect found [CalendarPro] (2026-03-05) Solution: Add await coordinator.start_all() in on_ready() of discord_bot.py; root cause is decoupled registration pattern and lifecycle management, unit tests cannot detect silent failure at the integration layer
8. Headless Docker container SAPIEN reports Render Error, bare except hides real exception, apt driver version does not match kernel module [VLA-RoboTwin] (2026-03-06) Solution: Expose real exception → confirm missing NVIDIA Vulkan ICD → extract user-mode GL library from official 535.104.12 .run package that matches kernel version strictly → inject via VK_ICD_FILENAMES/LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable (no root required)
9. Research Scout initial version performs deep evaluation of all papers (50) in a single stage, token waste is severe and low-relevance papers consume a lot of analysis resources [gadget/Research Scout] (2026-03-07) Solution: Refactored into a two-stage pipeline: lightweight screening in Stage 1 → deep analysis in Stage 2 (up to 20 high-relevance papers), aligned with real researcher reading habits
10. In code migration for error_recovery_benchmark, 65 symlinks cause indirect layers, removing symlinks requires recalculating sys.path parent chain depth [error_recovery_benchmark] (2026-03-08) Solution: 4-way parallel Agents clean all symlinks according to a 9-stage plan without overlap, main thread handles Makefile/Documentation; actively fix two unexpected sys.path depth errors (Path.resolve() no longer passes through symlink folding)
11. VLA-RoboTwin critical region annotation critical_region data is all zero, τ=0.10m threshold is purely based on estimation and does not match actual working space scale [VLA-RoboTwin] (2026-03-08) Solution: Do not adjust parameters directly, instead record original ee_target_distances (4–8 distance variables per task), analyze real data distribution first before data-driven calibration of the threshold
Learning Insights Architecture- Three standard checks after large-scale implementation: (1) Whether the new service is connected to the startup chain; (2) Whether cross-layer updates (IntentType→route→handler→service) are consistent; (3) Whether silent exceptions (except: pass) hide runtime errors. Passing tests is a necessary condition rather than a sufficient one, and defects in the integration layer can only be detected through end-to-end verification. Before designing an Agentic system, actively study mature similar projects—OpenClaw’s EventBus/CronScheduler/Plugin registration pattern and GSD’s STATE.md persistent memory/multi-Agent context isolation are highly reusable architectural patterns; related fixes should be merged into a single change rather than implemented in stages to avoid code rework. apply_tree(strict=False) is an implicit risk in ML training pipelines: if new training features that need normalization are not updated simultaneously with the norm_stats calculation script, it will cause silent scale mismatch affecting training quality; the mismatch records of AI systems are free annotation data, and automatically returning them as utterance augmentations can achieve low-cost continuous self-improvement. Two-stage information processing (rough screening + fine evaluation) is better than single-stage full processing in terms of token efficiency and analysis depth: Stage 1 focuses on problem relevance/innovation/authority of source (30 seconds judgment), Stage 2 focuses on key insights driving effects rather than engineering details, and critically examines the baseline and metrics chosen by the author. Debugging Analysis of the root cause of low GPU utilization in VLA inference: action chunking makes inference calls sparse (about 8 calls per trial × 2.5 s/200 s total time = 10%); multi-client concurrency does not improve strict serial inference throughput. The correct optimization direction is BatchedVLAServer batch inference + independent deployment on multiple GPUs. Diagnostic path for BC-RNN SR=0%; first check whether the observation key name/dimensions match training, then use historical training logs to distinguish “evaluation bug” vs “training already failed” to avoid misdiagnosis as model capability issues; bare except is the most common debugging obstacle in rendering/simulation frameworks, and should be immediately changed to except Exception: traceback.print_exc(). Parameter settings should be driven by experiments rather than intuitive estimation: first collect a small amount of data to verify the actual distribution before setting thresholds; incorrect estimation of key parameters (such as distance threshold, driving version) will cause the entire batch of data to be invalid or installation failure. Tools 4-way parallel sub-Agents + the main thread handling non-parallelizable parts can control the large-scale migration of 65 symlink files within a single session; the key is dividing agent task boundaries based on non-overlapping file sets; BatchedVLAServer parallel evaluation (44 minutes/9 tasks) saves about 80% time compared to serial execution. Standard solution for fixing headless HPC nodes’ Vulkan/EGL rendering: extract a user-space GL library from the NVIDIA official .run package that strictly matches the kernel version (no need to install kernel modules), inject it via VK_ICD_FILENAMES/__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES/LD_LIBRARY_PATH, without root; EGL/Vulkan device configuration is independent of CUDA; normal CUDA performance does not mean Vulkan is available. The arXiv comment field is a de facto conference acceptance announcement area; by searching the full text with all:"CVPR 2025" and filtering after comment, a specialized search for conference papers can be achieved; au:"Author Name" AND (kw1 OR kw2) is an effective way to track specific researchers’ latest work in the system. Domain Knowledge Learning-based fusion (QFormer) is significantly better than simple concatenation: scGPT 512d representations themselves are valuable but require non-linear projection to be fully activated (+117% vs scGPT-only); STAIG’s gene encoder is decoupled from GNN training, and differences between documents and code can only be found through code tracking; zero-shot capabilities are the core competitive point against methods that rely on training. Pi0.5 LoRA fine-tuning reaches 95–100% on Stack-like tasks (overall 58.9%), while BC-RNN fails completely (0%); task complexity (multiple steps, fine operations) is the main factor determining the success rate gap between VLA and traditional sequence modeling; the Pi0.5 LoRA mode also requires at least 2 × 80GB GPUs (FSDP is a necessary prerequisite). AI Usage Notes Effective Patterns:
✓ Multi-layer code tracking (3–4 call stacks) accurately identifies the facts of STAIG architecture, providing evidence at the line-level, which is more reliable than document analysis. ✓ 4-way parallel Agents divide tasks based on non-overlapping file sets, enabling the large-scale migration of 65 symlink files to be completed within a single session. ✓ Systematic analysis of sacct step timestamps correctly excludes misjudgments caused by AI operations leading to NODE_FAIL, establishing a causal evidence chain. ✓ Actively clarify ambiguous requirements by AskUserQuestion (whether author search needs LLM evaluation), precisely transforming product requirements into engineering solutions. ✓ Systematically verify the correctness of experimental configurations (source of base model) with three layers of evidence, outperforming intuitive judgment. Limitations:
✗ No verification that new features are connected to the system startup chain after implementation; only relying on unit tests omits integration layer checks (BackgroundCoordinator not started). ✗ No active study of mature industry implementations when designing Agentic systems; need user clarification before referring to OpenClaw/GSD architectural patterns. ✗ Parameter settings lack experimental validation (τ=0.10m purely estimated), resulting in all critical_region labeled data being 0. ✗ Research contributions describe technical details rather than competitive advantages; the differentiated positioning of zero-shot needs user clarification. ✗ Initial task scheduling is conservative and serial, without actively identifying opportunities for parallel execution of long-term GPU tasks + lightweight visualization tasks. ✗ Lack of necessary resume/fresh-start intent confirmation before resource-intensive operations (GPU training); misstarting fresh-start overwrites checkpoints. Next Week’s Priorities Core priorities next week: 1) Fix three bugs in CalendarPro’s context-aware section (streamline general_keywords removal of confirmation words/time words + pass _llm_classify with the last 3 conversation histories + reset GENERAL route utterances), completing the final loop from architecture upgrade to actual usability; 2) Complete the visual replay logic for pre-error trajectories (storage layer ready, complete initial state playback and frame rendering in the visualization script); 3) Monitoring and evaluation of zhaoganlong training results: Diffusion Policy is expected to be completed in 2–4 days, Pi0.5 FSDP requires about 31 hours, start batch eval immediately after training; 4) Unlock LLaVA MPM training: confirm the completeness of cpx2 user’s local llava-v1.5-7b, start training by pointing to the local path with --model_name_or_path; 5) Threshold calibration for key regions in VLA-RoboTwin: after analyzing the actual distribution of ee_target_distances, reset τ value and re-collect critical_region labels; 6) Formal fix and normal task evaluation for BC-RNN observation key bug; 7) Render demonstration video (comparison of success/failure for Pi0.5 high SR tasks). Research Scout is ready, can start configuring regular paper discovery processes for MIHD, error_recovery_benchmark, etc.

summary: This week, across three devices—DCC, Tianhe Supercomputing, and TzJsDesktop—four main projects were advanced in parallel: space transcriptome research, robot operation training/assessment, AI personal assistant, and paper management tools. The MIHD project completed the full set of fusion experiments for scGPT+UNI2 (QFormer avg ARI=0.370, +117% vs scGPT-only) and established a zero-shot cross-sample assessment framework; Pi0.5 LoRA fine-tuning achieved a total success rate of 58.9%, fully surpassing BC-RNN (0%), thereby quantitatively validating the advantages of the VLA model; CalendarPro achieved a structural leap from passive response to active decision-making (321 tests all passed), while exposing and fixing critical integration defects such as the BackgroundCoordinator never starting; gadget Research Scout was built from scratch to production-ready, completing a two-stage LLM paper evaluation pipeline in a single day and providing three research direction suggestions for the first time; error_recovery_benchmark completed the full cleanup of 65 symlinks and the infrastructure for visualizing error scenarios in MP4 format. The most important engineering experience this week is: test passing ≠ system availability (the integration layer must be verified independently), and before designing an agentic system, it is necessary to actively study the architectural patterns of mature similar projects.

Daily Report — 2026-03-08 Daily Overview Completed work: Expanded the research paper discovery tool, added author-based search functionality, generated visual charts for error benchmarks, designed and implemented a critical region annotation method for VLA training covering 10 operational tasks, fixed errors in RoboTwin rendering, and plans for a comprehensive symbolic link removal refactor Implementation methods: Implemented new arXiv search functionality supporting caching, used MuJoCo EGL rendering for batch video generation, designed distance-based heuristic algorithms combined with gripper state filtering to identify critical regions, configured the Vulkan/EGL environment for headless GPU rendering, and drawn a dependency diagram for 65 symbolic links Impact: The research tool now supports three search modes (keywords, conferences, authors), created 9 auditable benchmark videos, introduced a new VLA training method to address systemic failure patterns, resolved the RoboTwin data collection pipeline issue, and improved the maintainability of error_recovery_benchmark TzJsDesktop Completed work: Implemented author search functionality for research_scout.py and updated project documentation to reflect the current state Implementation methods: Added the search_arxiv_author() function, modeled on conference search patterns, updated the cache layer and CLI parser, corrected line count statistics and missing functional documentation in CLAUDE.md Impact: Users can now search for papers by specific researchers, the documentation accurately reflects the 2024 line code base, and includes all current features tianhe Completed work: Generated visual charts for error benchmarks, designed and implemented a VLA critical region annotation system, fixed RoboTwin rendering infrastructure, and plans for symbolic link removal refactor Implementation methods: Batch-generated MP4 files from existing.npz scene data, implemented critical region annotation for 11 files, based on distance heuristic algorithm, added Vulkan/EGL environment configuration, and fully drawn the dependency diagram for 65 symbolic links Impact: Created 9 auditable videos for different types of errors, provided a complete critical region annotation system with empirical tuning capabilities, resolved blocked rendering errors, and developed an executable refactor plan Expanded the research tool with author search functionality, updated documentation, generated visual charts for error benchmarks, designed a critical region annotation system for VLA training, and fixed RoboTwin rendering infrastructure
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Designed the critical region annotation method for VLA — Designed a gripper state filtering technique based on distance heuristic algorithm to annotate critical regions in 10 RoboTwin operational tasks ✅ Implemented the critical region annotation system — Modified base_task.py and 10 task files, injected critical_region tags and ee_target_distances into observation data ✅ Implemented author search functionality (–author flag) — Added the search_arxiv_author() function, updated the cache function to support author parameters, modified cmd_search() and cmd_report() functions to adapt to author search patterns, and added CLI parameters for searching and reporting sub-parser 🔄 Plans to remove symbolic links from error_recovery_benchmark — Drawn a dependency diagram for 65 symbolic links and developed a comprehensive refactor plan to eliminate technical debt due to backward compatibility Implementation and Fixes ✅ Generated visual videos for error benchmarks — Created 9 MP4 videos from error scenarios in coffee and stacking tasks, covering natural failures (grasp_miss, premature_release, overshoot) and injection errors (tip_over) ✅ Updated research CLAUDE.md documentation — Corrected line count statistics (from ~1870 lines to ~2000 lines), added –language flag, added early stop deduplication function (known ID + 5 consecutive known IDs), and updated chapter numbering ✅ Fixed RoboTwin rendering device errors — Added Vulkan/EGL environment variables to collect_data.sh to enable headless GPU rendering ✅ Located episode_num configuration — Identified the episode_num field in task_config YAML that controls data collection quantity ✅ Reviewed CLAUDE.md documentation — Confirmed that existing CLAUDE.md meets production quality and requires no modification Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. VLA model continues to fail during specific task phases (inaccurate pressing in click tasks,抓取/placement failures in operational tasks) Solution: Designed a gripper state filtering technique based on distance heuristic algorithm to annotate binary “critical region” tags during data collection, thereby supporting the training of the cls token classifier
Key insight: By training a binary classifier, high-risk areas requiring special attention can be predicted, addressing systematic VLA failures during task critical phases
2. All critical_region tags become 0 after data collection, indicating the threshold (0.10 m) is too conservative Solution: Added the get_ee_target_distances() method, recording the original EE-to-target distances for all tasks, thereby enabling empirical threshold adjustment
Key insight: When designing machine learning data annotation heuristic algorithms, original features should be recorded first before determining tag thresholds
General Issues 3. SAPIEN renderer encounters “RuntimeError: failed to find a rendering device” error in headless environment Solution: Added three Vulkan/EGL environment variables (VK_ICD_FILENAMES, __EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES, LD_LIBRARY_PATH) to collect_data.sh, pointing to the nvidia_libs directory
Key insight: Headless GPU servers require explicit Vulkan ICD and EGL supplier configuration to find NVIDIA rendering drivers, even if nvidia-smi works properly
4. “No such file or directory” error occurs when running visual scripts from a remote shell Solution: Changed the relative paths of the project root and Python script to absolute paths, ensuring the working directory is correctly set before execution
Key insight: SSH does not inherit the working directory; “cd /absolute_path&& command” or providing absolute paths for all files is required
Human and Artificial Intelligence Approaches Strategic Level Selection of critical region annotation threshold Role Method Human Users found the 0.10 m threshold too small after collecting data, requesting distance recording to adjust the threshold based on actual data distribution Artificial Intelligence AI selected the 0.10 m threshold based on code analysis of the existing pre_grasp_dis pattern, without empirical validation Analysis difference: Humans use iterative empirical methods and make decisions based on actual data; AI makes theoretical choices based on code patterns. Humans correctly identified the need for observability (distance recording) before finalizing heuristic parameters
Implementation plan for author search functionality | Role | Method | |——|——| | Human | Provided a complete implementation plan in advance, including specific line numbers, function signatures, mutual exclusion checks, and validation commands | | Artificial Intelligence | Initially wanted to explore the code base first, ask clarifying questions via AskUserQuestion, then launch the Plan agent to design features |
Analysis difference: Humans prefer detailed top-level planning methods, while AI prefers problem-driven bottom-up exploration methods
Scope of symbolic link removal refactor Role Method Human Users requested removal of all 65 symbolic links to eliminate technical debt, focusing on clear structure Artificial Intelligence AI fully drew the symbolic link dependency diagram and designed a precise refactor plan, minimizing disruption risk through careful import rewrite Analysis difference: Humans focus on strategic goals (eliminating technical debt); AI focuses on tactical execution (secure migration paths). Both are necessary—humans set direction, AI ensures safe implementation
Limitations of Artificial Intelligence Key Limitations AI initially selected the critical region threshold (0.10 m) based on code patterns, but no empirical validation was done, resulting in all tags being 0. Iteration is needed to add distance recording so appropriate thresholds can be adjusted based on actual data distribution General Limitations AI needs multiple sub-agents to fully draw the symbolic link dependency diagram (total of 65 symbolic links distributed across root directory, script directory, and nested output directories with complex import patterns) Fails to properly handle SSH working directory context, requiring multiple attempts to build commands with correct absolute paths Learning Outcomes Main Achievements For VLA training in operational tasks, distance-based heuristic algorithms and gripper state filtering can be used to systematically address failure patterns during critical task phases (pressing, grasping, placement) arXiv API supports author queries via “au:author name” syntax, which can be combined with keyword filters using AND/OR operators and sorted by relevance for author search When designing machine learning data collection heuristic algorithms, observability should be achieved before adopting threshold-based labels. Empirical adjustments require understanding the actual data distribution research_scout.py now supports three different search modes with distinct caching strategies: keywords/categories (sorted by date, filtered by review time), conferences (sorted by relevance, filtered by comments), and authors (sorted by relevance, no post-filtering) Backward compatibility via symbolic links creates complex dependency diagrams, requiring a comprehensive mapping before refactor (65 symbolic links × multiple import patterns = high disruption risk without careful planning) Practical Achievements MP4 generation can be achieved efficiently later on by using pre-saved.npz scene data without re-running the entire strategy SAPIEN headless GPU rendering requires three Vulkan/EGL environment variables: VK_ICD_FILENAMES, __EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES, and LD_LIBRARY_PATH, pointing to the NVIDIA driver library directory Dialogue Summary gadget/research ✅ Implemented author search functionality and updated documentation 03:25:22.536 | claude_code User provided a detailed implementation plan, added –author flag to search for papers by specific researchers. Assistant implemented search_arxiv_author() function, updated the cache layer to support author parameters, and modified search and reporting commands to handle author mode with mutual exclusion checks. Also verified the three previously implemented features (initialization –from-overview, weekly to daily renaming, search deduplication), updated CLAUDE.md, corrected line count (2024 vs 1870), added –language flag documentation, recorded early stop deduplication function, and adjusted chapter numbering. All changes passed syntax checks.**
error_recovery_benchmark ✅ Generated visual effects and reviewed CLAUDE.md 01:15:43.352 | claude_code User asked if rendering visuals could be provided. Assistant found existing visual effects from the old pick_place task but couldn’t find them in the current 6 tasks. Found scene data (150–743 scenes per task) that can be rendered immediately. After resolving SSH working directory issues, successfully generated 9 MP4 videos covering different error types in coffee and stacking tasks using MuJoCo EGL on GPU6. Also ran /init to review existing CLAUDE.md, confirmed its quality sufficient for production use without modification. Then user requested removal of all 65 backward-compatible symbolic links; AI drew the dependency diagram and developed a comprehensive refactor plan.**
RoboTwin VLA**✅ Design and Implementation of Key Region Annotation** 04:18:09.279 | claude_code The user identified systematic failures of VLA during critical task phases (pressing for task execution, grasping/placement for manipulation tasks). A heuristic annotation for “key regions” was requested to train the cls token binary classifier. Artificial intelligence comprehensively explored the RoboTwin workflow, analyzed 10 different task environments, designed distance-based heuristic algorithms, and implemented filtering for grasping states. The entire system was implemented in 11 files: the base_task.py file was modified, auxiliary methods (_ee_dist, get_critical_region_label, get_ee_target_distances) were added, critical_region and ee_target_distances were injected into get_obs(), and all methods in the 10 task files were replaced with task-specific heuristic algorithms. After collecting data, the user found that all labels were 0; artificial intelligence added distance records for empirical threshold adjustment. Rendering errors in collect_data.sh were also fixed by adding VK_ICD_FILENAMES, __EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES, and LD_LIBRARY_PATH exports, and the episode_num configuration was located in task_config/*.yml files.
summary: Extended research tools, including an author search function and updated documentation; capable of generating visual representations of error situations; a key region annotation system for VLA training was designed and implemented; some issues in the RoboTwin rendering infrastructure were also fixed.
