Daily Report — 2026-03-07 Daily Overview Completed Work: Parallel development was carried out on MIHD, ErrorRecovery, DesktopVideo, gadget, and CalendarPro projects. Technical documentation writing, initiation and fixes of training pipelines, application development, and construction of research infrastructure were all completed. Execution Methods: Documentation generation via parallel proxy code library exploration, multi-GPU training tasks initiation, errors in evaluation metrics fixing, implementation of WKWebView wallpaper browsing mode, batch generation of historical reports, construction of context-based intent classification system, and development from scratch of a research paper management system with LLM enhancements. Impact: Complete MIHD technical specifications and research positioning were established; zero-sample scGPT is significantly inferior to PCA in performance; reliable FLARE/BC-RNN training and evaluation pipelines were achieved; a complete Desktop Video solution was provided for any wallpaper; work records for over 20 days in February were supplemented for traceability; intent classification accuracy of CalendarPro was significantly improved; and an automated research paper discovery and evaluation infrastructure with bilingual support and efficient search functionality was established. DCC Completed Work: Precise update of MIHD CLAUDE.md was completed; research positioning document overview.md was created; scGPT/scGPT‑spatial performance was systematically studied; cross-sample RM-IDEAL benchmark tests were executed. Execution Methods: Parallel proxy code library exploration was used to extract APIs and statistics for incremental document patches; 4 parallel proxies were initiated to retrieve arXiv papers and benchmark data; Python benchmark test scripts were used to analyze Spearman correlation. Impact: Project documentation upgraded from descriptive overview to precise technical specifications; a clinical perspective-based narrative on the differences between zero-sample and STAIG was established; clustering of zero-sample scGPT is significantly inferior to PCA (PCA ARI = 0.261 vs scGPT = 0.170, with a 54% gap). MacBook Completed Work: Complete WKWebView wallpaper functionality for Desktop Video was implemented (e.g., YouTube/Bilibili), interactive issues in browsing mode, scroll bar transparency issues, and volume synchronization errors were fixed; Hugo automatic deployment functionality for both Windows/UNIX platforms was achieved for the gadget summary tool; some historical reports were generated in batch. Execution Methods: ContentType enumeration was expanded to include .web type; playback control via WKWebView was implemented; sandbox network permissions and JS injection techniques were used; window_level=.normal interactive layer issues were fixed; transparency problems were resolved by removing drawsBackground; update.ps1 PowerShell script and run_hugo_update() cross-platform detection function were created. Impact: Desktop Video can play any web video as a desktop wallpaper (solving sandbox network blocking, non-interactive window layers, and scroll bar transparency issues); the gadget tool can be automatically deployed on both Windows and UNIX platforms. TzJsDesktop Completed Work: gadget report tool processing was performed in batch for over 20 dates from early February to early March; tested on multiple devices; context-based intent classification system for CalendarPro was implemented (passed 360 tests); research paper management system was developed from scratch (approximately 750 core scripts + two-stage evaluation pipeline); then production-level optimization was applied (language configuration, reverse initialization, deduplication, error fixing). Execution Methods: daily_summary.py export and merging commands were repeated; keyword classification based on context and conversation-aware dialogue history management were implemented; summarize/LLM backend mode was reused for arXiv search and two-stage LLM evaluation pipeline; Hugo Extended was installed via winget; research_scout.py was systematically enhanced to enable overview.md parsing based on LLM; language configuration via a three-layer prompt system; deduplication based on arxiv_id with early stopping logic; issues with project ID/directory name mismatch were fixed. Impact: Comprehensive work archiving from February to early March was completed, ensuring historical traceability; CalendarPro completely resolved inaccurate intent classification caused by keyword pre-check拦截 (e.g., vague queries like “what time is it”); automated research paper discovery and evaluation infrastructure with bilingual output, efficient search, and reverse project initialization were established for 3–5 active projects. tianhe Completed Work: FLARE D0×4 training was initiated (stable operation time: 6.3 seconds/step); errors in 4 BC-RNN evaluation metrics were fixed (demo_len/trigger_step/transport/RP); 191 multi-task error scenarios were tested; parallel training of LLaVA MPM/MCM was started; data loading for Phoenix was optimized (from 5% to over 80% GPU utilization); bottleneck issues in downloading the LLaVA base model were resolved via offline format conversion. Execution Methods: PYTHONPATH isolation was used to resolve openpi configuration conflicts; code review was employed to fix distortion issues in BC-RNN metrics; _get_target_pos() function for dynamic target position retrieval was implemented; shared generation script for 6 tasks was achieved via task_registry dynamic routing; LLaVA base model was obtained via offline safetensors→pytorch_model.bin conversion; training bottleneck issues were resolved via ZeRO-3→ZeRO-2+HDF5 preloading. Impact: FLARE 4 D0 tasks operate stably on an53 GPU (approximately 63 hours per task); credibility of BC-RNN evaluation metrics is high (all 127 unit tests passed, with the highest GPU‑verified RP at 0.800); 191 error scenarios for 6 tasks provide a foundation for subsequent training; training time for LLaVA MPM/MCM was reduced from estimated 13.5 days to approximately 2 days, though dataset size estimation contains errors requiring replanning; Phoenix GPU utilization optimization solution is ready. Impact: Parallel execution on four devices: MIHD documentation system and scGPT research were completed; FLARE/Phoenix training was initiated and 4 BC-RNN evaluation errors were fixed; Desktop Video wallpaper with WKWebView was implemented; historical reports for over 20 days in February were generated in batch; context-based intent classification for CalendarPro was achieved; and a research paper management system with language configuration, reverse initialization, and deduplication functions was built from scratch. Tasks Architecture and Strategy - ✅ Fix of Vulnerability in BC-RNN Evaluation Process 4 — The field name error from demo_length→demo_len in collector.py was corrected; the logic for reading data from scene.dataset by trigger_step was fixed; detection logic in the transport phase was corrected (_get_target_pos() function added for dynamic target position retrieval); if success: rp=1.0 condition was added to collector.py; all 127 unit tests passed; GPU verification confirmed demo_len=605, trigger_step=55 and the highest RP is 0.800.- ✅ Complete implementation of desktop video WKWebView wallpaper — Created the WebNavigationHandler.swift file, extended theContentType enumeration type, implemented the showWeb/cleanupWebView/saveWebBookmark functions, updated the AppDelegate playback status management, updated the SingleScreenView interface (URL input field), and updated features such as history, thumbnails, localization, and ChangeLog. Added sandbox network permissions, and set customUserAgent to modern Chrome’s UA. ✅ Implementation of a research reconnaissance system from scratch — Implemented the research/research_scout.py script from scratch (approximately 750 lines of core code), including project CRUD management, arXiv search (arxiv package), support for three LLM backends (anthropic/openai/claude_cli), paper evaluation scoring, direction suggestion generation, weekly report output (JSON+Markdown), Hugo deployment, and a caching mechanism. Designed a two-stage paper evaluation process: the first stage quickly filters all papers (title + abstract, determining relevance levels); the second stage analyzes papers with high relevance (≤20 papers, including 3 highlights: insights/motivation/experiments/limitations). Completed the writing of requirements.txt, CLAUDE.md, and TUTORIAL.md Chinese tutorial. ✅ Update of MIHD CLAUDE.md accuracy — Added implementation details in Section 3.2 (5 subsections: detector/injector/verifier/classifier/coordinator), corrected the VLA model type (Pi0-FAST→Phoenix/Flare), updated code statistics (script 18→22, test cases 109→122), updated M14 actual evaluation data (726→6474 cases), added database stage/d severity distribution information, added a process configuration structure description, and detailed the cache directory structure. ✅ Creation of MIHD overview.md research positioning document — Written the 676-line overview.md file, including a one-sentence positioning description (systematic evaluation of zero-shot embedding of basic models in spatial transcriptomics multimodal clustering), 4 core questions, a 3-stage technical roadmap, a ranking of 10 fusion strategies, 8 open questions, search keywords, literature note template, quick reference to project structure, and a quick start command. ✅ Systematic study on scGPT/scGPT‑space and multi-view PCA performance — Obtained papers on scGPT‑space, zero-shot limited papers, and BioLLM framework papers, as well as internal MIHD results from 4 parallel agents. Summary analysis shows that zero-shot scGPT clustering performs significantly worse than PCA (PCA ARI=0.261 vs scGPT=0.170, a 54% difference). 🔄 Implementation of desktop video browsing mode and window layer fixes — Implemented the browsing mode framework (WallpaperWindow dynamic canBecomeKey, ESC listener, exit via control panel button). After multiple adjustments to the window layer, it was found that the .normal layer cannot receive any mouse/keyboard events. It was confirmed that this layer is needed, but it has not been fully implemented yet. ✅ Implementation of CalendarPro context-aware intent classification system — Implemented the context-aware intent classification system (dividing general_keywords into always_general and context_dependent to avoid incorrect classification due to ambiguous queries like “what time is it?”), and implemented session-aware conversation history management (automatic compression, session reset, token budget control). Completed the A/B/C/D four-phase plan, added 41 special tests, and all 360 tests passed. ✅ Fixes to error recovery benchmark project configuration issues — Fixed 3 critical errors: ID in project.json does not match directory names, chapter titles in overview.md do not conform to the process regular expression pattern, and missing automatic append markers. 🔄 FLARE D0×4 task training start-up — Ran coffee_D0, stack_D0, stack_three_D0, threading_D0 Pi0.5 LoRA warm-up training on an53 GPUs 1,2,4,7. Each task requires approximately 36K steps (about 63 hours). Due to a PYTHONPATH issue, the first attempt failed; after fixing, it was successfully restarted. Currently running stably, with a step duration of 6.3 seconds. ❌ Start-up of MPM/MCM parallel training for LLaVA MPM/MCM — Confirmed that the LaVA LoRA checkpoint has not been published yet. The cluster lacks a complete llava-v1.5-7b base model. The MPM training data llava_motion.json (460MB, 14M lines) is ready; the base model was obtained by converting offline safetensors→pytorch_model.bin format. modified lora.sh from ZeRO-3 to ZeRO-2 to avoid gradient splitting issues. MPM/MCM ran parallelly on an53 GPUs 3,5, but training time estimation was severely incorrect (13.5 days vs expected hours), and dataset size estimation was incorrect (160K→1M). User needs to replan. ✅ Phoenix data loading optimization — Modified TrajectoryIndexSpeedDataset in trajectory_data.py, added the preload_all_data() function to pre-load all HDF5 data into memory (uint8 type saves 4 times more storage space), changed getitem to numpy slicing, set get_dataloader parameters to num_workers=8, prefetch_factor=2, solving the DataLoader bottleneck problem, allowing GPU utilization to reach only 5-6%. ✅ Gadget summarize Windows cross-platform deployment support — Created the website and update.ps1 file (equivalent to the complete PowerShell version of update.sh), added a cross-platform run_hugo_update() function in daily_summary.py (update.ps1 is used for Windows first, Git Bash for update.sh; bash processes update.sh on UNIX), replaced 3 hard-coded bash calls in daily_summary.py, and one call in monthly_summary.py. ✅ Batch generation of historical reports for February (over 20 days) — Used the gadget/summarize tool on TzJsDesktop to generate historical reports covering more than 20 days from 2026-02-01 to 2026-03-06, including key aspects of multiple projects such as MIHD, ErrorRecoveryBenchmark, CalendarPro, gadget, and DesktopVideo. Handled cross-device (DCC, MacBook, tianhe, TzJsDesktop) conversation data through a two-step export/merge process. ✅ Implementation of a language configuration system in research_scout.py — Implemented full language support: _DEFAULT_LANGUAGE constant, _language_instruction() helper function, {language_instruction} in 3 prompt templates, passing language parameters throughout the process, –language command-line flag, and integration with config.json. ✅ Implementation of init –from-overview function — Added an LLM-driven reverse initialization function: created the _PROJECT FROM OVERSIGHT() function, used OVERVIEW_EXTRACT_PROMPT for parsing, command-line parameters (–from-overview, –api, –timeout). ✅ Generation of error scenarios for multi-task BC-RNN — Generated error scenarios for the BC-RNN model of 6 tasks using the injection+natural_capture mode in the training environment. Added –task parameter to 1c_generate_from_policy.py to automatically parse checkpoints/dataset/task configurations, fixed is_natural protection and load_demo_actions extension in 2_visualize_scene.py, and total 191 error scenarios were generated. ✅ In-depth evaluation of the robot control 3D-MVP paper — Conducted a deep analysis of arXiv 2406.18158v2 (3D-MVP: 3D multi-view pre-training for robot control), extracting three key points: ① 3D perception pre-training significantly improved downstream generalization ability, verified by the large-scale dataset in Objaverse; ② Modular separation of the visual encoder and action decoder made pre-training more flexible; ③ Multi-view input provided strong 3D scene understanding ability, achieved through implicit triangulation. Output included scores of relevance=4/novelty=4/inspiration=4, as well as suggestions for benchmark design. ✅ Elimination of duplicate and early stopping of arxiv_id in search — Added the _load_known_arxiv_ids() function to scan the cache, modified search_arxiv() function, using a continuous known paper counter (stopping after 5 consecutive papers in the cache), and processing known paper IDs through cmd_search and cmd_report. Implementations and Fixes ✅ Creation and improvement of CLAUDE.md file for research — Analyzed the 1871-line research_scout.py codebase, and created a comprehensive CLAUDE.md file including code organization sections (0-10 chapters), parameter table, key implementation details, and pipeline function names. ✅ Fixes to transparency and volume synchronization for desktop video — Removed webView.setValue(false, forKey: "drawsBackground") to fix WKWebView scroll bar tracking transparency issues, added .background(Color(nsColor: .windowBackgroundColor)) in AppMainWindow.swift to fix control panel slider transparency issues, removed isWebContent protection conditions in setVolume() so all types of content can use volume/mute controls, and fixed applyWebSettings function to check global mute status when switching content, achieving volume synchronization. ✅ Installation and configuration of Hugo on Windows — A daily_summary.py merge step caused an error 'hugo'未识别 when calling Hugo deployment. Installed Hugo.Hugo.Extended version 0.157.0 via winget. PowerShell needs to be restarted for the PATH environment variable to take effect, and finally Hugo building and deployment were successfully executed. ✅ Replace all ‘weekly report’ references with ‘daily report’” — Performed systematic text replacement in more than 12 places: function names (generate_weekly_report → generate_daily_report), documentation strings, UI messages, Markdown titles. Issues and Solutions Serious Issues 1. BC-RNN RP(0.003) is far lower than random RP(0.020), making the evaluation result completely unreasonable Solution: Code review identified 4 errors that distorted the metrics: demo_len=0 damaged SPL, trigger_step=0 further damaged SPL, transport always set the RP upper limit to 0.5, and successful episode RP not being 1.0 caused a baseline bias. Fixed collector.py:487 by changing the field name from demo_length to demo_len, changed collector.py:488 to read trigger_step from scene_dataset, added _get_target_pos() to envwrapper.py for dynamic target position retrieval, and added if success: rp=1.0 in collector.py.
Key insight: Distorted evaluation metrics are usually not due to a single error, but a chain of multiple errors. The RP upper limit of 0.5 reveals failure in the transmission stage, while demo_len=0/trigger_step=0 reveal field propagation errors.
2. WKWebView in browsing mode cannot receive mouse/keyboard events, even with ignoresMouseEvents=false; .desktopWindow layer causes non-interactive windows Solution: Set the window level to .normal during enterBrowseMode (not at the top but interactive), and restore .desktopWindow KeyForWindowLevel in exitBrowseMode.Key Insight: In macOS, the .docdesktopWindow layer lies beneath the Finder desktop icon layer. Windows on this layer cannot receive any input events at the system level; setting ignoresMouseEvents=false is ineffective for this layer. .normal(level=0) is the lowest level, providing interactivity without覆盖ting other applications.
3. The download of the LLaVA base model is hindered due to proxy bandwidth limitations (about 50KB/s, downloading a 14GB model takes several weeks); GPU nodes cannot be directly connected; xet’s CDN timeout via the proxy Solution: It was found that there is nyw of HF format llava-1.5-7b-hf (safetensors) in the cluster. A convert_hf_to_llava.py script was written to convert the HF format into the original LLaVA pytorch_model.bin format (including vocabulary truncation repair, changing from 32064 to 32000). The entire process can be completed locally without network access.
Key Insight: Do not assume that downloading is necessary—first try to find existing model copies on the cluster. Even models in different formats can be converted. Converting the HF model format involves more than just renaming keys; it also involves semantic differences (such as vocabulary size).
4. During Phoenix diffusion strategy training, GPU utilization is only 5–6%: DataLoader num_workers=0 causes the GPU to wait for the CPU to randomly read data from the NFS HDF5 file Solution: Preload all HDF5 data into memory once in the init method (uint8 type saves 4 times more storage space), close file handles, and then perform all getitem operations from a numpy array; set DataLoader’s num_workers to 8 and pin_memory to True
Key Insight: h5py file processing cannot be shared across subprocesses (this is a limitation of PyTorch DataLoader). The only safe solution is to fully load it in the main process before forking subprocesses. Random reading from NFS is much slower than sequential reading; one-time loading is 10 times faster than on-demand loading
5. After starting Phoenix MPM training, the estimated training duration is severely incorrect (actual 13.5 days, expected a few hours), and the dataset size estimation is wrong (160K→1M) Solution: The user must pause training and replan and optimize (possibly reducing training steps, increasing GPU count, optimizing data loading, etc.)
Key Insight: Before starting large-scale training, it is necessary to verify the actual dataset size, step time, and total number of steps to avoid resource waste. Incorrect dataset size estimation can lead to weeks of computational resource waste
6. CalendarPro intent classification is ambiguous due to the pre-check by general_keywords: “What time have you arranged?” → “What time is it” fits general_keywords → forced GENERAL → error Solution: Divide general_keywords into always_general (always forced GENERAL, such as ‘weather’) and context_dependent (only forced GENERAL when there is no active session, such as ‘what time is it’); add confirmation_words (‘ok’, ‘good’, ‘yes’, etc.) and provide a fast path via is_confirmation_input(); rewrite _process_input() to make it a 6-step process
Key Insight: Context-aware intent classification requires combining session state (session_id, last_activity_at) and conversation history. Simple keyword matching leads to ambiguity; when there are active proposals, confirmation phrases (‘ok’) should be routed directly
7. The current research reconnaissance paper evaluation process handles all 50 papers simultaneously, wasting labels and lacking in-depth analysis Solution: A two-stage process was designed: the first stage quickly filters all papers (only title + first 1000 characters of abstract, classified as high/low relevance); the second stage conducts in-depth analysis on high-relevance papers (up to 20 papers, extracting 3 highlights + detailed scoring + direction suggestions)
Key Insight: Mimicking the paper-reading workflow of human researchers (quick filtering → deep reading of high-value papers) can significantly improve the efficiency and quality of LLM evaluation, while generating literature reading records for low-relevance papers for future reference
8. Due to the ID (‘robot-manipulation’) in project.json not matching the directory name, the pipeline cannot read overview.md Solution: The ID field in project.json was updated to match the directory name; the pipeline uses project[‘id’] to build the path for overview.md
Key Insight: The directory name and the ID in project.json must be consistent; _extract_current_methods() uses project[‘id’] to locate overview.md
9. During the second-stage evaluation, the evaluation result of the current method is ‘(no record yet)’, because the title of the overview.md section ‘## 3. Current technical approach’ does not match the pipeline’s regex pattern ‘##\s*Current method and progress’ Solution: The title of the overview.md section was changed to match the OVERVIEW_TEMPLATE format; the numbering prefix and section separator were removed
Key Insight: The pipeline uses a strict regex for section extraction; the template format must be strictly followed
10. FLARE specification statistical calculation fails: After importing openpi in the specification statistics script, the version installed by Zhang Jialong cannot be found, nor can the new configuration name of Tang Zhijia be found Solution: In the script, PYTHONPATH=/HOME/…/tangzijia/shared_deps/openpi/src:$PYTHONPATH was set to prioritize loading Tang Zhijia’s openpi source code, bypassing the old version in the conda environment
Key Insight: When multiple users share the same conda environment, their source code modifications cause import priority conflicts. PYTHONPATH is a minimally invasive solution that does not affect other users
11. The WKWebView scroll bar tracking becomes transparent (ineffective through CSS injection of background color) + sandbox applications cannot load any network resources Solution: webViewsetValue(false, forKey: “drawsBackground”) was removed; the default opaque background was restored, making scroll bar tracking visible; com.apple.security.network.client=true was added to.entitlements
Key Insight: drawsBackground=false makes the entire WKWebView rendering layer transparent, but the semi-transparent style on the transparent layer remains transparent. The fix must be applied at the rendering layer rather than the CSS layer
12. The LLM output contains too much English content, while users expect Chinese; the output language cannot be configured Solution: A three-layer language system was implemented: _DEFAULT_LANGUAGE constant, __language_instruction() generator, and {language_instruction} in all prompts; the configuration order is CLI > project.json > config.json > default
Key Insight: Language instructions must be injected at the prompt level, not later in processing; different parts require different language rules (JSON keys and content)
13. It is impossible to create a project from the existing overview.md, unless keywords/categories are manually extracted Solution: A create_project_from_overview() function was added. The LLM (OVERVIEW_EXTRACT_PROMPT) is used to parse overview.md, extracting title, search keywords, arxiv classification, and open questions; then project.json is written, and the original overview.md is copied
Key Insight: The LLM can reliably extract structured metadata from unstructured text; the existing __call_llm() and __parse_json_response() tools are reused
14. When generating reports in batch, the JSON output produced by the LLM is often incomplete or contains syntax errors, leading to parsing failures Solution: The user provides the original text, and the AI manually extracts and fixes JSON fragments (removing non-JSON prefixes/suffixes, fixing quote escaping, completing missing closing parentheses, etc.)
Key Insight: LLM-generated structured output, especially JSON containing many nested objects and long text content, often has formatting errors; automatic repair and validation steps must be added to the pipeline
General Issues 15. The Hugo command cannot be found in a Windows environment. The merge step in daily_summary.py calls website/update.ps1 fails because “hugo” is not recognized Solution: Hugo 0.157.0 was installed via winget. The installation prompt suggests restarting the shell; after restarting PowerShell, the Hugo command can be used normally
Key Insight: In a Windows environment, command-line tools installed via winget require restarting the shell for PATH updates to take effect, and cannot be used immediately in the same session
Human and Artificial Intelligence Approaches Strategic Level BC-RNN RP anomaly diagnosis strategy Role Method Human The user noticed that BC-RNN SR was close to 0% during M14, which does not match the training progress. It directly suggests that there may be an issue with the evaluation metrics and requires a systematic check of the metric calculation logic Artificial Intelligence The AI initially tends to explain that “error recovery is essentially difficult”. It tries to interpret low SR as expected results rather than prioritizing the investigation of issues in the evaluation code Difference Analysis: Humans infer evaluation problems based on normal behavior observed during training, while AI tends to rationalize abnormal data. Human intuition is more accurate, and ultimately 4 cascading issues causing metric distortion were identified
Risk assessment before training starts Role Method Human After Phoenix training started, the user immediately noticed a serious estimation error in training duration (13.5 days) and stopped promptly, requesting replanning to avoid resource waste Artificial Intelligence The AI did not fully verify the actual size of the dataset (mistakenly treating 16K as 100K), nor verified the step time (7.2 seconds/step) and total steps (161,000 steps) before training started, leading to a serious estimation error in duration Difference Analysis: Humans are better at risk control and timely stoppage, while AI tends to ignore verification of resource consumption during task execution
Design of paper-reading workflow Role Method Human The user proposed a two-stage reading strategy—a quick filtering stage (30 seconds to decide whether in-depth reading is needed) and an in-depth understanding stage (identifying 3 core points: motivation/approach insight/experiment design/limitations) Artificial Intelligence The AI initially designed a single-stage full evaluation, sending the complete abstracts of all 50 papers to the LLM for evaluation at once Difference Analysis: Humans design based on the cognitive load of actual researchers, recognizing that quick filtering and in-depth reading require different levels of information. AI tends to process everything at once, ignoring the trade-off between tokens cost and evaluation depth
Debugging configuration errors in projects Role Method Human The user provided the path of overview.md and asked the AI to “fix the format”; but no root cause was diagnosed Artificial Intelligence The AI found 3 interrelated errors through code tracking: ID mismatch, header format, lack of markers Difference Analysis: The systematic code analysis by AI revealed cascading issues that the user could not see; the user correctly identified the symptom (“cannot read overview”) but failed to find the cause
Iterative decision-making for Window layer solutions Role Method Human The user directly rejected the.floating solution from a user experience perspective (“do not always be on top”). After the AI proposed a non-interactive.documentsWindow, it was decided to use the.normal layer Artificial Intelligence The AI tried various technical solutions: first using.floating to ensure interactivity, then abandoned hierarchical changes (retained.documentsWindow), later considered non-interactive solutions, and finally waited for user instructions Key Insight: The human decision-making process directly addresses user experience issues; the AI’s approach of introducing non-interactive elements is flawed.Difference Analysis: Humans quickly discard solutions that do not meet user experience and expected behavior, while AI conducts iterative experiments through technical implementation | Role | Method | |——|——| | Humans | Users describe their needs (“build a project from overview.md”, “modify daily report”, “remove duplicates”), but need AI to propose implementation plans | | AI | AI proposes multiple options for clarification (such as the difference between init –from-overview and substitution, removing duplicates by ID vs. content hash), and then implements them |
Difference Analysis: Users have clear needs, but need AI to explore implementation plans; AI correctly identifies ambiguity and proposes solutions instead of guessing
Identifying missing language configuration features Role Method Humans Users immediately identify UX issues (“too much English in the summary section”) and ask if language configuration is possible AI AI did not actively consider language configuration before the user asked; then implemented a comprehensive solution Difference Analysis: Users’ domain knowledge of bilingual academic workflows enables the discovery of gaps; AI requires a clear request
Implementation Level Adjustment to FLARE training task quantity Role Method Humans After AI started 9 training tasks, the user requested “reduce to 4 D0 tasks”, clearly stating only 4 D0 difficulty tasks are needed AI AI initially planned for a complete 9 tasks (3×D0 + 2×D1 + 1×D2) training, trying to complete all tasks at once Difference Analysis: Users prioritize the quality of completing D0 tasks based on resource and time trade-offs, while AI tends toward completeness
Limitations of AI Key limitations When diagnosing BC-RNN RP anomalies, AI initially tends to rationalize abnormal data (“error recovery is essentially difficult”) rather than prioritizing the evaluation of errors in the code. PCA performs task-related dimensionality reduction, and maximizing variance corresponds to maximizing cluster separation. This conclusion is validated by Microsoft and multiple papers, as well as MIHD’s own data (PCA has ARI of 0.261, while scGPT has 0.170, a 54% difference). The bias in evaluation metrics is usually not a single error, but a chain reaction of multiple errors: BC-RNN has demo_len=0, trigger_step=0, transport always False, and the successful scenario RP drops to 0.5 due to four errors, actually reaching 0.003. End-to-end validation is needed, not isolated unit tests. The macOS window layer not only controls visual Z order but also controls event routing permissions: .desktopWindow layer (below desktop icons) does not receive user input events, and the .normal layer at a higher level must be used for true interactive “browsing mode”; this is a system-level constraint, not an API configuration issue. When designing automated paper management tools, the actual cognitive process of human researchers should be imitated: quick screening (relevance + novelty + source authority) → deep analysis (core insights + problem definition + experimental design + limitations), rather than a full evaluation at once. h5py file processing cannot be shared between fork subprocesses (this is a limitation of PyTorch DataLoader); the only safe solution is to pre-load the main process into numpy before forking. NFS random read speed is much lower than sequential read speed, and loading once is 10 times faster than on-demand loading; using uint8 type can also save 4 times more memory. Before starting large-scale training, the size of the actual dataset, time per step, and total number of steps must be verified to avoid resource waste; in the Phoenix MPM training case, the dataset size estimation was incorrect (160K → 1M), resulting in a training time of 13.5 days—a serious error, highlighting the importance of early validation. Command-line tool parameter configuration should use a layered parsing strategy: CLI flags > specific project configuration > user-level global configuration > hard-coded defaults, which provides flexibility while maintaining reasonable defaults. The design of batch document generation tools requires a two-stage architecture: the export stage locally parses raw data on each device, and the merge stage combines data across devices; when the number of daily sessions is particularly large, an “internal merge” step is needed to eliminate duplicate content and combine multiple outputs from the same day. The solution to priority conflicts in conda environments shared by multiple users is: set PYTHONPATH=/path/to/user/src:$PYTHONPATH during script execution, loading user’s own source code copies first without affecting other users, and no need to create a separate environment. Language configuration for LLM processes should be injected at the prompt level, not later in processing; different parts of the output require different rules (e.g., JSON keys remain in English, content is expressed in the target language). Extracting structured data from documents is very suitable for LLMs; OVERVIEW_EXTRACT_PROMPT can reliably parse overview.md, extracting title/keywords/categories/problems. Pipeline regular expression patterns must match exactly; “## 3. Current technical route” will not match “##\s*Current methods and progress”; template-driven architecture needs strict format compliance. arXiv search results are returned in reverse chronological order; a continuous known paper counter is an effective early stopping heuristic because it indicates that the processed time range has been reached. Daily Report — 2026-03-06 Daily Summary Completed Work: Responsible for the development of six major projects, including spatial transcriptome analysis, debugging and documentation of life management chatbot, refactoring the robot control benchmark codebase, designing training workflows, and containerized simulation rendering. Execution Methods: Using parallel multi-agent exploration techniques to quickly understand the codebase, systematic code tracking for data pipelines and context management, restructuring the project structure based on symbolic links, matching Docker rendering drivers and library versions, and establishing a comprehensive design and training infrastructure. Impact: Resolved critical data format issues that affect research, diagnosed and designed solutions for user context loss, wrote a complete 1674-line tutorial, achieved 99% disk reduction (from 78GB to 37MB) through restructuring the research project, resolved obstacles in Docker GPU rendering during robot simulation evaluation, optimized the content of 67 lines of documentation, and built an end-to-end training workflow covering 9 tasks, while adopting resource optimization strategies. DCC Completed Work: Analyzed the standardization and preprocessing workflows in ContraVAE and STHD spatial transcriptome projects, clarifying the data format and processing steps. Execution Methods: Checked h5ad files, tracked preprocessing scripts, verified data features to trace the entire process from raw counts to standardized expression matrices. Impact: Eliminated user confusion about data formats, confirmed the meaning and handling of X matrices, layers[‘counts’], HVG selections, and spatial coordinates under different preprocessing methods. TzJsDesktop Completed Work: Fixed the context loss issue of CalendarPro Discord robot, and wrote a 1674-line Chinese tutorial covering end-users and developers. Execution Methods: Used parallel agents to explore dialogue history management, intent classification, and AI provider call chains, designed context-based solutions; systematically extracted all configurations, commands, and architectures to generate structured tutorials. Impact: Identified three root causes of robot forgetting problems (keyword pre-checking, timing selection, lack of historical parameters), and developed feasible solutions; created complete documentation resources including a user guide (60%) and a developer guide (40%). tianhe Completed Work: Optimized the error_recovery_benchmark CLAUDE.md document, re-designed the motion-based self-reflection framework as an independent Phoenix/FLARE project, set up a shared dependency project structure, designed a complete training workflow covering 9 MimicGen tasks, created CALVIN documentation, resolved SAPIEN rendering errors in Docker, and recorded RoboTwin simulation architecture. Execution Methods: Simplified document redundancy, achieved directory separation using symbolic links, reducing disk usage by 99%, explored the training framework architecture, and wrote 7 scripts (data generation, conversion, training, evaluation, orchestration), matched driver and library versions for Vulkan/OpenGL stack and environment configuration, and tracked multi-layer simulation code. Impact: Reduced the number of documents from 225 lines to 167 lines, improved readability, established maintainable project structures (Phoenix 37MB, FLARE 368KB, shared dependencies 9.3GB), built an end-to-end training workflow including missing configuration completion and checkpoint reuse strategies, resolved critical Docker rendering obstacles that prevent model evaluation, and recorded complex code libraries for beginners. Cross-project collaboration covered spatial transcriptome data analysis, CalendarPro bug fixes, comprehensive documentation writing, robot learning codebase refactoring, Docker rendering stack issues, and Phoenix/FLARE training workflow design.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Analyzed spatial transcriptome data preprocessing workflows — Traced the standardization steps in ContraVAE and STHD projects, clarified the relationship between X matrices and layers[‘counts’], HVG selection, and spatial coordinate systems. ✅ Diagnosed CalendarPro context loss issues — Identified three layers of problems that cause robots to lose subsequent message context, and developed solutions. ✅ Designed Phoenix/FLARE 9 task training plans — Established complete training infrastructure for the Phoenix diffusion strategy and FLARE retry framework, covering all MimicGen tasks. ✅ Resolved SAPIEN rendering errors in Docker containers — Diagnosed and fixed the “rendering error” that prevents robot simulation evaluation. The root cause is the lack of NVIDIA Vulkan/OpenGL libraries in Docker. Downloaded matching drivers (535.104.12), extracted library files, and configured VK_ICD_FILENAMES and LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variables. ✅ Wrote a comprehensive Chinese tutorial on CalendarPro — Created a 1674-line document/TUTORIAL.md covering installation, features, CLI/Discord commands, architecture, and developer guides. ✅ Separated Phoenix and FLARE projects and used shared dependency management — Re-designed the motion-based self-reflection framework as two independent projects (Phoenix for self-reflection, FLARE for failure guidance reset), using symbolic links to share dependencies of 9 packages. By symbolically linking large data/checkpoint directories to archive files, disk usage for each project reduced from 78GB to 37MB. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Created Phoenix training scripts — Built SLURM jobs scripts for Phoenix multi-task diffusion strategy training. ✅ Created FLARE data generation and training scripts — Built预热 data generation, LeRobot conversion, training, and evaluation scripts for FLARE workflows. ✅ Recorded RoboTwin data collection and simulation architecture — Explained the two-stage data collection process (seed search + replay with deterministic seeds) in detail, and traced the complete simulation execution flow using the place_dual_shoes task as an example. ✅ Optimized error_recovery_benchmark CLAUDE.md document — Reduced the number of lines from 225 to 167 by removing command sections, adding detailed PYTHONPATH information, and simplifying references. ✅ Completed OpenPI training configuration — Added missing fine-tuning and interpretation configurations for coffee_task_D1, stack_three_task_D1, and three_piece_assembly_task_D1. ✅ Fixed frozen dataclass mutation errors during policy loading — Resolved the FrozenInstanceError issue when loading pi05 policies. Fixed it by using dataclasses.replace() to replace direct attribute assignments, and also resolved path duplication issues in norm_stats loading. ✅ Created CLAUDE.md document to describe CALVIN project — Studied the CALVIN codebase (combining actions from language and vision), and wrote a complete project document covering architecture, build/test commands, Hydra configuration system, and MCIL model workflow. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. CalendarPro robot cannot understand subsequent messages, such as “What time did you schedule?”Solution: Identified three layers of problems: (1) General keyword pre-checking occurs before the AI sees dialogue history; (2) The pre-check uses overly broad keywords like “What time is it now”; (3) Historical data parameters are not passed in provider calls. The designed fix removes pre-check bypass behavior and passes the complete dialogue history to the AI. Key Insight: Context loss is usually a multi-layer issue: data not collected → data not passed → data not used. One must trace the entire call chain from storage, through provider interfaces, to prompt construction.
2. SAPIEN encounters “rendering error” in headless Docker container — RuntimeError: Could not find rendering device Solution: Found that the NVIDIA Vulkan/OpenGL rendering library (libGLX_nvidia.so, etc.) is missing. The container has CUDA computation libraries but no rendering stack. Downloaded matching NVIDIA driver version 535.104.12 to match the kernel driver, extracted the library into the user directory, and configured VK_ICD_FILENAMES and LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variables in eval.sh.
Key Insight: Docker containers with NVIDIA GPU require CUDA runtime and Vulkan/OpenGL libraries for graphical simulation. The driver version must fully match both the kernel module and user-space libraries; otherwise, Vulkan ICD cannot be loaded.
3. Phoenix training checkpoints exist in zhaoganlong’s directory; unclear whether they should be reused or retrained Solution: Users suggested checking existing checkpoints and creating symbolic links if available, training the missing parts only on the free GPU of an53.
Key Insight: Before designing the training plan, one must inventory existing resources (checkpoints, datasets, configurations) to avoid wasting computational resources. First establish a checkpoint reuse strategy.
4. Users believe standardized data comes from STHD workflow, but data characteristics do not match the workflow code Solution: Code analysis revealed that STHD does not perform standardization—it uses raw counts directly. The standardized data users see comes from external scanpy preprocessing (normalize_total + log1p).
Key Insight: It is necessary to distinguish internal workflow processing from external preprocessing. Code inspection is more reliable than assumptions based on data appearance.
General Issues 5. Missing pre-training configurations for 3 of the 9 MimicGen tasks in OpenPI configuration Solution: Used add_finetune_config and add_inference_config helper functions to add fine-tuning and inference configurations for coffee_task_D1, stack_three_task_D1, and three_piece_assembly_task_D1.
Key Insight: Use configuration generation functions to maintain consistency in task configurations instead of manual copying.
6. FrozenInstanceError: Unable to assign values to the field ‘asset_id’ in policy_config.py Solution: DataConfig was defined as @dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True), making it unchangeable. Used dataclasses.replace(data_config, asset_id=value) to replace direct assignment (data_config.asset_id = value), creating a new instance.
Key Insight: Frozen data classes enforce immutability at the language level—modifications require using dataclasses.replace() to create a new instance, rather than modifying in place.
7. FileNotFoundError, path duplication: assets/norm_stats.json/norm_stats.json Solution: When providing robotwin_repo_id, asset_id was incorrectly set to ’norm_stats.json’ (file name instead of directory). The modified code directly uses normalize.load() from the assets/ directory to load data, without adding the asset_id subdirectory.
Key Insight: Path construction errors usually occur due to mixing directory identifiers with file names. Explicitly handling special cases (local files and remote repositories) can prevent path duplication.
8. MulticoreTSNE build failed due to incompatible CMake version (system 3.26.4 is incompatible with required version <= 3.18) Solution: Found that MulticoreTSNE is only used for optional TSNE visualization, not core training/ evaluation. Suggested disabling dependencies to allow continued installation (user refused this approach).
Key Insight: It is necessary to distinguish critical dependencies from optional visualization tools. In research code, skipping non-essential dependencies that cause build issues is usually feasible.
Human and Artificial Intelligence Approaches Strategic Level Detecting robot context loss from user experience Role Method Human Users observed that the robot fails when answering “What time is it now?” from the end-user perspective Artificial Intelligence Diagnosed root causes by analyzing code layer by layer: keyword pre-check mechanism, passing historical data in provider calls, and double verification of intent streams Reusing checkpoints before training Role Method Human Users indicate that existing checkpoints should be reused via symbolic links, and only the missing parts are trained, considering resource efficiency Artificial Intelligence The AI designs a complete training plan from scratch without checking existing checkpoints first Difference Analysis: Humans have cost awareness and practical limitations; artificial intelligence tends to adopt clean implementation methods. Before planning new work, existing resources should be counted first.
Implementation Level Installing NVIDIA libraries in a restricted Docker environment Role Method Human Due to container security settings, users immediately know that apt-get must be accessed via a custom path/app/ubuntu/bin/apt-get Artificial Intelligence The AI initially tried using the standard apt-get command, but this would fail or require sudo privileges Difference Analysis: Humans have domain knowledge about package manager configurations for specific containers, which cannot be found in the code repository. The AI learns this through user corrections.
Identifying the target audience of the tutorial Role Method Human Users clearly understand that the tutorial should serve both end-users and developers Artificial Intelligence The AI initially asked the user/developer, rather than inferring from existing documents (README is for users, CLAUDE.md is for developers), and found a comprehensive tutorial needed to bridge the gap between them Difference Analysis: Users have a clearer understanding of project requirements; artificial intelligence should infer missing documentation content from existing distribution versions, rather than raising obvious questions.
Handling dependency conflicts of MulticoreTSNE Role Method Human Users rejected the idea of editing files to comment out MulticoreTSNE and may prefer installing the software in a different way or accept this limitation Artificial Intelligence The AI immediately suggested editing requirements.txt to remove problematic dependencies as a quick solution AI Limitations Key Limitations No check of existing checkpoints was performed during training plan design—users should be reminded to consider reuse strategies. Resources should be counted before implementation. The initial attempt was to install the NVIDIA graphics library (libnvidia-gl-535), but no version compatibility check for kernel drivers was done, resulting in version mismatch (535.288.01 vs 535.104.12). Multiple attempts were needed to find the correct way to download drivers and extract libraries. General Limitations Although the conversation history exploration is comprehensive, 3 parallel agents are required to identify the core issue that LLM calls do not receive historical parameters—if the initial exploration was more targeted, the problem could be found faster. A tutorial file of 1674 lines was directly created without previewing the structure for user confirmation—this method should be validated on large artifacts. test_render.py was modified by replacing the raw ’except:’ with ’except Exception as e:’ to print complete backtrace information, but this pattern (ignoring exceptions without logging) exists in the original code repository and was not introduced by AI. AI should have identified this anti-pattern earlier. Multiple/init commands ran similar explorations and analyses, but did not remember previous results—no session memory is maintained. A lot of time was spent on systematic exploration (searching commands, checking vulkaninfo)—if AI had a better understanding of common Docker+NVIDIA Vulkan setup patterns, this work could be shortened. Ultimately completed, but requires more steps than an expert would need. Lessons Learned Key Experiences Context loss requires tracking the complete call chain: data collection (conversation_history.json storage) → data transfer (provider call signature) → data usage (prompt construction). Missing any layer leads to context loss. Before designing a training plan, existing resources should be counted (checkpoints, datasets, configurations) and reuse strategies established to avoid wasting computational resources. Ask “what exists?” before “what should be built?” Running Docker containers for NVIDIA GPU work requires two different library sets: CUDA runtime (computation) and Vulkan/OpenGL (rendering). Many GPU-supported containers only have CUDA. For simulation frameworks like SAPIEN, the graphics API must be used, so both libraries must match the kernel driver exactly. In spatial transcriptomics data processing, adata.X can be a normalized value (scanpy pipeline) or raw counts (STHD pipeline)—code must be checked instead of assuming the data type based on context. Parallel multi-agent exploration can speed up understanding of complex codebases, but careful planning is needed to avoid redundant work. Use agents for independent dimensions (history management, message flow, provider interfaces) to avoid overlap. Two-stage data collection (seed discovery + deterministic replay) is a robust pattern in robot simulation: the first stage filters data that successfully completes tasks and saves the trajectory plan, the second stage uses the saved plan to re-execute and collect clean training data. This separates randomness from data quality. Dependency sharing via symbolic links can significantly reduce disk usage in large research projects (from 78GB to 37MB) while maintaining independent project structures. The key is using symbolic-linked data directories instead of copying, and using relative paths for portability. Core principle of documentation optimization: remove content that can be obtained otherwise (e.g., ‘make help’ for commands), and keep “global” insights that require cross-file understanding. Discovery of Vulkan ICD (installable client driver) requires the existence of nvidia_icd.json list and actual driver library, along with version matching. The VK_ICD_FILENAMES environment variable can override system search paths in containerized environments. Practical Experiences Python frozen data classes provide guaranteed runtime invariance, but explicit modification via dataclasses.replace() is required. Direct assignment triggers FrozenInstanceError. This pattern forces configuration objects to adopt functional programming style.
