Daily Report — 2026-03-05 Daily Summary Completed Work: Multiple projects executed concurrently on 4 devices: MIHD RM-IDEAL evaluation infrastructure, device documentation system, machine learning training process debugging, and CalendarPro autonomous smart upgrade. Implementation Methods: DCC runs long-running background computation tasks (RM-IDEAL cross-sample benchmark tests) and uses visual scripts; MacBook executes parallel research agents to generate documentation; Tianhe is responsible for environment setup and deep code analysis to identify machine learning vulnerabilities; TzJsDesktop implements a comprehensive personal assistant system with an event-driven architecture, including multi-agent coordination and systematic code quality audits. Impact: RM-IDEAL evaluation revealed specific embedding quality differences at key layers (Layer_1/5 performs well with ρ values of 0.42–0.66, Layer_3/6 shows negative correlation with ρ values of -0.21 to -0.36), providing guidance for subsequent optimization; the device received a monthly review mechanism and 676 lines of introductory guides; VLA training returned to normal, Openpi-moe normalization errors were fixed, avoiding scale mismatch issues; CalendarPro shifted from a passive scheduler to an active self-manager, 319 tests passed, but audits found critical technical debt that needs immediate fix. DCC Completed Work: MIHD project RM-IDEAL evaluation infrastructure: cross-sample benchmark tests 151673↔151508, writing visual scripts, optimizing project descriptions to highlight zero-sample/patch query functionality, and GPU acceleration planning. Implementation Methods: Performs long-term WWL+Wasserstein computations (3–4 hours per direction), writes three-panel visual scripts, iterates on project descriptions, emphasizes the necessity of zero-sample requirements, distinguishes it from STAIG end-to-end training, and starts the Plan agent for GPU Sinkhorn implementation design. Impact: Completed bidirectional 7-tag evaluations for 151673↔151508, found the highest Spearman ρ value at 0.657 (only in Layer_4), and identified a negative correlation between intermediate layer embeddings and topological ranking. A narrative framework starting from clinical perspectives was established (patch query cross-patient knowledge transfer). MacBook Completed Work: Device toolkit documentation: February monthly data analysis and merging, writing a comprehensive Claude Code usage guide. Implementation Methods: Uses LLM to analyze JSON data of daily AI conversation reports for the entire month, generates structured summaries, starts 3 parallel research agents to collect Claude Code information, reads research results in planning mode, and then produces a 10-chapter 676-line guide. Impact: Established a systematic review mechanism for historical conversation data; Claude Code guide covers installation/functionality/integration/best practices/pricing, providing standard reference documents for the team. TzJsDesktop Completed Work: Comprehensive upgrade of CalendarPro personal assistant system (16 new services + 21 file modifications + 68 tests), followed by systematic code quality audits (3 incomplete implementations + 16 dangerous silent exception handlers + missing BackgroundCoordinator startup). Implementation Methods: Studied the reference code library (openclaw multi-agent ACP/gateway/plugin SDK, get-shit-done wave execution/context engineering/200K window), designed a 5-phase 31-subgoal implementation plan, used parallel background agents to handle independent modules, directly modified coupled files, and then started specialized exploration agents (TODO/FIXME search, git analysis, exception auditing) to detect hidden issues. Impact: Transformed CalendarPro from a passive tool into an autonomous smart assistant with active task discovery, cross-domain recommendations, and autonomous decision-making capabilities; 319 tests verified core functionality; however, audits found critical technical debt (incomplete executor logic, over 50 masked errors, services never started), requiring immediate fix to ensure system reliability. Tianhe Completed Work: Fixed VLA training curobo installation environment issues, debugged Openpi-moe training normalization errors causing scale mismatch in trajectory VAE, and planned to separate Phoenix/FLARE projects (not executed). Implementation Methods: Analyzed CUDA header paths in conda environment, set CPLU_INCLUDE_PATH/C_INCLUDE_PATH for compilation; tracked data normalization process through multiple source files, found apply_tree(strict=False) silently skips missing keys; designed a shared dependency architecture for two intertwined projects. Impact: Made VLA training environment setup possible; identified and fixed a critical error: in trajectory VAE training, unnormalized prevActions are connected to normalized actions due to the lack of norm_stats.json key and overly permissive default behavior of apply_tree(). Parallel development across devices involved MIHD spatial transcriptomics (RM-IDEAL cross-sample benchmark tests revealing layer-specific performance patterns), device toolkit enhancement (monthly summaries + Claude Code comprehensive guide), VLA/Openpi-moe training process debugging (curobo installation + normalization error fixes), and comprehensive upgrade of CalendarPro personal assistant system (31 subgoals implemented, 16 new services, followed by systematic code audits to identify critical errors and dangerous exception handlers).
Tasks Architecture and Strategy - ✅ Implement comprehensive upgrade of CalendarPro personal assistant system — 31 subgoals completed across 5 phases: autonomous smart engine (situation_monitor, gap_analyzer, autonomous_executor, reminder_evaluator, context_detector), deep thinking processing (perspective_analyzer, goal_tracker, conversation_summarizer), comprehensive life management (sleep_service, diet nutrition), learning adaptation (preference_learner, time-slot efficiency), multi-agent coordination (agent_registry, agent_protocol, wave_executor, monitoring_agent). 21 core files were modified (9 event hooks, 15+ settings, 3 IntentTypes, 3-layer context assemblers) and 16 new service files were created. Its effectiveness was verified through 319 tests. ✅ RM-IDEAL cross-sample benchmark tests: bidirectional evaluation 151673↔151508 — Conducted PCA+UNI2+STAIG_fusion cross-sample RM-IDEAL evaluation, with bidirectional evaluations 151673→151508 and 151508→151673, each direction requiring about 3–4 hours of background computation. Layer_1/5 showed best performance (Spearman ρ 0.42–0.66, SL@50 reached 0.94–1.00), while Layer_3/6 showed negative correlation (ρ -0.21 to -0.36), and P@K was uniform at 0, indicating no exact overlap in positions but consistent overall ranking trends. ✅ Debugging normalization issues in Openpi-moe training — Identified why the missing prev_actions key in norm_stats.json does not cause errors during training. Found that apply_tree(strict=False) silently skips normalization of missing keys, leading to scale mismatch between normalized actions and unnormalized prevActions in trajectory VAE. By modifying compute_norm_stats.py to dynamically detect and calculate prevActions statistics, this issue was resolved. ✅ Multiple rounds of optimization for 5-sentence description of MIHD project — Human-led narrative architecture adjustments, with iterative language optimization using AI. The final version starts from clinical perspectives (cross-patient knowledge transfer), emphasizes the necessity of zero-sample requirements (basic difference from STAIG end-to-end training), highlights gap-filling work (first systematic evaluation), key findings (performance close to retraining methods), and value enhancement (moving toward clinical paradigms). Each sentence was compressed into two short subphrases for clear logic. 🔄 GPU-accelerated RM-IDEAL optimal transmission planning — Current RM-IDEAL uses CPU EMD computation from POT library as a performance bottleneck (about 4000 WWL+Wasserstein computations per point). The Plan agent was introduced to design GPU Sinkhorn approximation algorithms, and exploration into using GeomLoss or geomloss library for GPU parallel batch OT aims to reduce single-sample evaluation time from hours to minutes. ✅ Code quality audit and identification of critical vulnerabilities in CalendarPro — A specialized exploration agent systematically audited the code library. Some key issues were found: incomplete executor.execute_step() loop (lines 158–161 only return ‘pass’), stub get_progress() returning None, unimplemented _learn_meal_preferences() placeholder, and 16 dangerous silent exception handlers (all exceptions except Exception are directly handled via pass). These exception handlers appear in situation_monitor(5), context_detector(5), agent_registry(5), autonomous_executor(3), life_context(2), scheduler(1), energy_projection(1), and Missing BackgroundCoordinator.start_all(), causing all background services to fail. ✅ Fixing critical vulnerabilities and dangerous exception handlers in CalendarPro — Three unimplemented methods were fixed (removed useless executor loop, implemented get_progress() returning execution status, implemented learn_from_history() based on more than 3 data points for meal time learning). 16 silent exception handlers were replaced with logger.error/warning, and missing log import statements were added to scheduler.py. After fixing, all 319 tests passed. ✅ Writing viz_rm_ideal_151673_151508.py visual script — Created the viz_rm_ideal_151673_151508.py visual script for Layer_3 niche queries in the 151673→151508 direction, generating a three-panel comparison chart: Ground Truth annotations in reference section, RM-IDEAL score heatmap (structural similarity Ground Truth), and embedding cosine similarity heatmap, enabling intuitive evaluation of spatial topology capture ability of fused embeddings. ✅ Writing comprehensive Claude Code usage guide — Started 3 parallel research agents to collect official Claude Code documentation, best practices, and AI agent workflow information. Read research results in planning mode, then generated a 676-line complete guide claude-code-guide.md covering 10 chapters (definition/installation/functionality/integration/usage/capabilities/limitations/best practices/pricing) and quick reference cards, suitable as standard documentation for team onboarding. 🔄 Separation of Plan Phoenix/FLARE projects — Developed a detailed plan to separate two intertwined projects (Phoenix MPM/MCM motion framework and FLARE retry reset framework) from the mixed 1TB repository, placing them in independent directories while maintaining shared dependencies. The plan includes file categorization, large data symbolic link strategy (about 789G mimicgen, 245G openpi), and updates to CLAUDE.md. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Generation and merging of February 2026 monthly summary — Used LLM to analyze JSON data of daily AI conversation reports for the entire month, generating a monthly summary according to project overview/key achievements/repeated issues/AI collaboration trends/learning summary structure, then merging independent summaries from multiple time periods into a complete monthly report, supporting long-term work review and reflection. ✅ Installing curobo library in RefineVLA’s conda environment — Resolved CUDA header path issue by pointing CPLU_INCLUDE_PATH and C_INCLUDE_PATH to the CUDA package targets/x86_64-linux/include directory in the conda environment, fixing curobo compilation failures.Key insight: Python package init.py does not need an immediate import statement; for packages with circular dependencies, lazy loading combined with documentation comments is better;Interface exposure at the package level does not equate to mandatory immediate loading. 3. 16 dangerous exception handling: Using except Exception as the error handling method results in an incomplete state, but the system still appears to function normally, and the error source cannot be identified during debugging.Solution: Replace error handling with except Exception as e: logger.error/warning(f"Description: {e}"), retain error information for diagnosis, and distinguish between errors (critical functions) and warnings (secondary functions). Key Insight: Never use an empty pass to handle exceptions; if exceptions must be ignored, at least log them; silent failures in the state tracking layer lead to “Schrödinger states”—it is impossible to determine whether it is truly empty or a loading failure.
4. How to efficiently implement a major upgrade plan involving 31 targets without creating sequential bottlenecks? Solution: Adopt a parallel backend proxy execution mode: launch 4 independent proxies simultaneously to improve context_detector, checkin_service, learning_service, and energy_projection, while directly modifying another 8 files. All proxies completed successfully without conflicts.
Key Insight: Wave-based parallel execution can significantly accelerate large-scale refactoring when dependencies are properly isolated. The key is to identify independent work units that can actually be executed concurrently.
5. AI tried multiple times to enter the planning mode, but users prefer direct execution. Solution: The user rejected the call to the ExitPlanMode tool and directly provided the plan for AI to execute. AI read the results of the previous research proxy in planning mode, then directly wrote the documentation without replanning.
Key Insight: The user’s working style favors rapid iteration rather than long-term planning; AI should adaptively reduce the trigger frequency of planning mode, or learn this preference after multiple user rejections.
6. CalendarPro has 6 completely untested source files, 12 modified files containing untested new methods, while BackgroundCoordinator is implemented but never started. Solution: Created a testing infrastructure for the system: conftest.py for shared fixtures, 20 new test files created based on existing patterns (pytest, AsyncMock, patch decorator), fixed the on_ready() function so it actually calls coordinator.start_all(), and added 9 missing Discord intent processors.
Key Insight: Large-scale functions usually come with incomplete integration. Background services require a clear startup call, not just class definitions. System testing needs shared fixtures and consistent patterns across all test files.
7. The patch path in the testing fixture is incorrect (patch to the call point instead of the definition point), causing simulation failures after lazy loading, and multiple tests reported AttributeError. Solution: All singleton factory function patches (e.g., get_settings, get_calendar_service) must be placed in the source module (src.config/src.services.calendar_service), not at the call point (e.g., src.services.gap_analyzer), because lazy loading delays name binding.
Key Insight: The golden rule of unittest.mock.patch—patch to the location where it is looked up, not the definition location; lazy loading means the “lookup” location is always the source module, and no new bindings are created at the import location.
8. How to detect hidden errors and incomplete implementations after major refactoring in a large code base? Solution: Started multiple specialized exploration proxies: TODO/FIXME searcher, git status analyzer, test gap detector, and exception handler auditor. Multi-angle auditing of the system revealed key issues: incomplete executor loops, stub get_progress, unimplemented dietary preference learning, and more than 50 dangerous silent exception handlers.
Key Insight: Code auditing requires multi-dimensional searching across the system: static analysis (TODO, NotImplementedError), behavior analysis (exception handlers, empty loops), and integration analysis (service registration, startup hooks). A single-angle audit will miss certain types of errors.
Common Questions 9. RM-IDEAL computation is very time-consuming (3–4 hours per direction, approximately 3500–4000 positions × 7 tags × WWL+Wasserstein). Solution: Submit background tasks with run_in_background=true, regularly check progress via TaskOutput, and cache files (number of completed layers and file modification timestamps) to avoid blocking interaction.
Key Insight: Long computation tasks should run in the background and be monitored via file system status, not through stdout, because stdout may fail due to redirection issues and is unreliable.
10. The user mistakenly considers ID 151508 in the DLPFC part as 151608. Solution: AI actively confirmed the valid range of partial IDs (151508–151510 and 151669–151676), asked if the user meant 151508, and got confirmation before continuing.
Key Insight: AI should actively verify obviously unreasonable inputs and provide friendly corrections instead of blindly executing.
11. The path of the background task output file does not exist (/tmp/claude-1549010/...bvwfk6yeq.output). Solution: Although reading the output file failed, the calculation results of RM-IDEAL are correctly saved in outputs/rm_ideal_benchmark/ (e.g., summary.csv, detailed_results.json, rm_cache/*.npy), and it is possible to read data directly from the result files.
Key Insight: The actual output of background tasks (persistent files) are more reliable than temporary stdout logs; priority should be given to checking final results rather than intermediate logs.
12. curobo compilation fails with “cuda_runtime_api.h: No such file or directory”, even though the CUDA package is installed in the RefineVLA Conda environment. Solution: The CUDA header file is located in a non-standard path (targets/x86_64-linux/include instead of include/). This issue was resolved by setting the CPLU_INCLUDE_PATH and C_INCLUDE_PATH environment variables before pip installation.
Key Insight: Conda安装的 CUDA packages may place the header file in a subdirectory of a specific architecture, not a standard path. Always use the find command to check the actual header location before assuming a standard path.
Human and Artificial Intelligence Approaches Strategic Level System Architecture Design—How to Build an Autonomous Smart Butler Human Method Sets high-level requirements (active task discovery, automatic state understanding, idle search thinking, morning/evening summary, automation of everything), specifies reference architectures (multiple proxies in openclaw, wave-based execution of get-shit-done), but does not specify specific implementation paths. AI Studied existing code bases and reference libraries, identified reusable infrastructure (EventBus/BackgroundCoordinator/ContextAssembler/CronScheduler), designed a 5-stage 31-subtarget layered plan, detailed 16 new files and 21 modified files, including specific logic and dependencies. Difference analysis: Humans handle visual and constraint setting (what + why + reference direction), while AI focuses on architecture mapping and planning design (how + dependency analysis); humans’ “reference these two code bases” avoids AI’s zero-design risk and provides validated patterns; AI’s layered planning (main targets → intermediate targets → subtargets) enables the execution of a large plan. Narrative Architecture Design for MIHD Project Description Human Method Emphasized three core benefits: zero-sample training (not full-end training in STAIG), clinical vision across patient knowledge transfer, filling the gap in zero-sample multimodal fusion benchmarks. Should start from clinical applications rather than technical details. Narrative thread: clinical vision → why zero-sample training is needed → how to implement → result validation → moving toward ideal goals. AI Initial version started with problem definition and method details, longer sentences (over 70 words), and many technical terms. Under human guidance, adjusted to: first sentence establishes clinical vision + existing gap, second sentence distinguishes STAIG, third sentence describes the method, fourth sentence reports findings, fifth sentence explains value. Each sentence was compressed into two short sentences. Difference analysis: Humans design information hierarchy from the perspective of target audience and communication effect; AI tends to pursue technical completeness and ignores narrative strategy and cognitive load. Human strategic thinking (attracting attention first, then explaining technology) contrasts with AI’s logical thinking (defining the problem first, then listing methods). Testing Strategy—Unit Tests and Full-End Manual Tests Human Method Interrupted AI’s long-running pytest, asked for progress, suggested “testing should be left to humans so as to send messages to the Discord robot”, requested a test list and testing method, emphasized verification of real user experience. AI Initially focused on unit tests (68 simulated tests, isolating component dependencies), using pytest to ensure code correctness; after interruption, changed to creating a manual test list for the Discord robot (29 functional items + 4 background validation items, divided into regression tests, new feature tests, passive function verification). Difference analysis: AI defaults to automatic unit tests to ensure correctness—this is best practice in engineering; humans emphasize full-end real user experience testing because unit tests can only verify “code correctness” and not “functionality meets expectations”; they complement each other—unit tests provide quick feedback, integration tests verify experience. Document Workflow Control Human Method Rejected AI’s entry into planning mode, directly provided the plan (10-chapter framework + validation requirements), asked AI to read results of the previous research proxy, then directly write the documentation. AI Defaultly enters planning mode for structured planning, but can adapt to direct execution mode after user rejection, transcribes research results from planning mode, and generates a 676-line complete document. Difference analysis: Humans prefer rapid iteration and direct execution; AI prefers structured planning. Humans establish workflow preferences through multiple tool rejections, while AI needs to learn and adapt this preference during the session. Debugging Strategy for Silent Normalization Failures Human Method User immediately suspects that training data uses unnormalized data, but cannot determine the specific location of failure. Requests systematic data flow tracking. AI Tracks code paths through multiple files (e.g., dataLoader.py → transforms.py → pi0_moe.py), finds the default value of strict=False in apply_tree, causing omitted keys to be silently skipped. Proposes immediate fix (add keys in norm_stats) and system improvement (verifying all expected keys). Difference analysis: Users focus on macro symptoms (scale mismatch), while AI conducts detailed code archaeology to find the root cause deep in the 4-layer structure of practical functions. Humans intuitively identify problem areas, while AI’s systematic search finds implementation errors. Interpretation of RM-IDEAL Evaluation Results Human Method Proposed evaluation requirements (cross-sample benchmark with 151673↔151508), focused on key findings (which layers perform well/badly, why Layer_3/6 shows negative correlation). AI Responsible for data extraction, table organization, statistical significance explanation, and hypothesis generation (intermediate and adjacent layers confused leading to negative correlation, P@K=0 indicates precise positions do not overlap, but overall ranking is consistent). Difference analysis: Clear division of labor: humans define evaluation goals and priorities, AI performs computation and pattern recognition. AI’s hypothesis generation helps humans understand data, but final interpretation remains with humans. Testing Creation Strategy for Large Code Bases Human Method User provides a structured plan, specifies the number of tests for each file category (B3: 6 untested files, B4: 12 modified files, B5: 3 integration tests), and requires implementation. AI Starts parallel backend proxies, creates test files simultaneously, and extends existing tests in the foreground. Uses conftest.py pattern from existing tests instead of creating new styles. Limitations of Artificial Intelligence Key Limitation – Overly Triggering the Planning Mode: The user repeatedly refused to enter the planning mode when writing Claude code, indicating that AI fails to adapt to the user’s preference for direct execution. AI should learn to determine the degree of user acceptance of the planning mode during the conversation and dynamically adjust the trigger threshold. AI developed a complete plan for stages 1 to 5 (31 sub-targets in total), but actual implementation only completed file creation and basic testing for stages 1 to 3. More than 10 file modifications in stage 4 (such as energy prediction trend analysis, learning service time efficiency, double verification correction learning, diet service nutrition reminders, context detector cross-conversation function, idle detector activity reasoning, etc.) as well as the integration of new intents for Discord bots (setting targets, query targets, processing decision logic) have not been completed. The user needs to explicitly ask about progress to understand this gap. Key integration points were not verified during implementation: BackgroundCoordinator never started in setuphook() or main.py, which means all 7 new background services (gap_analyzer, autonomous_executor, reminer_evaluator, recommendation_engine, preference_learner, conversation_summarizer, weekly_report) actually never ran. This flaw was only discovered during the post-implementation audit phase. The initial project description ignored core selling points: The AI draft starts with technical details and problem definitions, with long sentences, without highlighting key differences such as zero样本/patch query/STAIG. Multiple manual instructions were needed to establish the correct narrative framework. When exploring a 1TB repository to separate Phoenix/FLARE, AI repeatedly ran commands to understand the directory structure, but encountered difficulties in distinguishing which files belong to which project. Multiple explorations were required to solve the problem, and if more information had been obtained in advance, these exploration processes could have been simplified. Overall Constraints Failed reading of output file from background task: The output_file path returned by TaskOutput (/tmp/claude-1549010/) does not exist, but the actual result is correctly saved. AI should prioritize checking the persistent output (output directory) of tasks rather than temporary stdout logs. During fixing the testing environment, AI constantly tried different patch paths (srcServices.gap_analyzer.get_calendar_service → srcServices.calendar_service.get_calendar_service → src.config.get_settings). After a one-time lazy loading (source module must be fixed), AI failed to understand the correct patch strategy, leading to multiple editing test cycles. The pytest-asyncio configuration was incorrect from the start (no asyncio_mode setting, tests used pytest.mark.asyncio but warned as unknown marker). AI spent several rounds realizing that [tool.pytest.ini_options] asyncio_mode=“auto” needed to be added to pyproject.toml, and pytest-asyncio was installed manually without immediate configuration check. Lessons Learned Key Lessons – The combination of EventBus, BackgroundCoordinator, and ContextAssembler is a powerful pattern for building modular AI assistants: EventBus enables service decoupled communication (publish-subscribe), BackgroundCoordinator manages the lifecycle of cron tasks uniformly (CronScheduler+conditional loading), and ContextAssembler dynamically loads the context layer based on intent type (avoiding full data transfer each time). These three components together support collaboration among more than 16 independent services. Spearman correlation of RM-IDEAL shows significant directional asymmetry: The ρ coefficient of Layer_4 between 151508→151673 is 0.657, while the reverse relationship between 151673→151508 is only 0.275. This indicates differences in fused embedding space for structural representations of the same label across different samples, which may be related to sample point density, noise level, or annotation quality. The topological ranking of intermediate layers (Layer_3/6) in the embedding space shows negative correlations (ρ -0.21 to -0.36): This may be because these layers are confused with adjacent layers (Layer_2/4/5) in the embedding space, resulting in the RM-IDEAL ranking based on embedding being opposite to that based on topology. This indicates that boundary layers (Layer_1/WM) and central layers (Layer_5) are easier to distinguish, while intermediate transition layers require stronger discriminative features. The data preprocessing process needs clear verification to ensure all expected features have standardized statistical information. Silent skipping (strict=False) may propagate scale mismatch issues throughout the training process without causing errors. For large refactoring projects, referring to mature open-source project architectures (such as openclaw’s ACP spawn/Gateway/plugin SDK, get-shit-done’s wave execution/context engineering/200K window) is more reliable than zero design; however, it is necessary to adapt to idioms of the target language (such as async/await from TypeScript→Python, singleton factory functions, dataclass), and direct copying is not possible. Unit tests (isolated components, simulated dependencies, rapid feedback) and integration tests (real Discord bot interactions, end-to-end experience) are two complementary dimensions: the former ensures code correctness (319 test cases passed), while the latter ensures user experience meets expectations (29 manual test items); passing 68 unit tests does not mean the system is ready, real user scenarios must be verified. Dangerous silent exception handling (only handling exceptions: pass) is a technical debt poison: it makes the system appear operating normally, but actually the state is incomplete (situation_monitor’s energy/diet/exercise/thinks/reminders may all be empty), and the source of errors cannot be found during debugging (Schrödinger state); exceptions should always be logged (logger.error/warning), distinguishing key functions (errors) from secondary functions (warnings), and diagnostic information should be retained. Large-scale refactoring should gradually verify key integration points (service startup, event connection, data persistence) rather than implementing all features first and then testing. The “implement all features first, then test” approach creates systems that exist but cannot run properly (services exist but never start). Project description narrative strategy: External communication should start from aspects relevant to the target audience’s application scenarios (such as clinical patch query knowledge transfer), then explain the technical path and key differences (zero-sample vs end-to-end training), and finally elevate to domain value. Technical details serve the narrative logic, not the opposite. Control each sentence within double short clauses to reduce cognitive load. Daily Report — 2026-03-04 Daily Overview Completed work: Cross-device multi-project work, including space transcriptomics literature research, document improvement, large-scale VLA training infrastructure setup, and comprehensive error recovery benchmark documentation synchronization. Methods of completion: DCC: Web-based Arxiv paper analysis to extract evaluation methods; MacBook: Codebase analysis via /init commands for document auditing; tianhe: Parallel agent exploration to align codebases and documents, checkpoint inventory through file system traversal, and multi-GPU training coordination planning. Impact: Improved document clarity and completeness, providing accurate file references and bilingual development workflow guides for future Claude code examples. tianhe Completed work: All-day time spent on zhaoganlong framework training setup, comprehensive error_recovery_benchmark documentation update, and BC-RNN performance investigation. Methods of completion: Created a 7-task implementation plan for the 6-phase training process, covering 9 MimicGen tasks; deployed 3 parallel exploration agents for codebase analysis; performed checkpoint inventory through file system traversal; systematically edited documents based on actual implementation; started comparison between BC-RNN training and evaluation. Impact: Laid the foundation for an 8× A800 GPU training activity lasting several weeks, with checkpoint locations confirmed; documents now match actual data, including accurate statistics, detailed API descriptions, and a three-source pipeline architecture; identified an abnormal 0% success rate for BC-RNN, requiring debugging. Multi-project research and documentation work: Studied the cross-sample query evaluation methods used in QueST papers for space transcriptomics, improved the CLAUDE.md documentation of Desktop Video, created a comprehensive zhaoganlong self-reflection framework training guide, and synchronized error_recovery_benchmark documents to match the actual codebase implementation, including a redesign of the pipeline architecture.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ zhaoganlong self-reflection framework training setup and documentation — Created a comprehensive 7-task implementation plan for all 6 phases (Phases 0–5: data preparation, diffusion strategy, LLaVA MPM, MCM feedback collection, LLaVA MCM, lifelong learning), performing 9 MimicGen tasks on 49 8× A800 GPUs. Recorded the complete training method, including a checkpoint list: Pi0.5 Phoenix (180GB, 21 steps, last modified on 2026-02-24), basic OpenPI model (about 12GB each), diffusion strategy snapshots (4, 253MB each). Started modifying 4 data preparation scripts to enable all tasks. Created docs/zhaoganlong_training_guide.md, which includes inference pipeline patterns and complete file path references. ✅ Updated the panoramic summary.md of error_recovery_benchmark project to match actual data — By deploying parallel agents, aligned the project overview documentation with the actual codebase: added detailed implementations for 6 detectors, 4 injectors, 4 validators, and 20 error classifiers, along with API descriptions; updated code statistics (scripts increased from 18 to 22, tests from 109 to 122, evaluation runs from 7 to 11); corrected M14 evaluation data (726 sets became 6,474 sets, ~83% completed, performance evaluation per strategy); corrected VLA model type (Pi0-FAST became Phoenix/Flare); recorded a plugin architecture with registration patterns. ✅ Redesigned the core pipeline architecture of error_recovery_benchmark — Updated Section 3.1 pipeline, showing three parallel error scenario sources: (1) playback and injection of demonstration datasets, (2) release and injection of VLA/strategies, (3) capture of natural failures—all fed into ErrorSceneDatabase. Resolved the issue where users believed the original diagram only showed paths based on demonstrations. Added explanations for the purpose and complementary relationships of each path. ✅ QueST cross-sample query evaluation method research — Obtained QueST paper (arxiv 2410.10652), and extracted the complete evaluation framework: used Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman graph kernel to build benchmarks from cell type labels, evaluated using top-1 accuracy for ecosystem matching accuracy and Pearson correlation with WWL benchmarks for overall similarity accuracy. Synthetic query experiment design used queries with 9 different cell types (1–3) and sizes (50–200 cells). Users corrected to use v3 instead of v1; confirmed the existence of v3, but no HTML version. 🔄 Investigation into the abnormal 0% success rate of BC-RNN — Users reported that BC-RNN had a 0% success rate on all normal tasks, despite expected success rates between 60–70% after training release. Started exploring differences between training and evaluation code (observation keys, environment settings, checkpoint loading), but stopped. Need to compare the release of training scripts with benchmark evaluation settings. Users mentioned a previously fixed “object” observation key issue—possibly related. Implementation and Fixes ❌ Review of ErrorSceneDatabase design — Users raised questions about the current database design. Discussed practical implementation (meta.json index, scene JSON+NPZ pair, deduplication, automatic classification, 4 segmentation strategies). Users felt some parts were “strange,” but abandoned discussion before identifying specific issues. ✅ Improvement of Desktop Video CLAUDE.md — Analyzed the codebase of Desktop Video via /init commands, identified three improvement areas in the existing CLAUDE.md, and implemented fixes: corrected case sensitivity issues in agents.md, added localization workflow hints (Localizable.xcstrings), enhanced ChangeLog format documentation, and adopted bilingual entry structure and date formatting. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. Mismatch between documentation and code in error_recovery_benchmark: The panoramic summary.md describes outdated pipelines, lacks implementation details, and statistical information is incorrect (726 sets vs. actual 6,474 sets) Solution: Deployed parallel exploration agents to thoroughly inspect the errorFramework/, scripts/, configs/, outputs/ directories, then systematically updated documentation with verified data: implementations of detectors/injectors/validators/classifiers, actual M14 evaluation data, and accurate code statistics. Key insight: In active projects, document changes are inevitable—a systematic code-document alignment process is needed. For large codebases, using parallel agents for exploration is effective: one agent per major directory, then integrating findings.
2. BC-RNN has a 0% success rate on all regular tasks (coffee, stack, thread, etc.), despite training results showing performance around 60–70% Solution: Started exploration but did not complete: Need to compare (1) observation dictionary keys between training and evaluation; (2) differences in environment initialization; (3) correctness of checkpoint loading; (4) consistency of action space. Users previously mentioned a fix for the “object” observation key issue—possibly related to BC-RNN.
Key insight: Mismatch between training and evaluation is a common failure mode. BC-RNN has a 0.28% success rate on error recovery tasks (5/1800 successes), but no success at all on regular tasks (0/250), indicating issues with environment or observation data, not the strategy itself. A systematic comparison list is needed: observation keys, environment configuration, action boundaries, camera settings, standardization.
3. zhaoganlong’s data preparation scripts only enable coffee_d1 task (other 8 tasks are commented out), hindering multi-task training Solution: Systematically uncomment all 9 tasks in TASK_MAPPING dictionary, removing pdb.settrace() debug breakpoints that would interrupt batch execution.
Key insight: The existing codebase is configured for a single-task prototype; to scale to a multi-task production environment, multiple task lists need to be enabled in the data pipeline, checkpoint paths, and orchestration scripts.
4. Flowcharts do not reflect users’ multi-source visual needs: Only demonstrates demonstration-based error injection, missing VLA injection and natural failure capture paths Solution: Rewritten Section 3.1 flowchart into three parallel paths (demonstration injection, strategy release injection, natural failure capture), all converging into ErrorSceneDatabase. Added explanations for the purpose of each path and how they complement each other.
Key insight: Visual diagrams must align with users’ mental models, not just code structure. Users’ concern about “VLA release injection during execution” indicates the feature exists in code but is ignored in documentation—missing documentation is as bad as incorrect documentation.
5. The PDF version of Arxiv papers returns binary-encoded content, making it impossible to directly extract methodological details Solution: Switch to using the HTML version provided by arxiv.org/html/2410.10652v1, which offers complete text and technical details.
Key insight: For Arxiv papers, the HTML version is easier for machines to read than PDF; always check the HTML version first.
6. zhaoganlong’s framework checkpoints are distributed across multiple locations (only Pi0.5 Phoenix has ~180GB checkpoints), and it is unclear which are usable Solution: Conducted a comprehensive file system search: found checkpoints in Pi0.5 Phoenix (21 steps, total 180GB, last modified on 2026-02-24), basic OpenPI checkpoints (pi0_base, pi05_base, pi0_fast_base, pi0_libero, each about 12GB), diffusion strategy checkpoints (4 snapshots, 253MB each, dated 2025-08-22). Confirmed all paths and sizes, and marked usable states.
Key insight: Checkpoint list is crucial for reproducibility. A large checkpoint directory (180GB) indicates many training steps—helpful for analysis, but need clear indication of steps used for evaluation. Date-based directory structure (2025-08-22, 2026-02-24) helps track training timeline.
General Issues 7. The user initially asked “How does this paper handle cross-sample queries?”—this question is not clear enough; could refer to methodology or evaluation methods Solution: User clarified they referred to the evaluation methodology, not implementation. Rechecked the paper, focusing on evaluation metrics, real data construction, and experimental design.
Key insight: The “how” question about the paper may refer to technical implementation or validation/measurement methods—always clarify which aspect the user needs.
8. The HTML version of QueST v3 returns a 404 error when accessed directly Solution: v3 has only a PDF version (no HTML rendering). Use the HTML version from v1 for content extraction, then check the v3 abstract page for version differences (no substantial changes).
Key insight: Not all Arxiv papers have an HTML version; if subsequent versions only make minor format adjustments, the v1 HTML version may suffice.
9. QueST v3 flowcharts return 404 errors when accessed directly Solution: v3 has only a PDF version. Use the HTML version from v1 for content extraction, then check the v3 abstract page for version differences (no substantial changes).#### 9. In the Desktop Video CLAUDE.md file, the lowercase “agents.md” is used as a reference file, while the actual file name is “AGENTS.md”. This may lead to a “file not found” issue in a case-insensitive file system.Solution: The citation was corrected, and the correct capitalized “AGENTS.md” was used as the file name.
Key Insight: File references in the document must strictly match case sensitivity to ensure reliability across different file system configurations (macOS defaults to case insensitivity, but it can be configured to be case sensitive).
Methods for Humans and Artificial Intelligence Strategic Level Pipeline Architecture with Multi-source Design Role Method Human Users immediately realize that the single-source (demo dataset) flow diagram does not reflect their core need: they want the VLA release injection and natural failure capture to be shown as the same error scenario sources. They see code supporting this (1c_generate_from_policy.py --mode injection), but the document ignores it. Artificial Intelligence AI initially focused on what is clearly stated in the README/comments, treating demo-based injections as the main path. It did not infer from code capabilities that users want a multi-source architecture emphasized. Difference Analysis: Humans think at a system level: “How do errors occur?” While AI thinks at a file level: “What exactly does this script do?” Humans discover gaps in the document by understanding the problem domain (the diversity of error scenarios requires multiple sources); AI needs clear instructions to add parallel paths.
Explanation of 0% Success Rate of BC-RNN Role Method Human Users immediately pointed out this anomaly: “Why is BC-RNN so poor? The difference from training results is large.” Based on domain knowledge, BC-RNN should have a 60–70% success rate in normal PickPlace tasks, so 0% indicates some issues, not a problem with the strategy itself. Artificial Intelligence AI began exploring the code structure (training scripts, evaluation scripts, configuration files), but did not immediately identify the most likely cause: mismatched observation keys (the “object” key fix mentioned by the user), environment initialization differences, or data normalization issues. Difference Analysis: Humans use domain knowledge + anomaly detection to infer possible root causes (environment mismatch). AI’s systematic exploration is comprehensive but slow—it will eventually find the issue, but does not directly jump to high-probability failure modes. This shows the value of domain expertise during debugging.
Distinguishing Implementation and Evaluation in Analyzing Papers Role Method Human When AI first provides implementation details, users immediately clarify: “No, I mean, how is evaluation performed?” AI AI initially interpreted “how does this paper perform cross-sample queries” as a question about technical methods (graph autoencoder, contrast learning, adversarial training). Difference Analysis: Humans clearly know which aspects are important for their research (evaluation framework), while AI provides a comprehensive technical overview by default. Human clarification is crucial to guide attention toward relevant evaluation metrics.
Granularity of Training Orchestration Role Method Human Users provide a complete implementation plan, including a 6-stage dependency graph, clear GPU allocation (Stage 1: GPU 0, Stage 2: GPU 1–4, etc.), parallel execution strategies, and tmux session management requirements. AI AI created a TodoList matching plan structure for 7 tasks and began systematically modifying each file, reading all files in parallel before editing. Difference Analysis: Humans pre-designed a complete orchestration architecture, considering hardware limitations (GPU 6–7 already in use), estimating timelines for each stage (Stage 1: 2–4 days, Stage 2: 4–8 hours), and specifying failure recovery plans (tmux sessions continue after disconnection). AI follows instructions but does not propose monitoring strategies, checkpoint validation, or resource contention handling to cope with multi-day training activities.
Method for Aligning Documentation and Code Role Method Human Users explicitly request: “Follow the content in the folder.” They want detailed implementation descriptions, as before (referring to the previous ErrorSceneDatabase API summary), prioritizing actual code behavior over document statements. AI AI deploys parallel exploration agents to read all code and then systematically updates the documentation. The pattern is: explore → verify → record. Use file system commands to obtain actual numbers (wc -l, du -sh, stat), rather than relying on statements in the document. Difference Analysis: Both agree on the priority of benchmark data, but humans specify the output style (detailed API documentation embedded in the overview document). AI defaults to a shorter update method—humans want comprehensive processing to prevent future deviations. This indicates that the document should be regarded as an “executable specification”.
Implementation Level Version Specificity of Research Papers Role Method Human Users explicitly corrected the statement “do not use v1; there is a v3 version with updates,” showing awareness of paper evolution. AI AI defaults to using the first available complete text version (v1 HTML) without checking subsequent versions. Difference Analysis: Humans track the version history of papers they are interested in; AI tends to use the easiest-to-access version (HTML rather than PDF). User intervention ensures access to the latest version.
Scope of Documentation Improvement Role Method Human Users start with /init commands to trigger a comprehensive code library analysis and a CLAUDE.md audit, expecting AI to autonomously identify vulnerabilities and propose improvements. AI AI analyzed the existing CLAUDE.md and found it “already very good and comprehensive,” performing only three simple targeted fixes instead of broader structural improvements. Difference Analysis: Humans use /init as a mechanism to discover potential documentation issues; AI defaults to a conservative “already good” evaluation, making only obvious corrections (case sensitivity, missing parts), possibly missing deeper organizational or completeness issues.
Limitations of Artificial Intelligence Key Limitations Unable to infer a multi-source pipeline architecture from code: Although 1c_generate_from_policy.py clearly supports --mode injection for policy rolling injection and natural capture, AI only recorded demo-based paths until users explicitly corrected. It fails to synthesize a system-level architecture from a single script function. Agent timeout in large code library exploration: When exploring the zhaoganlong framework, all three parallel agents timed out (each exceeding 1100 seconds), returning 0 tokens and requiring restart. Large directory trees and many files can exhaust agent token budgets or trigger tool call limits. No prioritization of high-probability failure modes in BC-RNN debugging: Instead of immediately checking the most likely cause (mismatched observation keys, which the user mentioned needing fixing), systematic exploration is comprehensive but slow—lacks debugging heuristics. AI was interrupted during Edit operations when modifying create_5hz_dataset_new_motion.py, leaving the multi-file data pipeline in a partially modified state. AI did not propose saving progress or suggesting an atomic batch operation (modifying all 4 files and testing one by one) to avoid intermediate state inconsistency. Unable to directly parse the PDF binary content returned by WebFetch tools. For arxiv papers, it relies heavily on HTML versions or preprocessed text. General Limitations Ambiguous query explanations: “How does this paper do X” may refer to technical implementation or evaluation methods. Clarification questions should be raised when ambiguity exists. Unable to identify design issues in ErrorSceneDatabase without specific user information: Users describe the design as “strange,” but AI cannot infer specific aspects (classification logic, source tracking, query API, architecture design). Clear problem statements are needed—code alone is insufficient to detect design issues. No check of paper version updates before using v1 HTML by default. When accessing arxiv papers, the latest version should always be verified. During /init-triggered CLAUDE.md audit, AI shows a confirmation bias toward existing document quality, concluding “already very good and comprehensive” after discovering well-structured content, instead of exploring potential vulnerabilities (e.g., lack of troubleshooting sections, unclear version requirements, incomplete architecture diagrams). Lessons Learned Key Lesson – QueST Evaluation Framework: When no ready-made benchmark labels exist, use Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman plots to verify cell type annotations and construct synthetic benchmarks, then validate model similarity rankings using Pearson correlation coefficients. A multi-task machine learning pipeline built via incremental prototype design (starting with one task) retains scattered single-task configurations (removed task list, hardcoded paths). To scale to a production environment, systematic review of data preparation scripts, dataset mapping JSON files, checkpoint directories, and evaluation configurations is required. Documentation synchronization pattern: Use parallel exploration agents (one per major directory), verify all numbers come from actual files (summary.json, file system statistics), and then systematically update document content part by part. Do not rely on statements in the document—always check code and data actual conditions. Debugging checklist for training and evaluation mismatch: If a strategy performs well in training but fails in evaluation, systematically check: (1) observation dictionary keys; (2) environment initialization parameters; (3) action space boundaries; (4) data normalization; (5) camera rendering settings. BC-RNN has a 0% recovery rate on normal tasks and 0.28% on error recovery tasks, indicating environment mismatch rather than strategy failure. Cross-sample query evaluation requires: (1) batch-invariant embeddings obtained via adversarial training; (2) benchmarking using graph kernels when labels are unavailable; (3) dual metrics, including highest accuracy and overall ranking correlation. For spatial transcriptomics, Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman graph kernels can convert discrete cell type labels into continuous segmentation similarity scores by calculating graph-level Wasserstein distances between subgraph representations. Large-scale HPC training orchestration requires clear dependency mapping (Stage 0→Stage 1+2 parallel→Stage 3→Stage 4→Stage 5), GPU allocation plans for each stage, and persistent session management (tmux) to continue running over multi-day training activities and SSH disconnections. Multi-source data collection architecture should be clearly stated in the document: Error scenarios benefit from diverse sources (demonstration injection for replicability, strategy deployment injection for realism, natural failure capture for realism). The flow diagram must present all sources as equal citizens, not hide them in script options. M14 evaluation results show baseline performance: 6,474 scenarios involving 4 strategies, with a random strategy having a 0% recovery rate and a recovery ratio of 1.9%; BC-RNN has a 0.28% recovery rate and a recovery ratio of 0.3%; Pi0 has a 0% recovery rate and a recovery ratio of 0.2%; Pi0.5 has a 0% recovery rate and a recovery ratio of 0%. Near-zero error recovery rates verify the difficulty of the benchmark and provide a foundation for future improvements (M15 human recovery data and LoRA fine-tuning are expected to show positive effects). Best practices for checkpoint inventory: Record complete paths, sizes, last modification dates, and availability status of all model checkpoints. Large checkpoint directories (180GB) indicate many steps saved—specific steps for evaluation need to be recorded. Date-based naming helps track training timelines, but steps must be clearly linked to dates. Scalability of error frameworks: A total of 53 Python files (about 1.47 thousand lines of code) include 6 detectors, 4 injectors, 4 validators, and 20 error classifiers, covering 3 domains (operation, planning, progress). The plugin architecture is scalable through DECTOR_REGISTRY, INJECTOR_REGISTRY, VALIDATOR_REGISTRY, CLASSIFIER_REGISTRY. A cooling time of 20 steps per detector prevents detection of junk behavior. Practical Learning /init command triggers a comprehensive code library analysis and the generation/improvement of CLAUDE.md, preparing for future Claude Code sessions. Even if CLAUDE.md already exists, this command still applies to document audits. Dialogue Summary MIHD (Spatial Transcriptomics) ✅ Research on QueST paper cross-sample query evaluation method 22:21:12.826 | claude_code User requested analysis of the evaluation methods in QueST papers (excluding implementation parts). The v1 HTML version and v3 summary of an arxiv paper were obtained, and the complete evaluation framework was extracted: Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman graph kernels build benchmarks from cell type labels, evaluated through highest accuracy and overall similarity accuracy (Pearson r value). The number of cell types (1–3) and size (50–200) for synthetic queries vary. After correction, v3 was used; v3 does not have an HTML version, but the content is quite rich.### Desktop Video
✅ Audit and improvement of CLAUDE.md document via init/command 20:56:25.688 | claude_code Users call the init command to trigger code repository analysis and the generation/improvement of CLAUDE.md. The AI analyzed the Swift/SwiftUI project structure, read the existing CLAUDE.md file, deemed it “excellent,” and performed three targeted fixes: correcting capitalization errors in the agents.md file references, adding a hint to check Localizable.xcstrings during code modification, and improving the ChangeLog format documentation. The AI confirmed no Cursor/.github copilot rules existed and verified the dead code detection configuration in .periphery.yml.
zhaoganlong Motion-based Self-Reflection Framework 🔄 Setup of training infrastructure and comprehensive documentation 22:23:48.001 | claude_code The user requested a complete 6-stage training plan for zhaoganlong’s motion-based self-reflection framework, involving 9 MimicGen tasks, running on an49 (8× A800). The AI created a decomposition diagram for 7 tasks, mapping the dependencies between stages (data preparation → Diffusion + LLaVA MPM parallel → MCM feedback → LaVA MCM → lifelong learning), and began modifying 4 data preparation scripts by removing comments from TASK_MAPPING entries and deleting pdb breakpoints to implement all 9 tasks. The framework directory was explored, and the complete training method was recorded, including 6 stages: HDF5→5Hz→Speed→LaVA JSON data preparation, diffusion strategy training using ResNet18+Transformer+UNet, LaVA MPM/MCM LoRA fine-tuning, lifelong learning, and OpenPI Pi0/Pi0.5 training. All checkpoints were listed: Pi0.5 Phoenix (180GB, 21 steps, 2026-02-24), base model (about 12GB each), diffusion strategy (4 snapshots, 253MB each). [[[HYMTPH_4]]] was created. The workflow was interrupted during the modification of create_5hz_dataset_new_motion.py. Three parallel exploration agents initially timed out (each over 1100 seconds), requiring restart.
Error Recovery Benchmark**🔄 Comprehensive documentation synchronization and architecture redesign** 03:04:05.254 | claude_code
A multi-session full-day meeting on updating the error_recovery_benchmark document. (1) By deploying parallel agents, the system-wide summary.md aligned with the actual implementation, covering directories such as error_framework/, scripts/, and outputs/. Six new detector types, four injectors, four validators, and 20 classifiers were added with API descriptions. Code statistics (22 scripts, 122 tests, 11 evaluation runs), M14 evaluation data (6,474 cases, while the document records 726 cases), and database statistics (649 scenarios categorized by error type, stage, and severity) were updated. Issues with VLA model type and version date were corrected. The pipeline diagram in section 3.1 was updated. Research into differences between training and evaluation code started but was interrupted midway. (5) Batch evaluation results for Pi0.5 were analyzed: overall recovery rate was 58.9%. Compared to the BC-RNN baseline (0%) and M14 error recovery results, all recovery rates were close to 0%.
