content:
Daily Report — 2026-03-03 Daily Overview Completed Work: Four parallel workflows: DCC completed the full cross-sample RM-IDEAL benchmark for the MIHD multimodal fusion framework; MacBook batch processed historical conversation records of 4 devices and 5 projects over 13 days, generating structured reports; Tianhe built the BC-RNN baseline and Pi0.5 LoRA evaluation infrastructure, identifying configuration errors in pi0.5_libero and pi0.5_base; MacBook also improved the clock visual effect of the screen protector and created Hugo website documentation. Execution Methods: DCC: Used 3 exploration agents to traverse the code repository, designed a method to extract independent script loads from the second-stage output using STAIG fusion embeddings, calculated topological scores and embedding cosine similarities using WWL graph kernels, and generated Spearman/Precision@K metrics and spatial heatmaps. MacBook: Used a two-phase process (export → merge) with gadget/summarize tools, combined Claude Sonnet to extract structured information from JSONL conversation files, and manually fixed JSON truncation issues. Tianhe: Refactored the multi-task supported evaluation script, debugged numpy dtype filtering for robot simulation compatibility, started batch GPU evaluations via Slurm, and investigated an53 node crashes due to sacct logs. Screen protector: Unified font thickness, disabled CALayer implicit animation, replaced SwiftUI material with NSVisualEffectView to achieve withinWindow blending effect. Impact: Established a reusable cross-sample evaluation toolchain, showing significant correlation between fusion embeddings and topological structures (Layer_3 r≈0.44); built a structured knowledge base covering robot simulation, spatial transcriptomics, and AI assistant projects for easy review and analysis; identified a basic training configuration error requiring retraining (using pi0.5_libero instead of pi0.5_base LoRA); implemented a screen protector feature to eliminate visual issues; established comprehensive documentation standards for website maintenance. DCC Completed Work: Completed the RM-IDEAL benchmark for the MIHD project, including design, implementation, validation, and documentation. Execution Methods: Used 3 agents to explore the code repository and design methods, created script/benchmark_rm_ideal.py (781 lines), fixed zero-embedding detection and CUDA compatibility issues, ran 151673↔151676 tests on RTX 2080 Ti, generated 6-panel spatial heatmaps using scanpy, and wrote documentation/CROSS_SAMPLE_QUERY.md (459 lines). Impact: Built a reusable cross-sample evaluation tool covering 10 stages from spatial graph construction to evaluation metrics; experimental results show significant correlation between fusion embeddings and topological structures. MacBook Completed Work: Batch processed historical AI conversation records of 4 devices and 5 projects over 13 days (February 7–19), generating structured daily reports; improved the clock visual effect of the screen protector (fixed ghosting, smooth animation, no video mode, glass transparency); created Hugo website CLAUDE.md documentation. Execution Methods: Ran daily_summary.py for 4.5 hours continuously, performed approximately 20 exports and over 10 merges; used parse_claude_code() to read JSONL session files in ~/.claude/projects, called AI to extract structured information (task/differences between human and AI/technical insights), and generated Markdown+JSON dual-format reports; manually fixed JSON truncation issues by correcting prompts. Screen protector: Unified font thickness between highlight layers and mask layers, wrapped mask updates within CATransaction.setDisableActions(true), replaced SwiftUI .ultraThinMaterial with NSViewRepresentable, and used NSVisualEffectView for withinWindow blending mode. Website: Analyzed Hugo blog structure and established a pipeline (update.sh incremental compression). Impact: Systematically generated 13 complete historical technical logs, documenting progress in robot simulation, spatial transcriptomics, and AI assistant projects over two weeks; established a structured knowledge base for error review, architecture review, and knowledge transfer. Eliminated visual issues in the screen protector in production applications; established maintainable documentation standards for future contributors. Tianhe Completed Work: Built the BC-RNN baseline and Pi0.5 LoRA evaluation pipeline with multi-task support; debugged training checkpoint formats; started 5 task evaluation batches; monitored 8 parallel Pi0.5 training jobs (17k–26k/36k steps); started 2-GPU evaluation after an53 crashes; identified a critical basic model configuration error (using pi0.5_libero instead of pi0.5_base). Execution Methods: Refactored the evaluation script, added –task parameter and per-task checkpoint resolution; created BC-RNN checkpoint symbolic links; modified policy_adapter._to_robosuite_obs to filter numpy scalar types (float64) that Robomimic TensorUtils cannot handle; created eval_pi05_lora_2gpu.sh for GPU architecture splitting (GPU 0: VLA server, GPU 1: MuJoCo rollout); analyzed Slurm logs (sacct) to investigate an53 NODE_FAIL at 08:30; parsed JSONL evaluation results. Impact: Identified coffee task BC-RNN training failure (0% SR); established an automated evaluation infrastructure for 250 rollout items of 5 tasks; identified critical basic model configuration errors requiring retraining; ruled out AI operations as causes of node failures (resource overload 3 hours after AI activity); successfully deployed evaluation on a backup node, expected to take 60–70 minutes. DCC completed the implementation of MIHD cross-sample RM-IDEAL benchmark (design, 781-line script, error fixing, visualization, 459-line documentation); MacBook batch processed historical AI conversation records from February 7–19 over 13 days, generating structured daily reports; Tianhe built the BC-RNN/Pi0.5 evaluation pipeline and identified critical basic model configuration errors; improved the screen protector UI and created website documentation.
Tasks Architecture & Strategy - ❌ Identify Pi0.5 basic model configuration error — Users found that the base model used in LoRA fine-tuning is pi0.5_libero instead of pi0.5_base. Comparison with zhaoganlong’s settings is needed, and possibly retraining using 8 GPUs of an49 for all tasks.- ✅ Implementation script/benchmark_rm_ideal.py — A benchmark script with 781 lines of code was created. Its core functions include: load_section_string_labels (loading string labels from the annotation file and sorting by cached barcode), load_fusedEmbeddings (loading STAIG fused embeddings from the second-stage output or recalculating them), compute_cross_embedding_similarity (cosine similarity at the center of the cross-section niche), evaluate_correlation (Spearman r / Precision@K / same-label rate), run_cross_section_benchmark (unidirectional cross-section evaluation process), generate_summary (CSV + JSON + standard output formatting). ✅ Running the Layer_3 benchmark and generating results — A bidirectional Layer_3 test 151673↔151676 was run on RTX 2080 Ti; the STAIG fused embeddings of 151676 were successfully recalculated, and the RM-IDEAL scores were loaded from the cache. Results: 151673→151676 Spearman r=0.4356 (p=6.24e-159), 151676→151673 Spearman r=0.4542 (p=2.66e-183), indicating a moderate positive correlation; P@K is close to 0 (with large ranking differences), and the same-label rate is low. ✅ Running the BC-RNN baseline evaluation (5 tasks × 50 iterations) — Batch evaluations for coffee, stack, stack three, thread, and three assemblies were completed; the success rate for all tasks was 0%. 🔄 Monitoring the Pi0.5 LoRA fine-tuning progress — 8 training tasks were run on 8x A800 GPU. Progress: coffee (72%), stack/stack three (69-71%), thread/three assemblies (50%). The average iteration time for all tasks is approximately 6.1 seconds. It is expected that each task requires an additional 17-31 hours. ✅ Summarizing the Pi0.5 and BC-RNN evaluation results — Pi0.5 (15,000th step): stack 95-100%, stack three 80-90%, coffee/thread/three assemblies 15-45%. BC-RNN baseline: success rate for all tasks is 0%. Phoenix comparison (99,999th step): coffee 0%, stack 12-24%. ✅ Fixing issues with zero embedding detection and automatic recalculation logic — It was found that all STAIG fused embeddings of 151676 were zero (model crash); zero embedding detection (np.allclose(embeddings, 0)) was added to load_fusedEmbeddings, automatically triggering –recompute_fusion to retrain STAIG (300 cycles, about 50 seconds). After fixing, the embeddings returned to normal. ✅ Generating spatial heatmap visualization — The DLPFC data (dataset/DLPFC/151673 path) was loaded using scanpy’s sc.read_visium() and a 2×3 panel plot was created using sc.pl.spatial(): each row represents a direction (151673→151676 / 151676→151673), and the three columns are the true values, RM-IDEAL score heatmap, and embedding cosine similarity heatmap; saved as outputs/rm_ideal_benchmark/rm_ideal_layer3_spatial.png. ✅ Batch generation of historical daily reports from 2026-02-07 to 2026-02-19 — 13 dates were processed, involving work on 4 devices (DCC/tianhe/TzJsDesktop/MacBook) and 5 projects (error-recovery-benchmark/MIHD/CalendarPro/gadget/Motion-based Self-Reflection Framework); approximately 20 export operations and more than 10 merging operations were performed; the JSON truncation issue in the report on 2026-02-14 was manually fixed. ✅ Fixing the transparency issue of the screen saver clock — SwiftUI’s.ultraThinMaterial was replaced with NSViewRepresentable, and the .withinWindow blending mode was used to display video content instead of the desktop screen. ✅ Starting the 2-GPU Pi0.5 LoRA evaluation on an53 — The eval_pi05_lora_2gpu.sh script was created, separating the VLA server (GPU 0) and MuJoCo iteration (GPU 1). 8 tasks × 20 trials were successfully started on an53. The total runtime is expected to be 60-70 minutes. ✅ Exploring the RM-IDEAL code library and designing benchmark test methods — Three exploration agents were used to fully explore the implementation of RM-IDEAL (RMIdealEvaluator in utils/rm_ideal.py), cross-sample capability (compute_niche_scores_cross_section method), and the experiment recording system; independent script methods were designed (only testing PCA+UNI2+STAIG_FUSION, with target profiles being 151673 and 151676), but the user rejected ExitPlanMode. ✅ Writing the documentation/CROSS_SAMPLE_QUERY.md method paper — A Chinese method paper with 459 lines was created, covering 10 chapters: overview (problem definition, two evaluation methods, application scenarios), spatial graph construction (build_grid_connectivity k-NN + symmetry), k-hop subgraph extraction (bfs_k_hop BFS precomputation), WWL graph kernel (message passing iteration, shared hash table), Wasserstein distance (Homma cost matrix, POT/scipy dual backends), cross-section evaluation process (global type mapping, node ID offset), embedding similarity comparison (niche center, cosine similarity), correlation evaluation metrics (Spearman ρ, Precision@K, same-label rate), experimental results (Layer_3 bidirectional query data), and summary of key code paths (complete file/function/data flow diagram). ✅ Implementing a screen saver for the no-video state — The media content protection function was removed; a black background window was created for screens without a wallpaper, and a clock was displayed on the black screen. ✅ Fixing video switch errors (bookmark URL mismatch) — A protection mechanism was added to ensureFileAccess to detect whether the bookmark parsed URL matches the request URL, and the original URL is returned in the case of NSOpenPanel. ✅ Fixing numpy dtype errors in BC-RNN evaluation — policy_adapter._to_robosuite_obs was modified to filter out numpy scalar types (float64) that TensorUtils cannot handle. ✅ Investigating the failure of an53 node (NODE_FAIL at 08:30) — The Sacct logs were analyzed to determine that an53 crashed due to resource overload (8 GPUs + high CPU load), not caused by AI operations. The AI’s srun command failed before the crash. The node restarted at 09:41, and the SSH host key also changed. Implementation and Fixes - ✅ Fixing CUDA compatibility detection and CPU fallback issues — Initially, a CUDA kernel incompatibility issue was encountered on the P100 GPU; PyTorch required sm_70+ version. try/except was added to handle torchzeros(1).cuda() exceptions, and when failed, it fallback to CPU. The user successfully ran it after switching to RTX 2080 Ti (sm_75). ✅ Fixing ghosting issues during clock text update in the screen saver — The mask layer was updated in CATransaction.setDisableActions(true), eliminating a 0.2-second ghosting effect when the time changed. ✅ Adding –task parameter to the BC-RNN evaluation script — 5_baseline_accuracy.py and visualize_policy_rollout.py were refactored to support task registration and resolution handling per task. ✅ Updating CLAUDE.md documentation with coding specifications and evaluation commands — The CLAUDE.md documentation was enhanced, adding 35 Makefile targets (from 15 to 35), incorporating coding specifications from AGENTS.md, recording the parallel VLA evaluation workflow, and adding references to training scripts. ✅ Fixing gray ghosting issues in the screen saver clock — The font weight of ScreensaverClockHighlight and ScreensaverClockMask was unified, eliminating the blur effect at the text edges. ✅ Creating BC-RNN checkpoint symbolic links — Symbolic links were set from checkpoints/bc_rnn/{task} to the actual BC-RNN d0 training directory for 5 tasks. ✅ Creating the website/CLAUDE.md documentation — The Hugo blog structure was analyzed, and a complete CLAUDE.md document containing build commands, content sections, and static resource specifications was created. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. SwiftUI .ultraThinMaterial displays a fixed color in the video, rather than transparent glass Solution: The SwiftUI material used the .behindWindow blending mode (displaying the desktop content behind the window) instead of .integralWindow mode (displaying on the same window content). NSVisualEffectView was replaced with NSViewRepresentable, and .integralWindow mode along with the clearBackgroundColor property were explicitly specified on NSHostingView.
Key insight: The abstraction level of SwiftUI hides the key rendering process details; for complex visual effects, such as transparency in windows, control at the NSView level is required.
2. All STAIG fused embeddings of 151676 are zero (embedding similarity is all 0, Spearman r is NaN), causing the model to crash completely Solution: np.allclose(embeddings, 0) detection was added to load_fused Embeddings; if this condition is detected, a warning is printed and –recompute_fusion is automatically triggered to reload the gene/visual embeddings from the cache and retrain STAIG (300 cycles, about 50 seconds on RTX 2080 Ti); after fixing, the embeddings return to normal (64 dimensions, norm = 1.0).
Key insight: Due to unstable training, the STAIG fused embeddings saved in the second stage may become zero; active detection and automatic recalculation should be performed in the benchmark script to avoid manual intervention.
3. The old video is still played when switching videos after selection in NSOpenPanel Solution: FileAccess must parse each screen’s bookmark as the URL of the old video, rather than the new request URL. A conditional check is added to compare the parsed URL with the requested URL; if different, the original URL is returned (this URL has the temporary sandbox permissions provided by NSOpenPanel).
Key insight: Bookmark storage per screen conflicts with multi-video history; a conditional check is needed to detect whether the bookmark points to an expired file.
4. The BC-RNN success rate for the coffee task is shown as 0%, likely due to an evaluation error Solution: The training logs were checked, confirming that the BC-RNN training for the coffee task reached a 0% success rate at all stages (600 cycles of training). This is not an evaluation error; the task actually failed during training.
Key insight: Before debugging the evaluation process, train metrics must be verified first; zero values downstream may reflect failures in upstream training.
5. The an53 node crashed at 08:30, causing the tmux session to be lost and job 46798 to fail Solution: Investigation via sacct logs determined that the crash was caused by resource overload (8 GPUs at 100% utilization, high CPU load). AI operations were excluded as the cause (the last completion was at 05:07, 3 hours before the crash). The SSH keygen -R an53 was used to resolve the SSH host key mismatch.
Key insight: The slurm report provided minimal details about the crash, but there is no ability to access system logs via root.
6. The CUDA kernel of the P100 GPU (sm_60) is incompatible with PyTorch (requires sm_70+ version); torch.cuda.is_available() returns True, but asynchronous operations fail **Key insight:**Solution: Initially, trying to catch the torchzeros(1).cuda() exception with try/except failed, as the asynchronous failure on P100 cannot be captured. The user succeeded after switching to RTX 2080 Ti (sm_75). Finally, the CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" environment variable was added so that CPU is forced in the script.
Key Insight: torch.cuda.is_available() only checks whether the driver and library exist, without checking whether the GPU’s computational capability is compatible with current PyTorch. CUDA operations may fail asynchronously and cannot be caught by Python’s try/except. The most reliable approach is to switch GPUs or use environment variables to force use of CPU.
7. The JSON generated by the LLM is truncated (…truncated marker), causing parsing failures in daily_summary.py on 2026-02-14 and other dates Solution: Send the truncated raw text as an independent prompt to the AI, asking it to only fix/extract valid JSON parts; the AI successfully restored the complete JSON structure.
Key Insight: Ultra-long JSON generated by LLMs is at risk of being truncated (especially when multiple paragraphs are merged); a truncation detection mechanism and automatic JSON repair retry logic should be added during merging, rather than relying entirely on manual discovery and intervention.
8. When the screen saver clock text updates, the previous numbers leave a 0.2-second ghosting effect Solution: CALayer has an animation effect of approximately 0.25 seconds for changes to content properties by default. In CATransaction, update blurView.layer?.mask and set setDisableActions(true) to force immediate replacement.
Key Insight: CALayer has an animation effect for almost all property changes; explicit transaction control is needed to achieve immediate visual updates.
9. The BC-RNN strategy evaluation crashes due to “cannot handle data type <class ’numpy.float64’>” Solution: robomimic’s TensorUtils.to_tensor() cannot handle numpy scalar types. The_to_robosuite_obs function was modified to filter out keys in raw_obs dictionary that contain only array/image values, and then it is passed to the robomimic strategy.
Key Insight: Robomimic expects a structured obs dictionary with array values; numpy scalars from robosuite (such as gripper width float64) must be filtered before being passed to TensorUtils.
10. The visualization script fails multiple times: Bash’s heredoc uses != instead of != (SyntaxError), the file name prefix does not match (151673_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 vs filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5), spatial/data path errors (located in Dataset/DLPFC, not directly in section directory), load_dlpfc_data() return value parsing error (returns 1 instead of 2), and read_10x_h5 lacks uns[‘spatial’], causing sc.pl.spatial() to fail Solution: Use an independent script/_viz_rm_ideal.py file instead of the heredoc format; use glob “*filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5” to find the correct file name; directly use sc.read_visium("/path/to/Dataset/DLPFC/151673") for loading (automatically handles spatial/subdirectory); the unpacking method of load_dlpfc_data() was fixed, now returning a single value; abandon use of load_dlpfc_data and directly use sc.read_visium to ensure uns[‘spatial’] exists.
Key Insight: Bash’s heredoc is sensitive to special character escaping; complex scripts should be written as separate files; the name of DLPFC data files has a chapter prefix; spatial data is located in Dataset/DLPFC/{chapter}/spatial instead of {chapter}/spatial; load_dlpfc_data uses read_10x_h5 instead of read_visium, resulting in missing spatial metadata; sc.pl.spatial heavily relies on uns[‘spatial’], and must be loaded using read_visium.
Common Issues 11. The edge of the screen saver clock text shows a gray ghost ghosting effect Solution: Root cause: The font weight mismatch between ScreensaverClockHighlight (.light) and renderTextMask (.regular) causes the mask to become thick, exposing the frosted glass edge of hudWindow. This issue is resolved by unifying the font weight to.pdf-regular.
Key Insight: The visual effect layer must achieve pixel-level alignment; even minor weight differences will expose the underlying content.
12. Batch processing 13 days of historical data requires frequent switching of date parameters and manual confirmation of export/merge status, which is very cumbersome and error-prone Solution: Manually execute the export –date YYYY-MM-DD command of daily_summary.py, and execute the merge command separately for each date, confirming the integrity of the output file via the file system.
Key Insight: The summarize tool lacks a batch mode (e.g., –date-range 2026-02-07..2026-02-19 auto-iteration); batch processing support and progress recovery mechanisms should be added in the future.
When using relative paths with nohup, it fails if SSH is started in the project directory rather than the user’s home directory Solution: Change the command from ‘ssh an53 “nohup bash scripts/…”’ to ‘ssh an53 “cd $PROJ && nohup bash scripts/…”’, ensuring the working directory is correctly entered before executing the script.
Key Insight: SSH’s non-interactive session starts from $HOME, not from the current local directory. Always switch the directory to the project root or use absolute paths in remote commands.
Human and Artificial Intelligence Approaches Strategic Level Discovery of Configuration Error in Pi0.5 Base Model Role Method Human The user noticed that LoRA fine-tuning uses pi0.5_libero instead of pi0.5_base as the base model, considering this a critical architectural decision that needs verification and possibly retraining. Artificial Intelligence The AI did not actively detect this configuration issue during multiple evaluations. The AI focused on progress and success rates of checkpoints, without questioning the choice of base model. Difference Analysis: Humans used domain knowledge about model architecture levels to identify basic training configuration errors. AI ignored this strategic issue while focusing on operational metrics.
Diagnosis of Zero Embedding Problem Role Method Human After discovering embedding similarity to 0, immediately asked “Can you show me the visualization result?”, shifting from numerical inspection to visual diagnosis; after finding the root cause, asked “Please summarize how you currently perform cross-sample patch queries.” Artificial Intelligence Initially tried to run a complete benchmark test to solve the zero embedding problem, and started troubleshooting only after NaN appeared; no visual request was made; only after the user asked for visualization did it realize the need for a spatial heatmap; documentation writing required a clear request from the user to begin. Difference Analysis: Humans formed a complete loop from numerical inspection to visualization to summary; AI tended to solve individual problems step by step, lacking a global perspective and initiative.
Cause Analysis of an53 Node Failure Role Method Human The user correctly suspected that AI operations might cause an53 to crash, requested timeline evidence, and mentioned the 11:22 crash time in peer reports. Artificial Intelligence The AI systematically analyzed Slurm logs (sacct), tracked all srun commands (04:55–05:07, all completed successfully), identified NODE_FAIL at 08:30 (3 hours after AI activity), and diagnosed it as resource overload. Difference Analysis: Humans used indirect evidence and peer reports to form hypotheses. AI used system logs and timestamps to build a clear timeline, proving operations ended 3 hours before the crash.
Design Decision for Benchmark Test Role Method Human The user explicitly specified testing only the PCA+UNI2+STAIG_FUSION combination, with target chapters 151673 and 151676. An independent script was created first to verify feasibility, then integrated into the workflow. Multiple times rejected ExitPlanMode, expecting direct execution when direction was clear. Artificial Intelligence The initial design covered multiple fusion methods and more chapters; each plan was tried using ExitPlanMode before approval; due to repeated rejections, the user’s execution style preferences were not understood. Difference Analysis: Humans made strategic decisions (scope control, priority ordering) while AI tended to cover everything comprehensively; humans preferred direct execution mode, and the AI’s conservative approval process conflicted with the user’s expected execution efficiency.
Batch Processing Strategy for Historical Data Role Method Human Humans clearly knew they needed to generate a 13-day historical report retrospectively, manually called tools for each date, interrupted processing when issues occurred, and continued for the next date. Artificial Intelligence As a daily report analyst, AI passively responded to each individual date request, reparsed the conversation, extracted information, generated reports each time, without realizing it was a batch task or suggesting workflow optimization. Difference Analysis: Humans had a global batch processing intent and time planning, while AI could only see a single call; AI lacked the ability to actively identify repetitive patterns and propose automation improvements.
User Experience of Screen Saver under No Video Role Method Human The user expected the screen saver to remain active without video loading, showing a black screen and clock (consistent with system screen saver). Artificial Intelligence AI initially saw only a guard preventing the screen saver, assuming it was intentional design; no assumption about user experience was questioned before explicit request. Difference Analysis: Humans applied the psychological model of macOS screen saver behavior; AI followed literal code constraints and did not infer broader user experience expectations.
Granularity Judgment for Merging Multiple Dialogue Segments| Role | Method | |——|——| | Human | The user explicitly requested analyzing multiple dialogue segments from the same day separately (possibly from different devices or projects) before merging them into a complete daily report, keeping logic clear. | | Artificial Intelligence | AI strictly followed instructions, analyzed each segment separately, and then merged them. However, redundant issues occurred during merging (similar problems listed repeatedly instead of true summarization). Humans needed to emphasize “integration and refinement, not word-for-word copying” in the prompt. |
Difference Analysis: Humans understood that “merging” meant information aggregation and deduplication; AI tended to retain all details, resulting in verbose output; AI needed clear integration instructions to achieve the summary quality expected by humans.
Limitations of Artificial Intelligence Key Limitations ### Key Limitations ```- During multiple evaluations, no configuration errors for the pi0.5 base model (the difference between libero and the base model) were actively identified until the user explicitly raised this issue. - Lack of initiative and global perspective: ① No visualization scheme was proposed actively, requiring a clear request from the user; ② No paper-style methods documentation was proposed actively, also needing a user request; ③ After multiple ExitPlanMode rejections, the user’s execution style preferences (direct implementation instead of waiting for approval) were still not understood; ④ After identifying the zero embedding issue, no root cause diagnosis was taken actively (why saving embeddings in the second stage caused a crash). - Design error in the compute_embedding_similarity function: The call to computeEmbedding_similarity(embeddings_ref, niche_mask_query=None) was made incorrectly in run_cross_section_benchmark, with incorrect parameter settings and confusing logic; it was only fixed after recreating the compute_cross_embedding_similarity function. This indicates a lack of deep understanding of cross-part similarity computation. - Errors frequently occur in Bash’s heredoc and path handling: ① Bash’s heredoc cannot be correctly escaped as \!= (syntax error); ② Multiple times, the situation where DLPFC file names contain chapter prefixes was missed; ③ The spatial/ directory is mistakenly placed under dataset/DLPFC/{chapter}/spatial; ④ Abuse of load_dlpfc_data() leads to the absence of uns['spatial']. This shows insufficient understanding of the DLPFC dataset file organization and scanpy API. - Incorrect CUDA compatibility detection strategy: torch.cuda.is_available() only checks the driver and libraries, not the compatibility of GPU computing capabilities; try/except cannot capture CUDA asynchronous errors; in the case of P100 asynchronous failures, multi-layer CPU fallback is ineffective. This indicates a lack of understanding of PyTorch CUDA mechanisms and asynchronous error propagation. - As a daily reporting analyst, multiple times required to handle similar tasks (analyzing historical conversations → generating structured reports), but failed to recognize this as a batch processing scenario, and did not actively suggest “using batch processing mode” or “automated scripts” to improve efficiency. - API tokens expired multiple times in the sub-agent exploration task, making it difficult to check checkpoints and zhaoganlong folders. Manual login operations were required. - During debugging the numpy dtype errors in BC-RNN, multiple attempts were made, including checking the traceback, retrying SSH connections, and examining checkpoints. Ultimately, it was found that _to_robosuite_obs is the key point for filtering scalar types. - When seeing that the SR in the coffee evaluation is 0%, no active inspection of training logs was performed; a clear statement of the problem was needed before investigating upstream training failures. ### General Limitations- In multi-segment dialogue merging tasks, the initial output is often very long (all tasks/problems are retained individually instead of integrating), and humans need to explicitly emphasize “integration and refinement, merging similar content, and retaining more important elements” in the prompt before producing a concise version. - It relies on humans to manually identify and provide repair prompts for handling truncated JSON files, without establishing a truncation detection and automatic retry mechanism at the tool level. - The immediate identification of CATransaction.setDisableActions() is an effective way to solve the delay in clock updates; the correct solution was found only after seeing the hexadecimal dump of emojis that caused the Edit tool matching failure – RM-IDEAL cross-section evaluation full workflow: ① Load string labels aligned by cached barcodes; ② Load fused embedding data (from second-stage output or recalculation); ③ Use the compute_niche_scores_cross_section() function of RMIdealEvaluator to calculate RM-IDEAL scores (based on WWL graph kernel and Wasserstein distance); ④ Calculate cosine similarity of embeddings (similarity between centers of different regions and all points); ⑤ Evaluate the correlation using Spearman correlation coefficient/Precision@K/label similarity rate; ⑥ Generate spatial heatmap visualization results (sc.pl.spatial). - The selection of the LoRA base model is crucial for transfer learning: pi0.5_base (general model), pi0.5_libero (Libero benchmark model), pi0.5_mimicgen_phoenix (model dedicated to MimicGen task). Using the wrong base model may lead to poor performance. - Details of the WWL (Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman) graph kernel algorithm: ① Perform K rounds of WL message passing, collect multiple sets of neighbor labels per round → sort and merge → search/assign new integers in a global hash table; ② Query subgraphs and reference subgraphs use the same hash table to ensure consistent label encoding; ③ Output the (K+1)-dimensional feature vector [a^0, a^1, ..., a^K] for each node; ④ The cost matrix uses standardized Hamming distance (different bits/total number of bits); ⑤ The ot.emd2() function in the POT library can efficiently calculate the Wasserstein distance (10 times faster), and if scipy linprog is not available, other methods are used; ⑥ RM score = 1 - W, where W ∈ [0, 1]. - Explanation of the evaluation metrics for cross-sample niche queries: ① The Spearman correlation coefficient ≈ 0.44 (p<1e-150) indicates a moderate positive correlation between cosine similarity of fused embeddings and RM-IDEAL topology scores, showing that the embedding data can indeed capture cross-section niche structure information; ② A P@K close to 0 indicates a large head difference between the two rankings (embedding similarity and topology measure different information dimensions), but the overall ranking trend is consistent; Avoid manual intervention to ensure the benchmark can recover automatically. - Key practices for batch processing historical data: ① Tool design should consider batch processing modes (date range parameters, progress recovery, parallel processing); ② Multi-segment merging requires clear integration instructions (“merge similar tasks into one entry”) to avoid long output; ③ Long JSON generation scenarios require truncation detection + automatic repair and retry mechanisms; ④ Visualization of batch task progress (e.g., “8 days completed in 13 days”) can significantly reduce manual monitoring costs. - The CALayer attribute (content, framework, etc.) has an implicit animation effect of approximately 0.25 seconds by default; immediate updating of the mask layer can be achieved using CATransaction.setDisableActions(true) + commit(). - Robomimic’s TensorUtils.to_tensor() requires dictionary values to be numpy arrays; numpy scalars (float64, int64) obtained from the robosuite dictionary need to be filtered before being passed to the robomimic strategy. - Slurm NODE_FAIL diagnostic workflow: sacct shows the job completion status, and scontrol show node allows viewing BootTime/SlurmdStartTime, but the root cause requires accessing syslog/dmesg. Common causes include OOM, GPU driver crashes, and cooling issues. - 2-GPU split evaluation architecture for VLAs: Server GPU runs the policy inference (using the openpi05 environment, serve_policy.py), and client GPU runs MuJoCo rendering (using mimicgen_env; attention should be paid to the re-mapping of MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID when CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is used). - Explanation of the evaluation results: Pi0.5 shows performance differences for specific tasks (Stack reaches 95–100%, while Coffee is only 15–45%), and the flat 0% of BC-RNN indicates basic training or architecture issues, not task difficulty issues. - Compatibility between PyTorch and CUDA and asynchronous error handling: ① torch.cuda.is_available() only checks whether the CUDA driver and library exist, but does not check whether the GPU computing capability is compatible with the current PyTorch version (e.g., P100 sm_60 is not compatible with the sm_70+ required by PyTorch); ② CUDA operations may fail asynchronously, and Python’s try/except cannot capture such errors (errors occur when CUDA kernels execute asynchronously); ③ The most reliable alternative is to use the environment variable CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" to force disable CUDA, or directly replace with a compatible GPU; ④ In cases of asynchronous failures, software-level multi-layer fault handling (device detection, try/except) is ineffective. - Layered design of structured daily report information: The global layer of daily_overview provides a panoramic view across devices (three sentences: what, how, impact), and the device layer provides detailed information for each device (also three sentences), ensuring both a global perspective and device-level details. Using a timer-based request collection method can improve throughput.
4. Due to PAM slurm_adopt rejecting connections, SSH access on GPU nodes an49/an53 is disabled, with the error message “No active tasks on this node”. Solution: By using Slurm’s srun command to bypass SSH restrictions and execute commands directly within the assigned job context: srun --jobid=45628 bash -c 'command' Key Insight: Slurm’s srun command allows command execution on assigned nodes, even if PAM blocks direct SSH connections, which is very useful in a cluster environment with strict access controls.
General Issues 5. When using srun on GPU nodes under heavy load, background tasks experience timeouts, and the command response time exceeds 60 seconds. Solution: The –overlap flag was added, and the timeout expectation was lowered. When nvitop is unavailable or too slow, it falls back to the simpler nvidia-smi. Accepting nodes with heavy load results in higher command latency. Key Insight: When GPU nodes are operating at full load, management commands executed via srun may experience significant delays; monitoring scripts should be designed to handle timeouts gracefully and use lightweight alternative commands.
6. MIHD: During the embedding process of scGPT (512 dimensions) and UNI2 (1536 dimensions), the mclust clustering program hangs indefinitely. Solution: In visualize_from_cache.py, the default mclust is replaced by kmeans via the –cluster_method flag. High-dimensional data makes the EM algorithm of mclust computationally difficult to implement. Key Insight: Gaussian mixture model clustering performs poorly after more than 100 dimensions. For basic model embedding (512d–1536d), kmeans or spectral methods must be used to achieve actual operation.
7. Desktop video log files contain over 1550 junk entries per session (updateClockLabels × 879, startScreensaverTimer × 671). Solution: Remove dlog from updateClockLabels (called once per second during screen saver). Move dlog in startScreensaverTimer after all early exit protections (only record actual scheduling timers). Remove dlog from idle timer callbacks. Key Insight: High-frequency dlog calls in timer callbacks generate large log files, masking real errors. Logging should be based on state transitions rather than periodic timing.
Approaches for Humans and Artificial Intelligence Strategic Level MIHD: It is recognized that scGPT+UNI2+STAIG should be equivalent to PCA+UNI2+STAIG Role Approach Human User (Yi Zhang) notices that the scGPT spatial embedding “is similar to PCA” from pilot results and suspects that the gene encoder may not be used in STAIG fusion Artificial Intelligence The assistant initially planned to run all scGPT+UNI2 fusion experiments to obtain STAIG ARI, assuming the gene encoder would be used Difference Analysis: Humans propose hypotheses based on domain expertise (viewing scGPT as a dimensionality reduction tool), while artificial intelligence acts according to task requirements (obtaining ARI values) without questioning the fusion architecture. Human-led investigations reveal actual implementation details.
VLA: Approach to analyzing the root cause of GPU utilization Role Approach Human The user provides detailed mathematical analysis: Pi0.5 outputs a 50-step data block, and a 400-step experiment requires only about 8 inference calls, each call taking 2.5 seconds = 20 seconds GPU / a total of 200 seconds = 10% utilization, and further analyzes CPU and GPU work within each 2.5-second inference cycle Artificial Intelligence Artificial intelligence may first use analysis tools or log analysis to identify bottlenecks before deriving mathematical models Difference Analysis: The user demonstrates system-level thinking, deriving expected utilization from the architecture rather than relying on measurements for debugging. This indicates a deep understanding of the VLA inference process structure.
Desktop Video: Diagnosing bookmark errors via log archaeology or directly checking code? Role Approach Human The user provides symptom descriptions and log file locations, enabling evidence-based diagnosis Artificial Intelligence The assistant reads 4438 lines of log files and identifies the “non-scope-preserving bookmarks” pattern (never “safely scoped”), traces it back to empty rights files via code search, and then verifies the hypothesis Difference Analysis: Log-based debugging reveals runtime behavior (bookmark creation is always non-scope-preserving), which cannot be detected by static code analysis. The root cause (empty rights files) is invisible in logs but becomes clear after identifying the non-scope pattern.
VLA: Format of external dependency documents Role Approach Human The user wants a clear, structured file list specifying the exact path, purpose, and reference location for each external dependency Artificial Intelligence Artificial intelligence initially creates EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCIES.md, which contains more narrative, document-like content explaining concepts and usage patterns Difference Analysis: The user recognizes the need for operational references (which files exist) and explanatory documents (how to use them). The user provides a clear plan with a table-based structure including paths, purposes, and references. This indicates that the user understands different documents serve different purposes.
Implementation Level Desktop Video: Use existing visualize_from_cache.py instead of writing new scripts Role Approach Human The user interrupts after the assistant writes new visualize_weekly_report.py and says “do not rewrite the script, use the existing visualize” Artificial Intelligence The assistant creates a custom visualization script (visualize_weekly_report.py, using matplotlib/seaborn) to generate 3 summary charts without checking whether the existing script can adapt Difference Analysis: Humans prefer reusing verified code (visualize_from_cache.py) rather than creating new scripts. The assistant focuses on precise specification compliance rather than code library consistency. In this case, both methods succeed: the new script generates summary charts (ranking, heatmaps, comparisons), while the existing script generates charts for each component.
Limitations of Artificial Intelligence Severe Limitations In MIHD scGPT experiments, no questioning was done about task assumptions. When asked “to obtain scGPT+UNI2+STAIG ARI”, the assistant should have verified whether STAIG fusion actually uses the gene encoder embedding before running the expensive 25-minute experiment. Human incidental observation (“similar to PCA”) is key to discovering architectural insights.
Desktop video debugging: The assistant rewrites errorLog() to fix concurrency issues but does not explain why no error logs appear in the 4438-line file. Competition causes complete log loss, not just corruption. “Severe: errorLog is silently failing, all historical errors are gone” should be clearly stated.
General limitations
Multiple failures occurred when trying to directly SSH to GPU nodes (an49/an53) without immediately realizing the access mode based on srun due to PAM slurm_adopt restrictions. The access control mode should be identified after the first failure, rather than retrying SSH multiple times.
The initial EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCIES.md is more narrative and explanatory rather than a structured list format required by the user. A clear plan with table-based specifications is needed. Clarifying questions about the purpose of the document (operational reference or conceptual guide) should be asked before writing.
MIHD visualization: The assistant creates a new script (visualize_weekly_report.py) but does not explore the existing visualization infrastructure first. New code should be written after investigating all visualize_*.py scripts using the Agent tool. The user had to interrupt and receive re-direction.
Lessons Learned Key Experience – Basic model embedding (scGPT 512d, UNI2 1536d) cannot replace dimensionality reduction in clustering tasks (PCA 50d). scGPT is designed for cross-dataset transfer, not variance handling within the same dataset. Architecture choice (only gene or multi-modal fusion) is more important than embedding quality: QFormer achieves 2× higher ARI improvement by learning gene visual alignment compared to using scGPT alone. STAIG graph-based fusion completely ignores the gene encoder output and directly uses the original HVG matrix. In VLA models, action chunking fundamentally changes GPU usage: Pi0.5 outputs a 50-step action sequence, so a 400-step evaluation experiment requires only about 8 inference calls (about 20 seconds GPU work) for a total of 200 seconds, resulting in a GPU utilization of about 10%. The bottleneck shifts from GPU computation to pipeline serialization (CPU preprocessing, WebSocket I/O, simulation steps). Batch evaluation using timer-based request collection can improve throughput. macOS sandbox security scope bookmarks require both compile-time permission declarations (in .entitlements file) and runtime lifecycle management (startAccessingSecurityScopedResource/stop). If the permission file is empty, it defaults to non-security-scope bookmarks, leading to failure during restoration. When permissions are missing, the bookmark system provides no visible error feedback. Log archaeology (reading complete log files) can reveal hidden patterns in code: “non-safety-scope-preserving bookmarks” appear 20 times across multiple sessions in Desktop Video, revealing missing permission information. Concurrent write errors (errorLog FileHandle competition) silently destroy diagnostic information. High-frequency timer logs (879 calls to updateClockLabels) mask real errors, so state-based logging should be used instead of count-based logging. Slurm’s srun with –jobid flag can bypass SSH PAM restrictions via srun in the assigned job context, such as slurm_adopt, which is very important in clusters with strict node access controls. When GPU nodes operate at 100% utilization, management commands executed via srun may experience significant latency (over 60 seconds). Therefore, robust monitoring scripts should handle timeouts gracefully and use lightweight alternative commands (such as nvidia-smi instead of nvitop). External dependency documents should serve operational purposes (structured list: path, size, purpose, reference), separate from conceptual documents (explatory guides). A clear file list with precise paths enables reproducibility and dependency auditing. For VLA benchmark projects, a comprehensive list includes 14 categories: configuration directories, logs, binary files, environment variables, Python packages, rclone paths, Git repositories, Ollama models, conda environments, datasets, checkpoints, startup programs, and troubleshooting guides. Practical Experience SwiftUI’s .mask() + .ultraThinMaterial can achieve “glassmorphism text” effects on macOS 12.4 and later by masking the blur effect of the material within the text shape. The material automatically samples the content below it in the window view hierarchy (video player → material → masked text). The dual-layer method (material mask + gradient overlay) simulates the physical glass effect with refraction and mirror highlights. Gaussian mixture model clustering (mclust) performs poorly after more than 100 dimensions. For basic model embedding (512d–1536d), kmeans or spectral methods must be used for actual operation. The EM algorithm of mclust becomes computationally difficult in high-dimensional data. Dialogue Summary MIHD Spatial Transcriptomics**✅ scGPT+UNI2 integration experiment, weekly report preparation, and visualization generation** 04:12:09.065 | claude_code The supervisor required the Monday report to include results of scGPT+UNI2+STAIG. The investigation revealed that the two-stage integration of STAIG ignored gene encoder embedding (instead using the original HVG matrix). The scGPT cache metadata was fixed, and the baseline condition based solely on genes was re-evaluated (ARI increased from 0.114 to 0.170). Five integration methods were tested for 11 parts (connection/mean/attention/llava_mlp/QFormer). QFormer achieved the best scGPT integration effect (ARI at 0.370). The visualize_weekly_report.py script was created to generate three summary charts (method ranking bar chart, part heatmap, PCA vs. scGPT comparison). Users were guided to use the existing visualize_from_cache.py script for part chart generation. A total of 36 visualization results were generated (3 summary charts and 33 part charts related to PCA/scGPT/UNI2 encoders), and key architectural findings were recorded in the weekly report.
Desktop video wallpaper 🔄 Fixes to the secure range bookmark system, redesign of the liquid glass screen protector, and ongoing debugging work 22:35:54.328 | claude_code Users reported that video files cannot be loaded after application restart, with an “operation not allowed” error. Analysis of 4438 lines of logs revealed the following issues: 1) The permission file was empty, causing bookmark creation to always be outside the secure range; 2) Concurrent writing in errorLog() lost all error logs; 3) There were over 1550 garbage log entries per session; 4) Two windows were opened at startup. The problem was solved by adding bookmark.app-scope permissions, implementing a fallback parsing outside the secure range, rewriting errorLog to use a shared log file, removing high-frequency log files, and fixing the startup order. The screen protector clock also changed from a card design to a liquid glass design using .lightMask() + .ultraThinMaterial + mirror gradient effects. Users subsequently requested completely transparent labels (not frosted glass) and reported video switching freezing issues. Investigation started through log analysis and exploration of SingleScreenView.swift, but the conversation was interrupted before a solution was found.
Error recovery benchmark testing 🔄 Pi0.5 VLA training monitoring, external dependency list, and GPU utilization optimization plan 06:44:17.740 | claude_code Users requested training status information for the entire GPU cluster. Data was successfully collected via Slurm commands (using srun –jobid to bypass PAM restrictions), training logs were analyzed, and a detailed report was provided: 6 Pi0.5 LoRA tasks on 49 GPUs (progress at 38.3%, ~37 hours remaining, 7/8 GPUs at 100% utilization), 4 tasks on 53 GPUs (progress at 26.8%, ~46 hours remaining, 7/8 GPUs at 100% utilization), and evaluation status (Stack tasks have a success rate of 95–100%, Coffee tasks have a success rate of 5–25%). A comprehensive external dependency list with 14 categories was created (docs/external_dependencies_inventory.md), covering over 65GB of data: configuration directories, AI assistant logs, external binary files, environment variables, Python packages, Google Drive rclone paths, external Git repositories, Ollama models, 4 conda environments, 10 HDF5 datasets (≈18.4GB), 9 BC-RNN checkpoints, 4 VLA checkpoints (≈47GB), startup scripts, and troubleshooting guides. The project panorama summary.md file was updated, and reference links were added. Users described a GPU utilization bottleneck: due to action chunking, GPU utilization was about 10% (only 8 inference calls per 400 steps, each call taking 2.5 seconds, i.e., 20 seconds of GPU time/200 seconds total time). Users requested an optimization plan and studied network resources for Pi0/Pi0.5 inference techniques, as well as implementation methods for batch evaluation, but the conversation was interrupted before a plan was delivered.
Token usage Total: $39.97 — 61.9 million tokens
summary: A critical error in the MIHD benchmark test was fixed, which is related to the limitations of the STAIG architecture. Meanwhile, permission issues associated with the macOS sandbox environment were resolved, and system performance was improved through secure bookmarks. Large-scale Pi0.5 VLA training was conducted on a GPU cluster, and a complete list of external dependencies was compiled. Additionally, bottlenecks in GPU usage during the evaluation process were identified.
title: Bug Journal 2026-03-02

content:
Weekly Report — 2026-W09 (2026-02-23 ~ 2026-03-01) This week, two main tracks were advanced concurrently on the DCC and Tianhe clusters: space transcriptomics (MIHD) and robot error recovery benchmark. On DCC, a fatal weight loading bug in scGPT was fixed (ARI improved by 44.4% on average), the MIHD benchmark was extended to the Visium HD dataset, and a large-scale repository refactoring of approximately 250K lines of code was completed; on Tianhe, the BC-RNN Phoenix baseline training pipeline was built from scratch (9 tasks parallelized), the root cause of 0% success rate in Pi0.5 evaluation was identified and fixed, key conclusions were obtained from M14 baseline evaluation (learning strategy yields SR≈0 in error scenarios, proving the necessity of M15 LoRA fine-tuning), and Pi0.5 LoRA 9 tasks were successfully fine-tuned parallelly on 6×A800 with stable startup.
Weekly Overview Metric Value Date Range 2026-02-23 ~ 2026-03-01 Active Days 5 / 7 Total Conversations 19 Projects Involved 5 Tasks Completed 35 Ongoing Tasks 6 Total Tokens 177,973,151 Total Cost $105.52 Average Daily Cost $21.10 Project Progress Error Recovery Benchmark (Robot Error Recovery Benchmark) (5 active days) — 🔄 active Completed:
M14 triple evaluation (Pi0/Pi0.5/BC-RNN) completed: BC-RNN SR=0.28%, Pi0/Pi0.5 SR=0%, while Random’s Recovery Progress is the highest, proving that learning strategies fail severely in distribution externalization under error injection scenarios, directly confirming the necessity of M15 LoRA fine-tuning Root cause of 0% success rate in Pi0.5 evaluation identified and fixed: Training task (MimicGen Task 5) and evaluation task (PickPlace) do not overlap at all; evaluation was moved to the training task BC-RNN Phoenix baseline fully implemented: image mode configuration rewritten (in line with MimicGen paper), 9 tasks trained parallelly and稳定运行, 64% SR reached after 22 epochs on Stack D0 Coffee BC-RNN configuration defect fixed: 57-dimensional object observation keys independently identified and added, fixing the root cause of Coffee’s 0% SR BC-RNN Stack_D0 error scenario generation pipeline completed: bug in 4-layer continuous image format fixed, 11 tip_over scenarios and MP4 visualizations generated Pi0.5 LoRA 9 tasks fine-tuned parallelly successfully started (6×A800, GPU utilization 100%, 77.7GB/card) Evaluation framework extended to 5 MimicGen tasks, with new task registry + –task parameter for unified management Pi0.5 Phoenix 9 task basic model evaluation: total SR=4.2% (24% on Stack D0, the rest ≤2%) 649 scenario database composition discovered: ~519 compatible scenarios + ~130 natural_* incompatible scenarios, actual valid evaluation targets are ~519 Blocked Items:
⚠️ Coffee environment initialization has object penetration/crushing issues (simulator bug), visualization of BC-RNN rollout shows the fix is incomplete ⚠️ Pi0.5 LoRA fine-tuning effect (compared to 4.2% baseline) will be verified after training completion MIHD (Multimodal Space Transcriptomics Fusion) (3 active days) — 🔄 active Completed:
Fixed fatal weight loading bug in scGPT: omission of self.use_fast_transformer in TransformerModel.init caused 17.7% random initialization of attention weights, after fixing, ARI improved by 44.4% and NMI improved by 33.3% STAIG fusion RM-IDEAL evaluation is significantly ahead (avg r=0.396 for 151673, peak r=0.644 for Layer_3), proving that multimodal fusion far exceeds single-modal baselines in capturing spatial niche structures (avg r≈0.06–0.12) Full support for Visium HD crop10large entire pipeline: 8 files modified, 4 path adaptation bugs fixed, end-to-end Silhouette=0.343 verified (vs PCA 0.086) VisiumHD barcode mapping discovered (r_big//4 pattern), three types of visualizations completed: pathologist annotation, STHD cell type, and STAIG fusion clustering comparison Vision Refine comparison experiment: found that scan_cluster refine is beneficial for weak fusion and harmful for strong fusion, qformer+no-refine is optimal (ARI=0.4832) Large-scale refactoring in Stage 6 of the repository: 41 files/~250K code + 5.3MB images removed, 6 functional modules extracted, 440 experiments verified via dry_run, logic reversal bug in BasicContrastive drop_feature fixed Three CPU acceleration implementations for STAIG fusion (cdist vectorization + GPUized random numbers + batch forward, expected 20–50x acceleration) Blocked Items:
⚠️ DLPFC slice 151676 has stable training collapse (NaN from epoch 1), requires independent parameter tuning, no fundamental solution currently Key Tasks- ✅ Fixes the scGPT use_fast_transformer weight loading bug and extracts all embeddings again (2026-02-28) — Omission of self.use_fast_transformer in TransformerModel.__init__ caused the key remapping in load_pretrained() to never execute, resulting in random initialization of all 12-layer attention Q/K/V weights (17.7% of parameters). After fixing a single line of code, ARI improved by 44.4%, and all 186/186 parameters matched. ✅ Identified the root cause of OOM during full fine-tuning of Pi0.5 and switched to LoRA architecture (2026-02-23) — Confirmed that JAX FSDP only slices parameter storage without reducing activation memory. The complete training state of Pi0.5 requires ~62GB/GPU, exceeding the A800 limit. Switching to gemma_2b_lora+gemma_300m_lora reduced VRAM to ~22.5GB, and Job 46553 ran stably at 2.0s/step. ✅ Completed the three-way evaluation of M14 and confirmed key conclusions (2026-02-27) — BC-RNN SR = 0.28%, Pi0/Pi0.5 SR = 0%, and the Random Recovery Progress (0.0199) was higher than all learning strategies. This proves that learning strategies fail severely in distribution外 generalization under error injection, directly supporting the necessity of M15 LoRA fine-tuning. ✅ Phase 6 cleanup and refactoring of the MIHD repository (2026-03-01) — Phase1 removed 41 dead files (~250K code + 5.3MB images); in Phases 2–4, shared functions in run_benchmark.py were migrated to 6 modules, and the bug of inverted logic in BasicContrastive drop_feature (>= changed to <) was fixed; a dry-run verified that 440 experiments passed. ✅ Full support for Visium HD crop10large across all links (8 files modified) (2026-02-28) — Modified the four modules in data_loader/clustering/run_benchmark/pipeline, added automatic clustering of HD without annotations (Leiden-estimated k), dedicated visualization logic for HD, and the hd_global configuration section, fixed coordinate space alignment and double preprocessing issues, and end-to-end verified Silhouette = 0.343. ✅ Identified and fixed compatibility issues in M14 scenarios (2026-02-23) — All three-way evaluations crashed on scene 122. AI analysis of EnvironmentMismatchError revealed that the 649 scenario library contained two types of environments (~519 compatible + ~130 natural_* incompatible). collector.py added a scene-level try-except to fix it, and the actual valid evaluation scenarios are about 519. 🔄 Built and started the parallel fine-tuning pipeline for Pi0.5 LoRA 9 tasks (2026-03-01) — Created train_pi05_benchmark.py (5 sub-commands), registered 18 configurations in openpi/config.py, and fixed 4 startup bugs (JAX_PLATFORMS, norm_stats path, boolean parameters, W&B agent), starting successfully with 6×A800, 100% GPU utilization, and 77.7GB/card. 🔄 Implemented the BC-RNN Phoenix baseline script and started parallel training for 9 tasks (2026-02-28) — Implemented train_bc_rnn_benchmark.py based on hyperparameters from the MimicGen paper, fixed 3 library-level bugs (mujoco_py import, MimicGen environment registration, inheritance chain in get_bounding_box_half_size), and parallelized 9 tasks on a single GPU (~2.2GB VRAM/task), including 50 rollout evaluations every 20 epochs. ✅ Identified and fixed the missing object observation keys in Coffee BC-RNN (2026-03-01) — By comparing the actual obs key structure of the HDF5 dataset, it was found that Coffee lacks 57-dimensional object states (Pod/Machine/Holder position + relative pose + hinge angle). Added extra_low_dim=['object'] for all 9 tasks, fixing the root cause of 0% SR in Coffee. ✅ Identified and fixed the root cause of 0% success rate in Pi0.5 evaluation (2026-02-26) — Confirmed that the training task (MimicGen 5 task) and the evaluation task (PickPlace) do not overlap at all; changed to evaluate on the training task. Human analysis directly pointed out the issue, and the AI’s initial analysis failed to identify this most obvious cause immediately. ✅ Rewritten the BC-RNN image mode configuration (5 tasks, consistent with MimicGen paper) (2026-02-26) — Rewritten all bc_rnn_configs from low_dim to image mode: ResNet18 + SpatialSoftmax encoder, CropRandomizer 76×76, RNN hidden_dim 1000, batch_size 16, epoch_every_n_steps 500, consistent with the main results of the MimicGen paper. ✅ Implemented three CPU acceleration methods for MIHD fusion training (2026-02-23) — Replaced scipy cdist vectorization with O(n²) nested loops (~100–500x), migrated random number generation to GPU to eliminate per-epoch transmission overhead, and added a batch forward interface to QFormerFusion (expected 20–50x). ✅ Developed the pipeline for generating error scenarios in BC-RNN Stack_D0 (2026-03-01) — Fixed four consecutive bugs in accessing image observations in robomimic BC-RNN (enable_camera detection, json.loads parsing checkpoint config, automatic detection of 84×84 resolution, HWC→CHW transpose + normalization), generating 11 tip_over error scenarios and MP4 visualizations. ✅ Full evaluation of RM-IDEAL across 27 embedding methods × 7 layers (2026-02-28) — Ran the full RM-IDEAL evaluation with 27 embedding methods, generated 189 three-panel visualizations for Zhang, and staig_fusion ranked first with an average r=0.396 (peak r=0.644 at Layer_3), quantifying the advantage of multi-modal fusion. ✅ Extended the evaluation framework to 5 MimicGen tasks (2026-02-26) — Created 5 new task YAML configs + task_registry.yaml, added --task parameter to the 1/3/4 scripts, fixed the observation dimension error caused by _D0 env suffix stripping (65→37), and rewritten run_full_eval.sh to support multi-task loops. ✅ Full slice benchmark for STAIG fusion (11 DLPFC slices) (2026-02-23) — Ran pca+uni2+staig_fusion and none+uni2+staig_fusion on 11 DLPFC slices, fixed the UNI2 patch_size compatibility bug (256×256→224×224), with success in 10/11 slices and an average ARI=0.546; known collapse at 151676. ✅ Comparison experiment between MIHD Vision Refine and Baseline (2026-02-23) — Ran full comparisons of 8 fusion methods with/without scan_cluster refine on slice 151673, and qformer+no-refine was optimal (ARI=0.4832). Found that refine is beneficial for weak fusion (attention +0.086) but harmful for strong fusion (qformer -0.054). ✅ Fixed key bugs in evaluate_mimicgen.py and collector.py (2026-02-23) — Fixed the in-place array modification bug in quat2axisangle (used np.clip+copy), captured EnvironmentMismatchError at the scene level in collector.py, ensured reproducibility with env.seed(), and verified the 8D state dimension assert. Issues and Solutions 1. Pi0.5 full fine-tuning training requires ~62GB/GPU, and JAX FSDP=4 cannot effectively reduce VRAM (only slicing storage does not reduce activation memory), repeatedly causing OOM [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-02-23) Solution: Switch to the gemma_2b_lora+gemma_300m_lora architecture, reducing training parameters by ~90% and reducing VRAM to ~22.5GB/GPU. Job 46553 runs stably at 2.0s/step.
2. All three-way evaluations of M14 crashed on scene 122/649: ~130 natural_* scenario XML hashes are incompatible with the current Mimicgen environment, triggering EnvironmentMismatchError without detection, causing the entire evaluation process to crash [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-02-23) Solution: Add a try-except for EnvironmentMismatchError in collector.py’s collect_on_scenes()for each scene, skip incompatible scenarios and log warnings, and restart with–resume`. The actual valid evaluation scenarios are about 519.
3. Training logs are severely distorted due to stdout buffering: Pi0.5 training shows only ~580 steps, but actually reached step 3000, leading to misjudged training termination and unnecessary restart [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-02-23) Solution: Add PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1+stdbuf -oL to the training script and sbatch submission scripts; use sbatch for long-term training and decouple the independent batch job from the interactive session lifecycle.
4. The success rate of Pi0.5 evaluation is 0%, misjudged as model quality issues [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-02-26) Solution: Confirmed that the training task (MimicGen 5 task) and the evaluation task (PickPlace) do not overlap at all; change to evaluating on the training tasks (Coffee/Stack/Threading/Assembly).
5. Observation dimension mismatch in BC-RNN evaluation (Expected 65, got 37) [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-02-26) Solution: Add a import mimicgen registration for the _D0 environment in create_env(); stop stripping the _D0 suffix and retain all MimicGen observables (_D0 environment provides additional object state observables).
6. scGPT TransformerModel.__init__ omits self.use_fast_transformer, causing the key remapping in load_pretrained() to never execute, and 17.7% attention weights are randomly initialized; strict=False silently skips without error [MIHD] (2026-02-28) Solution: Add a single line self.use_fast_transformer = use_fast_transformer in model.py. After fixing, ARI improved by 44.4%, and all 11 DLPFC slice embeddings were extracted again.
7. WebSocket client always reports ConnectionRefusedError; attempts with different address formats (localhost/127.0.0.1/0.0.0.0) all fail [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-02-28) Solution: Found that the http_proxy environment variable is set to 127.0.0.1:10087; the websockets library fails due to connection through the proxy.After unsetting all proxy variables at the beginning of run_eval.sh, the connection was established successfully.
8. CoffeeMachineBodyObject lacks the get_bounding_box_half_size() method, causing an AttributeError during the initialization of the MimicGen Coffee task rollout (An interface gap between MimicGen and the current robosuite version) [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-02-28)Solution: Trace the entire call chain (coffee_machine.py→CoffeeMachineBodyObject→CompositeBodyObject→MujocoXMLObject), and implement get_bounding_box_half_size() in three different base classes. 9. The HD data uns[‘spatial’] image is a full-resolution image, but its coordinates are in the cropped fullres pixel space, resulting in a mismatch during visualization; moreover, since X has been logged transformed, the pipeline will again normalize_total+log1p, causing a double transformation [MIHD] (2026-02-28) Solution: Replace the uns[‘spatial’] image with cropped_fullres.tif in load_hd_data() and recalculate the scalefactor; add the skip_log parameter to preprocess_data(), and pass skip_log=True for HD data only for HVG filtering.
10. The Coffee BC-RNN loss converges normally (-7.66→-15.4), but SR remains 0% all the time. With the same configuration, epoch 20 already reaches 64%, showing a high similarity to insufficient model capacity [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-01) Solution: Compare with the actual obs key structure of the HDF5 dataset, and find that Coffee requires a 57-dimensional object state (required for multi-stage precise operations), and the configuration template lacks this field; add extra_low_dim=[‘object’] for all 9 tasks and regenerate the configuration.
11. The robomimic BC-RNN image observation access fails at four consecutive levels: the detection logic of enable_camera/checkpoint config is in JSON string format/image resolution acquisition/HWC→CHW format conversion all have issues [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-01) Solution: ① Detect the rgb modality from the JSON string of checkpoint config (needs json.loads); ② Read the actual 84×84 size from shape_metadata; ③ Manually transpose HWC→CHW and convert uint8→float32/255 normalization (ObsUtils.process_obs automatically handles it in the standard rollout).
12. Pi0.5 LoRA training starts with four consecutive blocking bugs: ① Setting JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu separately is ineffective; ② Wrong path for norm_stats; ③ Boolean parameter–overwrite=False is ineffective; ④ Access to W&B external network on HPC nodes is blocked [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-01) Solution: ① Set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""+JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu simultaneously; ② The actual path for norm_stats is assets//benchmark//norm_stats.json; ③ Use–no-overwrite instead; ④ Predefine WANDB_MODE=disabled.
13. VisiumHD HD data pipeline path adaptation: The image path lookup in the vision encoder and spatial coords loading during fusion fail because they assume the DLPFC directory structure [MIHD] (2026-03-01) Solution: Add the cropped_fullres.tif pattern recognition to find_spatial_image(); pass the crop_dir.parent as data_root when calling the vision encoder; directly load coordinates from adata.obsm[‘spatial’] during fusion to bypass path lookup.
14. When calculating norm_stats, GPU util=0 but memory is fully used, and the task progresses slowly for a long time; the root cause is that PaligemmaTokenizer loads eagerly on all visible GPUs when calling get_config().model [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-01) Solution: Set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""+JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu simultaneously; ② The actual path for norm_stats is assets//benchmark//norm_stats.json; ③ Use–no-overwrite instead; ④ Predefine WANDB_MODE=disabled.
15. Architecture (architecture) JAX FSDP only splits parameter storage, which does not affect the full model loading and forward activation memory during initialization; the full training state of Pi0.5 requires ~62GB/GPU, and a single A800 with 80GB cannot support full fine-tuning; LoRA (gemma_2b_lora) is the only viable solution for the A800 cluster, reducing memory demand to ~22.5GB. When the warning “Can’t reduce memory use below 62.46GiB” appears, switch to LoRA immediately. The observation keys in BC-RNN configurations must match task complexity: Tasks like Coffee requiring multi-stage precise operations need a 57-dimensional object state, and a 84×84 image cannot provide sufficient spatial precision; the behavior of configuration bugs (normal loss but SR=0) is highly similar to insufficient model capacity, and differentiation requires comparison with dataset structures. Vectorization and batching accelerate significantly: O(n²) nested loops → cdist matrix operation approximately 100–500x, Python逐spot loops → batch GPU forward预计 20–50x. Similar bugs may exist in upstream open-source repositories, and the weight loading path needs active auditing rather than blind trust. Key details of robomimic BC-RNN inference: Checkpoint config is stored as a JSON string (needs json.loads, not direct dict access); when bypassing the standard rollout process, manually transpose HWC→CHW and convert uint8→float32/255 normalization (ObsUtils.process_obs automatically handles it in the standard rollout). The 649 scenario database consists of two types of environments: ~519 impulse/augmented compatible scenarios (xml_hash matching) and ~130 natural_* natural capture scenarios (xml_hash different). Approximately 519 actual valid evaluation scenarios exist in M14, and all document and target episode counts need corresponding updates. STAIG fusion leads comprehensively in RM-IDEAL evaluation (average r=0.396 for 151673, peak r=0.644 for Layer_3), and multi-modal fusion has a much better ability to capture spatial niche structures than single-modal baselines (gene/vision avg r≈0.06–0.12). Vision Refine performance is polarized: beneficial for weak fusion (attention +0.086 ARI), harmful for strong fusion (qformer -0.054); strong fusion already has the ability to handle high-dimensional inputs, and dimensionality reduction loses information. Cross-task evaluation is a common trap in robot learning: Non-overlap between training set tasks and evaluation tasks directly leads to 0% SR; ensure train/eval task consistency during experimental design. The MimicGen _D0 environment provides additional object observables; removing the _D0 suffix reduces the observation dimension from 65 to 37, breaking input consistency during inference. VisiumHD coordinate mapping: r_big//4 of 2um bin gives 8um grid row (same for col); the spatial visualization size parameter in scanpy is a multiple of spot_diameter_fullres; HD 8μm (diameter≈7.3) requires size≈4.0, DLPFC (diameter≈144) uses size=1.0; the Leiden community found that (resolution=1.0) is the default clustering strategy for unlabeled HD data (crop10large k=17, Silhouette=0.302). Tools (tools) Best practices for Slurm cluster training engineering: Long-term training requires using sbatch (not srun to avoid session timeout due to SIGTERM); standardize all training scripts with PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1+stdbuf -oL; clean zombie GPU processes with fuser /dev/nvidiaX before starting (monitoring tools like nvitop also hold CUDA context); MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID corresponds to the physical GPU number rather than the logic of CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. Key configurations for JAX/Pi0.5 training: ① Set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""+JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu in CPU mode; ② XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.95 is effective for A800 80GB (61→77.7GB); ③ HPC nodes must predefine WANDB_MODE=disabled; ④ Use–no-overwrite for argparse boolean flags, not–flag=False; ⑤ The path for openpi norm_stats is assets//benchmark//norm_stats.json. The HTTP/HTTPS proxy environment variable (http_proxy) is transparently proxied by the Python websockets library, so unset the proxy variable when debugging local services on HPC clusters. The MimicGen environment registers via the side effect of import mimicgen in robosuite; explicit execution of this import is required before calling external tools. Fixing methods missing in third-party libraries must be implemented in the entire inheritance chain across all base classes, and fixing only the recently called point will cause errors in other subclasses. The pam_slurm_adopt cluster GPU nodes do not support direct SSH; srun –overlap can attach new steps to existing interactive jobs to reuse node resources; robomimic in a non-TTY environment will exit with EOFError if a checkpoint directory already exists, so clean the directory thoroughly before each start.
