summary: This week, two main tracks—space transcriptomics (MIHD) and robot error recovery benchmark—were advanced in parallel on both DCC and Tianhe clusters. On DCC, the bug related to fatal weight loading in scGPT was fixed (average ARI improvement of 44.4%), the MIHD benchmark was extended to the Visium HD dataset, and a large-scale repository refactoring of approximately 250K lines of code was completed; on Tianhe, the BC-RNN Phoenix baseline training pipeline was established from scratch (9 tasks run in parallel), the root cause of the 0% success rate in the Pi0.5 evaluation was identified and fixed, key conclusions were obtained for the M14 baseline evaluation (the learning strategy achieves SR≈0 in error scenarios, proving the necessity of M15 LoRA fine-tuning), and the Pi0.5 LoRA 9 task was successfully fine-tuned in parallel on 6×A800 with stable operation.
title: Weekly Summary 2026-W09

content:
Daily Report — 2026-03-01 Daily Overview Completed Work: Parallel execution in three computing environments: using HPC (DCC) for spatial transcriptome visualization and code repository modernization; training robot learning models on supercomputers and managing cluster infrastructure; enhancing development tools on local workstations (MacBook) and conducting retrospective documentation. Implementation Methods: DCC utilizes the STHD/STAIG workflow and achieves it through dataset compatibility fixes and phased code refactoring; Tianhe uses Slurm job scheduling for iterative training debugging and GPU resource optimization; MacBook automatically integrates logs via gadget/summarize tools and employs plan-driven multi-file collaborative editing. Impact: Successfully unified multiple modal annotation sources for VisiumHD analysis, achieving 100% match rate; transformed MIHD from a massive structure at 136K to a modular architecture; recorded the full development history for February through over 28 automated reports; achieved producible robot learning baselines (98% on Stack’s BC-RNN, 4.2% on Phoenix Pi0.5), along with parallel training on 6 GPUs with 95% memory utilization; released Desktop Video 4.1 version, fixing critical playback issues, and adopting native macOS Tahoe design. DCC Completed Work: Completed VisiumHD crop10large multi-source annotation visualization (pathologists achieved 100% match at 8um resolution, STHD coverage was 96.3%, and STAIG Silhouette fusion coverage was 0.343); conducted a six-stage code repository refactoring for MIHD (removed 250,000 lines of useless code, extracted shared functions, and verified integrity); generated work logs on February 28, including over 60 visualization links; replaced scGPT from mclust with KMeans, reducing each processing step to 2 minutes. Implementation Methods: Resolved high-definition dataset path incompatibility through 5 rounds of debugging; implemented r_big//4 coordinate mapping for Zenodo annotations; used majority voting algorithm to partition STHD between 2um and 8um; performed stepwise dependency-aware refactoring (migrating dependencies before removing source code) and verified via pipeline dry-run (440 experiments) and grep checks on remaining references. Impact: Enables direct comparison of pathologist expert knowledge with clinical tissue computational predictions; MIHD transformed from a chaotic massive structure into a clear modular architecture; reduced scGPT workflow from 6 hours to less than 3 minutes (360x speedup); established STAIG baseline performance on high-definition data. MacBook Completed Work: Main device executed three parallel workflows: batch generation of historical reports (28 days of data from February to March), workflow optimization via –sync function for daily processing, and improvement of Desktop Video application (fixed 3 critical playback issues and completely redesigned Liquid Glass UI). Implementation Methods: Automated multi-device log integration through dailySummary.py merging operations (export → merge → deploy process); modified cmd_merge() function to delegate it to _mcmd_merge_sync_all() when –sync option is used without –date option; performed plan-driven collaborative editing on Desktop Video (fixed playback issues for 7 files, optimized UI for 6 files) and conducted comprehensive localization and build verification. Impact: Successfully synthesized 25 days of data into structured reports (3 reports failed due to output constraints); simplified future batch operations by eliminating over 50 manual commands; released Desktop Video 4.1 preview 0301 with fully functional PowerSave/PowerSave+/auto mode and Liquid Glass upgraded to native macOS Tahoe design (.regular glass, capsule container, localized formatting). Tianhe Completed Work: Completed BC-RNN 9 task training (success rate on Stack reached 98%, Coffee’s success rate was 0% due to lack of object observation data); conducted Phoenix Pi0.5 evaluation (overall success rate 4.2%, 450 cases); diagnosed reasons for training failures, cleared 468GB idle GPU memory, fixed Pi0.5 LoRA training process, and archived v4.17 project structure (mimgen_workspace old code, external dependency index). Implementation Methods: Used Slurm overlap mode for GPU resource management; monitored training process via file system polling and TensorBoard; conducted iterative diagnosis on startup scripts (JAX CPU configuration, path mismatch, CLI flags, W&B disabled); shut down idle VLA servers (Phoenix/Pi0/Pi0.5); increased GPU allocation from 4 to 6, using XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.95; file archiving based on bash scripts. Impact: Established BC-RNN baseline showing stack task success rate of 44–98% (verified training process correctness), identified the root cause of Coffee 0% SR (lack of 57-dimensional object observation keys); obtained complete Phoenix results for 9 tasks; released critical GPU resources; achieved parallel training on 6 GPUs with 100% memory utilization (memory allocation rate 95%), 77.7GB per GPU; organized code repository and recorded external dependencies. TzJsDesktop Completed Work: Made small contributions to the gadget tool: added conversation_summaries field into the daily report structure. Implementation Methods: Enhanced report structure through code editing. Impact: Enriched historical records and enabled detailed dialogue breakdown by project. Large-scale work across devices: completed integration of MIHD high-definition datasets, verified multi-source annotations, refactored large code repositories (cleaned 250,000 LOC), optimized 28 historical daily reports for batch generation, fixed BC-RNN/Pi0.5 training processes, achieved parallel training on 6 GPUs, and released Desktop Video 4.1 version with playback fixes and Liquid Glass interface improvements.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy - ✅ STAIG Fusion HD Dataset Support — Fixed 6 technical issues (path handling, image mode, coordinate loading, clustering backoff, standard output buffering), enabling the PCA × UNI2 × STAIG fusion process to run on HD crop10large; in the generated cluster visualization, Silhouette value is 0.343, k-value is 20, and training time is 300 cycles.- ✅ MIHD Phase 6 Code Repository Refactoring — Phase 1: Removed 41 unused files (approximately 250,000 lines of code and 5.3MB image files). Phase 2: Extracted shared functions in run_benchmark.py into models/staig_utils.py, models/vision_extractors.py, models/Fusion.py, and utils/clustering.py. Phase 3: Removed run_benchmark.py and 6 related models. Phase 4: Extracted generic STAIG code and fixed the BasicContrastive drop_feature vulnerability. Phase 5: Updated 5 documentation files and removed the benchmark_config.yaml file. Phase 6: Verified pipeline import and model import, and performed dry-run tests (440 experiments in total), checking for remaining grep references. ✅ BC-RNN Configuration Fix: Add Object Observation Key — Modified the train_bc_rnn_benchmark.py file by adding extra_low_dim=[‘object’] for all 9 tasks, solving the fundamental issue of Coffee 0% SR (lack of 57-dimensional object state, including container/holder positions). All configuration files were regenerated, the changes were verified, and the template and documentation updated to version v4.16. ✅ Fix Pi0.5 LoRA Training Workflow (5 Debug Cycles) — Fixed the startup script through iterative debugging: (1) Added JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu for norm_stats used only on CPU; (2) Changed the path of norm_stats from checkpoints/ to assets/; (3) Changed –overwrite=False to –no-overwrite syntax; (4) Set WANDB_MODE=disabled for HPC nodes; (5) Increased the number of GPUs from 4 to 6, adjusting XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.95 to achieve an allocation of 77.7GB/GPU. Finally achieved 6-GPU parallel training with 100% utilization. ✅ VisiumHD Pathologist Annotation Visualization and Mapping — Mapped the pathologist CSV data on Zenodo to the 8um interval, achieving a 100% match rate through the r_big//4 coordinate transformation (17,502 intervals in total), and generated H&E and annotation dual-panel visualization results. 4 spatial regions were identified: tumor (8498), connective tissue (5166), non-tumorous epithelial tissue (3826), and smooth muscle (12). ✅ Desktop Video Playback Mode Error Fixes (3 Interrelated Errors) — Fixed the following issues: (1) PowerSave/PowerSave+ did not delegate to global evaluation when creating new windows; (2) No low-power mode detection was present in auto mode; (3) Changes in UI mode did not trigger state re-evaluation. Coordinated editing of 7 files: AppState.swift (playbackMode.didSet), SharedWallpaperWindowManager.swift (delegated to global), AppDelegate.swift (NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChange observer + isLowPowerModeEnabled), removed redundant onChange handler, updated localization for 5 languages, and created a ChangeLog entry for the v4.1 preview version 0301. ✅ Training and Evaluation of BC-RNN 9 Tasks — Monitored the 20-cycle training process for coffee_d0/d1, stack_d0/d1, stack_three_d0/d1, threading_d0, and three_piece_assembly_d0/d1; initial evaluation results showed: stack_d0 reached 64%, stack_d1 reached 44%, while the coffee series did not reach 0% (root cause: lack of object observation key); final result: accuracy for Stack D0/D1 reached 98%, while accuracy for coffee D0/D1 reached 0%. ✅ Phoenix Pi0.5 Evaluation (9 Tasks × 50 Experiments) — Completed the full MimicGen benchmark evaluation for the Pi0.5 Phoenix checkpoint, step 99999. Overall success rate was 4.2% (19/450), with significant learning outcomes for stack tasks (24% in D0 stage, 12% in D1 stage), while coffee/stack three/thread/assembly tasks were close to 0%. ✅ scGPT Clustering Performance Optimization — Changed from mclust to KMeans, reducing processing time for all DLPFC parts to approximately 2 minutes, with an average ARI of 0.1695 and NMI of 0.2772; speed increased by 360 times while maintaining acceptable quality. ✅ Implement Gadget Merging — Daily Processing Synchronization — Modified the cmd_merge() function in daily_summary.py so that when –sync is used and –date is not specified, logs can be processed daily automatically. First checked if args.date was None, then delegated to _ncmd_merge_sync_all() function, which groups files by date, generates a sub-process per day, skips existing reports, and finally deploys in batch. ✅ Desktop Video UI Optimization: Liquid Glass and Duplicate Content Removal — Removed duplicate PlaybackMode selectors and idlePauseSensitivity sliders from GeneralSettingsView; redesigned CombinedGlassClock to match the macOS Tahoe interface style (using Capsule/RoundedRectangle styles, 28pt date and 96pt time font, 20pt spacing, no shadow, removed GlassCompat); unified the clock position factor to a constant of 0.85; implemented localized date formatting via the EEEMMMMd template. ✅ GPU VRAM Cleanup (Releasing 468GB of Memory) — Disconnected 3 idle VLA servers: Phoenix serve_policy.py (PID 2413737, approximately 407GB of memory, occupying 7 GPUs, zero utilization), Pi0 server (PID 2138978, approximately 61GB of memory), Pi0.5 server (PID 2046779, approximately 61GB of memory). All GPUs 0–6 were fully released, and only GPU 7 was used for BC-RNN training. ✅ Error Recovery Benchmark Project Cleanup (v4.17) — Phases 1–4: Archived top miscellaneous files (19MB PDF file), outdated documentation (README_V4), old code for mimicgen_workspace (v1-v3 frameworks, over 13 files), temporary logs, and pycache files; merged VLM tutorial; created README.md, .gitignore, docs/EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCIES.md; updated CLAUDE.md and project summary to v4.17 version. ✅ Finalization Mechanism for Gadget Merging Phase — Tracks the finalization status of source logs in the cmd_merge() function; when the target date is later than today and all source logs are finalized, set report._finalized=True; _cmd_merge_sync_all() function skips already finalized reports; added –force parameter to override checks and pass to sub-processes. Implementations and Fixes ✅ Batch Generation of February Historical Daily Reports (28+ days) — By running the daily_summary.py merge command, structured JSON/Markdown reports for February 1, 3, 5, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13 (×3), 14 (×3), 15 (×2), 16, 17 (×3), 18, 19 (×3), 20, 22 (×2), 23, 26 (×2), 28, and March 1 were generated. Each report covers the MIHD/error-recovery-benchmark/CalendarPro/gadget projects. Three complex dates resulted in a 32K output token limit. ✅ Generation of MIHD February 28 Work Log and Visualization Links — Created docs/experiments/daily_summary_20260228.md, including metrics for 3 main directions (Visium HD support, visual refinement process, performance optimization), 7 experimental groups, and over 60 visualization links using relative paths, enabling rendering via GitHub/Hugo. ✅ Improvement of STHD/MIHD CLAUDE.md — Enhanced the STHD CLAUDE.md file by adding missing CLI commands (hdpp, sthdviz), detailing the structure of frontline/qcmask/roi/sim modules, and pdata format description, Numba JIT comments. Enhanced the MIHD CLAUDE.md file by adding visual enhancement models (STEGO/BYOL/SCAN/SpatialGAT), high-definition dataset command examples, test scripts, cache directory descriptions, etc. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. VisiumHD Dataset Path and DLPFC-Oriented Process Incompatibility: Image files do not match, spatial coordinate loading fails, mclust cannot handle the number of high-definition intervals (17,502 intervals, while DLPFC has 4,992 positions) Solution: 5 rounds of debugging: fixed path parsing logic, refactored coordinate loading mechanism, implemented a fallback from mclust to KMeans for large datasets, added tqdm and PYTHONUNBUFFERED for better visibility. HD crop10large now runs the full STAIG process, with speed increased by 360 times (2 minutes vs over 40 minutes per part). Key Finding: DLPFC and VisiumHD differ in scale by more than 3 times; mclust’s EM algorithm cannot scale (17,502 partitions require 40 minutes), while KMeans provides acceptable quality trade-offs in exploratory spatial transcriptomics (ARI approximately 0.17 vs 0.20–0.25).
2. Coffee BC-RNN Achieves 0% Success Rate Across All 600 Cycles, While Stack Reaches 98% Solution: User identified the root cause: all 9 task configurations from the same template only contained robot-centered observation data (eef_pos, eef_quat, gripper_qpos), lacking 57-dimensional object state information (pod/holder position). Coffee’s multi-stage precise operations require object information; simple Stack tasks can rely on visual recognition. This issue was fixed by adding extra low_dim=[‘object’] to all tasks and regenerating the configuration.

7. The Desktop Video auto-mode does not have a battery status awareness function; even when macOS is in low-power mode, it always uses the PowerSave logic. Solution: A observer NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChange was added to applicationDidFinishLaunching; a powerStateDidChange handler was implemented; shouldPauseAllVideos() was updated to check ProcessInfo.processInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled: allOverlaysCompletelyCovered() is called when normal power mode is used, and anyOverlayCompletelyCovered() is called when low-power mode is active.
Key Finding: The low-power mode of macOS can be queried via ProcessInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled, and observed through NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChange; adaptive behavior requires both querying and observation simultaneously.

Solution: It was found that Phoenix serve_policy.py (PID 2413737) consumes approximately 407 GB of memory on 7 GPUs, but the utilization is only 0% (idle server). Key Finding: If not monitored, idle model service processes may occupy GPU memory for days. Regular use of nvidia-smi and process auditing can prevent resource shortages. Multi-GPU models waste resources especially when idle.

Key Finding: HPC compute nodes usually have no internet connection; for batch tasks, cloud logging services (such as W&B, MLflow, Comet) can be disabled or offline mode can be configured.

This tool groups files by date (in the format YYYY-MM-DD_device.json), processes each date in a separate subprocess, skips dates already reported, and finally performs batch deployment.
Key Finding: Unifying the --sync behavior to match --sync-all eliminates confusion and makes the batch filling process more efficient (more than 50 manual commands were eliminated for the February history).

content:
Daily Report — 2026-02-28 Daily Overview Completed work: Used advanced MIHD spatial transcriptomics technology to support Visium HD high-resolution data and implemented automatic clustering; completed RM-IDEAL correlation analysis for 27 embedding methods; fixed a serious ML model checkpoint loading issue that caused 17.7% parameter loss; implemented a complete wallpaper history tracking system; resolved multi-screen power management issues; and started the Pi0.5 Phoenix VLA evaluation, identifying some basic training problems. Implementation methods: Implemented an HD data adapter based on Leiden algorithm and optimized automatic clustering and visualization functions; conducted root cause analysis on PyTorch model loading and found missing instance attributes; designed a full-stack history feature including asynchronous thumbnail generation and SwiftUI interface; explored multi-agent code and identified stub functions; systematically debugged issues in the GPU cluster environment (such as proxy variables, CUDA memory shortage, library mismatch, etc.); and started a comprehensive 9-task robot control benchmark. Impact: Enables MIHD to handle next-generation HD data; determined that STAIG fusion is the optimal method (r=0.396); improved scGPT clustering performance by 44% (ARI increased from 0.118 to 0.170), resulting in valid research outcomes; implemented a desktop wallpaper history feature with an appropriate user experience mode; fixed two completely damaged energy-saving modes; and found that the trained VLA model’s success rate on its own training task was only 0–24%, indicating basic architecture or training issues. DCC Completed work: Expanded MIHD spatial transcriptomics workflow to suit Visium HD (17K points), implemented automatic clustering; performed RM-IDEAL evaluation for section 151673 using 27 methods; and fixed a serious scGPT checkpoint loading issue that caused 17.7% attention layer parameter loss. Implementation methods: Developed an 8-step HD implementation plan, performing label-free clustering using Leiden algorithm; conducted detailed correlation analysis and generated 189 visualization results; added the missing self.use_fast_transformer attribute to achieve correct Wqkv→in_proj key remapping. Impact: Determined the basis for HD data integration and quantified the advantages of STAIG fusion; average ARI increased from 0.118 to 0.170 (+44.4%), NMI increased from 0.208 to 0.277 (+33.3%) across all 11 DLPFC parts. MacBook Completed work: Implemented a complete history feature for the desktop video wallpaper application, including a thumbnail user interface; fixed critical cross-screen support issues (4 stub functions caused failure in energy-saving mode); created comprehensive project documentation; and added an automatic build number function. Implementation methods: Designed and implemented 5 new Swift files (data model, storage, view, thumbnail generator), using UserDefaults persistence, activation with double-click, and cooling time setting; started 3 parallel exploratory agents to systematically analyze cross-screen logic, identify stub functions and bookmark persistence issues; and added an Xcode run script phase to automatically update CFBundleVersion. Impact: Implemented a production-ready history system with an appropriate user activation experience mode; identified and recorded 4 severe stub functions that damaged energy-saving/powerSavePlus feature characteristics, as well as persistence issues causing user data loss; recorded the architecture for future development; and automated version tracking, eliminating manual updates. tianhe Completed work: Established a comprehensive evaluation of the pre-trained Pi0.5 Phoenix VLA model, which was evaluated on 9 MimicGen robot control tasks; investigated training completion; and prepared a BC-RNN benchmark test baseline for the Phoenix paper, considering compatibility with error injection. Implementation methods: Systematically debugged the GPU cluster environment (proxy variable blocking WebSocket, zombie processes causing CUDA memory shortage, robosuite version mismatch, etc.); reused existing server processes; configured correct library versions into PYTHONPATH; started a SLURM job considering resource requirements; traced training checks and configurations through the file system; and checked existing robomimic modes and error framework adapters. Impact: Successfully started the 9-task benchmark evaluation (7/9 completed), showing that even on its own training task, the trained model performed poorly (success rate only 0–24%), indicating basic architecture or training issues; identified severe evaluation gaps (no evaluation of a model trained with 100,000 steps); clarified three different Pi0.5 variants and their data sources; and laid the foundation for systematically replicating Phoenix benchmarks in the future through error injection integration. Advanced spatial transcriptomics workflows support Visium HD and conducted comprehensive RM-IDEAL benchmark tests; fixed serious scGPT model loading issues, improving clustering metrics by 44%; implemented desktop wallpaper history features while solving multi-screen power management issues; and established VLA evaluation processes, showing that despite training on target tasks, Phoenix models still perform poorly.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy - ✅ Fixed scGPT checkpoint loading errors — Added the missing self.use_fast_transformer attribute, causing 17.7% attention layer parameters (9.4M weights) to use random initialization instead of pre-trained weights. Re-extracted all 11 DLPFC parts’ embedding data; after fixing the model, clustering metrics improved significantly. 🔄 Evaluated Pi0.5 Phoenix VLA on 9 MimicGen tasks — Started a complete evaluation process on a GPU cluster, evaluating pre-trained Pi0.5 Phoenix (checkpoint step 99999) on 9 robot control tasks. Resolved key environmental issues (proxy variables, CUDA memory shortage, robosuite version mismatch). Although the model was fine-tuned for these tasks, 7/9 tasks had very poor performance (success rate 0–24%). 🔄 Supported Visium HD (crop10large) data — Developed an 8-step plan to integrate high-definition data (17,502 data points) with Leiden algorithm automatic clustering, visualization adaptation, and benchmark testing workflows. The main challenge was the lack of real labels, requiring a unsupervised evaluation strategy. ✅ Fixed multi-screen power management and persistence errors — Analyzed multi-screen errors using 3 parallel exploratory tools and identified 4 critical function vulnerabilities (allOverlaysCompletelyCovered, anyOverlayCompletelyCovered, reassignAllWindows, windowScreenDidChange), which caused powerSave/powerSavePlus modes to fail. Additionally, BookmarkStore.purge() lacked certain keys, leading to data loss. Although an implementation plan was developed, users stopped using it. ✅ RM-IDEAL benchmark for section 151673 — Evaluated 27 embedding methods and calculated the Spearman correlation between cosine similarity and RM-IDEAL scores. Generated 189 visual PNG files and detailed CSV summary tables, showing that STAIG fusion is optimal (r=0.396). ✅ Investigated Pi0.5 training status and distinguished different variants — Traced Pi0.5 Phoenix training checkpoints and found training completed to step 99999, but no evaluation was performed. Identified three Pi0.5 variants: (1) the official pre-trained base version (M14 error recovery), (2) our Phoenix LoRA fine-tuning version (9 MimicGen tasks, 4500 episodes), (3) zhaoganlong’s single-task variant. Associated each variant with its training dataset. 🔄 Planned BC-RNN benchmark/ evaluation scripts — Designed the train_bc_rnn_benchmark.py script, including 4 modes (generation configuration, training, evaluation, report), for reproducing the Phoenix baseline. Investigated existing robomimic configurations and error framework modes and confirmed compatibility issues with RobomimicPolicyAdapter. Due to user interruption, implementation has not started yet. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Implemented desktop wallpaper history feature — Created a complete history tracking system including 5 new Swift files (WallpaperHistoryEntry, WallpaperHistoryStore, HistoryView, HistoryItemRow, ThumbnailGenerator), supporting UserDefaults persistence, a thumbnail interface with a screen selector, activation via double-click, and a history clearing button. ✅ Reusable visualization script (visualize_from_cache.py) — Created a script that can generate clustering visualizations from cached embedding data, supporting embedding loading, clustering, metric calculation, and scanpy visualization. Designed for multi-process optimization because GPU acceleration is not applicable. ✅ Created desktop wallpaper CLAUDE.md documentation — Generated comprehensive project documentation including build commands, MVVM architecture, key conventions, playback modes, code style, and git workflow. ✅ Automated build number updates — Added a function in the Xcode Run Script build phase to set CFBundleVersion to the current date (YYYYMMDD format). ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING needs to be disabled to allow modification. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. The scGPT spatial clustering ARI score is very low (about 0.10), despite using pre-trained checkpoints; colleagues suspect flash attention incompatibility causing checkpoint loading problems Solution: The root cause is that TransformerModel.init never saves use_fast_transformer as an instance attribute, so getattr(model, ‘use_fast_transformer’, True) always returns True, preventing the Wqkv→in_proj key remapping. This issue was fixed by adding self.use_fast_transformer = use_fast_transformer. After fixing, the average ARI increased from 0.118 to 0.170 (+44%), and NMI increased from 0.208 to 0.277 (+33%).
Key insight: When an instance attribute is missing in a PyTorch model class, even with strict=False, checkpoint loading may fail, causing partial parameter initialization failures (17.7% random weights), manifested as performance degradation rather than obvious errors. Always verify whether the checkpoint key matches the model state dictionary and clearly record mismatches.
2. Visium HD data lacks real labels, making traditional ARI/NMI metrics unsuitable for benchmark evaluation Solution: Use the Leiden community detection algorithm to automatically estimate the number of clusters from k-NN plots, outputting only cluster visualization results with contour scores. Modify compute_metrics() to conditionally skip supervised metric calculation when labels are unavailable. The Resolution parameter can control the granularity.
Key insight: Unsupervised spatial transcriptomics data require different evaluation strategies — focusing on visual consistency and internal consistency metrics (contour scores) rather than external validation. Tracking data sources is crucial for detecting pre-applied transformations.
3. In the multi-screen wallpaper application, powerSave and powerSavePlus video pause modes do not work, despite an occlusion detection infrastructure Solution: Identified 4 critical function vulnerabilities: allOverlaysCompletelyCovered() and anyOverlayCompletelyCovered() are hardcoded to return false; reassignAllWindows() and windowScreenDidChange() have no effect. The automatic mode is a viable template. These four functions were implemented using the existing overlayWindows.values and .occlusionState.contains(.visible) patterns.
Key insight: To-do comments in production code may disrupt functionality, while it appears to compile successfully but fails at runtime. This is a dangerous technical debt that may have gone unnoticed. The occlusion detection infrastructure already works in the automatic mode; only the connections need being established.#### 4. An error occurred during the Pi0.5 server evaluation, indicating that the WebSocket connection was rejected, even though the TCP port is open and the server is listening on localhost:8000.Solution: The proxy environment variables (http_proxy=127.0.0.1:10087, https_proxy, HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, no_proxy, NO_PROXY) interjected into WebSocket connections, even those to localhost. The problem was resolved immediately by removing all proxy variables. Key Insight: Even if the original TCP layer works properly, proxy environment variables may quietly interfere with localhost connections—they intercept at the application layer before socket creation. When debugging WebSocket issues on a development machine or shared cluster, be sure to check and remove the values of proxy variables.
5. HD adata_8um.h5ad has been transformed via logging (range [0, 6.05]), but preprocess_data() defaults to applying log1p, resulting in double transformation and data corruption. Solution: Add the skip_log parameter to preprocess_data() and preprocess_for_encoding(). Detect HD datasets through metadata checks, and set skip_log=True to skip redundant normalization operations. Use theadata.uns[’log1p’] flag or X.max() heuristic for detection.
Key Insight: Preprocessed external datasets need clear tracking of transformation history to prevent pipeline corruption. The HD point diameter (7.3px) is 20 times smaller than that of Visium, so dynamic adjustment of visualization parameter sizes (size=4.0 vs 1.0) is required to avoid invisible points.
6. When trying to load the 50.7 GiB Pi0.5 model on a GPU cluster, CUDA memory was insufficient—existing processes on the GPU consumed most resources. Solution: Run nvidia-smi and ps to identify the zombie server process (PID 2413737) that is already loaded and listening on port 8000. Reuse existing server instances instead of restarting new ones to avoid OOM issues and save 3–5 minutes of startup time.
Key Insight: When loading models exceeding 50GB on shared GPUs, be sure to check nvidia-smi and existing processes before attempting to restart. Reusing zombie servers is more efficient than killing and restarting them, and also ensures resource utilization and proper behavior for multi-user clusters.
7. Initial confusion about the Pi0.5 training state—Slurm job 46553 crashed at step 5000, and it is unclear whether 100k steps were completed. Solution: Directly check the checkpoint directory and find that the timestamp in the checkpoint records goes up to February 24, confirming successful training, even though the job crashed early (possibly recovering from a checkpoint). It was also noted that there was never an evaluation performed.
Key Insight: Slurm job logs do not reflect everything—they only show execution history, not the completeness of results. Always verify completion by checking actual checkpoint files and their timestamps, rather than relying solely on log tail information. Training completion does not mean evaluation completion.
8. The Robosuite environment lacks the get_bounding_box_half_size method, and env.seed() API is incompatible when evaluating Pi0.5 Phoenix. Solution: Configure PYTHONPATH to use zhaoganlong’s robosuite/mimicgen from the deps/ directory, rather than the local mimicgen_workspace version. For effective evaluation, the environment must have exactly the same library versions as the training environment.
Key Insight: VLA policy evaluation requires identical library versions to the training environment—even minor differences in robosuite/mimicgen versions can cause API incompatibility (missing methods, signature changes). Version mismatches may render benchmark results invalid.
9. Exploration of GPU acceleration for visualization widgets—cuML/FAISS is not installed, and mclust is unavailable (problem related to R_HOME). Solution: Analysis shows that the clustering process (100–300 milliseconds) is not the bottleneck; data loading and matplotlib rendering consume most time. Multiprocess parallel processing should be used instead of solely optimizing GPU performance.
Key Insight: Overly early attempts at GPU optimization—analysis indicates that I/O and rendering are the limiting factors, not computation. For this I/O-dependent workload, parallel CPU processing is more effective than GPU. Analyze before optimizing.
General Issues 10. When trying to modify the Info.plist for building the product, Xcode build scripts attempt to automatically update CFBundleVersion, but encounter “Operation Not Allowed” errors. Solution: Enable ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = YES in project settings to prevent build scripts from writing files. Set it to NO, allowing PlistBuddy to modify the Info.plist of the built application.
Key Insight: Xcode’s user script sandbox feature (introduced in the latest version) defaults to blocking build scripts from accessing files, which is separate from the application’s runtime sandbox permissions. To make changes, this feature must be disabled.

Daily Report — 2026-02-26 Daily Summary Completed Tasks: A production‑level LaTeX resume was developed on MacBook, the image training process based on BC‑RNN was implemented, and a multi‑task evaluation framework was adopted; exploration of the Pi0.5 VLA policy evaluation infrastructure for the MimicGen task was conducted at Tianjin Hai Laboratory. Implementation Methods: Professional formatting was done using Jake’s resume template on MacBook; BC‑RNN configuration was converted to an image mode with ResNet18 encoder; the evaluation framework was extended to support 5 MimicGen tasks; parallel infrastructure exploration was carried out at Tianjin Hai Laboratory, mapping Pi0.5 checkpoints, VLA server architecture, and evaluation processes. Impact: LaTeX resumes suitable for ATS were generated for job applications; a reproducible BC‑RNN benchmark test process was established, and the 0% success rate issue was resolved through task alignment evaluation; a complete mapping of the Pi0.5 evaluation infrastructure was completed, making systematic testing of trained MimicGen cases possible. MacBook Completed Tasks: Professional LaTeX resumes were created from markdown drafts using Jake’s resume template. Implementation Methods: Format was improved through multiple editing iterations, and the publication section layout was optimized to ensure compatibility with Overleaf. Impact: A concise, ATS‑friendly resume template was generated, which can be directly used for job applications. Tianjin Hai Laboratory Completed Tasks: The BC‑RNN image mode training system was implemented, the root cause of the 0% success rate was analyzed, a multi‑task evaluation framework supporting 5 MimicGen tasks was built, and the Pi0.5 evaluation infrastructure was explored in multiple repositories. Implementation Methods: Five BC‑RNN configurations were rewritten to use ResNet18 encoders for image observation; parallel GPU training was initiated; task mismatch issues were diagnosed; a task registry was created and scripts were extended to include the –task parameter; the _D0 environment observation dimension handling issue was fixed; a parallel exploration agent was used to map Pi0.5 checkpoints, VLA server startup mechanisms, and evaluation processes. Impact: A reproducible BC‑RNN benchmark test process aligned with MimicGen paper standards was established; the critical 0% success rate issue was resolved through proper task alignment; a comprehensive understanding of Pi0.5 evaluation components was obtained, making systematic testing possible. LaTeX resumes were created on MacBook, a comprehensive BC‑RNN image mode training system was implemented at Tianjin Hai Laboratory, and the Pi0.5 model evaluation infrastructure was explored
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Convert BC‑RNN training configuration from low‑dimensional mode to image mode — Five BC‑RNN training configurations were rewritten using image observation data (84×84, ResNet18Conv encoder, RNN hidden layer dimension 1000, batch size 16), meeting the requirements of MimicGen paper. ✅ Implement multi‑task evaluation framework — Five task YAML configuration files were created, three evaluation scripts were modified to accept –task parameters, and run_full_eval.sh was updated to support multi‑task evaluation. ✅ Resolve observation dimension mismatch issue — The create_env() function in four scripts was modified, mimicgen was imported, and the _D0 environment variant was retained instead of removing a suffix, ensuring consistent observation between training and evaluation. 🔄 Design Pi0.5 evaluation plan — A detailed implementation plan was developed for running Pi0.5 evaluation on 9 trained MimicGen tasks using the discovered infrastructure. ✅ Diagnose Pi0.5 and BC‑RNN training results — Pi0.5 (99,999 steps, 0% success rate) and BC‑RNN (600 cycles, dimension mismatch) were analyzed, and the root causes were identified as task distribution mismatch and object state handling issues. 🔄 Start BC‑RNN training for 5 tasks — Parallel BC‑RNN image mode training was initiated on GPUs 0–4 for coffee, stack, stack three, thread, and three piece assembly tasks (600 cycles per task). ✅ Explore Pi0.5 training settings — The Pi0.5 checkpoint was mapped in zhaoganlong’s directory to understand checkpoint structure and available training models. ✅ Explore VLA evaluation infrastructure — The VLA server was understood through start_vla_server.py, model type support, port configuration, and service architecture. ✅ Explore zhaoganlong evaluation process — The evaluation process of the Pi0.5 model based on motion self‑reflection framework on MimicGen tasks was understood. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Create professional LaTeX resume — Markdown drafts were converted to professional LaTeX format using Jake’s template, and the format of the publication and experience sections was gradually improved. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. Despite completing 99,999 steps, Pi0.5 had a 0% success rate, and the input dimension of BC‑RNN did not match (expected 65, actual 37) Solution: Analysis revealed that Pi0.5 was trained on 5 MimicGen tasks (coffee, stack, thread, assembly, stack three), but evaluation was performed on PickPlace, which is not in the training data. The dimension mismatch in BC‑RNN occurred because the create_env() function removed the ‘_D0’ suffix from the environment name, resulting in fewer object observations returned by the base robosuite environment than the MimicGen variant. Solution: mimicgen was imported to register the _D0 environment using the full environment name, and training/ evaluation tasks were adjusted accordingly.
Key Insight: Task distribution mismatch is a critical yet often overlooked issue in robot learning evaluation; environment naming conventions can disrupt observation consistency between training and deployment.
2. BC‑RNN training configuration was in low‑dimensional mode (state‑based), while the MimicGen paper uses image mode (pixel‑based) as the main benchmark Solution: All five BC‑RNN configurations were rewritten to adopt image mode: ‘object’ was removed from obs.low_dim, agentview_image and robot0_eye_inhand_image were added to obs.rgb, a ResNet18Conv+SpatialSoftmax encoder was used, the RNN hidden layer dimension was increased from 400 to 1000, the batch size was reduced from 64 to 16, and hdf5_cache_mode was set to ’low_dim’.
Key Insight: Image‑based BC‑RNN requires a completely different architecture (ResNet18 visual encoder, larger RNN, smaller batch size) compared to low‑dimensional mode; the official MimicGen benchmark uses image mode with 600 cycles.
3. The evaluation framework only supports PickPlace task and cannot evaluate the 5 tasks actually trained by Pi0.5 Solution: A comprehensive multi‑task framework was built: five task YAML configuration files were created, containing task‑specific objects, phases, and thresholds; task_registry.yaml was created to map task names to datasets/checkpoints/prompting; 1.generate_scenes.py, 3.collect_data.py, and 4.analyze_results.py were modified to accept –task parameters and auto‑parse; run_full_eval.sh was rewritten to process tasks cyclically.
Key Insight: The evaluation infrastructure should be independent of tasks from the beginning; adding multi‑task support requires coordinated changes in configuration, scripts, and orchestration layers.
4. It is unclear whether the official BC‑RNN checkpoint or self‑training was used, nor which observation mode is used** Solution: The MimicGen repository was investigated to confirm that they only provide datasets and no pre‑trained checkpoints. Users explicitly wanted image mode (pixel‑based ResNet18 model, 600 cycles) to match the main results of the paper, rather than low‑dimensional mode (state‑based model, 2000 cycles). Key Insight: Benchmark papers usually do not provide model weights but only datasets; clear configuration selection (observation mode, training duration) can avoid wasting time on incorrect settings.
5. Complex multi‑repository evaluation infrastructure is needed, including error_recovery_benchmark and Motion-based-Self-Reflection-Framework, which contain interdependent components. Solution: Three parallel exploration agents were started, and training settings, evaluation infrastructure, and flowcharts were drawn simultaneously, then results were combined.
Key Insight: Parallel exploration of independent aspects can significantly accelerate understanding of complex systems compared to sequential investigation.
General Issues 6. Current login nodes cannot access GPUs (nvidia‑smi fails to communicate with NVIDIA drivers) Solution: It was determined that evaluations must run on compute nodes via Slurm scheduling (active tasks with GPU allocation were found on node an49).
Key Insight: Always check GPU availability and job scheduling systems before planning evaluation tasks that require a large number of GPUs.
Human‑and‑AI Approaches Strategic Level Availability and training strategy of BC‑RNN checkpoints Role Approach Human Before continuing training, asked whether BC‑RNN used the official checkpoint and wanted to verify if MimicGen paper provided a pre‑trained model. AI Initially directly implemented the training script without checking the official checkpoint; after the human questioned, a thorough investigation of the MimicGen repository was conducted, confirming no checkpoints were provided. Analysis of Differences: Humans show better caution by questioning assumptions before investing expensive computing resources; AI is eager to implement solutions without first verifying whether training is truly necessary. This indicates AI tends to solve problems without questioning upstream requirements.
Task alignment strategy for evaluation Role Approach Human Clearly stated the principle: “Train on task X, evaluate on task X,” after understanding the root cause of the 0% success rate; confirmed that BC‑RNN should follow the same strategy. AI Provided detailed root cause analysis and initially suggested retraining Pi0.5 or evaluating on PickPlace, or evaluating on trained tasks; humans chose the latter approach. Analysis of Differences: Humans make architectural decisions based on resource constraints and research goals; AI offers options but leaves strategic direction to humans.
Observation mode selection for BC‑RNN Role Approach Human Clearly chose image mode (pixel‑based) when faced with two options, which matches the main results of MimicGen paper. AI Prepared a trade‑off analysis between low‑dimensional and image modes, but waited until humans made a decision. Analysis of Differences: Humans make informed choices based on research reproducibility goals; AI provides technical background but transfers decision‑making authority to humans in method selection.
Planning of evaluation methods Role Approach Human Requested direct testing of “Pi0.5 trained on Mimicgen test set” — a clearly defined goal‑driven task. AI Interpreted the request as requiring full infrastructure understanding before execution, initiating a broad exploration phase to map all components. Analysis of Differences: Humans focus on final results, while AI recognizes the need for complete infrastructure knowledge to avoid failure — its approach is more conservative and systematic.
Limitations of AI Key Limitations BC‑RNN training process was implemented without first verifying whether the official pre‑trained checkpoint was available, and investigation only occurred after human questioning. This indicates AI is quick to solve problems without validating upstream assumptions. Detailed technical diagnosis was provided for the 0% success rate, but strategic questions such as whether retraining on PickPlace or evaluating on original tasks were not raised first. This requires humans to set the direction. General Limitations After collecting comprehensive information about Pi0.5 evaluation through parallel exploration and file reading, a plan was announced, but the complete implementation plan was not shown in the conversation logs. When creating the resume, format details were iterated multiple times rather than deeper understanding of user preferences to reach a final design faster. Lessons Learned Key Lesson — Task allocation mismatch between training and evaluation is a serious failure mode, manifesting as 0% success rate. In this case, Pi0.5 was trained on {Coffee, Stack, Threading, Assembly, Stack Three} but evaluated on PickPlace, resulting in a system failure despite successful training.- The MimicGen paper only provides a demonstration dataset (HDF5 file), without offering pre-trained model checkpoints. Researchers must train the BC-RNN model using robomimic, which is the official benchmark protocol. There are two different observation modes for BC-RNN, and their architectures are also completely different: the low-dimensional mode (state-based, 2000 cycles, a larger MLP) and the image mode (pixel-based, ResNet18 encoder, 600 cycles, a larger RNN). The main results in the MimicGen paper use the image mode. The environment naming convention in robosuite/MimicGen has semantic meaning: removing the ‘_D0’ suffix changes which environment category is instantiated, thereby changing the object properties returned. The objects returned by the basic robosuite environment have fewer dimensions than the MimicGen’_D0’ version, resulting in a dimension mismatch (65→37 dimensions). The VLA strategy evaluation requires coordination among multiple components: checkpoint locations, strategy servers (based on websocket/TCP), evaluation scripts, conda environment management, and GPU resources allocated via Slurm — any missing component will hinder the entire process. The multi-task evaluation infrastructure needs coordinated design at different levels: task configuration (YAML), registry mapping (datasets/checkpoints/tips), script parameters (with automatic parsing of –task flags), and orchestration (task loops in bash scripts). Post-final adjustments are much more expensive than early-stage task-independent design. Image-based robot learning strategies require camera rendering functionality during both training data collection and evaluation. The camera resolution must match the training resolution (84×84 for BC-RNN image mode) to avoid a mismatch in the input dimensions of the visual encoder. Parallel exploration agents are very effective for understanding multi-component systems — independently exploring training settings, evaluation infrastructure, and process code, and then integrating this information, allows faster system comprehension than sequential investigation. The Pi0.5 evaluation stack uses a dual-process architecture: the strategy server (openpi05 conda environment) serves the model via websocket, and the evaluation script (mimicgen_env) runs through the network environment and queries the server. Practical Experience Jake’s resume template on Overleaf is a popular ATS-friendly LaTeX format that is easy to customize. It uses a simple chapter format and horizontal lines, requires no special fonts or packages, and can be used with any standard LaTeX distribution. Conversation Summary Personal Resume ✅ Creating a professional LaTeX resume from markdown 04:33:57.481 | claude_code The user provided a markdown-formatted resume draft and requested it to be converted into LaTeX format. The assistant selected Jake’s resume template on Overleaf because it is suitable for ATS and handled the formatting of the resume. After multiple iterations, the inline format of the publication section was changed to a double-line header format. The final deliverable is a complete .tex file that can be compiled using Overleaf.
Error Recovery Benchmarking ✅ Implementation of a multi-task evaluation framework 02:34:46.032 | claude_code A comprehensive multi-task evaluation infrastructure was implemented as planned. Five task YAML configuration files were created (coffee, stack, stack three, thread, three items assembled), each containing task-specific objects, phases, and thresholds. The task_registry.yaml file was built to manage the mapping between datasets/checkpoints/tips centrally. Three evaluation scripts were modified to accept –task parameters with automatic parsing. Five BC-RNN training configuration files were created, and run_full_eval.sh was updated to handle task loops. By importing mimicgen and retaining the _D0 environment name, the dimension mismatch issue was resolved. When asked about the availability of BC-RNN checkpoints, the assistant confirmed that MimicGen only provides datasets, and the user chose the image mode for training.
✅ Implementation of BC-RNN image mode training 04:00:34.795 | claude_code A comprehensive BC-RNN image mode training process was implemented. Five training configuration files were rewritten, converting from the low-dimensional mode to the image observation mode (ResNet18 encoder, 84×84 resolution, RNN hidden layer dimension 1000, batch size 16). The evaluation script was modified to enable camera rendering for the BC-RNN strategy. Parallel training was initiated across all five MimicGen tasks, running on GPUs 0–4, with each task running for 600 cycles. Successful training began was confirmed via logs, and the image observation mode was verified.
✅ Analysis of Pi0.5 and BC-RNN training states 01:10:41.534 | claude_code The user requested information about the running status of the previously started Pi0.5 and BC-RNN training. The assistant investigated and found that Pi0.5 completed 99,999 steps but had a 0% success rate, while BC-RNN completed 600 cycles but encountered a dimension mismatch error. Root cause analysis showed that Pi0.5 was trained on the five MimicGen tasks, but PickPlace (task mismatch) was used during evaluation, and the dimension issue in BC-RNN occurred because the _D0 suffix was removed, causing loss of object state. The user decided to make the training and evaluation tasks consistent.
🔄 Exploration of Pi0.5 and MimicGen evaluation infrastructure 04:10:57.207 | claude_code The user requested testing of the Pi0.5 model trained on MimicGen on training cases. The assistant started three parallel exploration tasks to understand training settings, VLA server infrastructure, and evaluation processes. Checkpoint locations were found in the zhaoganlong directory, the serve_policy websocket architecture was understood, GPU requirements were determined via Slurm, and a implementation plan was begun. The complete evaluation infrastructure across multiple repositories was organized, and key files such as evaluate_mimicgen.py and start_vla_server.py were identified.
